name: 3d-chromatin-structure-data-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell Hi-C TAD/TLD predictors against a known reference partition, or when ground-truth-free experimental scHi-C data cannot disambiguate predictor accuracy.

name: 4dn-portal-data-retrieval
description: Use when extending the DNALONGBENCH contact map prediction task beyond the five primary cell lines (HFF, H1hESC, GM12878, IMR90, HCT116) to new cell types whose Hi-C matrices are available on the 4DN portal.

name: ablation-study-performance-comparison
description: Use when a multi-input deep learning model combines two feature extractors (e.g. dna2vec and motif features) and you must quantify whether fusion outperforms each module trained alone across multiple cell lines.

name: adapter-trimming-quality-filtering
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads (single- or pair-ended NGS data, e.g. ChIP-seq/RNA-seq/ATAC-seq) must be cleaned of adapters, low-quality bases, and short or poorly mapping reads before alignment and downstream peak calling, differential expression, or nucleosome positioning.

name: adaptive-head-transfer-learning-enformer
description: Use when benchmarking a motif-based classifier (e.g., BOM) against a pretrained sequence model on binary or multiclass distal-CRE classification across cell types, and Enformer must be fine-tuned on identical train/test partitions.

name: adjusted-mutual-information-comparison
description: Use when two cluster label vectors cover the same set of cells and you need a chance-corrected score of clustering stability, e.g. before vs. after removing CNV-harboring chromosome peaks from a scATAC accessibility matrix.

name: adjusted-mutual-information-evaluation
description: Use when comparing TLD/TAD partitions predicted by multiple algorithms (e.g., deDoc2, deTOKI, scHiCluster, Higashi) on downsampled, simulated, or single-cell Hi-C matrices at 40 kb binsize and you need an accuracy ranking.

name: adjusted-mutual-information-partition-comparison
description: Use when comparing two genome partition/TLD call sets — e.g., predictions from noise-perturbed vs. original downsampled Hi-C matrices — to measure how much domain structure is preserved.

name: adjusted-rand-index-computation
description: Use when scoring clustering quality of single-cell epigenomic methods against known ground-truth cell labels (e.g. sorted cell lines), comparing methods such as ChromSCape, SnapATAC, CisTopic, Cusanovich2018 and EpiScanpy on a shared dataset.

name: age-breakpoint-detection-in-temporal-omics
description: Use when you have age-ordered omics or feature trajectories (e.g., PBMC aging series from ATAC-seq/RNA-seq of adults aged 22-93) and need to detect abrupt age windows of rapid epigenomic or transcriptomic change rather than assuming gradual accumulation.

name: age-correlation-analysis-of-pc1-scores
description: Use when donor-level PCA coordinates (e.g., PC1 scores) from ATAC-seq or RNA-seq are available together with donor age and sex metadata, and the goal is to confirm that the top PC axis tracks aging and sex-dimorphism.

name: agglomerative-hierarchical-clustering-of-genomic-peaks
description: Use when you need to group peak regions from one or more ChIP-seq marks by signal-shape similarity without anchors such as TSSs or gene annotation, using DTW distances between binned coverage profiles.

name: aggregate-peak-analysis-zscore
description: Use when comparing CTCF-mediated loop callers (e.g., GILoop vs. Peakachu) on Hi-C contact maps and you need a threshold-independent visual/quantitative check that predicted loops are enriched in real contact signal, via APA z-scores computed around each caller's predicted loops.

name: aic-likelihood-based-model-selection
description: Decision support for choosing the number of sub-compartments (N_subcompartment) when running CscoreTool-M on Hi-C data, where no prior annotation fixes the compartment count.

name: aic-model-order-selection
description: Use when you have a feature-by-donor abundance matrix (peaks or genes) from chronological samples and need to distinguish true age-driven longitudinal trends from noise before clustering trajectories.

name: aic-model-selection
description: Use when binary RRBS read matrices Y (reads x CpGs) at a locus must be partitioned into an unknown number of epialleles and Q must be chosen without manual specification or overfitting.

name: aligner-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when an NGS workflow's alignment step dominates compute time (e.g. a 6-8 h baseline on 100 mammalian FASTQ files) and a decision is needed on whether swapping to HISAT2 or Rsubread within systemPipeR reduces it below ~3 h.

name: aligner-workflow-template-configuration
description: Use when an existing systemPipeR RNA-Seq workflow is too slow because its alignment step dominates compute time, and the goal is to substitute HISAT2 or Rsubread for Bowtie2/TopHat2 and quantify the runtime speedup.

name: alignment-ambiguity-filtering
description: Use when aligning bisulfite-treated reads across four converted genomes (CT/GA x Watson/Crick) and you must merge mapRDDs, then filter ambiguous reads to guarantee unique alignments before methylation profiling.

name: alignment-parameter-configuration
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads (e.g. H3K4me3 ChIPseq or RNAseq from mouse embryonic stem cells) must be mapped as an automated pipeline step and per-sample aligner choice and parameters must be configured.

name: alignment-penalty-parameter-tuning
description: Use when configuring EpiAlign's mismatch/deletion penalties (epsilon_N=1.5, epsilon_D=1 defaults) or choosing equal vs frequency-based chromatin state weights W(k,S) before scoring local alignments of compressed state sequences.

name: alignment-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking the computational cost and discriminative power of a chromatin state sequence alignment method, specifically when validating that compressing consecutive identical ChromHMM states preserves EpiAlign's ability to separate real from randomized epigenomes while reducing runtime.

name: alignment-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing alignment runtimes of bisulfite sequencing aligners across read volumes (10M/50M/100M/200M reads) and cluster sizes, or when validating scale-out Spark aligners against MapReduce, MPI, or single-server baselines.

name: alignment-score-distribution-comparison
description: Use when validating an alignment-based epigenomic method: you need to show horizontal alignment scores on real ChromHMM chromatin state sequences separate from a randomized negative control, or to normalize scores by a randomized baseline.

name: allele-frequency-binned-constraint-regression
description: Use when gnomAD SNVs overlap fine-mapped eCLIP enriched windows and you need to test whether disruptive variants are depleted from factor-bound sequences as evidence of constraint.

name: allele-frequency-matching-of-variant-sets
description: Use when building labeled variant training sets for a variant-effect or disease-association classifier and you need negative controls frequency-matched to positives (MAF thresholds or matched MAF distributions) to avoid allele-frequency artifacts.

name: allele-specific-haplotype-assignment
description: Use when ChIA-PET (or similar chromatin interaction) data must be resolved into haplotype-specific peaks and loops for a genome whose SNP phasing information is available, and allelic bias in binding coverage needs statistical testing.

name: allele-specific-methylation-visualization
description: Use when WGBS reads have been aligned and methylation-called with Msuite and you need per-read, genotype-preserved methylation views at imprinted or allele-specific loci, e.g. to phase reads at a heterozygous A/G SNP and observe reciprocal methylation bars.

name: allele-specific-pet-assignment
description: Use when analyzing ChIA-PET bedpe data from a heterozygous sample (e.g., GM12878 with Illumina Platinum Genomes phased genotypes) to determine which parental allele mediates each chromatin loop.

name: allele-stratification-by-detection-efficiency
description: Use when evaluating how per-allele data quality (fraction of detected targeted segments in chromatin tracing/FISH data) affects chromatin loop caller sensitivity or false-positive discovery, or when deciding a detection-efficiency cutoff before loop calling.

name: amplicon-cycle-reconstruction
description: Use when low-coverage WGS FASTQ/BAM files from cancer samples (e.g. SRA SRP081035, CCLE PRJNA523380) must be converted into a catalog of eccDNA coordinates (chromosome, start, end, copy count), as in the eccDNAdb study of 3395 tumor samples.

name: analytic-vs-empirical-power-comparison
description: Use when validating or trusting scPower power estimates for low-mean eQTL genes, i.e. when pseudobulk mean expression falls below the regime where the analytic linear-model approximation holds and simulation is needed as a cross-check.

name: ari-clustering-agreement-evaluation
description: Use when a clustering method's output assignments must be compared against known cell-type labels on single-cell data (e.g., scATAC-seq Forebrain, k=8), or when ARI degradation under graded input corruption must be tabulated across tools.

name: arima-time-series-trend-modeling
description: Use when a feature-by-donor abundance matrix (e.g., ATAC-seq peaks or RNA-seq genes across adults aged 22–93) must be scanned for features whose abundance changes systematically with donor age rather than fluctuating randomly.

name: arm-level-copy-number-calling
description: Use when you have a normalized, filtered binned scATAC-seq accessibility matrix and need per-cell chromosome arm-level gains/losses (e.g., to separate malignant from nonmalignant cells or define genetic subclones).

name: assay-category-stratified-statistics
description: Use when you have per-sample ChIP-seq/DNase-seq QC metrics (FRiP, PBC, fragment size, mapping rate) and need to test whether metric correlations differ across assay categories before pooling them.

name: assembly-quality-assessment-with-quast
description: Use when two shotgun read sets (e.g. a chemically treated library such as RIMS-seq and its untreated control) have each been assembled de novo and you must quantify whether treatment altered assembly quality via N50 and mismatch rate.

name: atac-dnase-chipseq-peak-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have ENCODE narrowPeak files from two open-chromatin assays (e.g. ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq) in the same cell type and need QC plus overlap/benchmarking against a ChIP-seq reference.

name: atac-dnase-technology-benchmarking
description: Use when contrasting open-chromatin peak files generated by different technologies (e.g. K562 ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq narrowPeak files from ENCODE) and you need ChromHMM-based annotation differences as the benchmarking readout.

name: atac-rna-cross-modal-correlation
description: Use when single-cell multiome ATAC+RNA data has been aggregated into pseudo-bulk cell types and the goal is to test whether observed peak–gene correlations exceed a genomic-structure-aware null.

name: atac-seq-dar-input-preparation
description: Use when starting from aligned ATAC-seq data or a DiffBind contrast and you must produce a chromosome-coordinate region BED (e.g., mm10_RUNX1.bed) as the query input for BIT or comparable TR-identification methods.

name: atac-seq-differential-accessibility-peak-classification
description: Use when comparing two ATAC-seq aging signatures (e.g., male vs female donors) on a shared peak set, needing a between-sex correlation of log2 fold-changes plus per-sex opening/closing DA peak counts.

name: atac-seq-differential-accessibility-scoring
description: Use when you have ATAC-seq (or similar accessibility) data for two cell types and want sequences ±100 bp around an anchor motif scored by a log2 fold-change so downstream motif analysis can test whether motif spacing correlates with cell-type-specific accessibility.

name: atac-seq-peak-liftover
description: Use when query genomic intervals (e.g., human brain ATAC-seq peaks in hg38) must be mapped to another species' genome (e.g., zebrafish rn6 via a UCSC reciprocal- chain file) and scored for regulatory conservation rather than mapped by sequence alone.

name: atac-seq-peak-query-processing
description: Use when a set of genomic intervals (e.g. mouse mm10 ATAC-seq peaks) must be mapped to orthologous candidate target regions in another species (e.g. human hg38) with epigenomic and sequence-grammar prioritization.

name: atac-seq-peak-set-analysis
description: Use when you have a set of ATAC-seq peaks or a DiffBind differential accessibility report (e.g. Fold/FDR columns from a TR knockout in mouse thymocytes) and need to identify or rank transcriptional regulators from the region coordinates.

name: atac-seq-replicate-sample-sheet-configuration
description: Use when setting up a bulk ATAC-seq differential accessibility comparison from perturbation (e.g., cKO-vs-WT) experiments with ≥2 replicates per condition and processed BAM plus MACS2 narrowPeak files available.

name: atac-seq-tn5-offset-correction
description: Use when processing paired-end ATAC-seq alignments (e.g. GEO GSE66386) into fragment midpoint-count observables, where raw insert sizes must be shortened by 8 bp for the Tn5 9-bp duplication before classifying fragments.

name: atacseq-chromatin-accessibility-annotation
description: Use when sgRNA genomic coordinates must be assigned chromatin accessibility values from genome-wide ATAC-seq tracks (ATACdb) as epigenetic features for sgRNA activity prediction.

name: atacseq-peak-gene-annotation
description: Use when you need to derive a TF-target gene prior from open-chromatin ATAC-seq peaks (e.g. the TCGA Genomic Data Commons ATACseq-AWG atlas) to constrain a neural decoder's TF-to-gene layer, as in CITRUS.

name: atc-score-reconstruction
description: Use when a high-dimensional matrix (e.g., gene expression or CpG methylation) needs a feature-selection score for subgroup/consensus partitioning, especially when features should be ranked by their global correlation to other rows rather than by variance.

name: attention-mechanism-configuration-analysis
description: Use when tuning or reproducing the attention hyperparameters of the CITRUS PyTorch model on the TCGA 5803-sample/17-tumor-type pickled dataset, where attention size and head count must be grid-searched against prediction correlation.

name: auc-metric-computation
description: Use when a ranked, score-filtered list of candidate target regions (e.g. from adaptive_liftover plus gr_candidate_filter) must be evaluated against matched orthologous ground-truth regions, or when tuning a window-size parameter via AUROC/AUPR in leave-one-out cross-validation.

name: auc-prc-performance-computation
description: Use when a set of ranked predicted regulatory interactions (e.g., gene–peak pairs) needs to be evaluated against a trusted positive set such as cis-eQTLs to quantify prediction performance.

name: aupr-mcc-model-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether a motif-count classifier (BOM) or any sequence model outperforms established baselines on the same binary/multiclass CRE classification task, using auPR and MCC.

name: auprc-f1-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a binary enhancer-target interaction classifier (e.g., XGBoost on BENGI All-Pairs.Natural-Ratio pairs) and you need AUPRC/F1 estimates free of genomic leakage via chromosome-split cross-validation.

name: auroc-auprc-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing supervised variant-prioritization classifiers across multiple tissue-specific folds or cross-validation splits, where per-fold AUROC and AUPRC must be computed and summarized (e.g., median across 44 GTEx tissues or mean across 5 folds).

name: auroc-evaluation-across-cell-types
description: Use when benchmarking a sequence model on the DNALONGBENCH eQTL task and you need per-cell-type AUROC values plus an average to compare against the paper's reported scores (Expert Model average AUROC 0.681).

name: auroc-performance-comparison-across-datasets
description: Use when you need to test whether a motif-count feature category (e.g., overlapping vs. non-overlapping FIMO annotations) is biologically informative by retraining BagOfMotifs models and comparing auROC before and after the ablation.

name: auroc-performance-evaluation-of-enhancer-classifiers
description: Use when a trained motif-count enhancer classifier (e.g., BagOfMotifs/XGBoost on FIMO-scanned CREs) needs quantitative performance assessment via auROC, or when verifying that models generalize across species or cell types.

name: auto-correlation-characteristic-length-fitting
description: Use when diagnosing multi-scale spatial structure in binned ChIP-seq data: compute and fit the auto-correlation curve at each coarse-graining scale to distinguish real broad-domain signal (growing lambda) from synthetic/random-placement data (flat lambda ~100 kb).

name: autocorrelation-length-fitting-for-coarse-graining-termination
description: Use when running RECOGNICER coarse-graining on binned ChIP-seq read counts and you need an objective, scale-aware criterion to terminate the recursive block transformation and proceed to domain retrieval.

name: autoencoder-gof-regularized-scoring
description: Use when detecting non-B DNA structures from ONT translocation-time windows as a novelty detection problem, where only canonical B-DNA training windows and labeled non-B motifs (e.g., G-quadruplex, short tandem repeat) are available.

name: autoencoder-goodness-of-fit-modeling
description: Use when detecting non-B DNA structures as novelties from Oxford Nanopore translocation-time windows (e.g. NA12878 SRR15058166), needing per-window P-values with FDR control against B-DNA background.

name: automated-scientific-report-rendering
description: Use when a systemPipeR workflow has been initialized with SPRproject(), its steps imported with importWF(), and executed with runWF(), and you now need a reproducible HTML analysis report or a diagnostics log of the run.

name: average-pooled-heatmap-smoothing
description: Use when building or tuning a MEPP motif score heatmap from scored FASTA sequences and JASPAR PWMs and you need to set the positional blur/smoothing window via the --margin parameter.

name: b-spline-expression-profile-smoothing
description: Use when preparing noisy time-course expression data (e.g. GEO series such as GSE6865) for Genexpi ODE regulation modeling and a continuous smoothed profile is needed before fitting.

name: background-free-lambda-window-peak-detection
description: Use when you have qbed/ccf Calling Cards insertion data and no matching background (spontaneous insertions) control, and you need to call enriched TF binding peaks genome-wide.

name: background-mutation-rate-testing
description: Use when you have hg19 somatic mutations from WGS or WES tumour cohorts and need to model expected per-element mutation counts (nMut, nSample, length) so that excess burden can be tested for driver candidates.

name: background-snp-matched-sampling
description: Use when assessing whether a variant set (e.g. GM12878 cell-type-specific GTEx v7 eQTLs) carries higher deepC saliency scores than expected for SNPs drawn from the same open-chromatin or CTCF-peak regions.

name: bacterial-genome-assembly-spades
description: Use when processing RIMS-seq (or similar shotgun) paired-end FASTQ reads from a bacterium for which no exact reference genome is available, and an assembled genome is needed for read mapping and motif discovery.

name: bacterial-genome-de-novo-assembly
description: Use when paired-end Illumina-style bacterial reads (e.g. RIMS-seq FASTQ pairs from PRJNA706563) must be turned into a reference-free genome assembly, or when alkaline-treated reads must be shown to assemble as well as a DNA-seq(+3H) control.

name: bacterial-genome-read-alignment
description: Use when the input is adapter/quality-trimmed ChIP-seq FASTQ from a bacterial sample and the goal is genome-mapped reads (BAM) as the substrate for transcription factor peak calling with macs2.

name: bacterial-m5c-methylation-sequencing-analysis
description: Use when paired-end Illumina fastq.gz reads from heat-alkaline-treated bacterial DNA need m5C motif identification plus shotgun sequencing, or when C-to-T variant enrichment must be quantified per sequence context (e.g. CCWGG) per read mate.

name: bacterial-transcriptional-regulon-quantification
description: Use when RNA-seq count matrices from a regulator-deletion versus control strain are available and the goal is to enumerate the regulon (repressed/derepressed gene counts) and confirm specific loci such as luxCDABE are recovered.

name: bag-of-motifs-count-matrix-construction
description: Use when the input is a four-column BED file (chromosome, start, stop, condition) of cell-type-specific distal CREs from snATAC-seq (e.g., mouse E8.25, mm10) and a per-sequence motif-count feature matrix is needed for XGBoost classification.

name: bag-of-motifs-count-representation
description: Use when you need to classify or regress context-specific cis-regulatory elements (enhancers) from sequence alone across species, cell types, or disease states, and want an interpretable motif-count model rather than a deep-learning sequence model.

name: bag-of-motifs-gradient-boosted-tree-model-training
description: Use when you have condition-annotated CRE coordinates (chromosome, start, stop, condition BED) from scATAC-seq or similar, and need to classify cell-type-specific distal regulatory elements from sequence-derived TF motif counts.

name: bagsize-parameter-perturbation
description: Use when validating the stability of SRIQ cluster solutions on TCGA LUAD RNA-seq data by perturbing the BagSize gene-sampling parameter and quantifying how cluster assignments co-occur across runs.

name: balanced-accuracy-model-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking cell-specific enhancer classifiers on the Liu et al. eight-cell-line FASTA data, or when measuring cross-cell-line transferability (e.g., average BACC of a model trained on one cell line evaluated on the other seven).

name: bam-alignment-file-processing
description: Use when you have mapped ChIPseq/RNAseq reads in .bam files from a NEAT project and need to filter, reorganize, or route them into downstream modules such as peakcalling or GRanges.

name: bam-downsampling-normalization
description: Use when comparing two spike-in ChIP-seq conditions (e.g. H3K79me2 25:75 vs 75:25 mixed Jurkat cells) with unequal fly spike-in read totals, and you need to equalize spike-in depth by downsampling the human BAM, or you need a baseline uniform-scaling normalization to benchmark against spikChIP.

name: bam-file-generation
description: Use when linker-filtered ChIA-PET/HiChIP FASTQ tags must be mapped to a reference genome and reduced to unique, nonredundant PET alignments (MAPQ ≥ 30) in a BAM for downstream peak and loop calling.

name: bam-file-generation-from-mapped-reads
description: Use when raw fastq files (e.g. H3K4me3 ChIPseq or RNAseq from mouse embryonic stem cells) must be aligned as an automated pipeline step and .bam outputs are needed for downstream QC, filtering, or peak calling.

name: bam-file-read-downsampling
description: Use when you need to determine the minimum sequencing depth at which a ChIP-seq mark's genome-wide profile becomes visually distinguishable, by comparing BedGraph profiles generated from BAM files sub-sampled to controlled read counts.

name: bam-granges-wiggle-file-size-profiling
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking an NGS pipeline's runtime and output file-size footprint on truncated ChIPseq/RNAseq test data, or validating that produced bam/GRanges/wig files match expected size regimes.

name: bam-indexing-and-sorting
description: Use when mapped reads (BAM) must be filtered by fragment-size thresholds, deduplicated, sorted, and indexed before ChIPseq/RNAseq peak calling in an NEAT-style pipeline.

name: bam-read-duplicate-removal
description: Use when raw ChIP-seq BAM alignments (e.g. SHR/BN rat H3K27me3 or CD-1 mouse H3K9me3 data) are about to be aggregated into fixed-width bins for downstream read-count-based modeling, and duplicates have not yet been removed.

name: bam-read-filtering-and-splitting
description: Use when raw ChIP-seq FASTQ reads have been mapped to a combined sample+spike-in genome and unaligned reads must be removed before per-bin counting or human/fly separation.

name: bam-read-processing-for-visualization
description: Use when raw ChIP-seq or RNA-seq data must be mapped, cleaned, and packaged with chromosome/refGene annotation files so SeqCode commands like buildChIPprofile, produceTSSplots, or produceTSSmaps can generate plots and heatmaps.

name: bam-read-subsampling-and-quality-filtering
description: Use when ChIP-seq/DNase-seq replicate BAMs must be normalized to equal read depth before QC metrics (FRiP, PBC, replicate correlation) so comparisons across replicates are not biased by library size.

name: bam-read-total-quantification
description: Use when running spike-in ChIP-seq normalization (e.g. ChIP-Rx in spikChIP) where each human bin count must be divided by total fly (dm3) spike-in reads, or when BAM totals must be reported or used for downsampling.

name: barcode-span-annotation-processing
description: Use when phasing with 10× linked-reads and fragments must be filtered against barcode-sharing artifacts — e.g. requiring end-read MAPQ >= 30, capping barcode span at 60 kb, and bounding haplotype blocks over filtered variants.

name: base-pair-step-stiffness-parameter-mapping
description: Use when preprocessing DNA sequences (uPBM, HT-SELEX, or gcPBM) into per-sequence feature matrices for DNAffinity affinity prediction, requiring tetramer counts and base-pair-step structural/electrostatic encoding.

name: base-quality-filtering-for-variant-counting
description: Use when counting C-to-T read variants (e.g. heat-alkaline deamination signals in RIMS-seq) from Read1/Read2 mpileups and background noise from sequencing errors must be suppressed via quality thresholds.

name: baseline-classifier-benchmarking
description: Use when a new sgRNA-activity prediction model must be shown competitive with established methods: you have binarized sgRNA labels and need a like-for-like ROC-AUC comparison table against Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, DeepHF, and C-RNNcrispr.

name: baseline-matrix-normalization-benchmarking
description: Use when a new Hi-C or capture Hi-C normalization method must be evaluated against established baselines (ICE, SCN, KR, raw) using replicate contact map reproducibility rather than a single qualitative comparison.

name: baseline-method-result-compilation
description: Use when a paper claims a new model outperforms methods on shared benchmarks and the reproduction requires merging locally reproduced metrics with reported baseline values into one comparison table.

name: baseline-model-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a trained predictor (e.g. a CNN regressor for sgRNA activity) must be benchmarked head-to-head against comparator algorithms on identical train/test splits, with significance testing on correlation, MSE, or cosine similarity metrics.

name: batch-bioinformatics-workflow-configuration
description: Use when many ChIP-seq or DNase-seq FASTQ datasets (treatment plus control, single- or paired-end) must be QC'd and analyzed in batch, with per-sample JSON QC statistics emitted for aggregation.

name: baum-welch-em-parameter-estimation
description: Use when fitting a hidden Markov model of DNA-binding factor occupancy to paired-end MNase-seq and/or ATAC-seq fragment data plus nucleotide sequence, requiring EM learning of transition probabilities with constrained TF transitions.

name: baum-welch-hidden-markov-model-training
description: Use when a time-series expression matrix must be segmented into bifurcating submatrices and an input-output HMM tree-structure model needs parameter initialization and Baum–Welch training, e.g. to assign TFs to the time points at which they act.

name: bayesian-epiallele-model-fitting
description: Use when you have an N-reads × d-CpGs binary methylation read matrix Y (0/1, RRBS-derived) for one locus and need to infer how many distinct epialleles are present, their methylation patterns, the noise level ε, and which epiallele each read originated from.

name: bayesian-gam-posterior-variance-estimation
description: Use when pointwise variance or standard errors of smooth estimates are needed for statistical testing in a sparse penalized GAM fit where forming the full inverse Hessian is infeasible.

name: bayesian-hierarchical-model-mcmc-inference
description: Use when the input is a processed peak/region set (BED from MACS2, DiffBind, or ArchR DARs) and the goal is an in-silico ranked list of TRs with credible intervals rather than motif-based or frequentist enrichment.

name: bayesian-hyperparameter-optimization
description: Use when tuning hyperparameters (e.g., convolution filter counts/sizes, fully-connected layer widths, dropout) of the EpiCas-DL TensorFlow CNN, and grid/random search is deemed unreliable.

name: bayesian-inla-model-fitting-in-r
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon sequencing standard-control data (known methylation percentages per AMP) must be modelled jointly across CpGs with Bayesian inference in R, e.g. deriving PCR-bias calibration curves or correcting case/control methylation levels.

name: bayesian-latent-gaussian-model-specification
description: Use when raw apparent methylation levels from bisulfite amplicon sequencing standard controls (e.g. 0/25/50/75/100% AMP) must be modeled jointly per CpG to derive PCR-bias calibration curves.

name: bayesian-latent-variable-model-fitting
description: Use when bisulfite-sequencing reads from multiple samples of the same tumour must be decomposed into latent epialleles at a locus, and Q, methylation patterns, and noise must be inferred from data rather than fixed a priori.

name: bayesian-pca-missing-value-imputation
description: Use when an ANNOVAR-annotated variant feature table (e.g. EIGEN, CADD, DANN, GWAVA, FATHMM scores) contains missing entries and a complete matrix is required before computing summary statistics, correlations, or training a deep learning model.

name: bayesian-posterior-postprocessing-inla
description: Use when you have fitted MethylCal/INLA calibration models per assay (e.g. from BWS standard controls at 0/25/50/75/100% methylation) and must numerically convert observed apparent methylation levels into corrected methylation degrees.

name: bayesian-transcriptional-regulator-ranking
description: Use when you have a BED file of differential accessibility or binding peak regions from a TR knockout, CRISPR perturbation, cancer-type, or cell-type comparison and need to identify/rank the perturbed or cell-type-specific TRs in silico with posterior uncertainty.

name: bdna-motif-free-control-region-selection
description: Use when reproducing the Fig. 4 TT-quantile deviation analysis and you need a matched B-DNA control set: motif positions are loaded from non-B DNA DB hg38 and you must exclude all motif-overlapping windows before computing per-window translocation-time quantiles.

name: bed-coordinate-manipulation
description: Use when running Skipper's GFF partitioning step on a GENCODE/Ensembl GFF3 (e.g. gencode.v49.basic.annotation.gff3.gz) to produce the fixed <=100-nt window BED used for CLIP-seq binding site detection.

name: bed-coordinate-processing
description: Use when a BED file of genomic intervals (e.g. CTCF ChIP-seq peaks on hg38) lacks strand annotation and strand signs must be inherited from an overlapping strand-annotated feature file such as MA0139.1 CTCF motif occurrences.

name: bed-file-coordinate-handling
description: Use when you have chromosomal coordinates of identified eccDNA elements and need to annotate overlapping genes, requiring BED interval conversion and overlap-fraction computation.

name: bed-file-export-with-rtracklayer
description: Use when a GRanges object of differential regions (e.g., a DiffBind dba.report result) must be written out as a BED file to feed region-set tools like BIT.

name: bed-file-generation
description: Use when producing BED interval outputs from ChIA-PET loop data — e.g., calling chromatin contact domains from CTCF ChIA-PET loops as chromosome/start/end BED records after peak-support and PET-count filtering.

name: bed-file-subsetting-and-partitioning
description: Use when you have peak-supported ChIA-PET/HiChIP loop BED files (e.g., RNAPII ChIA-PET loops with PET count >= 3 and unique loop IDs) and need to split them into category-specific tracks (E-P vs P-P vs neither) for separate browser visualization.

name: bed-format-genomic-file-handling
description: Use when raw narrow-peak BED files (chrom, start, end) from ENCODE/Roadmap chromatin profiles must become fixed 1000 bp, non-redundant training intervals for a Basset/DeepFun CNN input window.

name: bed-genomic-track-generation
description: Use when Hi-C contact maps (bulk or pseudo-bulk single-cell, resolutions up to 10 kb) must be converted into per-bin compartment score tracks in a BED-like output, with automated PC1/PC2 and sign orientation per chromosome.

name: bed-interval-overlap-classification
description: Use when a spikChIP-style spike-in normalization needs every segmentation bin of the sample (and spike-in) genome labelled as ChIP-enriched or background, from user-supplied BED peak files.

name: bed-like-methylation-file-conversion
description: Use when preparing bisulfite sequencing methylation callsets (e.g. bismark_methylation_extractor .cov files) as input for DXM's dxm_solveMethylation, which requires a tab-delimited BED-like file with a unique regionName per region.

name: bedgraph-custom-track-coordinate-conventions
description: Use when you must convert mapped ChIP-seq reads (BAM/SAM) into genome-wide signal profiles (BedGraph) for browser visualization, especially when comparing profiles across sequencing depths or histone marks (e.g. sharp H3K4me3 vs broad H3K36me3).

name: bedpe-loop-pooling-and-thresholding
description: Use when you have raw per-pixel interaction probability scores (BEDPE) from Peakachu score_genome/score_chromosome and need to derive a final non-redundant loop set with a model-specific probability threshold.

name: bedtools-genomic-interval-intersection
description: Use when preparing per-cytosine bismark/bsmap/biscuit methylation output for DXM: each CpG needs a unique regionName from an overlapping feature BED (CGIs, promoters, imprinted DMRs) before dxm_solveMethylation can run.

name: benchmark-community-figure-reproduction
description: Use when per-species mapped read counts from BWA-mem-mapped RIMS-seq, DNA-seq, and bisulfite-seq libraries are available and the goal is to test whether a sequencing protocol biases species relative abundances in a defined synthetic community.

name: benchmark-method-comparison-reporting
description: Use when a new predictor must be benchmarked against an existing published tool under identical cross-validation on shared datasets (e.g. DNA 6mA site prediction) and the deliverable is a side-by-side metrics table.

name: benchmark-metric-comparison-across-methods
description: Use when two or more enhancer-prediction methods must be compared on a shared benchmark with independent test sets and per-cell-line metrics such as BACC, to verify a claimed improvement.

name: benchmark-results-tabulation-across-cell-lines
description: Use when comparing multiple model classes (CNN baseline, DNA foundation models, task-specific expert) on the same prediction task across several biological subsets (e.g., cell lines) and a per-subset plus averaged score table is required.

name: benchmark-sensitivity-evaluation
description: Use when a new network/pathway-detection method must be validated against established clustering tools on a time-series dataset for which a curated set of known associated pathways exists.

name: benchmark-table-compilation
description: Use when a study reports execution time and memory footprint of a tool on named datasets and the task is to reproduce or extend that performance table on a local machine.

name: benchmark-table-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing the paper's functional-validation benchmarks: measuring what fraction of base pairs and genes of a known functional gene set (e.g. X-inactivated genes) are covered by differential modification calls.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when novelty scores (reconstruction error, Mahalanobis distance, IF/LOF/SVM scores) have been converted to empirical P-values against a B-DNA null and a per-window significance decision is needed at a fixed FDR level.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when testing thousands of phased heterozygous SNPs for allelic imbalance in ChIA-PET read coverage and needing multiple-testing-corrected significance calls before classifying allele-specific loops.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a family of hypothesis tests has been run per cluster (cluster-vs-rest Wilcoxon tests across regions, or hypergeometric tests across MSigDB v5 gene sets) and raw p-values must be adjusted before thresholding significant regions or pathways.

name: benjamini-yekutieli-fdr-correction
description: Use when a family of P-values is large and potentially dependent (e.g. MEPP positional correlations at adjacent sequence positions, or all motifs at all positions) and a dependency-robust FDR adjustment is required.

name: beta-binomial-differential-methylation-testing
description: Use when you have a clustered-region methylation counts table (combined.csv with chr, start, end, CpG, per-sample -N and -X columns) and need to identify DMRs between two or more sample groups from MethylC-seq data.

name: beta-binomial-emission-probability-computation
description: Use when an HMM-style methylation deconvolution (e.g. DXM's Viterbi decoding over user-defined regions) needs emission probabilities for observed fractional methylation plus read coverage at each CpG of a region.

name: beta-binomial-enriched-window-testing
description: Use when analyzing eCLIP/CLIP-seq FASTQs that have matched input controls and at least 2 CLIP replicates, and you need reproducible, annotated binding-site windows rather than peak calls.

name: beta-binomial-enrichment-testing-with-gc-overdispersion-correction
description: Use when detecting significant RBP binding to annotated repetitive elements or transcriptomic windows from eCLIP data with matched inputs, especially multi-mapping/repeat targets that peak callers miss.

name: beta-binomial-hierarchical-dmr-testing
description: Use when Bismark-aligned MethylC-seq reads must be tested for region-level differential methylation between two sample groups (e.g., IMR90/H1 replicates) with strict false-positive control, such that self-replicate contrasts yield minimal DMRs.

name: beta-binomial-regression-modeling
description: Use when analyzing tiled transcriptomic (or repetitive-element) windows from eCLIP data with matched IP and input read-start counts, and you need GC-bias-aware enrichment p-values accounting for count overdispersion.

name: bias-correction-evaluation
description: Use when a RNA-Seq expression-estimation method has been run with and without fragment-bias correction and the improvement must be validated against an independent qRT-PCR truth set (e.g., 907 uniquely probed MAQC HBR transcripts).

name: bifurcation-pattern-comparison-vector-construction
description: Use when a time-series expression matrix must be split at candidate bifurcation time points and Baum-Welch training of a tree-structure model needs effective initial parameters, e.g., TSMiner runs on mouse liver regeneration RNA-seq time courses.

name: bigwig-genomic-coverage-extraction
description: Use when you have TCGA or ENCODE ATAC-seq BigWig signal tracks and need to quantify or visualize chromatin accessibility over a specific locus (e.g., an eccDNA-containing region) in cancer samples.

name: bilinear-feature-fusion-layer-design
description: Use when reconstructing or adapting GILoop's dual-branch architecture: two single-view encoders (GCN and U-Net) must be combined per pixel into one fused representation that feeds loop vs. non-loop pixel classification.

name: bin-level-genomic-matrix-generation
description: Use when duplicate-filtered cfMeDIP-seq BAM files must be converted into per-bin methylation estimates with correction for CpG density bias, or when relative vs. absolute (vs. strand-aware) methylation strategies must be compared per sample.

name: binarized-accessibility-bin-counting
description: Use when scATAC-seq nuclei need a peak-free similarity representation — SnapATAC's runNormJaccard requires a binarized cell-by-bin matrix (makeBinary + addBmatToSnap) because per-cell signals are too sparse for peak-based clustering.

name: binary-and-multiclass-cell-type-classification
description: Use when snATAC-seq-derived distal CRE BED files (chromosome, start, stop, condition) must be assigned to their cell type of origin using motif-count features rather than sequence-based deep learning.

name: binary-classification-auroc-auprc-evaluation
description: Use when comparing binary classification models on DNALONGBENCH tasks such as enhancer-target gene prediction, where AUROC and AUPRC on a held-out test split are the benchmark metrics.

name: binary-classification-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a trained motif-count classifier (e.g., BOM/binModel on cell-type-specific enhancer BED labels) must be scored, and held-out predictions need F1, auPR, or regression correlation metrics.

name: binary-epihaplotype-matrix-parsing
description: Use when bisulfite-sequencing reads have been processed by ampliMethProfiler into a binary epiallele/epihaplotype matrix and you need to load CpG positions and sample metadata for methylated-core analysis.

name: binary-matrix-validation-testing
description: Use when you have a SCALE-imputed scATAC-seq accessibility matrix (peaks as rows, barcodes as columns) and need a validated binary matrix matching SCALE's --binarization behavior for downstream clustering or storage.

name: binary-regulatory-matrix-construction
description: Use when building a chromatin-informed TF-target prior to constrain decoder weights of a transcriptional-regulator model, from ATAC-seq open-chromatin peaks and a motif reference.

name: binned-genome-coverage-construction
description: Use when converting mapped single-end short reads (BED/ELAND) into a binned genome-wide coverage profile for peak calling, especially when fragment sizes are only approximately known from size selection.

name: binomial-distribution-based-tfbs-identification
description: Use when predicting sequence or DNA shape motifs and TFBSs from trained DESSO CNN models on ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks and an objective, statistically grounded motif cutoff is needed instead of a manual threshold.

name: binomial-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when counting strand-annotated feature occurrences (same vs opposite orientation) yields success/failure counts and you need a P-value for deviation from p = 0.5, e.g., motif-in-region strand bias tests.

name: binomial-significance-testing
description: Use when reproducing or extending DESSO's TFBS identification step, where motif instance candidates from a CNN motif detector must be statistically assessed with binomial P-values at varying signal cutoffs instead of a fixed subjective cutoff.

name: binomial-strand-orientation-testing
description: Use when you have BED files with '+'/'-' strand annotations for both motifs (e.g., TFBS occurrences) and regions (e.g., GENCODE transcribed regions) and need to quantify orientation bias per motif with statistical significance.

name: binomial-test-snp-coverage-bias
description: Use when allele-specific (haplotype-resolved) binding or looping from ChIA-PET data is needed and phased SNP genotypes (e.g., NA12878 hg19 Broad bundle) are available to assign haplotype labels to uniquely aligned reads.

name: binomial-test-with-bonferroni-correction
description: Use when a strand-orientation count (e.g. template vs non-template or vs lagging occurrences of breakpoints or motifs) must be tested against a background orientation probability, with multiple element classes tested simultaneously.

name: bionet-heinz-subnetwork-search
description: Use when SMITE-scored genes (scorePval output on a PvalueAnnotation) need to be converted into ranked subnetwork modules on an interactome, or when comparing Heinz-derived modules against spin-glass results.

name: bismark-sam-alignment-parsing
description: Use when Bismark-produced SAM/BAM alignments from MethylC-seq data must be converted into per-CpG methylated/unmethylated count tables, especially when novel CpG sites from variants (e.g. rs11348696) should be retained in the output.

name: bisulfite-amplicon-epiallele-frequency-quantification
description: Use when bisulfite sequencing reads (e.g. FASTA from DDO1/DAO amplicons) must be reduced to per-molecule methylation configurations and single-epiallele frequency distributions, or when benchmarking these frequencies against MethCoresProfiler core annotations.

name: bisulfite-amplicon-read-preprocessing
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ bisulfite amplicon reads must be converted into binary single-molecule epihaplotype tables before downstream methylation-core or epiallele-family analysis.

name: bisulfite-amplicon-sequencing-methylation-data-processing
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon sequencing data include standard controls with known methylation percentages (e.g. 0-100% AMP series) and observed methylation levels need PCR-bias correction and calibration across multiple CpGs.

name: bisulfite-conversion-rate-quality-control
description: Use when analyzing direct-BSP or cloning-BSP .ab1 chromatogram traces in ABSP and you must verify bisulfite conversion efficiency at non-CpG positions before computing or interpreting CpG methylation percentages.

name: bisulfite-free-read-alignment
description: Use when aligning reads from bisulfite-free protocols such as TAPS or 5hmC-CATCH where only CpG-context cytosines are converted to thymines and non-CpG methylation is very low, so the reads retain 4-letter alphabet information.

name: bisulfite-like-ct-variant-methylation-detection
description: Use when analyzing RIMS-seq paired-end FASTQ reads from a bacterial strain to de novo identify m5C methylase specificities (e.g. non-CpG motifs) while only having a reference genome or SPAdes assembly available.

name: bisulfite-methylation-bed-formatting
description: Use when bisulfite sequencing methylation data (e.g. Bismark .cov, RRBS/MethylC-seq calls) must be reformatted for DXM tools such as dxm_solveMethylation or dxm_estimateFracs.

name: bisulfite-methylation-data-deconvolution
description: Use when bisulfite sequencing (e.g. Methyl-Seq, RRBS/WGBS) data from a heterogeneous sample must be resolved into two subpopulation methylation profiles and fractional prevalences over defined regions.

name: bisulfite-pcr-bias-correction
description: Use when bisulfite-amplicon/pyrosequencing methylation data include standard controls at known methylation percentages (e.g. 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) and apparent methylation levels must be corrected for PCR bias before case/control classification.

name: bisulfite-pcr-qc-failure-assessment
description: Use when ABSP direct-BSP analysis of .ab1 reads yields a very short trimmed sequence covering few CpG sites, or aborts with 'no CpG sites were found covered by sequencing results', and the trimming thresholds must be diagnosed and adjusted.

name: bisulfite-pcr-trace-trimming
description: Use when raw .ab1 Sanger trace files from bisulfite sequencing PCR show low-quality ends or mixed/overlapping base peaks, and a trimmed sequence must be produced before computing per-CpG methylation percentages.

name: bisulfite-read-alignment
description: Use when WGBS/bisulfite FASTQ reads must be aligned to a reference genome (e.g. hg19) at large scale (10M–200M reads) where single-node 'three-letter' aligners are too slow and a distributed scale-out approach is needed.

name: bisulfite-read-alignment
description: Use when raw MethylC-seq or bisulfite-treated sequencing reads (e.g. FASTQ from the Lister et al. IMR90/H1 cell lines) must be mapped to a reference genome before methylation count extraction and DMR identification.

name: bisulfite-read-rdd-construction
description: Use when WGBS FASTQ/A reads (e.g. GEO GSE80911) must be loaded into Spark key-value RDD tuples and re-partitioned with portable_hash so per-partition record counts become approximately even across executors.

name: bisulfite-read-three-letter-transformation
description: Use when aligning bisulfite-treated sequencing reads (FASTQ/A) under the 'three-letter' approach and you need to transform reads and reference genomes into CT/GA-converted variants before mapping.

name: bisulfite-read-to-reference-alignment-offset-mapping
description: Use when computing methylation levels from trimmed BSP sequencing reads (.ab1 chromatograms) requires converting each read cytosine position into the corresponding CpG coordinate on the reference .fasta template.

name: bisulfite-sequencing-methylation-call-interpretation
description: Use when working with Bismark-aligned MethylC-seq reads (e.g., IMR90/H1 data) and needing to interpret per-CpG methylation calls, extract methylated/unmethylated counts, or examine spatially-linked methylation patterns across reads.

name: bisulfite-sequencing-methylation-data-gathering
description: Use when per-sample individual ABSP methylation tables already exist for multiple .ab1-derived samples assigned to two groups (e.g. high vs low methylated DNA) and group-level CpG methylation comparison, plots, and significance testing are needed.

name: bisulfite-sequencing-read-simulation
description: Use when validating or benchmarking an epiallele inference method on RRBS-style data and you need synthetic reads at a single locus with known ground-truth epialleles, mixing proportions, and a specified noise probability.

name: bit-rank-table-parsing
description: Use when you have BIT rank tables from cancer-type-specific accessible regions and need to determine which top-ranked TRs are functionally essential via DepMap CRISPR Chronos knockout scores.

name: bivalent-chromatin-mark-interpretation
description: Use when ChIP-seq peak lists for two chromatin marks have been intersected (e.g. H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 MACS peaks in mESCs) and you must assign peaks to genes and biologically characterize bivalent targets.

name: bivalent-chromatin-state-annotation
description: Use when two ChIP-seq peak lists (e.g. BED files of H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 peaks from Beringer et al., GSM2098958 and GSM2098952) must be partitioned into mutually exclusive active, bivalent, and silent site classes via overlap.

name: bivariate-gp-zip-paired-sample-classification
description: Use when paired treated/control ChIP-Seq aligned reads must be classified into ChIP-enriched versus background bins via an HMM whose emissions model both channels simultaneously (GP for enriched, ZIP for background).

name: bivariate-hidden-markov-model-differential-calling
description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq profiles of two samples (e.g. SHR vs BN rat heart H3K27me3) for broad, diffuse histone marks where peak-style callers produce false positives/negatives, and per-bin probabilistic differential calls are needed.

name: bivariate-hidden-markov-model-fitting
description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq profiles of two samples for a broad, diffuse histone modification and you need genome-wide calls of differentially modified regions rather than peak-like enrichment calls.

name: blacklisted-genomic-region-removal
description: Use when input peak files (BED/GRanges, e.g. ChIP-seq, CUT&Run, CUT&Tag peaks) must be cleaned of anomalous-signal regions before comparison/QC, and when a blacklist-overlap percentage metric is needed per sample.

name: block-bootstrap-null-range-generation
description: Use when testing overlap/enrichment between two genomic range sets (e.g. ChIP-seq peaks, caQTLs, CREs) and a null distribution is needed that preserves local genomic correlation structure rather than shuffling ranges.

name: boltzmann-transition-probability-initialization
description: Use when training RoboCOP's multivariate HMM to compute genome-wide probabilistic occupancy of nucleosomes and ~150 TFs from MNase-seq or ATAC-seq accessibility plus nucleotide sequence, and you must initialize the transition matrix before Baum-Welch learning.

name: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many p-values are produced simultaneously (e.g., 48 K-S tests per lane pair on genome-partitioned read distributions) and per-combination significance calls must be corrected for multiple testing.

name: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a strand asymmetry analysis produces many P-values from repeated two-tailed binomial tests (p = 0.5 expected asymmetry) and you need Bonferroni-corrected significance for each feature (TF PWM, motif, repeat class, ChIP-seq peak set).

name: bootstrap-confidence-interval-estimation
description: Use when reporting a point estimate of entropy decrease (or similar per-cluster statistic) after DGW warping and you need an uncertainty range, e.g. mean 1.72% TSS decrease with a 95% bootstrap CI of 0.83–2.81%.

name: bootstrap-confidence-interval-estimation
description: Use when a benchmark metric is a proportion derived from a finite set of significant peaks (e.g., motif-proximal peak fraction) and its sampling uncertainty must be reported as a 95% bootstrap confidence interval for method comparison.

name: bootstrap-null-distribution-analysis
description: Use when testing whether an observed overlap between genomic range sets (e.g., caQTL SNPs and peaks, or DEGs and differential accessibility peaks) is significant, and shuffling-based nulls may be too narrow.

name: bootstrap-resampling-reproducibility-assessment
description: Use when you need to test whether ranked cis driver predictions from an iEDGE-style mediation analysis (Rank-1 cis gene per SCNA) are stable under sample resampling rather than artifacts of a single cohort draw.

name: bowtie-transcriptome-remapping
description: Use when reproducing transcript-level expression baselines (e.g. mseq) that need reads aligned directly to transcript sequences instead of a genome, or when comparing against count-based methods on MAQC HBR qRT-PCR benchmark data.

name: bowtie2-based-short-read-alignment
description: Use when short paired-end or single-end methylation sequencing reads (36-100 bp FASTQ, e.g., SHERMAN-simulated TAPS data) must be aligned to a reference genome such as hg19 as the core step of a bisulfite or bisulfite-free methylation analysis.

name: boxplot-visualisation-of-per-locus-statistics
description: Use when per-locus scalar statistics (e.g. Shannon entropy of epiallele distributions phi_s) have been computed for multiple tissue samples and you need to compare their distributions across normal vs. tumour regions graphically.

name: boxplot-visualization-of-genomic-signal
description: Use when you have sequencing-depth-normalized ChIP-seq (or similar) read-count levels computed over gene bodies and need to compare signal distributions across categorical gene sets (e.g. expression classes) with publication-quality boxplots.

name: brain-region-epiallele-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon sequencing of phased CpG regions must resolve stable epiallele families and methylated cores in complex DNA populations, e.g. tracking mCpG signatures across brain regions or developmental time points.

name: bridge-linker-chia-pet-pipeline-execution
description: Use when processing bridge-linker ChIA-PET FASTQ data from raw reads to chromatin loops, or when reproducing stepwise PET retention statistics and QC figures for a ChIA-PET dataset.

name: bridge-linker-sequence-parameterization
description: Use when trimming linkers from bridge-linker ChIA-PET paired-end FASTQ with ChIA-PET2 and you must set the linkerA/linkerB 15-mers and mismatch tolerance (-e 0 vs -e 1) to avoid losing valid PETs to sequencing errors.

name: budget-constrained-experimental-design-optimization
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq DE or eQTL study has a fixed monetary budget and you must choose the optimal trade-off between sample size, cells per individual, and sequencing depth to maximize detection power.

name: bulk-vs-single-cell-peak-overlap-analysis
description: Use when a scATAC-seq atlas has per-cluster pseudo-bulk peak sets and a bulk ATAC-seq reference from the same tissue exists, and you must report the fraction of cell-type-specific CREs missed by bulk profiling.

name: bulk-vs-single-cell-qbed-preprocessing
description: Use when starting from raw bulk or single-cell calling cards qbed/ccf files (e.g. Brd4 bulk GSE156821 or SP1 scCC HCT116/K562 data) and you need cleaned insertions, called peaks, and a filtered Anndata object before downstream motif or differential analysis.

name: bwa-read-alignment-and-bam-processing
description: Use when starting from raw ChIP-seq or DNase-seq FASTQ files and you need aligned, sorted BAM files against hg19 as the substrate for MACS2 peak calling and FRiP-based quality control.

name: bws-imprinting-dmr-methylation-calling
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon methylation data from cases and controls at imprinted DMRs (e.g., KCNQ1OT1, H19/IGF2) need PCR-bias-corrected patient calls (gain/loss of methylation), or when assessing sensitivity of those calls to the decision threshold (±3SD vs 1%).

name: c-to-t-deamination-rate-quantification
description: Use when paired-end reads from heat-alkaline (NaOH)-treated DNA are available and you need per-condition C-to-T deamination rates or the Read1/Read2 fold imbalance at reference cytosines.

name: c-to-t-deamination-signature-detection
description: Use when RIMS-seq (alkaline-treated) Illumina paired-end fastq.gz reads from bacteria must be converted into a de novo m5C methylase motif with a significance P-value, e.g. recovering CCWGG from E. coli K12 MG1655 time-course data.

name: cadd-functional-score-integration
description: Use when calling cancer driver candidates with DriverPower and you want to incorporate functional impact evidence (CADD scores) alongside mutational burden tests, on coding or non-coding element sets.

name: cage-tss-distance-calculation
description: Use when you have sgRNA genomic coordinates (e.g. from CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa screening tables) and FANTOM CAGE TSS positions, and need TSS-proximity/nucleosome-positioning features per sgRNA for a model or filter.

name: calibrated-methylation-data-analysis
description: Use when analyzing bisulfite amplicon sequencing methylation data (e.g. BWS KCNQ1OT1 / H19/IGF2 DMR assays) where PCR bias must be corrected before gain/loss-of-methylation calls are made for patient samples.

name: calibration-model-goodness-of-fit-comparison
description: Use when pyrosequenced or MiSeq methylation data from standard controls with known methylation percentages (e.g. AMP 0/25/50/75/100) are available and competing PCR-bias calibration models must be fitted and compared per assay.

name: calling-cards-peak-calling
description: Use when input is bulk or single-cell Calling Cards qbed/ccf transposon-insertion data (e.g. Brd4 or SP1 CC datasets from GEO) and TF binding sites must be identified as peaks before annotation, differential analysis, or peak-gene pairing.

name: cancer-cohort-expression-profiling
description: Use when you have a defined gene set (e.g. genes on an eccDNA like hsa_Chr7_3S_1) and expression matrices from tumor and matched normal samples, and need per-gene expression ranks and t-test p-values per cancer cohort.

name: cancer-driver-call-overlap-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking a driver discovery method's called elements against a gold-standard set (e.g. CGC) on PCAWG whole genomes, to compute precision, recall and F1 per element class (coding, splice site, non-coding).

name: cancer-driver-candidate-comparison-against-reference-catalogs
description: Use when you have a tool-called driver candidate list (e.g. DriverPower [outDir]/[name].result.tsv) and need to benchmark its novelty and error rate against CGC or PCAWG-consensus catalogs.

name: cancer-driver-gene-curation
description: Use when a ranked candidate driver gene list (e.g., iEDGE Rank-1 cis genes per SCNA) needs in silico validation against curated oncogene/tumor suppressor compendia (COSMIC, TUSON, OMIM, UniProt) or DepMap dependency data via one-sided Fisher/hypergeometric enrichment.

name: cancer-driver-mutation-inference
description: Use when you have processed somatic mutation response tables (nMut, nSample, effective length per element) for coding or non-coding test elements and a pre-trained BMR model, and need to call driver candidates at q < 0.1.

name: cancer-lineage-specific-essentiality-thresholding
description: Use when a ranked list of candidate TRs (e.g., BIT scores from TCGA cancer-type-specific accessible regions) must be checked for knockout-validated essentiality using DepMap CRISPR/Cas9 Chronos scores per cancer lineage.

name: cancer-type-subset-analysis-ucec-brca
description: Use when reproducing Figure 5A-B TF-alteration associations: you have the CITRUS output 'hid_tmr' TF activity matrix, the binary SGA matrix (11998 genes), and need per-cancer-type (UCEC, BRCA) associations for specific alteration genes.

name: candidate-cis-regulatory-element-merging
description: Use when you have scATAC-seq fragment data with cluster/barcode assignments and need a cell-type-resolved set of candidate regulatory elements that a single bulk peak call would miss.

name: candidate-target-region-filtering-with-threshold
description: Use when a GRangesList of candidates already carries epigenomic and sequence-grammar similarity scores per query region and must be reduced to high-confidence orthologous target regions before downstream use.

name: capture-hic-significant-interaction-calling
description: Use when you have promoter-other (P-O) pcHi-C fragment-pair tables with coverage values, interaction frequencies and distances, and need reproducible significant cis-interaction calls within 15 kb–2 Mb.

name: caqtl-snp-overlap-analysis
description: Use when testing whether observed genomic range overlaps (e.g., liver caQTL peaks vs. trait-associated SNPs) are significant, and you need a block-bootstrap null instead of naive shuffling.

name: cca-based-cross-modality-annotation
description: Use when a scATAC-seq clustering lacks cell-type identities and a matched or same-tissue scRNA-seq reference with curated labels is available; triggered by the need to color scATAC clusters (e.g. on a t-SNE embedding) with RNA-derived cell types.

name: ccle-expression-data-retrieval
description: Use when a task needs expression values for cancer cell lines (CCLE) or TCGA tumor/normal cohorts to quantify differential expression of genes located on specific eccDNAs, e.g. genes on hsa_Chr7_3S_1 in TCGA-GBM.

name: cell-by-bin-matrix-construction
description: Use when raw scATAC-seq fragment/BAM data must be converted into a snap-format cell-by-bin count matrix (e.g., at 5-kb resolution) as the starting feature representation for clustering or dimensionality reduction without population-level peak calling.

name: cell-by-peak-anndata-construction
description: Use when single-cell calling cards qbed insertions and called peaks (e.g., 902 Brd4 peaks from mouse cortex GSE148448) must be converted into a cell-by-peak count matrix for integration with Scanpy gene-expression AnnData.

name: cell-coverage-outlier-filtering
description: Use when a raw single-cell ChIP-seq/scATAC-seq count matrix (cells x bins/peaks/TSS regions) contains low-quality or extreme-coverage cells that must be filtered before PCA, t-SNE/UMAP, or clustering.

name: cell-cycle-stage-comparison
description: Use when you have single-cell Hi-C contact matrices resolved by cell-cycle stage and need to test whether nested TLD hierarchy (modularity, TLD-adjR2, weighted similarity WS) changes across stages such as G1 vs S phase vs G2.

name: cell-line-cluster-assignment-scoring
description: Use when cells from a scATAC-seq or scChIP-seq dataset have known labels (cell line, replicate, sample) and clusters computed by ChromSCape must be scored for label concordance or compared between samples with Fisher's exact test.

name: cell-line-enhancer-sequence-processing
description: Use when enhancer training/test FASTA sequences for one of the eight human cell lines must be converted into dna2vec and motif-based features before running Enhancer-MDLF (main.py) training or prediction.

name: cell-line-similarity-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify how well a cell-specific enhancer model trained on one human cell line transfers to the other seven cell lines' test sets, and to rank cell line similarity from cross-prediction BACC.

name: cell-line-specific-enhancer-model-interpretation
description: Use when you have a trained Enhancer-MDLF model on one of the eight human cell lines and need to identify which TFBS motifs drive enhancer predictions via SHAP attribution over motif-module features.

name: cell-line-specific-model-training
description: Use when you have fasta-formatted SE/TE sequences for one cell line (e.g. mESC) and want a cell-line-specific sequence-only classifier with user-set learning rate and epochs.

name: cell-number-subsampling-scaling-analysis
description: Use when evaluating how loop-calling performance scales with the number of single cells, e.g. comparing SnapHiC on per-cell subsamples of mES scHi-C data against HiCCUPS on pooled contacts.

name: cell-taxonomy-reference-database-construction
description: Use when a cluster-based cell annotation tool (e.g. scCATCH) needs a tissue-specific reference of marker genes linked to cell types, subtypes, tissues, and species, or when the bundled cellmatch data must be rebuilt or extended.

name: cell-type-agnostic-feature-computation
description: Use when candidate enhancer-gene pairs (e.g. cCRE-ELS within 500 KB of target gene TSSs) have been formed with createPairs and the CENTRE workflow requires the non-cell-type-specific feature columns before calling centrePrediction.

name: cell-type-classification-performance-evaluation
description: Use when you have trained cell-type CRE classifiers (e.g., BOM/XGBoost on motif counts) and need to quantify prediction accuracy, such as fraction of elements assigned to the correct cell type or cross-species transfer rates.

name: cell-type-comparative-epigenomics
description: Use when CpG-level methylation calls (e.g., Roadmap WGBS) must be summarized per interval set and compared across cell types to test differential methylation level/variation between HOT regions and control regions like non-HOT CpG islands.

name: cell-type-consistency-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell type annotation accuracy of cluster-based vs cell-based methods on scRNA-seq datasets with known reference labels, or when quantifying how swapping the underlying reference database affects annotation consistency.

name: cell-type-epiallele-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when comparing methylated-core/epiallele structures across purified cell populations (e.g., astrocytes, neurons, MOEs from cerebellum and cortex) to test for shared precursor cores during postnatal differentiation.

name: cell-type-label-supervised-feature-ranking
description: Use when building a Cellcano reference for scATAC-seq celltyping: the reference gene score matrix (from ArchR) has annotated cell type labels and features must be reduced to cell-type-specific genes before MLP training.

name: cell-type-prediction-confusion-matrix-computation
description: Use when you have Cellcano (or similar supervised) predicted cell-type labels for a target scATAC-seq dataset plus ground-truth labels (e.g., FACS-sorted FACS labels embedded in cell identifiers) and need to quantify per-class prediction accuracy.

name: cell-type-score-computation
description: Use when you have EpiRegio GeneQuery REM tables (regressionCoefficient, per-cell-type DNase1 signal) for a gene and need cell type-specific REM contributions to gene expression.

name: cell-type-score-ranking-of-rems
description: Use when a set of REMs from an EpiRegio Gene Query must be prioritized by cell type/tissue specificity (e.g. 'heart') before downstream TF motif enrichment such as PASTAA.

name: cell-type-specific-differential-peak-analysis
description: Use when single-cell CC/qbed insertion data (e.g., Brd4 mouse cortex, GSE148448) must be converted to a cell-by-peak AnnData and differential TF binding peaks per cell type must be linked to nearby gene expression.

name: cell-type-specific-enhancer-motif-ranking
description: Use when you have trained BOM/XGBoost classifiers on cell-type-specific distal regulatory elements (e.g. mouse E8.25 scATAC-derived CREs) and need per-motif SHAP importance rankings plus local explanations at a locus of interest.

name: cell-type-specific-gene-expression-identification
description: Use when single-cell expression data for known cell types (e.g., Astro, MG, L2/3, Vip) and per-cell nested TLD boundary calls are available and you need to designate genes or boundaries as cell-type-specific.

name: cell-type-specific-genomic-data-integration
description: Use when scoring structural variants (inversions, translocations, deletions, duplications) with hg19 breakpoints against phenotypes like head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system or pituitary to identify causative genes and coding vs long-range.

name: cell-type-specific-locus-annotation
description: Use when DA peaks or age-related expression changes from PBMC ATAC-seq/RNA-seq must be assigned to cell-type-specific loci to test whether aging signatures (e.g., B cell decline) are shared or sex-specific between men and women.

name: cell-type-specific-loop-summit-annotation
description: Use when scHi-C-derived loops from matched cell type subsets (e.g. 261-cell astrocyte/microglia/ODC/L2/3 neuron SnapHiC runs) need epigenomic and expression validation against matched bulk references.

name: cell-type-specific-regulatory-landscape-integration
description: Use when interpreting patient structural variants (inversions, deletions, duplications, translocations) whose pathogenic effect is suspected to be non-coding/long-range, and cell type-specific enhancer and TAD data are needed to nominate disease genes.

name: cell-type-specific-regulatory-variant-mapping
description: Use when mapping enhancer-resident noncoding GWAS SNPs to putative target genes via cell type-specific chromatin loops (SnapHiC *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe), e.g. neuropsychiatric SNPs in human prefrontal cortex.

name: cell-type-specific-rem-filtering
description: Use when submitting a gene list to EpiRegio's Gene Query and you need REMs restricted to a relevant cell type or tissue context rather than genome-wide REMs.

name: cellmatch-reference-mapping
description: Use when clustered scRNA-seq data needs cell type annotation and one-against-all marker lists (e.g. Seurat FindAllMarkers) may contain pseudo markers upregulated in multiple clusters, or when a reproducible, reference-database-based annotation is required.

name: center-distance-feature-matching
description: Use when a BED feature file (e.g. CTCF ChIP-seq peaks on hg38) lacks strand annotation but an overlapping strand-assigned reference file (e.g. MA0139.1 CTCF motif occurrences) exists, and downstream strand-asymmetry analysis requires oriented features.

name: cfmedip-methylation-quantification
description: Use when estimating bin-level methylation from cfMeDIP-seq enrichment data and CpG-density bias must be corrected, e.g. choosing among linear-regression, sigmoidal, or strand-aware sigmoid normalization models.

name: cfmedip-seq-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw cfMeDIP-seq or (cf)MeDIP-seq FASTQ files (single-end or paired-end, with or without spike-in/UMI sequences) need automated QC, alignment, methylation quantification, and multi-sample aggregation into tab-delimited bin-sample matrices.

name: cfmedip-seq-read-qc
description: Use when starting from raw FASTQ files of cfMeDIP-seq (or (cf)MeDIP-seq) libraries and you need adapter trimming, conditional UMI barcode handling, and per-sample QC reports as the first module of an automated pipeline.

name: cfmedip-seq-short-read-alignment
description: Use when raw or Trim Galore-trimmed cfMeDIP-seq FASTQs (single-end or paired-end, with or without spike-ins/UMIs) must be mapped, duplicate-processed, and QC-assessed to produce sorted BAMs and fragment-size metrics.

name: chain-file-coordinate-conversion
description: Use when query regions in one genome (e.g., hg38 SNP coordinates) must be mapped to another genome (e.g., mm10), especially when regulatory function of mapped loci matters and plain chain-based liftOver may multi-map or miss orthologous elements.

name: changepoint-segmentation-of-binned-coverage
description: Use when you have a normalized, binned scATAC-seq accessibility matrix and need to call focal amplifications (e.g., double minutes) at single-cell resolution without a matched normal control.

name: chi-square-contingency-analysis
description: Use when comparing categorical occurrence counts (e.g., motif families from Genomatix MatBase) between test and control sequence sets to quantify which category is most enriched, such as STAT motif enrichment in ChIP-Seq peaks versus ChIP-chip regions.

name: chi-square-independence-testing-of-mcpg-combinations
description: Use when bisulfite-sequencing epihaplotype matrices (binary mCpG per molecule) must be mined for statistically significant co-methylated CpG combinations underlying stable epiallele families.

name: chi-square-score-transformation
description: Use when a weighted, correlation-corrected per-gene p-value (e.g. from SMITE's scorePval/stoufferTest with MCM bootstrapping) must be converted into a single comparable score statistic and calibrated against a known null distribution for gene- or module-level significance.

name: chi-square-significance-testing
description: Use when compartment scores (PC1/PC2) from two or more Hi-C contact maps are quantile-normalized and you must call per-bin significant compartment differences, including changes without a compartment flip.

name: chia-pet-bedpe-binning
description: Use when PET pairs are already in a duplicate-removed bedpe file (e.g. prefixname.rmdup.bedpe from ChIA-PET2) and a genome-binned 2D contact matrix in triplet sparse format is needed for HiCPlotter-style visualization.

name: chia-pet-contact-matrix-generation
description: Use when a deduplicated ChIA-PET PET alignment BAM (unique, MAPQ >= 30, nonredundant PETs from CPU dedup) must be turned into .hic and/or .cool contact maps for Juicebox.js or HiGlass visualization.

name: chia-pet-linker-filtering
description: Use when raw ChIA-PET, HiChIP, or PLAC-seq FASTQ read pairs (e.g., 2 × 21 bp or 2 × 150 bp) must have their bridge linker sequences detected before mapping and downstream peak/loop calling.

name: chia-pet-linker-sequence-scanning
description: Use when raw paired-end ChIA-PET (or HiChIP/PLAC-seq) FASTQ reads must be classified by bridge-linker detection before genome mapping, so only genuine linker-flanked PETs carry forward to interaction analysis.

name: chia-pet-linker-trimming
description: Use when raw ChIA-PET paired-end FASTQ reads contain bridge-linker sequences at the 5' ends and you need linker-trimmed reads before alignment, or when quantifying how much the valid PET ratio improves with mismatch tolerance.

name: chia-pet-loop-anchor-processing
description: Use when ChIA-PIPE has called RNAPII ChIA-PET loops (PET count ≥3 with peak support, unique loop IDs) and you need to classify each loop as E-P, P-P, or neither using enhancer/promoter genomic coordinates.

name: chia-pet-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads from ChIA-PET (short 2×21 bp or long 2×150 bp), HiChIP, or PLAC-seq libraries need automated processing into peaks, loops, contact domains, and 2D contact map visualization files.

name: chia-pet-quality-control-assessment
description: Use when processing a ChIA-PET (or related HiChIP/PLAC-seq) library through ChIA-PIPE and you need an automated QC assessment plus visualization files to judge dataset quality after the full pipeline run.

name: chia-pet-quality-control-metrics
description: Use when processing bridge-linker or half-linker ChIA-PET FASTQ data through ChIA-PET2 and you need stepwise PET-retention statistics (valid PETs pre/post-alignment, post-duplicate-removal fraction, intra-chromosomal >=4 PET fraction) to judge dataset quality.

name: chia-pet-read-mapping
description: Use when processing raw ChIA-PET (or related HiChIP/PLAC-seq) FASTQ read pairs that have passed linker filtering and need to be aligned to a reference genome before peak and loop calling.

name: chia-pet-tag-alignment
description: Use when linker-filtered ChIA-PET FASTQ tags must be mapped to a reference genome and deduplicated into analysis-ready PETs before peak and loop calling.

name: chiapet-pet-read-processing
description: Use when raw ChIA-PET (or HiChIP/PLAC-seq) FASTQ reads must be converted into deduplicated PET alignments, peaks, and interaction loops with reproducible QC, as in the GM12878 CTCF MiSeq test data workflow.

name: chiapet-pipeline-configuration-execution
description: Use when raw ChIA-PET (or HiChIP/PLAC-seq) paired-end FASTQ reads need end-to-end processing into chromatin interaction loops and peaks, with automated QC assessment.

name: chip-annotation-ground-truth-mapping
description: Use when a probabilistic TF occupancy method needs quantitative validation against ChIP-chip/ChIP-exo/ORGANIC ground-truth binding annotations, e.g. comparing RoboCOP runs to COMPETE variants and FIMO baselines across many TFs.

name: chip-exo-peak-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have genome-wide binding-affinity predictions from an in vitro-trained regressor (e.g. DNAffinity gcPBM model for CBF1) and experimental peak coordinates (ChIP-exo/PB-exo BED-like intervals) to compute TP and FP rates in vivo.

name: chip-seq-anchor-occupancy-overlap-validation
description: Use when a set of chromatin loop calls (e.g., bedpe from MICC/ChIA-PET2) needs orthogonal validation against independent CTCF/cohesin ChIP-seq peaks in the same cell line (e.g., GM12878).

name: chip-seq-binding-library-based-tr-identification
description: Use when a set of differentially accessible region BED files (e.g., from bulk TR perturbation cKO experiments via DiffBind export.

name: chip-seq-broad-domain-calling
description: Use when the goal is to identify broad ChIP-seq enrichment domains spanning kb to Mb scales (e.g., H3K27me3 or H3K9me3) from mapped-read BED files, especially where whole-domain integrity (covering full gene bodies of repressed genes) matters more than sharp peak positions.

name: chip-seq-coverage-binning
