description: Use when raw ChIP-seq BAM files for one or more epigenomic marks (e.g. ENCODE K562 H3K4me3/H3K9ac) plus a MACS/MACS2 peak list must be turned into fixed-width binned coverage profiles for shape-based alignment or clustering.

name: chip-seq-coverage-profile-generation
description: Use when mapped ChIP-Seq short reads (BED or ELAND format, or paired-end with known insert size) must be converted into a binned, end-weighted WIG-format coverage profile as input to HMM-based peak calling.

name: chip-seq-data-retrieval-from-geo
description: Use when a differential ChIP-seq analysis needs its raw aligned reads (BAM) fetched from public repositories, specifically when reproducing the ENCODE H1-hESC vs K562 histone mark comparison via GEO sample accessions.

name: chip-seq-duplicate-read-removal
description: Use when aligned ChIP-seq BAM files are about to be binned and counted (e.g. with histoneHMM getBins/countBamInGRanges) and PCR/sequencing duplicates would inflate per-bin read counts; the article applied this to all H3K27me3/H3K9me3 datasets from rat, mouse and human cell lines.

name: chip-seq-enriched-vs-background-binning
description: Use when ChIP-Seq short-read data (e.g. BED/ELAND single-end or pair-end) must be binned into enriched vs. background regions to model read-count distributions or call protein-DNA binding peaks.

name: chip-seq-genome-binning-and-hdf-counting
description: Use when raw aligned ChIP-Seq reads (BED or ELAND format, single- or pair-end) must be converted into a fixed-bin coverage profile prior to peak calling or HMM classification.

name: chip-seq-genome-browser-profile-generation
description: Use when you have BAM/SAM files of mapped ChIP-seq reads and need genome-wide coverage profiles (BedGraph) for genome-browser visualization or for testing sequencing-depth saturation of a histone mark.

name: chip-seq-histone-modification-data-processing
description: Use when raw ChIP-Seq BAM files for histone marks (e.g. wgEncodeBroadHistoneK562H3k4me3StdAlnRep1.bam) must be converted into binned enrichment profiles over peak regions before alignment/clustering with DGW.

name: chip-seq-motif-prediction
description: Use when raw or processed human ChIP-seq peak calls (e.g. ENCODE BED with summits) are available and the goal is to discover TF-DNA binding motifs with significance scores and compare them to documented motifs.

name: chip-seq-peak-calling
description: Use when the input is raw ChIP-Seq short reads (BED or ELAND format, human or mouse) or BED files for transcription-factor or histone-mark datasets, and the goal is to identify read-enriched regions and compare peak callers.
tools: PeakFinder / FindPeaks / MACS / SISSRs / CisGenome / ChIPseeqer

name: chip-seq-peak-calling
description: Use when a ChIP-seq FASTQ dataset (with a matched input/control) needs peaks, peak annotation, or motif identification, and CIPHER is being used to run the full two-stage pipeline from raw reads to called peaks.

name: chip-seq-peak-calling-for-loop-anchors
description: Use when processing ChIA-PET data where chromatin loops must be called between ChIP-Seq-like peak anchors, e.g. after bwa alignment and removeDup, before bedpe2Interaction/MICC loop calling.

name: chip-seq-peak-calling-replicate-handling
description: Use when raw sequencing data of lncRNA:DNA capture experiments (ChIRP-seq, ChOP-seq, CHART-seq, RAP-seq) from GEO/ENA must be uniformly re-processed and replicate-inconsistent peaks reconciled into benchmark BED peak sets.

name: chip-seq-peak-calling-with-control
description: Use when starting from aligned-read BAM files of one or more ChIP-seq marks plus a matched input/control BAM, and you need enriched peak regions (e.g. as BED input for unsupervised alignment/clustering) rather than gene-anchored windows.

name: chip-seq-peak-motif-classification
description: Use when ChIP-seq peaks for multiple TFs (e.g. the 100 TFs expressed in K562) have DESSO-predicted motifs and TFBSs, and you need to separate direct from indirect binding to infer tethering.

name: chip-seq-peak-sequence-extraction
description: Use when preparing summit-centered, score-annotated FASTA inputs for MEPP positional motif profiling from MACS2 narrowpeak calls (e.g. ENCODE K562 GATA1 ChIP-seq or mESC Nanog ChIP-seq/ChIP-nexus peaks).

name: chip-seq-peak-signal-integration
description: Use when you have TR ChIP-seq peak bed files with signal enrichment values and gene TSS annotations and need quantitative TR-target scores (RP scores) rather than binary target lists.

name: chip-seq-peak-strand-orientation-analysis
description: Use when strand-annotated ChIP-seq peak BED files and strand-assigned TFBS BED files are available and the goal is to test whether motif-level strand asymmetry (e.g. CTCF non-template strand preference) is recapitulated within peaks.

name: chip-seq-quality-atlas-stratification
description: Use when compiling ChiLin QC outputs (e.g., id_frip FRiP JSON records) and you need to benchmark what proportion of ChIP versus input samples exceed a 1% FRiP threshold.

name: chip-seq-read-alignment-spike-in-genome
description: Use when raw ChIP-seq FASTQ libraries from a spike-in experiment (e.g. Jurkat H3K79me2 GSE60104 with fruit fly spike-in) must be mapped to a concatenated synthetic reference and filtered before genome segmentation and normalization.

name: chip-seq-read-count-binning
description: Use when preparing raw ChIP-seq BAM files of broad-footprint histone modifications (e.g. H3K27me3) for histoneHMM differential or single-sample calling, where per-bin bivariate read counts must be computed before HMM fitting.

name: chip-seq-read-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw Illumina ChIP-seq FASTQ files (e.g., TF immunoprecipitation samples from GEO accession GSE136050) must be adapter- and quality-trimmed prior to genome alignment and macs2 peak calling.

name: chip-seq-read-window-binning
description: Use when preparing mapped ChIP-seq (or control) BED files for broad-domain calling with RECOGNICER, i.e. when the analysis requires converting raw read coordinates into nucleosome-resolution (default 200 bp) binary blocks before recursive block transformation.

name: chip-seq-sequence-encoding-and-gc-matched-background-sampling
description: Use when predicting TF-DNA binding specificity from ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks with long DNA sequences (1001 bp) and a gated CNN, or when comparing GCNN AUCs against the 101-bp one-layer CNN baseline.

name: chip-seq-signal-aggregation-over-peaks
description: Use when benchmarking peak callers on qbed calling-cards data and you need orthogonal validation: average ChIP-seq (bigWig) signal under each caller's peaks plus pairwise peak-overlap concordance between callers.

name: chip-seq-signal-benchmarking
description: Use when validating Hi-C-derived sub-compartment probabilities against independent enrichment tracks (TSA-seq, ChIP-seq, cTSA-seq) and comparing correlation performance against published compartment callers.

name: chip-seq-signal-scoring-of-motif-sites
description: Use when motif-centered genomic sequences need a continuous biological-activity score (e.g. mESC Nanog ChIP-seq signal from GSE203135) so MEPP can profile partner-motif enrichment along a score continuum instead of arbitrary binding thresholds.

name: chip-seq-target-gene-set-analysis
description: Use when you have a BED file of TF ChIP-seq peaks and want to learn the biological function of the target genes linked to those binding regions via GO/KEGG enrichment.

name: chip-seq-target-inference
description: Use when you need to infer which genes a transcriptional regulator targets from ChIP-seq peak data (e.g., ENCODE), especially as input to regression-based drug response association such as RePhine on CCLE data.

name: chipseq-alignment-to-track-conversion
description: Use when filtered .bam/.bai ChIPseq alignments (e.g. post-samtools filter output) must be turned into genome-browser track files and GRanges objects for visualization and downstream analysis.

name: chipseq-control-based-significance-testing
description: Use when you have paired ChIP and control mapped-read BED files for a broad histone mark (e.g. H3K27me3/H3K9me3, kb-to-Mb domains) and need to call integral domains and compare their functional association across methods.

name: chipseq-control-signal-profiling
description: Use when you have region intervals stratified by TF occupancy (e.g. HOT >99th percentile, MILD 75th-99th, COLD <75th) plus IgG-control bigWig tracks, and need to quantify/plot class-wise control enrichment.

name: chipseq-count-based-gam-fitting
description: Use when modeling ChIP-Seq read-count frequencies along chromosomes as smooth functions (e.g. factorial designs with genotype or treatment), or when genome-wide base-level and region-level significance testing with data-driven smoothing is required.

name: chipseq-count-smoothing-model-statistics
description: Use when standard errors or position-wise significance are needed for smooth (spline) terms fitted to ChIP-Seq count data with a sparse penalized Hessian, and forming the full matrix inverse is infeasible.

name: chipseq-differential-modification-gene-mapping
description: Use when ChIP-seq differential modification calls (e.g., broad marks like H3K27me3/H3K9me3) must be intersected with a DESeq-derived DE gene list (FDR<0.01) and the overlap significance quantified and compared across peak-calling methods.

name: chipseq-differential-region-intersection
description: Use when you have differential region calls from two or more ChIP-seq peak/broad-mark callers on the same genome assembly and an independent ground-truth coordinate set (qPCR-validated regions, X-inactivated gene bodies) to score sensitivity and false discovery per method.

name: chipseq-duplicate-read-filtering
description: Use when processing mapped ChIPseq reads (BAM) downstream of the 'map' module and before peakcalling, and duplicate-read handling and fragment-size bounds must be applied reproducibly across a project.

name: chipseq-fasta-dataset-handling
description: Use when you need to benchmark DiNAMO's execution time and memory footprint on the article's ChIP-seq FASTA signal/control dataset pairs (e.g. GATA1) or compare its runtime with MEME-CHIP, HOMER and Discrover as in Table 3.

name: chipseq-fold-enrichment-over-hot-regions
description: Use when assessing whether ChIP-seq signal at HOT regions is a technical artifact: you have KO transcription factor ChIP-seq IP/control FASTQ pairs and a HOT region interval set, and need per-experiment fold-enrichment over those regions.

name: chipseq-functional-annotation-of-peak-features
description: Use when narrowPeak/BED peak files from epigenomic assays (e.g. K562 ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq vs H3K27ac ChIP-seq) need biological interpretation — genomic state (ChromHMM), nearest-gene (ChIPseeker) and TSS-enrichment annotation — rather than just QC metrics.

name: chipseq-gene-body-signal-quantification
description: Use when you have mapped ChIP-seq BAM files plus RefSeq gene groups ranked by expression (e.g. highly/moderately/silent RNA-seq groups) and need per-group, sequencing-depth-normalized signal levels over gene bodies to build boxplot correlation panels.

name: chipseq-genome-wide-binned-read-counting
description: Use when ChIP-seq BAM files (experimental sample plus exogenous spike-in) must be converted into fixed-bin read-count tables across the whole genome, e.g. to support comparative spike-in normalization or peak-vs-background signal quantification.

name: chipseq-overrepresented-motif-discovery
description: Use when you have a positive multi-FASTA of ChIP-seq peak sequences (e.g. GATA1, SOX2, OCT4, STAT3, KLF1 peaks) plus a negative control FASTA, and need exhaustive IUPAC motif discovery to identify over-represented TF binding sites.

name: chipseq-peak-boundary-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have TAD boundary coordinates (e.g., from TOAST on GM12878 Hi-C) plus ENCODE narrowPeak ChIP-seq files or enhancer/promoter interval sets, and need to quantify the fraction of boundaries anchored by each regulatory signal.

name: chipseq-peak-calling
description: Use when base-level ChIP-seq peak calling is needed for factorial-design experiments (IP vs control/genotype), especially on gigabase-scale genomes where memory-efficient, out-of-core GAM fitting is required.

name: chipseq-peak-calling
description: Use when running the peakcalling step of a NEAT ChIPseq project: a filtered alignment (.bam) exists and an algorithm (MACS or SPP) is selected in Targets.txt under 'Steps_to_execute_pipe'.

name: chipseq-peak-calling-with-macs
description: Use when mapped ChIP-seq reads (BAM/SAM, e.g. Bowtie-aligned to mm9/mm10) must be reduced to a peak set that serves as the region reference for meta-plots, heatmaps, or ChIP-level quantification in SeqCode-based workflows.

name: chipseq-peak-count-comparison
description: Use when raw ChIP-seq FASTQ files (e.g. GEO GSE136050) need trimming, alignment to the V. harveyi reference, macs2 peak calling, and validation of per-factor peak counts against published figures.

name: chipseq-peak-file-retrieval
description: Use when you have a transcription factor of interest and need its ChIP-seq peak regions as a BED file to query against a REM database such as EpiRegio for target-gene association.

name: chipseq-peak-overlap-classification
description: Use when two BED-format peak lists from ChIP-seq experiments (e.g. H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 in mESC) must be partitioned into overlap-based classes such as active, bivalent, and silent regulatory states.

name: chipseq-peak-summit-density-windowing
description: Use when you have many narrowPeak ChIP-seq peak files for numerous TFs in a genome assembly and need to call HOT regions by peak-summit density rather than individual binding sites.

name: chipseq-peak-to-enclave-overlap-counting
description: Use when BHi-Cect cluster output (named lists of loci per enclave) is available and you need to characterize each bottom enclave's regulatory content by quantifying ChIP-seq TF binding per enclave.

name: chipseq-quality-control-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw ChIP-seq or DNase-seq FASTQ files (treatment and control) must be quality-controlled and analyzed end-to-end, and per-sample QC metrics such as FRiP, PBC, and replicate correlation are the required outputs.

name: chipseq-quality-metric-computation
description: Use when processing FASTQ/BAM ChIP-seq or DNase-seq samples through ChiLin-style QC steps and you need per-sample read-layer metrics (FastQC score, uniquely mapped ratio, PBC, FRiP, fragment size) for quality assessment.

name: chipseq-read-alignment-and-filtering
description: Use when starting from raw ChIP-seq FASTQ files (IP and matched control, e.g. KO transcription factor experiments from ENA accessions in Supplementary Table S1) that must be trimmed, aligned, and filtered before computing read coverage or fold enrichment over genomic intervals.

name: chipseq-read-alignment-and-unaligned-read-filtering
description: Use when starting from raw ChIP-seq FASTQ files (e.g. GEO accessions such as GSM2645501/GSM2645502) that must be mapped to a genome (mm9, mm10, hg38, dm3) and converted into clean BAM files for peak calling or SeqCode read-count/visualization commands.

name: chipseq-read-count-ingestion-genomic-intervals
description: Use when raw ChIP-seq BAM files from a factorial design experiment (e.g. two conditions × two replicates) must be converted into position-indexed read counts over overlapping genomic tiles as input to a GenoGAM model fit.

name: chipseq-read-distribution-analysis
description: Use when two or more sequencing lanes from the same ChIP-Seq sample group (e.g., stimulated or unstimulated STAT1) must be checked for consistent genome-wide read distributions across chromosome/strand combinations, or when within-group vs cross-group reproducibility must be contrasted.

name: chipseq-read-mapping
description: Use when raw ChIPseq FASTQ reads must be aligned to a reference genome inside an automated pipeline, especially when standard and spike-in (exogenous epigenome) samples must be aligned with identical parameters for ChIP-rx normalization.

name: chipseq-read-quality-trimming
description: Use when starting from raw ChIP-seq FASTQ files (e.g. ENA/ENCODE IP and control libraries) that must be cleaned prior to alignment with a short-read aligner such as Bowtie, especially when computing read coverage or IP/control enrichment over genomic intervals like HOT regions.

name: chipseq-rnaseq-regulatory-integration
description: Use when you have two genome-wide binding peak sets (e.g. MACS2 ChIP-seq peaks for two TFs) and RNA-seq differential expression results, and need to define promoters bound and co-regulated by both regulators.

name: chipseq-sample-metadata-annotation
description: Use when setting up a new NEAT ChIPseq project on an institution's cluster and raw compressed fastq files must be mapped to user-defined sample names, replicates, antibodies and pipeline blocks before execution.

name: chipseq-signal-aggregation-per-cluster
description: Use when BHi-Cect tree output (nested cluster list) and ChIP-seq tracks must be combined to compute epigenomic signal prevalence per bottom enclave for gene ranking or enrichment analysis.

name: chipseq-spike-in-normalization
description: Use when ChIPseq samples must be quantitatively compared genome-wide and an exogenous spike-in epigenome (ChIP-rx) control was sequenced, or when reconstructing/running the NEAT 'chiprx' module.

name: chipseq-spikein-normalization
description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq signal across conditions (e.g. drug treatment series) using spike-in chromatin, and a genome-wide normalization that preserves background signal while correcting peak signal is needed.

name: chipseq-target-set-integration
description: Use when pharmacogenomic drug sensitivity data (e.g. CCLE) must be linked to ChIP-seq-defined TR target sets to infer drug-response-associated transcriptional regulators or to organize drugs into mechanism-of-action clusters.

name: chipseq-test-dataset-processing
description: Use when a NEAT project must be exercised end-to-end on the bundled truncated H3K4me3 ChIPseq test fastq files (Targets.txt registered), or when validating that NEAT's double-clickable pipeline modules run without programming experience.

name: chipseq-tss-meta-plot-generation
description: Use when you have a mapped ChIP-seq BAM (e.g. H3K4me3 in mESC), RefSeq refGene and chromosome-size files for the assembly, and need standardized TSS-centered meta-plots or heatmaps to visualize enrichment around transcription start sites.

name: cholesky-factorization-whitening
description: Use when combining two-sided p-values (e.g. methylation promoter/other-context p-values in a genomic interval) that are correlated, so Stouffer-style combination would otherwise be invalid.

name: chromatin-accessibility-data-processing
description: Use when paired-end chromatin accessibility reads (BAM from MNase-seq or ATAC-seq) must be classified by fragment length and converted to per-base midpoint-count tracks for nucleosome/TF occupancy modeling.

name: chromatin-accessibility-deviation-computation
description: Use when analyzing sparse single-cell (or bulk) ATAC-seq fragment counts to identify motifs or genomic annotations associated with cell-to-cell variability in chromatin accessibility, or to derive per-cell deviation scores for downstream clustering/t-SNE.

name: chromatin-accessibility-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when lifted-over SNP or interval sets must be linked to cell-type-specific regulatory activity — e.g., testing whether mapped SCZ GWAS SNPs are enriched in chromatin accessible regions of mouse excitatory vs inhibitory neuron populations.

name: chromatin-accessibility-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when ATAC-seq DA peak sets (opening vs. closing with age) must be tested for enrichment of cell-type-specific chromatin annotations per sex, e.g. to verify male-specific B cell locus decline or female opening patterns.

name: chromatin-accessibility-expression-integration
description: Use when you have paired DNase1-seq and RNA-seq samples across multiple cell types/tissues and need to link regulatory regions to genes whose expression variation they explain.

name: chromatin-accessibility-visualization-at-egfr-locus
description: Use when you need to test whether a mapped eccDNA/amplified region (e.g. chr7:54370001-55996000 at the EGFR locus in GBM) overlaps highly accessible chromatin using TCGA ATAC-seq signal tracks.

name: chromatin-contact-domain-calling
description: Use when ChIA-PIPE loop-calling output (PET clusters with coordinates, PET counts, and anchor peak-support flags) from CTCF ChIA-PET data must be converted into chromatin contact domain (CCD) intervals.

name: chromatin-contact-map-analysis
description: Use when you have an intra-chromosomal NxN Hi-C contact matrix (e.g., KR-normalized at 50/25/5 Kb from GM12878) and need unsupervised TAD boundary detection without complex parameter tuning.

name: chromatin-contact-matrix-generation
description: Use when you hold a deduplicated ChIA-PET bedpe (e.g., in.rmDup.bedpe) and need a fixed-binsize Hi-C-style contact matrix (e.g., 10 kb, triplet sparse) to overlay with Hi-C maps or interrogate loop structure at anchors.

name: chromatin-contact-significance-calling
description: Use when normalized Hi-C or capture Hi-C fragment-pair data are available and you need per-contact significance scores, reproducibility fractions between biological replicates, or a ROC AUC comparison against Fit-Hi-C.

name: chromatin-contact-table-processing
description: Use when Hi-C or capture Hi-C fragment-pair tables have already been coverage-normalized (bias-removed residuals with freq and dist columns) and the goal is to remove the distance-dependent decay background to obtain normalized interaction frequencies or call significant interactions.

name: chromatin-domain-modularity-assessment
description: Use when you need to evaluate or rank TLD/TAD predictions from a Hi-C matrix (bulk or single-cell) by 2D structural entropy and modularity indices, e.g., to confirm a predictor's first-class performance beyond AMI/WS benchmarks.

name: chromatin-factor-wt-vs-knockout-signal-comparison
description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq signal of a chromatin regulator (e.g. MLL2) or its histone mark (e.g. H3K4me3) between WT and genetic-knockout samples, and you need depth-normalized ChIP levels plus averaged peak-centered meta-plots and boxplots.

name: chromatin-feature-prediction-model-training
description: Use when the goal is to pre-train a sequence-based convolutional network on chromatin feature datasets (e.g. ENCODE/Roadmap marks such as CTCF, DNase, ChIP-seq) as the first phase of deepC transfer learning for chromatin interaction prediction.

name: chromatin-interaction-data-processing
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ from ChIA-PET, HiChIP, or PLAC-seq libraries must be processed end-to-end into peaks, loops, chromatin contact domains, and 2D contact maps viewable in Juicebox/HiGlass.

name: chromatin-interaction-loop-calling
description: Use when processing ChIA-PET, HiChIP, or PLAC-seq read pairs (short 2×21 bp or long 2×150 bp) and you need to call chromatin interaction loops with peak-supported anchors from uniquely aligned, nonredundant PETs.

name: chromatin-interaction-pet-preprocessing
description: Use when raw paired-end ChIA-PET FASTQ reads must be scanned for bridge linker sequences and partitioned by linker status prior to read mapping and loop calling.

name: chromatin-interaction-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when assessing how well sequence-based 3D genome folding predictions (deepC) reproduce observed Hi-C contacts on holdout chromosomes, e.g. computing Pearson correlations for raw vs smoothed maps or low-depth training sets.

name: chromatin-interaction-sindel-annotation
description: Use when validating that predicted noncoding indels are biologically meaningful by testing their enrichment in enhancer/promoter chromatin interactions or histone-mark regions against true cis-eQTL sindels.

name: chromatin-loop-anchor-resolution
description: Use when ChIA-PET reads must be resolved to allele-specific loops for a sample with genome-wide SNP phasing (e.g., NA12878), and you need statistically biased SNPs at loop anchors.

name: chromatin-loop-calling-from-imaging-data
description: Use when the input is per-cell, per-allele 3D coordinates of genomic loci from multiplexed DNA FISH or DNA seqFISH+ (e.g., 25 Kb or 5 Kb bins) and the goal is de novo chromatin loop detection and benchmarking against HiCCUPS references.

name: chromatin-loop-calling-from-schic
description: Use when you have per-cell (tab-separated, optionally gzipped) scHi-C contact files for mm10/hg19/hg38 and need cell-type-specific chromatin loop candidates and summits.

name: chromatin-loop-calling-statistical-testing
description: Use when input is per-cell scHi-C or sn-m3C-seq contact files (e.g. 2,869 human prefrontal cortex sn-m3C-seq cells or 742 mouse ESCs) and the goal is to call cell-type-specific chromatin loops at 10-kb resolution.

name: chromatin-loop-prediction-from-contact-maps
description: Use when you have a 10 kb-binned .cool/.hic contact map and a positive interaction set (ChIA-PET/HiChIP/Capture Hi-C bedpe) and need supervised, data-driven chromatin loop calls that are robust to low sequencing depth.

name: chromatin-loop-transitivity-and-redundancy-analysis
description: Use when a Hi-C contact map implies a transitive or redundant chromatin loop between loci and a ChIA-PET2 CTCF bedpe/contact matrix is available to confirm or refute the direct interaction.

name: chromatin-ndr-dynamics-visualization
description: Use when comparing timepoint-specific nucleosome dyad positions (e.g., 0 min vs 60 min cadmium MNase-seq) across promoter-aligned gene groups to detect +1 nucleosome shifts and nucleosome-depleted region remodeling.

name: chromatin-peak-calling
description: Use when processing ChIA-PET (or HiChIP/PLAC-seq) libraries and protein-factor binding peaks must be called from self-ligation PETs to support loop calling, CCD calling, and enhancer-promoter annotation.

name: chromatin-profile-score-interpretation
description: Use when a set of query noncoding SNPs must be functionally screened for their impact on chromatin accessibility, histone marks, or TF binding across many ENCODE/Roadmap epigenomic profiles in a tissue- or cell type-specific manner.

name: chromatin-state-annotation
description: Use when you have genome-wide multi-track epigenomic signals (histone mark ChIP-seq tracks) for one or more Roadmap/ENCODE samples and need discrete chromatin state sequences as input to EpiAlign alignment or compression benchmarking.

name: chromatin-state-frequency-vector-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking an order-aware chromatin-state comparison method (e.g. EpiAlign) against a simple, order-agnostic baseline, or when only overall chromatin state composition — not sequence order — is needed to distinguish epigenomic samples.

name: chromatin-state-regulatory-element-classification
description: Use when RNAPII ChIA-PET loop calls (PET count ≥3 with peak support) need to be annotated as enhancer-promoter or promoter-promoter interactions and exported as separate per-category loop files for visualization in BASIC Browser tracks.

name: chromatin-state-sequence-compression
description: Use when chromatin state sequences (e.g. from ChromHMM on Roadmap epigenomes) are about to be aligned with EpiAlign, or when uncompressed sequences contain long runs of a single state such as the quiescent state 'o'.

name: chromatin-state-weight-scoring
description: Use when two genomic regions are represented as ChromHMM-derived chromatin state label sequences and you need a similarity score that accounts for varying state lengths, state frequencies, mismatches, and deletions (e.g. -match queries in 500 kb regions).

name: chromatogram-peak-height-quantification
description: Use when you have .ab1 Sanger trace files plus a reference .fasta from a bisulfite sequencing PCR experiment and need per-CpG methylation percentages computed from dye peak heights.

name: chromatogram-trace-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw .ab1 Sanger sequencing trace files must be trimmed of low-quality and mixed-base ends prior to computing CpG methylation percentages from direct-BSP or cloning-BSP data, or when a final trimmed sequence is too short and trimming thresholds need adjustment.

name: chromhmm-annotation-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when comparing open-chromatin or ChIP peak sets (e.g. ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq narrowPeak files) and you need a ChromHMM-based functional annotation heatmap showing the percentage of peaks overlapping each chromatin state per sample.

name: chromhmm-state-annotation-retrieval
description: Use when a query genomic region's ChromHMM-annotated chromatin state sequence (e.g. from NIH Roadmap sample E071) must be compared against all gene regions to rank local-alignment similarity, especially when long quiescent stretches would otherwise dominate uncompressed alignments.

name: chromosome-based-cross-validation-design
description: Use when evaluating enhancer-target interaction prediction models on genomic coordinate data (e.g. BENGI All-Pairs.Natural-Ratio ET pairs) where random folds would leak spatially autocorrelated loci between train and test chromosomes.

name: chromosome-cluster-nesting-analysis
description: Use when you have a 3-column sparse Hi-C contact matrix (e.g. IMR90 at 50 kb or 5 kb resolution) and need a recursive, hierarchy-aware clustering of loci without imposing genomic contiguity.

name: chromosome-holdout-cross-validation
description: Use when evaluating sequence-based chromatin contact predictors under a chromosome-holdout cross-validation scheme, where predicted and observed Hi-C contact maps on held-out chromosomes are compared via distance-stratified Pearson correlations across cell lines.

name: chromosome-naming-convention-handling
description: Use when preparing a spike-in ChIP-seq normalization run (e.g. spikChIP with human hg19 sample plus dm3 fly spike-in) and a chromInfo file or combined reference genome must be assembled with renamed exogenous chromosomes.

name: chromosome-wise-hic-matrix-processing
description: Use when per-chromosome Hi-C contact maps (bulk or pseudo-bulk, resolutions up to 10 kb, or 5 kb with optimized PCA) need to be converted into A/B compartment score tracks for downstream differential analysis.

name: chromscape-workflow-execution
description: Use when the input is a sparse single-cell epigenomic count matrix (e.g. gzipped reads-in-peaks from GEO like GSE99172) and the goal is to cluster cells into subpopulations with common epigenomes and validate clustering against known labels such as cell line or replicate.

name: chromvar-deviation-score-statistical-testing
description: Use when you have a chromVARDeviations object with bias-corrected deviations/Z-scores and cell-type or sample annotations, and you want per-motif tests of differential deviation or differential variability between groups.

name: chromvar-motif-deviation-scoring
description: Use when analyzing scATAC-seq peak-count data (e.g., h5ad from SCALE) to quantify motif activity per cell and compare motif detection between raw and imputed/denoised matrices.

name: cis-driver-gene-rank-derivation
description: Use when assessing the reproducibility of iEDGE Rank-1 cis driver predictions across bootstrapped resamples of a TCGA-style SCNA/gene-expression cohort, or when a stability measure for mediation-ranked cis genes is required.

name: cis-eqtl-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a list of predicted enhancer–gene (gene–peak) pairs must be validated against an independent cis-eQTL reference set and summarized with AUROC/AUPRC benchmark metrics.

name: cis-gene-rank-stratification
description: Use when an iEDGE mediation (bipartite/pruning) output for SCNAs yields ranked cis gene lists and you must isolate Rank-1 cis genes (most-mediating per alteration) from non-Rank-1 genes for downstream driver validation.

name: cis-trans-gene-signature-annotation
description: Use when significant cis/trans gene sets from iEDGE differential expression and mediation analysis need functional annotation, e.g. detecting hallmark pathways recurrently enriched across multiple SCNAs.

name: cis-trans-mediation-ranking
description: Use when a cis/trans differential-expression signature table exists for SCNA events and candidate cis genes must be ranked by their trans mediation to designate the Rank-1 driver per alteration.

name: cistrome-definition-from-topic-specific-motifs
description: Use when a cisTopic object with a selected topic model (e.g. 30 topics on 10X 5k PBMCs) is available and per-topic TF cistromes or master regulators must be identified from topic-enriched regions.

name: class-imbalanced-binary-classification
description: Use when labeling enhancer-target pairs as interacting/not-interacting on imbalanced BENGI All-Pairs.Natural-Ratio datasets, or when comparing boosted-tree classifiers (CENTRE/XGBoost, TargetFinder GBM, Random Forest) under chromosome-split cross-validation with AUPRC and F1.

name: classification-regression-metric-evaluation
description: Use when trained sgRNA editing-efficiency predictors on CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa screening data must be scored on a 10% held-out test split, compared across feature-combination ablations via AUC and Spearman correlation with s.e.m. and t-tests.

name: classifier-performance-metrics-comparison
description: Use when a prediction pipeline must choose among several candidate learning algorithms: train each on identical encoded features, evaluate with 5-fold cross-validation, and tabulate Sn/ACC/MCC/AUC/F1 to justify the final classifier choice.

name: classifier-versus-novelty-detector-evaluation
description: Use when reproducing or extending the simulated translocation-time benchmark (Fig. 6, Supp. Table S6) that compares novelty detectors and supervised classifiers for non-B DNA detection at varying non-B ratios.

name: clingen-haploinsufficiency-score-integration
description: Use when replicating POSTRE's dosage-sensitivity scoring for structural variant pathogenicity prediction, especially when genes on sex chromosomes lack triplosensitivity (TS) scores and a proxy must be substituted before thresholding.

name: clinical-correlate-association-analysis
description: Use when per-sample subclonal methylation feature counts (e.g. i-DMRs from DXM on bisulfite data) must be related to clinical outcomes such as relapse or patient covariates like age.

name: clinvar-nc-sindel-test-set-curation
description: Use when an independent test set of pathogenic vs benign non-coding small indels is needed to benchmark TIVAN-indel or comparable functional-impact predictors (CADD, FATHMM-indel, DeepSEA/DanQ) on ClinVar variants.

name: clip-seq-window-enrichment-testing
description: Use when analyzing eCLIP/CLIP-seq data to detect RNA-binding protein binding sites transcriptome-wide, especially when peak callers underperform or when binding to repetitive elements or low-abundance transcripts must be tested.

name: clonality-index-computation
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon epihaplotype tables are available and you need to distinguish clonally expanded (dominant) epiallele families from stochastic methylation by scoring each methylated core with a clonality index and E index.

name: clone-methylation-status-thresholding
description: Use when you have per-clone methylation percentage tables from ABSP individual cloning-BSP analyses and need to classify each clone into methylation statuses for a grouped analysis across samples.

name: clone-mix-quality-flagging
description: Decision support for cloning-BSP grouped analysis when per-clone CpG methylation percentages need conversion into methylation statuses and mixed clones must be flagged before producing methylation_status_table.csv.

name: cloud-executor-integration-without-ssh
description: Use when the target compute environment for Watchdog tasks is a cloud service or other execution backend that is not reachable via SSH and is not covered by the built-in local, remote-SSH, or DRMAA/Slurm executors.

name: cluster-based-cnv-smoothing-and-consensus-genotyping
description: Use when scATAC fragment matrices have already been normalized (normalizeMatrixN/collapseChrom3N), CNV clusters identified (identifyCNVClusters/clusterCNV), and per-cluster CNV calls need smoothing into consensus genotypes before plotting or per-cell annotation output.

name: cluster-based-expression-profiling
description: Use when you have a completed SRIQ cluster solution with core-cluster assignments plus a log2-transformed expression matrix (e.g., newFiltered_35k.txt) and need per-cluster DEGs and GO terms to interpret cluster biology.

name: cluster-co-occurrence-similarity-computation
description: Use when you have two or more sample-to-cluster assignments over the same cohort (e.g., a reference SRIQ run at BagSize 1200 and perturbed runs) and need to quantify cluster stability per K solution.

name: cluster-parameter-specification
description: Use when configuring a new NEAT project (Targets.txt) that will execute its unzip/QC/chiprx/map/filter/peakcalling blocks on an institutional qsub or bsub cluster and the cluster-specific header fields must be set.

name: cluster-scalability-throughput-analysis
description: Use when you must quantify how a distributed aligner's runtime and throughput scale with read volume and number of cluster nodes, compared against alternative aligners on the same WGBS dataset.

name: cluster-solution-stability-assessment
description: Use when running SRIQ (or similar permutation-based clustering) and you need to determine which clustering solution (K and diameter) is stable enough to trust, based on recurrence across iterations, QSS, and silhouette scores.

name: cluster-specific-peak-ranking
description: Use when you have scATAC-seq cluster assignments (e.g., SCALE Leiden clusters saved in adata.h5ad from a dataset like Breast_Tumor.h5ad) and need to extract the peaks most specific to each cell-type cluster (e.g., CD45+ vs Epcam+) to feed into motif enrichment with Homer.

name: clustering-accuracy-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing cluster assignments from a scATAC-seq method (e.g., SCALE latent-feature clustering with K-means) against reference cell-type labels, and a quantitative ranking of competing tools (ARI/NMI/F1) is required.

name: clustering-agreement-evaluation-ari-nmi
description: Use when cluster or cell-type assignments from one or more methods must be scored against reference labels across multiple conditions (e.g., coverage levels), producing ARI/NMI rows suitable for paired significance testing.

name: clustering-reproducibility-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking clustering robustness of scATAC-seq methods across sequencing depths or cell counts — e.

name: clustering-separation-benchmarking-across-methods
description: Use when two or more scATAC-seq embedding/clustering methods must be compared on the same cells and you need a quantitative separation metric (connectivity index) rather than eyeballing t-SNE overlays.

name: cnn-architecture-implementation
description: Use when implementing or verifying the DESSO CNN in TensorFlow 1.1.0/Python 2.7 to predict TF–DNA binding from 690 ENCODE ChIP-seq datasets, or when validating that layer/parameter shapes match the published 16-filter, 32-neuron FC, single-sigmoid-output architecture.

name: cnn-architecture-implementation-tensorflow
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce, extend, or validate the EpiCas-DL sgRNA-activity CNN — i.e. one-hot encoded 40-nt sequences plus min–max normalized epigenetic tracks must be mapped through a 150-filter multi-size convolutional layer in TensorFlow/Keras.

name: cnn-kernel-architecture-tuning
description: Use when tuning a Keras/TensorFlow 1D-CNN that classifies promoter sequences: you need to sweep learning rate, kernel count, and kernel size and select the -performing configuration.

name: cnn-model-training-for-tf-dna-binding
description: Use when you have GC-matched ChIP-seq peak/background data (e.g. the 690 ENCODE datasets, 101-bp or 1001-bp windows) and need to train a CNN classifier of TF-DNA binding on sequence or DNAShape features.

name: cnn-model-training-on-genomic-features
description: Use when training supervised deep learning classifiers on ENCODE ChIP-seq peak data — either DNA sequence or DNA shape feature matrices — to later extract motifs and TFBSs, e.g. reproducing DESSO's 690-dataset benchmark.

name: cnn-model-training-with-bayesian-hyperparameter-optimization
description: Use when predicting sgRNA on-target editing efficiency for CRISPR-mediated epigenome editing from one-hot encoded 40 bp sequences plus min-max normalized epigenetic channels (nucleosome positioning, ATAC-seq accessibility, DNA methylation, RNA expression), and hyperparameters must be optimized.

name: cnn-regression-model-training
description: Use when predicting continuous sgRNA gene-repression/activation activity from encoded sequence-plus-epigenetic matrices (11x40: 4 one-hot channels + nucleosome, chromatin accessibility, methylation, expression), or reproducing Fig. 2b-2c benchmark.

name: cnn-sequence-model-inference
description: Use when you need single-base-resolution functional impact scores (SAD = P(alt) − P(ref)) for non-coding SNPs across chromatin accessibility, histone mark, and TF binding profiles in a tissue-specific manner.

name: cnn-sgrna-activity-prediction
description: Use when predicting sgRNA editing/knock-down or knock-up efficiency from a 40-nt target sequence plus genomic coordinates and epigenetic tracks (methylation, ATAC accessibility, RNA expression, nucleosome/TSS distance), e.g., screening dataset scoring or sgRNA design ranking.

name: cnn-super-enhancer-classification
description: Use when the task is to predict SEs vs TEs from raw DNA sequences (FASTA) alone, without ChIP-seq data, for one cell line, pooled cell lines, a held-out cell line, or across species (hg19 vs mm9).

name: cnn-variant-effect-prediction
description: Use when you need to score the reference vs. alternative allele of a non-coding GWAS variant against chromatin profiles (DNase, histone marks, TF binding) in a tissue-specific manner, or to identify the motif driving a predicted effect (e.g., NFE2 at rs6426833).

name: cnv-chromosome-peak-removal
description: Use when scATAC clusters may be confounded by CNVs and you need to assess how cluster structure changes after removing peaks from CNV-harboring chromosomes before reclustering.

name: cnv-expression-linear-regression-adjustment
description: Use when gene-expression matrices will be correlated with drug response or other phenotypes, and CNV-driven expression variation must be removed first to avoid spurious associations.

name: co-expressed-gene-pair-ranking
description: Use when you have a mean-centered, gene-by-experiment expression matrix (e.g., COnTORT_organized_transcriptomic_data.txt with 5 GenBank annotation columns plus per-GSM columns) and need to rank co-expressed or anti-correlated gene pairs to nominate transcription factor targets.

name: co-occupancy-quantification-across-strains
description: Use when you have MACS2 ChIP-seq peak interval files for two DNA-binding proteins in two or more strain backgrounds and need per-strain counts of co-occupied, ORF-proximal regions.

name: coarse-graining-block-transformation
description: Use when calling broad ChIP-seq enrichment domains (e.g., H3K27me3/H3K9me3 spanning kb to Mb) from mapped-read BED files, or when characterizing multi-scale structure via auto-correlation length under coarse-graining.

name: coding-and-noncoding-driver-evidence-classification
description: Use when you have DriverPower result tables ([outDir]/[name].result.tsv) of coding and non-coding driver candidates and need to estimate FDR by cross-referencing candidates against CGC and PCAWG-consensus driver catalogs and literature evidence.

name: coefficient-table-interpretation
description: Use when you have per-donor flow cytometry cell proportion data plus donor metadata (age, sex) and need to determine which individual-level factor is most strongly associated with each immune cell population's composition.

name: cohesin-depletion-loop-loss-quantification
description: Use when validating a supervised chromatin loop caller on a perturbation system where loops are expected to disappear, such as a cohesin (RAD21-AID) auxin-depletion Hi-C experiment, to estimate the model's false discovery rate.

name: command-line-tool-parameterization
description: Use when an existing NGS workflow's default tool (e.g. Bowtie2/TopHat2 alignment in systemPipeR) is too slow or unsuitable and you need to swap in an alternative command-line aligner by editing its parameter files and re-running the affected step.

name: compartment-flip-annotation-genomic-bins
description: Use when a pairwise Hi-C comparison (e.g., ESC vs NPC at 100 kb bins) yields dcHiC significance calls and each significant bin must be labeled as A->B flip, B->A flip, or within-compartment change, with flip fractions and HOMER concordance tallied.

name: compartment-score-parameter-correlation
description: Use when a Hi-C dataset (real or simulated from known models) has been deconvolved by CscoreTool-M and each inferred sub-compartment must be assigned to, or validated against, a reference cell-type or model parameter set.

name: compartment-score-time-series-clustering
description: Use when you have compartment (PCA) scores for the same genomic bins across ≥3 ordered time points or developmental stages and want to cluster bins by trajectory shape rather than compare transitions one at a time.

name: composite-dyad-probability-plotting
description: Use when comparing nucleosome positioning around +1 dyads between two conditions (e.g., 0 min vs 60 min cadmium) for gene groups defined by RNA-seq response, using RoboCOP_MNase dyad probabilities.

name: computation-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantify how compute cost scales with Hi-C matrix resolution for a TAD-calling method, and demonstrate that chromosome-parallel execution reduces total runtime for a fixed cell line and parameter set.

name: computational-performance-reporting
description: Use when quantifying how much time a workflow management system itself adds on top of the real task runtimes, e.g. when validating that adopting a WMS does not inflate analysis wall time.

name: computational-resource-benchmarking-runtime-memory
description: Use when validating that a fast analytic estimator matches slower simulation-based alternatives and you must quantify the computational cost trade-off (wall-clock time and peak memory) alongside accuracy.

name: computational-resource-profiling
description: Use when comparing the speed, memory footprint, mapping efficiency, or accuracy of methylation read-alignment tools (e.g., Msuite vs. Bismark vs. BWA-meth) on a controlled read set.

name: conditional-aligner-dispatch-by-experiment-type
description: Use when building an automated ChIPseq/RNAseq mapping step where samples in a project must be routed to bwa, bowtie, or Tophat according to the experiment type recorded per sample.

name: confounder-adjusted-correlation-analysis
description: Use when inferring whether transcriptional regulators (TRs) are associated with drug response from pharmacogenomic data (expression, CNV, mutation, pharmacology profiles) plus ChIP-seq-derived target information, and naive mRNA-level correlation would be confounded by copy number or mutations.

name: confusion-matrix-model-evaluation
description: Use when a trained binary classifier (e.g. randomForest RFT for enhancer vs. non-enhancer elements) must be validated on held-out test classes and its accuracy quantified via a confusion matrix.

name: consecutive-enriched-window-merging
description: Use when peak-calling Calling Cards (CC) insertions from a qbed dataset and you need candidate TF binding regions formed by merging windows that are consecutively enriched in experimental over background insertions, as in the MACCs algorithm.

name: consensus-clustering-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking a novel clustering method against consensus clustering on the same gene expression matrix, or when you need to quantify cluster-solution agreement (e.g., Jaccard Pair Similarity per K) between two cluster assignments on shared samples.

name: consensus-clustering-epigenomic-subpopulations
description: Use when sparse single-cell histone-modification count matrices from multiple samples must be partitioned into reproducible epigenomic subpopulations with per-cluster differentially enriched regions and consensus-score stability checks.

name: consensus-focal-amplification-pooling
description: Use when calling focal amplifications at single-cell resolution from a normalized, binned scATAC-seq matrix to discriminate malignant from nonmalignant cells based on CNVs.

name: consensus-partition-stability-metrics
description: Use when you have per-k consensus partitioning results (individual partitions, consensus partition, sample-sample consensus matrix) and must choose the number of subgroups k using stability metrics.

name: consensus-partitioning-analysis
description: Use when a high-dimensional genomic data matrix (gene expression, methylation probes, or scRNA-Seq) must be classified into subgroups and no known labels exist, i.e. unsupervised consensus clustering with stability assessment is the goal.

name: consensus-partitioning-method-benchmarking
description: Use when you must decide which top-value and partitioning method combination produces the most stable consensus partitions, e.g. comparing ATC/skmeans versus hclust-based combinations over many expression datasets.

name: consensus-peak-computation-across-peaksets
description: Use when multiple peak files from related samples or technologies (e.g. CnT and CnR H3K27ac peak sets) need to be collapsed into a single consensus GRanges/BED peak set for QC or benchmarking.

name: conservation-distribution-boxplot-visualization
description: Use when a research question requires scoring genomic intervals for evolutionary conservation, e.g. ranking candidate regulatory regions by PhastCons average scores across annotated gene features.

name: constrained-genomic-interval-shuffling
description: Use when testing whether a contiguous set of genomic intervals (e.g., a TLD-clique of >4 TLDs) shows enriched inter-interval contacts, by building position-randomized null cliques on the same chromosome.

name: contact-map-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking DNA sequence models on 2D genome-organization prediction from long-range inputs (up to ~450 kb) and comparing them against an expert model with SCC on test splits of the Harvard Dataverse CMP deposit.

name: contact-map-visualization-file-generation
description: Use when a deduplicated PET alignment BAM (unique, MAPQ >= 30, nonredundant PETs) is available and the goal is to produce .hic and .cool 2D contact map files for Juicebox.js or HiGlass visualization.

name: contact-map-window-feature-extraction
description: Use when converting a binned contact map (e.g., 10 kb cooler with ICE 'weight' column) into per-interaction feature vectors for machine-learning loop detection or similar pixel-level prediction tasks.

name: context-length-scaling-analysis
description: Use when a long-range genomics task (e.g., contact map prediction with 100–200 bins) requires quantifying whether model performance improves monotonically as input context length grows, and whether it still trails the task-specific expert model.

name: contingency-table-probability-estimation
description: Use when a set of candidate motifs (or features) has already been ranked by a score such as mutual information and each candidate has a 2x2 contingency table of counts in a positive and a negative dataset that must be tested for over-representation with multiple-comparison control.

name: contingency-table-subtype-refinement-analysis
description: Use when you have an unsupervised cluster solution (e.g., SRIQ core/spiral labels) and an established molecular subtype scheme (TRU/PI/PP centroid calls) and need to quantify subtype-level enrichment or refinement per cluster.

name: control-interval-threshold-analysis
description: Use when patient gain/loss-of-methylation calls must be shown to be robust (or sensitive) to the choice of differential methylation decision threshold, e.g. comparing a ±3SD control interval against α = 0.01.

name: convex-optimization-interior-point-solving
description: Use when fitting a probabilistic mixture/sub-compartment model to Hi-C interaction data where the joint likelihood is non-convex but separates into convex blocks (per-compartment scores Ci on each chromosome, plus alpha/beta Rabl-effect parameters) amenable to block-coordinate.

name: cooler-contact-matrix-format-conversion
description: Use when a deduplicated ChIA-PET/HIChIP PET BAM (unique alignments, MAPQ ≥ 30, nonredundant PETs) must be turned into .hic and/or .cool files for visualization in Juicebox.js or HiGlass.

name: copy-number-alteration-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have paired copy-number alteration data (e.g. Firehose GISTIC2.0 lesion files) and matched gene expression data per tumor sample, and need to detect cis/trans genes associated with amplifications or deletions.

name: copy-number-alteration-driver-prioritization
description: Use when binary copy-number alteration events (e.g., GISTIC arm/focal SCNAs) are paired with matched gene expression data and the goal is to prioritize the cis driver gene most likely to mediate the alteration's trans effects.

name: copy-number-alteration-pathway-interpretation
description: Use when you have pruned iEDGE cis/trans signature gene lists per SCNA and need to identify recurrently enriched MSigDB pathways via hypergeometric testing.

name: copy-number-alteration-signature-testing
description: Use when you have per-sample SCNA alteration calls (e.g. GISTIC2.0 focal peaks) and matched gene expression data (e.g. RSEM log2) and need to identify cis genes within each peak and trans genes genome-wide whose expression shifts with the alteration.

name: copy-number-confounder-correction-in-expression-analysis
description: Use when testing whether samples carrying mutations in a candidate driver element show differential expression of a target gene, and you must correct for copy-number state and tissue-of-origin confounding.

name: copy-number-distribution-analysis
description: Use when a merged eccDNA catalog with per-entry copy-number records must be summarized as a distribution statistic (e.g., mean copy count) for a catalog table or figure aligned with Supplementary Tables S2–S5.

name: copy-number-variation-calling
description: Use when low-coverage WGS FASTQ/BAM files from tumor samples (e.g. SRA study SRP081035, CCLE BioProject PRJNA523380) must be screened for focal amplifications (copy number >5, size >100 kb) as candidate eccDNA regions prior to AmpliconArchitect reconstruction.

name: copy-number-vs-dependency-regression
description: Use when in silico validation of predicted cancer drivers requires linking somatic copy-number amplifications to gene essentiality from DepMap RNAi screens and CCLE copy-number data.

name: correlation-matrix-computation
description: Use when a preprocessed high-dimensional matrix (rows = features such as genes or CpG probes, columns = samples) needs per-row feature scores based on global correlation structure before consensus partitioning in cola.

name: correspondence-analysis-of-categorical-associations
description: Use when you have a two-way contingency table of categorical associations (e.g. TF binding site content per BHi-Cect bottom enclave) and want to summarize rows and columns as gradients on CA dimensions.

name: count-distribution-maximum-likelihood-fitting
description: Use when you need to justify or select an emission/count distribution (GP, ZIP, Poisson, NB) for binned sequencing read counts, e.g. before configuring an HMM peak-caller on 25 bp bin HDF counts.

name: count-matrix-cpm-normalization
description: Use when a raw barcode-by-bin fragment count matrix from scATAC data has already passed cell/bin filtering (e.g., minFrags=5000, zero-density bins removed) and must be converted to a comparable normalized read-depth matrix before CNV calling.

name: count-matrix-generation-from-genomic-intervals
description: Use when starting from gzipped single-cell BED files of sparse histone-modification or chromatin-accessibility data and a per-cell count matrix is needed as the entry point for QC filtering, PCA, UMAP and clustering.

name: count-matrix-normalization
description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQ files plus a (MergeID, ID, Path) config and expInfo-style condition table must be converted into normalized gene counts and DEG tables, especially for multi-factor or time-series designs.

name: count-matrix-read-count-normalization
description: Reference for converting a raw single-cell genomic bin/peak count matrix into a filtered, normalized matrix prior to PCA/clustering, when cell coverage varies and sparse outlier cells or regions must be removed.

name: coverage-based-hic-normalization
description: Use when Hi-C or capture Hi-C replicate contact maps must be bias-corrected before reproducibility assessment, or when comparing how normalization methods hold up as sequencing depth is downsampled to 15%-50%.

name: coverage-threshold-filtering-pchic
description: Use when normalizing pcHi-C promoter-other (P-O) interaction tables with covNorm's normCoverage, where promoter-anchored fragments need stricter coverage filtering (cov1_thresh=200) than the interacting 'other' fragments (cov2_thresh=50).

name: cpg-context-cytosine-conversion
description: Use when aligning reads from bisulfite-free methylation protocols (TAPS, 5hmC-CATCH, ATAC-me) where CpH methylation is very low, and full 3-letter C-to-T conversion would destroy strand-discriminating information.

name: cpg-density-bias-correction
description: Use when quantifying methylation from cfMeDIP-seq (MeDIP-seq) enrichment data — e.g. duplicate-filtered BAM files after alignment/QC — where CpG density bias must be corrected, and a choice among relative, absolute, or strand-aware methylation estimates is needed.

name: cpg-dinucleotide-coordinate-annotation
description: Use when direct-BSP or cloning-BSP trace files (.ab1) must have their cytosine/CpG positions converted to genomic coordinates from a reference .fasta template, as in ABSP individual sample methylation analysis.

name: cpg-distance-binned-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you need to characterize how correlation between adjacent DNA methylation p-values decays with genomic distance, e.g. to justify correlation-aware p-value combination in SMITE or reproduce its Figure 2 correlation analysis.

name: cpg-island-annotation-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when interpreting top-value-method-selected CpG probes from an Illumina 450K methylation matrix (e.g. cola SD vs ATC top probes) by CpG-island association category, to judge whether features capture local or global methylation patterns.

name: cpg-island-length-normalization
description: Use when preparing binned scATAC accessibility data for arm-level copy-number inference: binned matrix rows must be reduced to chromosome arms with length-aware weighting prior to pseudodiploid reference generation and clusterCNV Gaussian mixture fitting.

name: cpg-methylation-computation-from-trace-files
description: Use when input data are raw .ab1 chromatogram trace files from bisulfite sequencing PCR (direct-BSP or cloning-BSP) and the goal is to estimate and compare CpG methylation percentages of a studied DNA region without manual chromatogram inspection.

name: cpg-methylation-count-extraction
description: Use when starting from a Bismark-aligned MethylC-seq SAM/BAM file (with XM methylation strings and XG genome designations) and per-CpG methylation count tables (*.cov) are needed for DMR analysis or linkage analysis.

name: cpg-methylation-lollipop-plot-generation
description: Use when individual direct-BSP or cloning-BSP samples have already been analyzed in ABSP and you need per-replicate, per-CpG methylation-state visualizations comparing sample groups (e.g. high- vs low-methylated DNA).

name: cpg-methylation-percentage-calculation
description: Use when raw .ab1 Sanger trace files from direct-BSP (or cloning-BSP) experiments must be converted into per-CpG methylation percentages anchored to a reference .fasta sequence.

name: cpg-methylation-read-quality-filtering
description: Use when bisulfite-sequencing FASTA reads (e.g. DDO1/DAO amplicons from PRJEB28662) must be quality-filtered prior to epiallele-frequency or methylated-core extraction with ampliMethProfiler or MethCoresProfiler.

name: cpg-methylation-table-processing
description: Use when you have per-clone CpG methylation percentages from ABSP individual analyses of cloning-BSP samples and need grouped-level status annotations for comparison across sample groups.

name: cpg-oe-ratio-calculation
description: Use when you have FASTA sequences of candidate regulatory regions (e.g., HOT vs COLD) and need CpG O/E and GC-related features to test whether CpG/GC-rich sequence characteristics discriminate between region classes.

name: cpg-probe-feature-selection-sd-atc
description: Use when preprocessing an Illumina 450K methylation matrix for subgroup classification and deciding which top-value method (SD vs ATC) should drive CpG probe selection before consensus partitioning.

name: cpg-site-region-clustering
description: Use when Bismark alignment outputs (SAM/BAM or *.cov count tables) from one or more MethylC-seq samples must be aggregated from individual CpG sites into candidate regions prior to DMR testing with findDMRs.r or equivalent beta-binomial approaches.

name: crem-cluster-statistics-reproduction
description: Use when you have chromosome start/end coordinates of REMs (e.g. the 2,404,861 REMs from Zenodo record 3758494) and need to merge them into CREMs and recompute the paper's clustering statistics.

name: crispr-off-sgrna-activity-feature-ranking
description: Use when a trained CRISPRoff sgRNA-activity model (or comparable tree-based efficiency model) must be interpreted to identify which epigenetic features (nucleosome positioning, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, RNA expression) most favor editing efficiency.

name: crispr-screen-label-thresholding
description: Use when sgRNA screening datasets provide continuous phenotype scores or activity scores that must be converted to binary high-activity labels for classification model training or independent validation.

name: crisproff-crispra-model-attribution-averaging
description: Use when you have a trained sequence-based CNN for sgRNA activity (e.g., EpiCas-DL CRISPRoff/CRISPRa models) and need per-base, per-position feature attributions to explain sequence determinants of efficiency.

name: cross-aligner-coverage-comparison
description: Use when two alignment sets (e.g., a Msuite.final.bam and published reference BAMs) exist for the same murine ESC TAPS/WGBS samples and you need region-level (CpG island) read-coverage comparison rather than overall mapping-efficiency metrics.

name: cross-assay-chromatin-accessibility-comparison
description: Use when two or more open-chromatin peak files (BED-derived GRanges from ATAC-seq, DNase-seq, or similar) must be benchmarked against a gold-standard reference peak set to quantify assay-level differences in peak overlap.

name: cross-assay-chromatin-interaction-comparison
description: Use when you have FASTQ data from related 3D genome mapping assays (ChIA-PET, HiChIP, PLAC-seq) and need to check whether their interaction calls agree with each other and with Hi-C.

name: cross-assay-open-chromatin-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing peak files from different chromatin accessibility assays (e.g. ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq narrowPeak from ENCODE) to quantify assay-specific differences and benchmark against a ChIP-seq gold standard.

name: cross-assay-peak-overlap-tabulation
description: Use when two or more peak files from different epigenomic assays or technologies (narrowPeak/BED, e.g. ENCODE ATAC-seq and DNase-seq) must be compared at the chromatin-state annotation level, as in EpiCompare's ChromHMM functional-annotation report section.

name: cross-build-chain-file-application
description: Use when input peak files (e.g. BED files from CUT&Run, CUT&Tag or ChIP-sek studies) carry coordinates from mixed genome builds (hg19 vs hg38) and must be harmonized to one build before overlap/QC analysis.

name: cross-category-qc-distribution-aggregation
description: Use when benchmarking ChIP-seq/DNase-seq QC: you need cumulative distributions and cutoffs for read-layer metrics (FastQC score, uniquely mapped ratio, PBC) across many public samples, or to place a new sample against the historical quality atlas.

name: cross-cell-line-enhancer-prediction
description: Use when FASTA enhancer sequences with binary labels for specific human cell lines (e.g. NHLF, HEK293, HUVEC, K562, NHEK, HMEC) must be classified, or when models trained on one cell line must be evaluated on or transferred to other cell lines' test sets.

name: cross-cell-line-generalization-evaluation
description: Use when a trained promoter-prediction model on one human cell line must be evaluated on independent test sets of the other cell lines, and results compared to Z-curve and same-cell line baselines.

name: cross-cell-line-loop-transfer-evaluation
description: Use when a Hi-C loop-calling model trained on one cell line must be applied to Hi-C data from a different cell line, and transferability must be quantified via precision-recall curve comparison against the source-cell-line baseline.

name: cross-cell-line-model-generalization
description: Use when you have encoded SE/TE sequence datasets for multiple cell lines and need to evaluate whether a sequence-only classifier trained on some cell lines predicts super-enhancers in a novel, held-out cell line.

name: cross-cell-line-performance-comparison
description: Use when a DNA-sequence-only super-enhancer vs typical-enhancer classifier must be evaluated per cell line and compared against reported baseline methods on shared test benchmarks.

name: cross-dataset-method-comparison
description: Use when a choice among feature-selection (top-value) or partitioning methods for consensus clustering must be justified by large-scale empirical comparison across many datasets rather than a single example.

name: cross-dataset-peak-overlap-analysis
description: Use when multiple peak files from different epigenomic assays (e.g. CUT&Tag, CUT&Run, ChIP-seq BED/narrowPeak) must be benchmarked against a reference for QC, overlap statistics, and functional annotation.

name: cross-dataset-reference-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when cell type-specific genomic features (loops, peaks, enhancers) from one dataset must be validated against independent cell type-matched epigenomic or transcriptomic reference datasets.

name: cross-dataset-tf-binding-transfer-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating cross-platform transfer of a TF binding affinity model — train on HT-SELEX per-cycle enrichment data, test on uPBM affinities, and benchmark Pearson correlation against DeepBind, BEESEM, and BindSpace.

name: cross-dataset-validation-of-tr-identification
description: Use when a ranked TR list (e.g., BIT scores/ranks from TCGA cancer-type accessible regions) must be independently validated by asking whether top-ranked TRs are essential upon CRISPR/Cas9 knockout in the same cancer lineages (DepMap Chronos).

name: cross-entropy-weight-optimization
description: Use when two trained promoter classifiers (RF probability outputs and CNN/Keras outputs) must be fused via a weighted average whose weights are tuned by minimizing cross-entropy on a labeled weighted set.

name: cross-lane-reproducibility-assessment
description: Use when multiple sequencing lanes exist within the same sample group (e.g., stimulated or unstimulated STAT1 ChIP-Seq lanes) and you must quantify whether their genome-wide read distributions are consistent before downstream peak calling.

name: cross-method-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when a new cell type annotation method must be quantitatively compared to established baselines on shared scRNA-seq datasets, with accuracy expressed as consistent rates against curated reference cell types.

name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you have ranked TR lists from multiple TR-identification methods applied to the same query region sets (e.g., TR perturbation-derived DARs or cancer-type-specific accessible regions) and need to quantify inter-method agreement or rank-based accuracy.

name: cross-method-clustering-comparison
description: Use when a scATAC-seq (or scRNA-seq) dataset with reference cell-type labels is available and you must quantify how accurately competing clustering tools recover those labels, including under graded data corruption.

name: cross-method-compartment-score-comparison
description: Use when you have compartment-score tracks from dcHiC, HOMER, and/or CscoreTool over identical genomic bins of the same Hi-C map (e.g., mouse ESC at 100 kb) and need to quantify cross-method concordance and lamin-association agreement.

name: cross-method-loop-set-overlap-analysis
description: Use when comparing loop sets from a supervised predictor (Peakachu) with enrichment-based callers (HiCCUPS, Fit-Hi-C) on the same Hi-C matrix, to quantify overlap and orthogonal validation.

name: cross-method-network-comparison
description: Use when you need to validate a network inference tool against a baseline method on the same time-series dataset, comparing recovery of literature/ChIP-derived regulons against random regulator profiles.

name: cross-method-performance-comparison
description: Use when a Source Data supplementary table must be re-analyzed to verify reported average accuracies across competing celltyping methods, e.g. the 7-task FACS-sorted PBMC targets in Fig 3a.

name: cross-platform-chip-comparison
description: Use when two genome-wide protein-DNA binding assays (e.g., ChIP-Seq and ChIP-chip) must be compared on biological signal quality rather than peak overlap, using motif enrichment of the expected TF-binding motif as the figure of merit.

name: cross-protocol-abundance-ratio-analysis
description: Use when multiple shotgun libraries of the same synthetic or mixed microbial community (e.g. RIMS-seq +3H, DNA-seq, bisulfite-seq) have been mapped to the same reference and you need to check whether protocol choice distorts species relative abundances.

name: cross-sample-chip-signal-distribution-analysis
description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq signal across ≥2 conditions with spike-in chromatin (e.g. drug titration series), especially when total-read normalization would mask a global occupancy reduction, and peak/background classification (MACS2 broad-peak BEDs) is available.

name: cross-species-cell-type-assignment-from-motif-importance
description: Use when you have cell-type-annotated CRE BED intervals from two species sharing homologous cell types (e.g. seven adult heart cell types in human and mouse) and need to classify cell-type-specific regulatory sequences or assign single cells across species using motif-based models.

name: cross-species-chip-seq-peak-liftover
description: Use when orthologous non-coding regulatory elements (e.g., TF ChIP-seq peaks) must be lifted between species and naive chain-file liftOver suffers from multi-mapping, low precision, or low mapping rate.

name: cross-species-dna-6ma-dataset-handling
description: Use when raw labeled FASTA sequences (e.g., the cross-species DNA 6mA benchmark of 2,768 positive / 2,716 negative 41-nt samples) must be converted into fixed-length numeric k-mer frequency features for machine-learning classification.

name: cross-species-enhancer-classification-transfer
description: Use when you have cell-type-specific CRE models trained in one species (e.g., mouse cardiomyocyte/erythroid) and want to classify homologous CREs from another species, or to test whether predictions depend on sequence alignment.

name: cross-species-epigenomic-region-mapping
description: Use when mapping regulatory peaks (ChIP-seq, DNase-seq, ATAC-seq) across species and sequence-based liftOver alone yields multi-mappers or low precision, and matched orthologous epigenomic datasets are available for both species.

name: cross-species-hot-region-comparison
description: Use when DRIP-seq IP/control raw data (with RNaseH-treated or mock controls) are available for cell lines and C. elegans, and the goal is to test whether HOT regions are enriched for R-loops relative to occupancy-matched control regions.

name: cross-species-hot-region-count-validation
description: Use when narrowPeak ChIP-seq peak files for multiple genomes (hg19, mm9, dm3, ce10) must be converted into HOT region BED tracks and per-species counts checked against published HOT-region numbers.

name: cross-species-model-transfer
description: Use when a trained sequence-classification model must be evaluated for cross-species transfer, e.g. training DeepSE-integrative on human hg19 cell lines (H2171, MM1.S, U87) and testing on mouse mm9 cell lines (mESC, myotube, macrophage, pro-B, Th-cell), or vice versa.

name: cross-species-promoter-model-validation
description: Use when you must reproduce or extend iPro-WAEL's promoter-vs-enhancer discrimination benchmark: enhancer sequences as negatives, subsampled to match promoter counts, with model parameters kept unchanged.

name: cross-species-sequence-dataset-handling
description: Use when building a training/testing corpus from 6mA benchmark datasets spanning multiple species (M. musculus + rice), requiring CD-HIT-EST redundancy reduction at threshold 0.80 on 41-nt sequences.

name: cross-tissue-epigenome-comparison
description: Use when the goal is to detect tissue-specific genes or tissue-specific chromatin patterns by comparing compressed ChromHMM chromatin state sequences across two Roadmap epigenome samples at gene regions.

name: cross-tissue-indel-model-validation
description: Use when evaluating whether a tissue-specific regulatory indel classifier generalizes across GTEx tissues, i.e. when labeled cis-eQTL sindel sets for 44 tissues are available and generalization must be quantified.

name: cross-tool-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when two sequence-based variant-effect tools (e.g. DeepFun/Basset and DeepSEA) have scored the same SNP set across matched assays (CTCF, DNase-seq, H3K4me3, H3K9ac) and you need a quantitative agreement metric.

name: cross-tool-benchmark-count-comparison
description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking DMR-calling software with a same-sample replicate pair where no differential methylation should be detected, and you need comparable region counts across tools.

name: cross-tool-chromatin-loop-reproducibility-comparison
description: Use when comparing chromatin loop callers on identical ChIA-PET replicates — e.g. quantifying whether one pipeline's loop calls are more reproducible between replicates or recover another tool's calls.

name: cross-tool-concordance-comparison-homer-vs-dchic
description: Use when you need to validate a differential compartment caller by comparing its significant bin calls against an orthogonal tool (e.g. HOMER) on the same paired Hi-C conditions.

name: cross-tool-dmr-comparison-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking DMR-calling tools for false-positive rates (e.g., contrasting replicates of the same sample should produce zero DMRs) or reproducing the DMRfinder vs. DSS/bsseq comparison.

name: cross-tool-epigenomic-pipeline-execution
description: Use when scChIP-seq or scATAC-seq count matrices with known ground-truth labels are available and the goal is to reproduce or extend a multi-method benchmark comparing clustering performance via adjusted Rand index.

name: cross-tool-motif-prediction-alignment
description: Use when comparing motif discovery tools on datasets with known implanted motifs (length-6 IUPAC/degenerate or exact strings) at controlled frequencies, and a nucleotide-level recovery metric such as nCC is needed.

name: cross-tool-nucleosome-caller-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing nucleosome-calling tools on identical chromatin accessibility data — e.g., deciding whether RoboCOP run on ATAC-seq alone suffices versus NucleoATAC, or whether RoboCOP's MNase+ATAC profile outperforms DANPOS2 — by nucleosome-position AUPR on a shared validation set.

name: cross-tool-performance-comparison
description: Use when choosing a CC peak caller for large calling cards datasets, or when reproducing Fig. 2f-g style runtime/memory scaling benchmarks across tools on downsampled qbed data.

name: cross-tool-performance-comparison-analysis
description: Use when comparing the computational cost (wall time, peak memory) of alternative Hi-C compartment-calling tools on the same binned contact maps at multiple resolutions or down-sampling depths.

name: cross-tool-runtime-comparison
description: Use when a time-course regulon analysis must be made feasible on commodity hardware and you need measured per-regulon wall-clock times for Genexpi (OpenCL/GPU) versus TD-Aracne before choosing one.

name: cross-validated-auc-evaluation
description: Use when you have labeled genomic region sets (e.g. HOT vs COLD) with per-region sequence features such as 2-4-mer frequencies, GC content, and CpG O/E ratio, and need an honest accuracy estimate via cross-validated AUC plus feature-importance rankings.

name: cross-validated-roc-auc-evaluation
description: Use when a deep learning predictor (e.g., ncDeepBrain variant score) has been trained on labeled positives/negatives and you must quantify classification performance via cross-validated ROC curves and AUC.

name: cross-validation-performance-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a DNA 6mA (or similar sequence-classification) predictor against an existing tool under matched 5-fold cross-validation on benchmark datasets such as cross-species, rice, or M. musculus.

name: cross-wms-workflow-reimplementation
description: Use when benchmarking the scheduling overhead of a workflow management system (e.g. Watchdog vs. Snakemake) against the runtime of the tasks themselves, or when re-implementing a Watchdog workflow as Snakemake rules.

name: crup-enhancer-promoter-probability-extraction
description: Use when you need cell-type-specific enhancer/promoter activity probabilities and regulatory distances for candidate enhancer-target pairs from H3K27ac/H3K4me1/H3K4me3 ChIP-seq BAM files plus input controls.

name: csrna-seq-tss-sequence-scoring
description: Use when you have csRNA-seq TSS calls and need score-continuum sequences centered on each TSS for positional motif enrichment analysis (MEPP) of core promoter elements such as Inr, TATA-box, and DPE.

name: ct-ga-rich-region-sequence-selection
