description: Use when benchmarking DNA methylation aligners on reads from CT/GA-rich regions, or when stratifying human genome bins by CT/GA proportion (≥70%/≥80%) to compare 4-letter vs 3-letter mapping efficiency and accuracy.

name: ctcf-binding-site-variant-prioritization
description: Use when fine-mapping a locus to decide which of several non-coding SNPs overlapping CTCF binding sites is the likely causal variant driving altered chromatin architecture or gene expression.

name: ctcf-chipseq-peak-orientation
description: Use when you have BED-formatted genomic peaks or features lacking strand annotation and a second BED file of the same features with '+'/'-' strand labels, and you need every feature oriented before strand asymmetry analysis.

name: ctcf-dnase-peak-chromatin-class-annotation
description: Use when a BED file of regulatory elements (CTF/DNase peaks, promoters, enhancers) needs chromatin class labels before scoring deletion effects on predicted chromatin interactions with deepC.

name: ctcf-mediated-loop-calling
description: Use when you need to identify CTCF-mediated chromatin loops from Hi-C data — especially at reduced sequencing depth or when transferring a loop-calling model trained on one cell line (e.g., GM12878) to another (K562, HeLa-S3) — rather than threshold-based callers like SIP or Chromosight.

name: ctcf-motif-orientation-classification
description: Use when you have SnapHiC loop calls (*.postprocessed.summits.bedpe) with CTCF binding on both anchors and need to quantify convergent vs tandem vs divergent CTCF motif orientation.

name: ctga-rich-genomic-bin-mining
description: Use when you need to extract CT/GA-rich regions from a reference genome (e.g., hg19) as in silico read-restriction sets for a bisulfite-free 4-letter alignment benchmark, or to test promoter enrichment of such regions against genomic background.

name: cubic-spline-interpolation-of-random-effects
description: Use when fitted MethylCal/INLA calibration models and observed apparent methylation levels from bisulfite amplicon sequencing are available, and the PCR-corrected methylation degree must be recovered numerically rather than analytically.

name: cutandrun-cutandtag-peak-quality-control
description: Use when you have CUT&Run, CUT&Tag, or other novel epigenomic peak files (e.g. BED/GRanges H3K27ac or ATAC-seq peaks) and need to QC or benchmark them against a gold-standard such as ChIP-seq reference peaks.

name: cwl-step-parameter-binding
description: Use when constructing a systemPipeR CL workflow step and you need to connect targets-file columns (e.g. FileName1, FileName2, SampleName) to CWL/yml parameters to render exact command-line calls.

name: cycle-to-ecdna-coordinate-conversion
description: Use when AmpliconArchitect has produced reconstructed cycles from WGS focal amplifications and you need tabular eccDNA coordinate records for a database or BED/TSV catalog.

name: cytosine-deamination-context-quantification
description: Use when RIMS-seq or DNA-seq mpileup data must be classified by cytosine sequence context to test whether C-to-T deamination variants are enriched in a methylated motif (e.g. dcm CCWGG) in R1 rather than R2.

name: data-augmentation-performance-tabulation
description: Use when Hi-C replicate binPairs count matrices are available with FreeHi-C augmented versions and a spike-in ground truth, and the goal is to quantify how data augmentation affects differential chromatin interaction detection performance.

name: dbscan-anchor-clustering-loop-pooling
description: Use when you already have per-pixel loop probabilities (e.g. from `peakachu score_chromosome` or `score_genome`) and need to reduce them to discrete, non-redundant loop calls with anchor coordinates and probability/frequency columns.

name: de-novo-methylated-motif-discovery
description: Use when analyzing paired-end RIMS-seq FASTQ reads (adapter-ligation libraries) from bacteria without a known methylome, to de novo determine m5C methylated motifs while also assembling/sequencing the genome.

name: deconvolution-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when validating a methylation deconvolution method (e.g. DXM) on simulated mixtures with known subpopulation prevalences, where reference profiles are binarized to 0/1 and per-region accuracy can be computed.

name: deep-learning-ctc-sequence-decoding
description: Use when raw Oxford Nanopore FAST5 signal files must be base-called directly without an event-detection/segmentation preprocessing step, or when comparing end-to-end deep-learning base-callers.

name: deep-learning-enhancer-classification
description: Use when comparing a motif-count classifier against deep-learning baselines for cell-type-specific distal cis-regulatory element prediction, or when establishing whether a simple motif representation suffices for enhancer classification.

name: deep-learning-model-inference-cnn
description: Use when sgRNAs need activity predictions from a pretrained CRISPRoff/CRISPRa CNN, or when an independent screening dataset must be scored to reproduce validation metrics (ROC-AUC, Spearman correlation).

name: deep-learning-model-interpretation
description: Use when a trained deep learning model over biological sequences (e.g., one-hot encoded sgRNA matrices) needs feature-level interpretation, such as identifying which nucleotides at which positions contribute most to predicted sgRNA activity.

name: deep-learning-model-training-tuning
description: Use when training or re-tuning CITRUS on a TCGA-style SGA/GEP/TF-target pickle dataset and you need to select attention architecture and optimizer settings by grid search over prediction performance.

name: deep-learning-motif-tool-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when reproducing or extending motif-prediction benchmarks over ChIP-seq peak sets, especially when comparing a CNN-based tool's significance scores (E/P/q-values) against multiple existing motif finders.

name: deep-learning-training-log-management
description: Use when training a Keras/TensorFlow model (e.g., a two-layer CNN on dna2vec-encoded data) whose console output must be captured into a persistent log file for later review or provenance.

name: deep-neural-network-training-keras
description: Use when you must train a supervised deep neural network on annotated variant features (e.g. EIGEN/CADD/DANN/GWAVA/FATHMM scores, GNOMAD frequency, brain eQTL and enhancer/promoter flags) to output a 0–1 prioritization score for non-coding variants.

name: deep-neural-network-variant-classification
description: Use when building or reproducing a supervised classifier for non-coding variant prioritization in mental-disorder genomes, where labeled disease vs. non-disease variant sets exist and AUC/ROC benchmarking against comparators (e.g., logistic regression ncLGBrain) is required.

name: degenerate-motif-enumeration
description: Use when you need to discover over-represented degenerate DNA motifs exhaustively — e.g. from ChIP-seq peak sequences or position-specific sequencing-error motifs — without restricting the motif space to a predefined consensus or PWM family.

name: delila-book-regeneration-from-filtered-sequences
description: Use when running the Delila-PY pipeline's second cycle and you have per-sequence information content values in bits that must be filtered with the ri program's ≤0-bit cutoff before regenerating the delila book.

name: delila-pipeline-cycle-orchestration
description: Use when you have a GenBank file and a tab-delimited file of genomic positions (e.g., ChIP-seq peaks or transcription start sites) and need to reconstruct a DNA binding motif as a sequence logo and position weight matrix.

name: delila-sequence-book-extraction
description: Use when a Delila-PY run must go from a raw NCBI GenBank file plus a four-column tab-delimited sites file (chromosome, name, strand, base-pair position) to the delila-generated book of sequences, or when validating that book before motif cycling.

name: density-clustering-of-loop-candidates
description: Use when a per-cell scHi-C loop-calling step has produced many candidate bin pairs and you need to consolidate them into non-redundant loop calls (summits) before downstream annotation.

name: depmap-chronos-essentiality-classification
description: Use when you have a ranked list of candidate TRs (e.g., BIT scores from TCGA-derived accessible regions) and need to quantify what fraction are functionally essential using DepMap CRISPR knockout viability data.

name: deseq2-size-factor-normalization
description: Use when a GenoGAMDataSet of per-position ChIP-Seq counts (BAM-derived, chunkSize 50000) has just been built from multiple samples/conditions and must be depth-normalized before calling genogam().

name: desktop-hardware-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing or updating the execution time and memory footprint of a command-line bioinformatics tool (here DiNAMO) on the article's evaluation datasets, and when comparing its tractability against alternatives like MEME-CHIP, HOMER or Discrover.

name: determination-coefficient-evaluation
description: Use when assessing how well a regression model reproduces experimental TF–DNA binding affinities (uPBM, gcPBM, HT-SELEX k-mer data) and you need a comparable average R2 benchmark against the DNAffinity paper.

name: deviance-information-criterion-model-selection
description: Decision support for choosing among MethylCal's four model specifications (equations 2–5) per assay when calibrating apparent methylation levels from standard controls at known percentages (e.g. 0/25/50/75/100% or 0–100% at 12.5% steps).

name: dgw-clustering-output-analysis
description: Use when you have DGW clustering outputs (config, warping paths, cluster BED files) plus gene-annotation POI coordinates and need to verify that warping improves alignment of TSS/first splicing sites.

name: dhs-blacklist-region-overlap-annotation
description: Decision support for evaluating whether called ChIP-seq/DNase-seq peaks fall in biologically credible regulatory space (DHS) versus artifact-prone blacklist regions during QC.

name: differential-accessibility-analysis
description: Use when comparing chromatin accessibility between a TR-perturbed condition (e.g., Runx1 cKO) and wild-type controls with replicate BAM and narrowPeak files, to produce a DAR BED set as downstream query input.

name: differential-alignment-significance-testing
description: Use when two Roadmap-style chromatin state annotated epigenomes must be compared gene-by-gene to identify cell-type-specific genes from chromatin state sequence patterns alone (no expression data).

name: differential-call-recall-assessment-across-depths
description: Use when you need to test whether pairwise differential compartment calls remain stable at reduced sequencing depth, e.g., before committing to lower-depth runs or justifying shallow replicate removal.

name: differential-compartment-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing compartmentalization across ≥2 bulk Hi-C maps (with replicates, e.g. ESC vs NPC at 100 kb) and you need per-bin significance calls for compartment changes, including within-A/within-B differences without compartment flips.

name: differential-enrichment-analysis-scchipsq
description: Use when scChIP-seq count matrices have been clustered into epigenomic subpopulations (e.g. via ConsensusClusterPlus in ChromSCape) and you need per-cluster differentially enriched regions and biological interpretation.

name: differential-enrichment-region-testing-cluster-vs-rest
description: Use when a filtered, normalized single-cell epigenomic count matrix (H3K27me3 scChIP-seq or scATAC-seq) has per-cell cluster labels and you must find regions enriched or depleted per cluster versus all other cells, then interpret them via gene set enrichment.

name: differential-expression-gene-list-processing
description: Use when RNA-seq gene expression data must be converted into a differentially expressed gene set and tested for significant overlap with differential histone modification calls (e.g. H3K27me3 or H3K9me3).

name: differential-expression-log2foldchange-scoring
description: Use when raw sequencing counts from paired control/condition anchored genomic regions must be converted to a continuous biological activity score for a score-based motif enrichment analysis such as MEPP.

name: differential-expression-threshold-estimation
description: Use when overlap counts between differential expression genes and differential accessibility peaks (or SNP/gene statistics) are available and an objective, bootstrap-justified logFC or P-value cutoff is needed instead of an arbitrary threshold.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when RNA-seq differential expression results must be integrated with ChIP-seq peak-to-promoter annotations to identify loci where two regulators both bind and co-regulate the same genes.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files and sample metadata need end-to-end processing (QC, STAR/BBMap alignment, featureCounts quantification, RUVSeq normalization) followed by DEG testing, or when a two-factor CIPHER expInfo schema must be extended to multi-condition or time-series contrasts.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have paired copy-number/epi-DNA alteration calls (e.g. GISTIC2.0 focal SCNAs) and matched RSEM log2 expression for the same tumor samples, and need cis (in-peak) and trans (genome-wide) DE genes per alteration.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when cluster assignments from an unsupervised expression clustering solution (e.g., SRIQ, 6 clusters at diameter 0.63) exist and per-cluster up-/down-regulated gene lists and GO terms are needed.

name: differential-gene-expression-stratification
description: Use when RNA-seq expression changes across an environmental perturbation (e.g., 0 min vs 60 min cadmium in yeast, GSE153609) must be binned into ranked gene groups to subset downstream chromatin analyses such as +1 nucleosome dyad composites.

name: differential-methylation-classification
description: Use when PCR-bias-corrected (MethylCal or Moskalev's CPR) methylation levels for case/control pyrosequencing or bisulfite amplicon data must be called as gain/loss of methylation against a healthy-control ±3SD interval, e.g. BWS KCNQ1OT1 and H19/IGF2 calls.

name: differential-methylation-region-testing
description: Use when Bismark-aligned MethylC-seq (bisulfite) data in SAM/BAM format needs post-alignment processing to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) between two or more sample groups, e.g., IMR90 vs H1.

name: differential-peak-motif-verification
description: Use when two condition-specific differentially bound peak sets (e.g. female vs male GBM CC peaks) exist and the goal is to identify which TF motif families are enriched in one condition but not the other, reproducing published family-level enrichment patterns.

name: differentially-accessible-site-subsetting
description: Use when comparing motif activity between raw and imputed scATAC-seq matrices: the differentially accessible sites (e.g. 4100 peaks) must define the peak set for chromVAR on both matrices.

name: dimensionality-reduction-feature-space-comparison
description: Use when you need to evaluate whether one single-cell epigenomic clustering method (e.g. ChromSCape on scChIP-seq H3K27me3 data) performs as well or better than alternatives on data with known ground-truth cell labels.

name: dimensionality-reduction-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how the CPU runtime of dimensionality reduction for single-cell epigenomic data scales with cell number, or when comparing scalability/reproducibility of SnapATAC vs LSA vs cisTopic on cell-by-bin matrices.

name: dimensionality-reduction-umap-visualization
description: Use when analyzing gzipped single-cell BED files from sparse single-cell histone-modification assays (e.g. H3K27me3 scCUT&Tag K562/H1, H3K4me3 scChIC-seq) and you need a 2D embedding to assess whether known cell populations or expected clusters separate.

name: directionality-penalty-specification
description: Use when integrating expression with promoter/body methylation or histone-mark p-values in SMITE and you have prior knowledge of the expected direction of each modification–expression relationship, so opposite-direction evidence should be penalized rather than treated as concordant.

name: dirichlet-hyperparameter-configuration
description: Use when a cisTopic object holds a binary accessibility matrix (e.g. ~97k regulatory regions over 5,335 PBMCs) and multiple LDA models across a topic-number grid must be fitted for downstream model selection.

name: discriminative-positive-negative-dataset-construction
description: Use when preparing inputs for discriminative motif discovery with DiNAMO: you have genomic coordinates or event positions (e.g., 3272 monocyte SSE coordinates on Hg18) and must build signal.fa and a matched control.fa pair.

name: distance-based-phylogenetic-tree-inference
description: Use when you have decontaminated epiallele (or analogous binary/continuous feature) profiles per tumour region and need a phylogenetic tree linking sample evolutionary relationships.

name: distance-dependent-background-removal
description: Use when a preprocessed 40 kb-resolution cis-interaction Hi-C or capture Hi-C contact map still shows distance-decay-dominated ligation frequencies after coverage-bias removal and you need background-corrected contact frequencies.

name: distance-dependent-noise-sampling-per-secondary-diagonal
description: Use when stress-testing TLD/TAD prediction robustness on sparse (single-cell-like) Hi-C matrices: noise must respect distance-dependent decay, so each secondary diagonal is sampled independently rather than uniformly across the whole matrix.

name: distance-normalization-oe-matrix-computation
description: Use when a KR-normalized intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact map must be converted to an O/E matrix before tiling into 64x64 kb patches for dual-branch (image + graph) loop-calling model training or prediction.

name: distance-stratified-contact-decile-binning
description: Use when converting raw KR-normalized Hi-C contact matrices (e.g. Rao et al. GSE63525 at 5 kb bins) into categorical skeleton annotations to train or run predictions with deepC.

name: distance-stratified-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a sequence-derived chromatin contact prediction (e.g. from deepC) needs quantitative validation against observed Hi-C on held-out chromosomes, requiring distance-stratified Pearson correlations for raw and smoothed maps.

name: distance-weighted-genomic-scoring
description: Use when a SMITE PvalueAnnotation has been built from methylation/expression/ChIP-seq p-values and you must decide whether to weight interval contributions by distance from the TSS, or must verify that weighted and unweighted aggregated scores agree.

name: distributed-cluster-throughput-measurement
description: Use when benchmarking a Spark/HDFS-based distributed aligner's scalability: you need per-cluster-size throughput for two algorithmic variants (e.g. --testmode plain vs balancing) on the same dataset.

name: distributed-short-read-alignment
description: Use when aligning bisulfite-treated sequencing reads (e.g., WGBS FASTQ from simulated Sherman data or GEO accessions) is computationally bottlenecked on a single node and a scale-out Spark/HDFS cluster is available.

name: dmr-caller-concordance-benchmarking
description: Use when you have simulated or known-composition heterogeneous bisulfite sequencing mixtures plus methylation calls from the sorted underlying cell types, and need to quantify how many independently called DMRs a deconvolution method recovers as i-DMRs.

name: dmr-statistical-calling-from-bisulfite-methylation-counts
description: Use when comparing DXM i-DMRs from heterogeneous bisulfite data against an independently called DMR set between sorted reference cell types, or when a DMR caller with explicit count-based statistics is needed on sorted methylation counts.

name: dmr-threshold-filtering
description: Use when beta-binomial-tested clustered regions from MethylC-seq data must be filtered into a final DMR table using CpG-count, methylation-difference, and p/q-value cutoffs.

name: dna-binding-motif-information-content-alignment
description: Use when you have a GenBank genome and a set of genomic positions (e.g., ChIP-chip/ChIP-seq peak centers or transcription start sites) and need to discover or reproduce a DNA binding motif as a sequence logo and PWM.

name: dna-binding-motif-sequence-curation
description: Use when running Delila-PY's second cycle and per-sequence information content (bits) values are available, and poorly matching sequences (≤0 bits) must be removed before regenerating the book with delila.

name: dna-contact-map-prediction-inference
description: Use when evaluating whether DNA foundation models capture long-range genomic dependencies via 3D contact map prediction, e.g., reproducing the Figure 2 case-study comparison of HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, and Akita on chr6/chr3 HFF regions.

name: dna-electrostatic-direct-readout-encoding
description: Use when building DNAffinity feature matrices from DNA sequences and the direct-readout electrostatic block must be derived per tetramer, or when validating the encoding against the AACT worked example.

name: dna-foundation-model-finetuning
description: Use when evaluating how a pretrained DNA foundation model captures long-range genomic dependencies (up to 1,000,000 bp) on a supervised regression or classification task with train/valid/test splits, and you need reproducible per-model benchmark scores.

name: dna-kmer-sequence-embedding
description: Use when raw enhancer DNA sequences (FASTA) must be converted into fixed feature vectors/matrices before feeding a CNN classifier such as DeepSE, and pre-trained k-mer embeddings exist for the genome.

name: dna-mechanical-property-feature-classification
description: Use when random-forest models have been trained on multiple experimental binding datasets (gcPBM, uPBM, HT-SELEX) and you need to compare which DNA-property feature classes drive predictive power in each run.

name: dna-methylation-call-from-bisulfite-free-reads
description: Use when analyzing reads generated by bisulfite-free methylation assays such as TAPS or 5hmC-CATCH, where non-CpG methylation is low and the default 3-letter BS alignment wastes read complexity.

name: dna-methylation-call-parsing
description: Use when methylation calls from a bisulfite (BS) or bisulfite-free (TAPS) library have been produced by Msuite and you need per-CpG methylation densities, or mode-to-mode (4-letter vs 3-letter) call agreement statistics.

name: dna-methylation-pcr-bias-calibration
description: Use when pyrosequenced or MiSeq-amplified methylation levels in a targeted CGI/DMR need PCR-bias correction, and standard controls with known methylation percentages (AMPs) are available alongside case and control samples.

name: dna-methylation-read-alignment-benchmarking
description: Decision support for choosing a methylation read aligner, or when reproducing/comparing alignment speed, memory, mapping efficiency, and accuracy across 3-letter and 4-letter methylation protocols.

name: dna-motif-generalization
description: Use when you need to enumerate all degenerate IUPAC motifs of length L whose exact instances all occur in a positive DNA dataset, or to reimplement/validate lattice-based motif generalization from counted L-mers.

name: dna-motif-overrepresentation-analysis
description: Use when searching a large signal (e.g. ChIP-seq peak) FASTA against a control FASTA for over-represented degenerate IUPAC motifs of a fixed length, without any prior restriction on the motif.

name: dna-physical-property-feature-preparation
description: Use when training or validating DNAffinity regressors on in vitro binding data (gcPBM, uPBM, HT-SELEX) and you must assemble the per-protein input files and 6-mer feature inputs correctly.

name: dna-sequence-binary-encoding
description: Use when raw 41-nt DNA sequences (A/C/G/T FASTA records) must be converted into fixed-length binary features before classifier training, e.g. reproducing csDMA's Binary feature block alongside Motif and Kmer subsets.

name: dna-sequence-multitask-regression
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking multi-task DNA regression on DNALONGBENCH RSAP (TensorFlow-record train/valid/test splits) and per-sample PCC on human vs mouse tracks is the target metric.

name: dna-shape-contribution-analysis
description: Use when quantifying how much each DNA shape feature (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) contributes to predicting TF-DNA binding specificity across many ChIP-seq datasets, or when comparing shape-feature AUCs against sequence-only baselines.

name: dna-shape-feature-generation
description: Use when you need to compute HelT/MGW/ProT/Roll shape features for ChIP-seq peak regions (2*peak_flank+1 bp, e.g. peak_flank 50 = 101 bp) and evaluate their predictive power for TF-DNA binding versus a gc-matched background.

name: dna-shape-feature-input-handling
description: Use when training or evaluating DESSO CNN models on ChIP-seq peaks with --feature_format DNAShape, or when reconstructing the shape-kernel CNN that uses 24x1 kernels per shape channel instead of 24x4 sequence kernels.

name: dna-shape-motif-discovery
description: Use when ChIP-seq peak regions and precomputed DNA shape feature matrices (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) are available and the goal is to discover shape-based regulatory motifs and TFBSs with DESSO.

name: dna-tetramer-sliding-window-composition-counting
description: Use when raw DNA sequences from uPBM, HT-SELEX or gcPBM must be converted into fixed-length tetramer-count feature vectors to feed DNAffinity's random forest regressor.

name: dna2vec-kmer-sequence-embedding
description: Use when raw DNA sequences of enhancer regions (FASTA format) must be converted into fixed numeric feature vectors for a downstream classifier, and no ChIP-seq or experimental signal data is available.

name: dnase-fragment-size-anticorrelation-analysis
description: Use when a compiled ChIP-seq/DNase-seq QC metrics table (FRiP, PBC, fragment size, mapping rate, peak number) needs category-wise correlation analysis to validate quality-atlas expectations or benchmark a new pipeline against the ChiLin reference results.

name: dnase-hypersensitive-site-overlap-validation
description: Use when predicted enhancer coordinates (e.g. from CIPHER's --function predictEnhancers on H3K4me1/H3K4me3/H3K27ac ChIP-seq plus DNase-seq) need an orthogonal validation against DNase hypersensitive sites.

name: dnase1-signal-standardization
description: Use when computing or reproducing EpiRegio Cell type scores from GeneQuery REST API output, where per-cell-type DNase1 signals of REMs must be log-transformed and z-scored per REM before weighting by regression coefficients.

name: dominance-based-graph-pruning
description: Use when a candidate motif set forms a partial-order lattice (e.g. IUPAC generalizations of observed L-mers) and redundant/generalized motifs must be eliminated using an objective function computed from 2x2 contingency tables over positive/negative datasets.

name: downsampling-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when comparing how robustly normalization methods preserve inter-replicate contact map reproducibility as sequencing depth is reduced, or when needing reduction-rate curves of a reproducibility metric across sampling ratios.

name: driver-call-set-differential-comparison-across-test-schemes
description: Use when you need to quantify how adding functional impact scores (CADD, DANN, EIGEN, LINSIGHT) changes DriverPower driver calls for a tumour cohort, or to report burden-only precision against a CGC-gene truth set.

name: driver-candidate-literature-curation
description: Use when a driver-discovery result table contains candidates absent from CGC and PCAWG-consensus catalogs and you need to triage them via literature/orthogonal evidence and compute an empirical FDR.

name: dropout-batchnorm-regularization-configuration
description: Use when constructing or re-training the EpiCas-DL CNN (150 multi-size convolutional filters, MaxPooling, three 80/60/40 dense layers) and you need its batch-normalization + dropout(0.4) regularization block.

name: drosophila-core-promoter-motif-analysis
description: Use when you have scored DNA sequences centered on an anchor point (e.g. csRNA-seq TSSs) and need to determine whether motif presence correlates with biological activity at specific positions relative to that anchor, such as core promoter element positioning.

name: drug-response-biomarker-identification
description: Use when you need to identify transcriptional regulators independently associated with pharmacological drug response from cell line pharmacogenomic data (expression, CNV, mutation) plus ChIP-seq target information, as with CCLE/ENCODE and PLX4720.

name: drug-response-tr-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing methods for identifying drug response-related TRs on synthetic pharmacogenomic data (gene expression + drug response + ChIP-seq targets), especially under injected noise or spurious-correlation confounders.

name: drug-sensitivity-group-comparison
description: Use when a drug-sensitivity table (e.g. CCLE pharmacological profiles) can be split into mutation-defined groups — such as BRAF+H3K27me3/PRC2 double mutants versus BRAF-only — and the goal is a two-sample test of response difference.

name: dss-wald-test-workflow
description: Use when MethylC-seq methylation counts have already been clustered into genomic regions (combined.csv) and you need to test regions for differential methylation between two or more sample groups.

name: dtw-alignment-of-epigenomic-peak-shapes
description: Use when ChIP-seq enrichment measurements within peak regions (e.g. MACS2-called peaks) must be aligned and clustered by shape similarity in a completely unsupervised way, without transcription start sites or gene annotation.

name: dtw-prototype-shape-averaging
description: Use when clustering multiple epigenomic marks (e.g. ChIP-Seq H3K4me3/H3K9ac coverage vectors per 50 bp bin) by shape and you need a warping-invariant pairwise distance plus per-cluster prototype sequences.

name: dtw-warped-profile-visualization
description: Use when epigenomic ChIP-Seq peak regions (e.g. ENCODE H3K4me3/H3K9ac K562) have already been DGW-aligned and clustered and you need to visually inspect DTW-warped heat-maps, cluster prototypes, and validate alignment against TSS/FSS points of interest.

name: dual-mean-threshold-imputation-filtering
description: Use when you have a SCALE-imputed scATAC-seq peak-by-barcode matrix and need a close-to-binary accessibility matrix; scATAC-seq open-chromatin data is inherently close-to-binary and binarization removes replicate-specific imputation artifacts.

name: dual-orientation-motif-scoring
description: Use when scanning centered, scored DNA sequences (e.g. FASTA with score headers) for transcription factor motif occurrences where motif strand is unknown, and positional enrichment profiles must reflect matches on either orientation.

name: duplicate-read-removal
description: Use when a mapped-read BAM from a NEAT ChIPseq/RNAseq pipeline step must be deduplicated according to user-defined duplicate-management settings in AdvancedSettings.txt.

name: dynamic-programming-alignment-scoring
description: Use when two or more genomic regions must be compared by their single-track chromatin state sequences (e.g. ChromHMM output) rather than raw multi-track signal matrices, and ordered state patterns—not just state frequencies—must drive the similarity score.

name: dynamic-time-warping-peak-alignment
description: Use when epigenomic enrichment peaks (e.g. ChIP-Seq H3K4me3/H3K9ac coverage in 50 bp bins) must be aligned by shape and clustered despite variable lengths, strand orientation, or local rescaling of genomic features like TSSs and FSSs.

name: eccdna-catalog-aggregation
description: Use when reproducing eccDNAdb summary statistics or summarizing a merged eccDNA catalog into a stats table (counts, size distribution, segment counts, copy numbers) with exact reference values.

name: eccdna-gene-annotation-mapping
description: Use when a catalog of eccDNA genomic coordinates (BED-style intervals) must be mapped to overlapping genes from a reference annotation (e.g., GENCODE GRCh37) to build an eccDNA gene table with Re/Rg overlap fractions.

name: eccdna-region-signal-aggregation
description: Use when you need to test whether chromatin is highly accessible at an eccDNA-containing region by extracting per-base ATAC-seq signal from BigWig tracks over a fixed coordinate interval and aggregating per-sample coverage.

name: ecdna-candidate-region-filtering
description: Use when low-coverage WGS of tumor samples has been aligned (e.g., BWA to hg19) and focal amplification candidates must be narrowed before AmpliconArchitect eccDNA reconstruction.

name: eclip-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when candidate eCLIP binding sites must be evaluated against orthogonally ascertained true binding sites (e.g., chrM for FASTKD2, splice sites for PRPF8, GURUG motif for TARDBP) to compare peak callers.

name: eclip-enriched-window-feature-quantification
description: Use when Skipper has produced reproducible_enriched_windows tables for two or more eCLIP conditions (e.g., wild-type vs missense-mutant RBP constructs) and the goal is to compare the fraction of binding sites per transcript region or per annotated locus class such as tRNA.

name: eclip-peak-calling-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing the number of enriched CLIP-seq/eCLIP binding sites called by a new caller against established methods (Piranha, CLIPper) on shared ENCODE eCLIP datasets.

name: eclip-repeat-read-aggregation
description: Use when eCLIP/eCLIP-seq IP and matched input samples must be tested for significant binding to annotated repetitive elements (e.g., GU-rich simple repeats, LINE1) rather than annotated transcripts.

name: eclip-significant-window-filtering
description: Use when you have per-window IP and input read-start counts from tiled CLIP/eCLIP windows plus matched input replicates, and need genome-wide enrichment p-values to call reproducible RBP binding windows.

name: effective-length-fold-change-computation
description: Use when you have paired bias-corrected and uncorrected Cufflinks/eXpress output per transcript and need to quantify how much fragment bias correction shifted effective lengths, or to test if GC content predicts the bias signal.

name: eigenvector-principal-component-analysis
description: Use when you need compartment scores (A/B calls) from one or more Hi-C contact maps, especially at high resolution (up to 5-10 kb) or across multiple maps/replicates needing comparable scores.

name: elastic-net-classification
description: Use when a labeled set of genomic intervals (e.g. HOT vs COLD regions) must be classified from sequence-derived features such as k-mer frequencies, GC content, and CpG observed/expected ratio, with feature importance ranking.

name: em-baum-welch-hmm-parameter-estimation
description: Use when fitting a bivariate Hidden Markov Model to binned ChIP-seq read counts (e.g. histoneHMM on 1000 bp bins of broad marks like H3K9me3/H3K27me3) to classify bins as modified or differentially modified.

name: embedding-clustering-annotation
description: Use when you already have low-dimensional node embeddings (e.g., 16-dim GAE output per 400x400 Hi-C submatrix) and need density-based, parameter-light unsupervised clustering to label every bin.

name: empirical-cdf-comparison
description: Use when you have per-SNP saliency (or other continuous variant) scores for a candidate SNP set plus a matched background set and need to test whether the two distributions differ, as in fine-mapping GTEx v7 eQTLs.

name: empirical-cdf-feature-scoring
description: Use when a high-dimensional genomic matrix (e.g., gene expression or CpG methylation) needs feature scoring before partitioning and variance-based top-value methods (SD, MAD, CV) are insufficient because the global correlation structure matters.

name: empirical-density-estimation
description: Use when tumour RRBS samples contain normal tissue contamination and per-locus epiallele distributions are available for tumour regions and matched normal tissue, so that purity can be estimated from the empirical density of xi.

name: empirical-null-hypothesis-testing-by-random-bisection
description: Use when you need an empirical P-value for a clustering-agreement metric (VI) between a hierarchical partition and benchmark annotations, and a parametric null is unavailable.

name: empirical-permutation-pvalue-calculation
description: Use when testing whether a strand asymmetry ratio (e.g. same vs opposite orientation of consecutive motif pairs) is statistically significant and a closed-form binomial test needs empirical confirmation via strand-label permutations.

name: empirical-pvalue-computation
description: Use when novelty/outlier scores (reconstruction or model-based) must be turned into calibrated per-window P-values and FDR-controlled non-B DNA calls on ONT translocation-time windows.

name: ena-accession-based-data-retrieval
description: Use when a pipeline needs raw ChIP-seq FASTQ files (paired IP and matching control) for a defined list of ENA accessions — e.g., the 25 knocked-out transcription factor experiments listed in Supplementary Table S1 of the HOT-or-not study.

name: encode-enhancer-region-annotation
description: Use when ChIP-seq (H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K27ac) and DNase-seq RPM-normalized bedGraph signals are available and genomic regions must be classified as enhancers versus promoters, e.g. enhancer discovery in a human cell line.

name: encode-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw fastq files from RNA:DNA pulldown high-throughput experiments (ChIRP-seq, ChOP-seq, CHART-seq, RAP-seq) must be uniformly peak-called and replicate-harmonised to build a binding-site benchmark.

name: endothelial-mesenchymal-transition-gene-set-analysis
description: Use when a set of differentially expressed genes (e.g. during EndoMT) must be linked to regulatory elements and screened for enriched TF binding motifs in a cell type-specific manner.

name: enhancer-disconnection-analysis
description: Use when an hg19 structural variant (deletion, inversion, translocation or duplication) lies outside a gene's coding sequence and a long-range, enhancer-driven pathomechanism is suspected for a congenital phenotype (limb, craniofacial, cardiac, neurodevelopmental, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system.

name: enhancer-disconnection-gof-lof-gene-scoring
description: Use when a structural variant has been mapped to a cell-type-specific rearranged enhancer-gene domain and per-gene direction of enhancer activity change (loss vs gain) must be assigned from control vs patient H3K27ac bigWig signals.

name: enhancer-enrichment-background-comparison
description: Use when a set of predicted open-chromatin regions or candidate CREs needs functional benchmarking against an external enhancer catalog with per-region assay outcomes, and you must report an enrichment rate versus a defined background rate.

name: enhancer-probability-prediction
description: Use when you have cell-type-specific BAM files for H3K27ac, H3K4me1 and H3K4me3 (plus matched input control) and RNA-seq TPM values, and need CT-specific features (EP/PP probabilities, regulatory distances, TPM) for ET pairs.

name: enhancer-promoter-anchor-fraction-computation
description: Use when you have a TAD boundary file and ChIP-seq narrowPeak or enhancer/promoter interval files and need per-factor fractions of boundaries anchored by regulatory signals.

name: enhancer-promoter-chromatin-loop-linking
description: Use when assigning target genes to enhancer-resident noncoding GWAS SNPs (e.g. neuropsychiatric SNPs in prefrontal cortex) using cell type-specific chromatin loops such as SnapHiC summit BEDPE files from scHi-C/snm3C-seq data.

name: enhancer-promoter-expression-linking
description: Use when scHi-C-derived loop calls (e.g., SnapHiC *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe per cell type) must be connected to promoter-linked genes and tested whether anchors and linked genes show highest activity/expression in the matched cell type.

name: enhancer-promoter-loop-annotation
description: Use when RNAPII ChIA-PET (or HiChIP/PLAC-seq) loops have already been called with PET count >= 3 and peak support, and each loop must be labeled E-P, P-P, or neither using enhancer/promoter BED annotations.

name: enhancer-sequence-classification
description: Use when labeled enhancer FASTA sequences (e.g. 'data/train/${cell_line}.fasta' with '${cell_line}_y_train.txt' labels) must be classified per cell line, or generic/enhancer-promoter benchmarks must be reproduced.

name: enhancer-target-gene-prediction
description: Use when benchmarking whether DNA foundation models capture enhancer-gene regulatory interactions over very long sequences, or when reproducing the DNALONGBENCH ETGP AUROC/AUPRC table.

name: enhancer-target-generic-feature-computation
description: Use when building training/prediction features for enhancer-target pairs from BENGI-style ET pair lists and you need cell-type-independent statistics (Wilcoxon rank-sum P-values, Fisher combination, CRUP correlation) to complement CT-specific ChIP-seq/RNA-seq features.

name: enhancer-target-interaction-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a new or existing enhancer-target prediction method must be compared against TargetFinder and Random Forest baselines on BENGI ground-truth datasets with cross-validated AUPRC/F1 metrics.

name: enhancer-target-pair-classification
description: Use when you need to predict which candidate cCRE-ELS enhancers within 500 KB of a target gene's TSS actively interact with that gene in a specific cell type, given ChIP-seq (H3K27ac, H3K4me1, H3K4me3) and RNA-seq data for that cell type.

name: enrichment-based-absolute-methylation-estimation
description: Use when estimating methylation levels from cfMeDIP/(cf)MeDIP-seq enrichment data where CpG density bias must be corrected, and a choice among linear, sigmoidal, or strand-aware normalization models is needed.

name: enrichment-odds-ratio-visualization
description: Use when a set of labeled regulatory variants (true cis-eQTL indels vs model-predicted scores) must be tested for enrichment/depletion in interval annotations (promoter-centered chromatin interactions, open chromatin, histone marks) across multiple tissues, with odds-ratio comparison tables and.

name: ensemble-model-inference-evaluation
description: Use when labeled DNA promoter/enhancer sequences must be classified by a pre-trained ensemble without retuning, e.g. cross-cell-line prediction or promoter-vs-enhancer discrimination on balanced datasets.

name: ensemble-output-aggregation-across-model-runs
description: Use when CITRUS has been trained multiple times (--run_count 1..10) and a single-run 'hid_tmr' TF activity matrix is too unstable for downstream clustering or TF–tumor-type association testing.

name: ensemble-weight-optimization-slsqp
description: Use when fusing probabilistic outputs of two heterogeneous base classifiers (e.g., RF on encoded features and CNN on word2vec features) into a single weighted-average ensemble and the optimal weights must be learned rather than hand-tuned.

name: entanglement-index-computation
description: Use when bisulfite-sequencing epiallele data has been reduced to significant methylated cores and you must quantify per-CpG coupling (entanglement/stability index E) and core clonality in each population.

name: entropy-based-anchor-cell-selection
description: Use when running two-round Cellcano prediction (target cell number > 1,000 or default two-round mode) and you need confident target cells to serve as training anchors for the KD model.

name: epiallele-entropy-quantification
description: Use when you have per-locus epiallele proportions from multi-region tumour RRBS data and need a scalar measure of epigenetic heterogeneity (disorder) to compare tumour regions against matched normal tissue.

name: epiallele-family-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when comparing bisulfite amplicon-seq epihaplotype data across two or more conditions to test whether specific families of phased mCpG combinations (methylated cores) expand clonally or remain stochastic between time points or populations.

name: epiallele-hierarchical-clustering-heatmap
description: Use when you have epialleles annotated by MethCores_Combinator (Module 2) from bisulfite-sequenced single-molecule CpG configurations and need to visualize, cluster, and significance-test epiallele families across samples or cell populations.

name: epiallele-methylation-state-extraction
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon sequencing reads (FASTQ, e.g. from ENA PRJEB28662) must be converted into phased single-molecule CpG methylation states and stable mCpG combinations (cores) traced in complex DNA populations.

name: epiallele-profile-distance-computation
description: Use when multi-region tumour RRBS data have been processed into decontaminated epiallele profiles t_hat_s per sample and you need a sample-by-sample distance matrix or a tumour phylogenetic tree.

name: epigenetic-feature-ablation-analysis
description: Use when you need to test whether integrating all epigenetic features with sgRNA sequence improves CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa efficiency prediction versus sequence-only or sequence-plus-one-epigenetic-feature models.

name: epigenetic-feature-matrix-encoding
description: Use when preparing sgRNA training/prediction inputs for a CNN that must combine target-site sequence with cell-type epigenetic signals (nucleosome, accessibility, methylation, expression) around CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa target sites.

name: epigenetic-feature-minmax-normalization
description: Use when building model inputs from sgRNA genomic coordinates and you need chromosome-position-based epigenetic annotations (ATACdb accessibility, FANTOM TSS distances, WGBS methylation, GEO RNA-seq expression) scaled to a common range.

name: epigenome-transcriptome-module-visualization
description: Use when SMITE modules have already been identified (runSpinglass/runBioNet) from scored gene networks and you need to assign pathway meaning and render interpretable subnetwork figures for reporting.

name: epigenomic-annotation-data-processing
description: Use when multi-track epigenomic signals have been reduced to chromatin state annotations and you need compressed state sequences to compute horizontal alignment scores, or to distinguish real epigenomes from randomized negative controls.

name: epigenomic-cluster-exploration
description: Use when DGW clustering outputs ({prefix}_config.dgw, {prefix}_dataset.pd, {prefix}_linkage.npy, {prefix}_prototypes.pickle, {prefix}_warping_paths.pickle) exist and you need to visually inspect, validate and export shape-based clusters of epigenomic peaks.

name: epigenomic-dataset-summary-statistics-validation
description: Use when a task asks to rebuild or validate a regulatory-element database from chromatin accessibility plus matched expression data, and database-level counts (total REMs, associated genes, mean REM length) must be reproduced.

name: epigenomic-feature-annotation
description: Use when you have BED-like interval data (methylation, histone marks) plus a gene annotation and need to map each interval to promoter/body/other-TSS categories before combining p-values into gene scores.

name: epigenomic-feature-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when BHi-Cect enclave loci must be intersected with epigenomic tracks (DNase, LAD, ChromHMM, CAGE, RNA-seq, TF, RNAP2, CTCF/RAD21/CHD1) to test whether activity varies with nestedness along the BPT.

name: epigenomic-peak-binarization
description: Use when downloaded ENCODE/Roadmap narrow-peak BED calls must be converted into fixed-length (1000 bp), non-redundant candidate 'peak' regions that serve as binary training targets for a Basset/DeepFun CNN.

name: epigenomic-peak-file-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing peak files from different epigenomic technologies (ATAC-seq, DNase-seq, ChIP-seq, CUT&Run, CUT&Tag) against a gold-standard reference to quantify overlap, precision, recall, and annotation differences.

name: epigenomic-peak-file-granges-handling
description: Use when peak files from epigenomic assays (narrowPeak/BED, e.g., ENCODE ENCFF044JNJ K562 DNase-seq) need to be loaded into R and standardized as GRanges with consistent genome build and blacklist filtering prior to overlap or ChromHMM annotation analysis.

name: epigenomic-peak-granges-manipulation
description: Use when peak files originate from different genome reference builds (e.g. hg19 and hg38 mixed inputs) or raw BED formats, and they must be imported as GRanges, coordinate-lifted, and standardized before EpiCompare quality-control and benchmarking.

name: epigenomic-peak-quality-control
description: Use when you need to compare or QC epigenomic peak files (narrowPeak/BED GRanges) across technologies such as ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq, or CUT&Tag/CUT&Run vs a ChIP-seq gold-standard reference.

name: epigenomic-peak-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking peak-shape clustering/alignment methods against a known ground truth: you have seed epigenomic peaks (e.g. ENCODE H3K4me3 K562) and need a controlled (v, p) noise grid with verifiable cluster labels.

name: epigenomic-query-search-horizontal-alignment
description: Use when you have ChromHMM chromatin state sequences for a single Roadmap epigenome and want to find recurrent local chromatin state patterns or -matching genomic regions for a query region.

name: epigenomic-sequence-conservation-scoring
description: Use when mapping non-coding regulatory regions (e.g. ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, DNase-seq peaks) across species and sequence-based liftOver alone suffers from multi-mapping, low precision, or low mapping rate.

name: epigenomic-signal-quantification-at-loop-anchors
description: Use when you have cell type-specific chromatin loops (e.g. SnapHiC *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe) plus matched ATAC-seq, H3K27ac and RNA-seq reference data and need to validate loop anchors and linked genes against matched cell type signatures.

name: epigenomic-significance-scoring
description: Use when a genomic interval has multiple non-independent p-values (e.g. correlated methylation or H3K4me1 probes within one gene) that must be combined into a single valid gene-level significance score.

name: epigenomic-similarity-based-candidate-filtering
description: Use when UCSC liftOver or adaptive_liftover has produced many candidate orthologous target regions per query interval and you need to prioritize them by functional regulatory similarity rather than sequence conservation alone.

name: epihaplotype-methylation-call-extraction
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon-seq paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. ENA PRJEB28662) must be converted into binary epihaplotype tables of phased per-molecule mCpG calls as input for epiallele or methylated-core analysis.

name: eqtl-binary-classification-finetuning
description: Use when evaluating whether DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) can match a task-specific expert model on binary classification of long-range eQTL sequences across multiple cell types.

name: eqtl-dataset-assembly
description: Use when building labeled positive/negative SNP training sets for a non-coding variant prioritization model, sourcing from deltaSVM dsQTLs, HGMD regulatory SNPs, brain eQTLs, or GRASP/DeepSEA-associated SNPs with matched negatives.

name: eqtl-saliency-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have per-SNP deepC variant-impact/saliency score tracks and want to test whether a candidate SNP set (e.g. cell-type-specific eQTLs) is enriched for high saliency against a re-sampled, region-matched background via a two-sample KS test.

name: euler-ode-integration
description: Use when fitting ODE-based gene regulation models with sigmoidal activation and per-gene mRNA decay to smoothed time-course expression data, and a fast, OpenCL-friendly numerical integrator is needed.

name: example-dataset-qc-reporting
description: Use when short-read sequencing data supplied as FASTQ files needs quality assessment — e.g., per-cycle quality scores, read-quality distributions, and QC summaries across many samples rendered in one combined multi-panel report figure.

name: exponential-fit-scaling-analysis
description: Use when analyzing how the spatial auto-correlation of a binned ChIP-seq signal changes under coarse-graining, e.g. diagnosing whether broad-domain enrichment grows with scale as in H3K27me3 data.

name: expressed-gene-count-thresholding
description: Use when 2D single-cell UMI/read count matrices plus cell annotations (donor and cell type) must be converted to pseudobulk and the number of expressed genes per sample counted at specific per-cell thresholds, e.g. to validate expression probability models.

name: expression-matrix-dimension-validation
description: Use when a mean-centered GEO expression matrix has been produced (e.g., by COnTORT's gffMatch step) and you must confirm the transformation did not alter rows/columns or annotation columns before downstream analysis.

name: expression-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw numeric expression or methylation matrix (e.g., from golubEsets, ALL, HSMMSingleCell) must be cleaned before cola's feature selection and consensus partitioning.

name: expression-prior-validation-scrnaseq
description: Use when a fitted expression prior (gamma.linear.fit.new, disp.fun.general.new, read.umi.fit.new) has just been estimated from pilot scRNA-seq UMI matrices and must be checked before use in experimental design or power calculations.

name: expression-probability-estimation-from-gamma-mixed-fits
description: Use when designing or powering an interindividual scRNA-seq DE/eQTL study and you need the probability that a gene passes expression detection thresholds (e.g. min.counts=3, perc.indiv=0.5) at given cells-per-sample and read depth.

name: expression-probability-model-validation
description: Use when a planned or pilot scRNA-seq design needs its predicted expressed-gene numbers checked against real data, e.g. subsampled UMI count matrices with per-cell-type annotations available.

name: expression-probability-prediction
description: Use when designing or validating single cell RNA-seq experiments and you need per-gene detection probabilities at a given read depth, cells per individual, and sample size, or when checking that model-predicted expressed gene counts match observed counts in a held-out dataset.

name: extra-trees-classifier-training
description: Use when training a DNA 6mA site predictor from labeled 41nt sequence benchmarks (e.g. cross-species, rice, M. musculus) and you must select among RandomForest, GradientBoosting, AdaBoost, ExtraTrees, and SVM classifiers via 5-fold cross-validation.

name: f-test-feature-selection
description: Use when a reference scATAC-seq gene score matrix with known cell type labels must be reduced to informative, cell-type-specific genes before training a supervised celltyping model.

name: f1-score-model-comparison
description: Use when comparing a novelty detection model (e.g. GoFAE-DND) against other anomaly detectors and supervised classifiers using F1 scores across imbalanced class ratios of simulated data.

name: false-discovery-rate-control
description: Use when comparing differential chromatin interaction detection performance (precision, power, empirical FDR) between original Hi-C replicate pairs and FreeHi-C-augmented replicates called at the same nominal FDR level.

name: false-discovery-rate-correction
description: Use when the goal is to call significant chromatin contacts from covNorm distance-normalized interaction data, i.e. a p-value and FDR are needed for each pairwise contact after removal of distance-dependent background.

name: false-discovery-rate-estimation
description: Use when a driver-discovery candidate list (e.g. DriverPower .result.tsv calls) needs an empirical FDR: intersect calls against known catalogs (CGC, PCAWG-consensus), isolate method-exclusive candidates, and compute the unsupported fraction per category.

name: false-positive-annotation-against-chromatin-structure
description: Use when you have genome-wide in vitro TF binding predictions and a set of experimental in vivo peaks, and need to quantify TP rate, filter corroborated false positives, and test whether remaining FPs sit in nucleosome-occupied regions.

name: false-positive-rate-estimation-at-alpha
description: Use when simulating or reanalyzing two genomic range sets x and y with no true association, to check whether a null-generation method (block bootstrap vs shuffling) controls FPR near alpha.

name: fast5-electrolytic-current-decoding
description: Use when starting from Oxford Nanopore raw FAST5 electrolytic-current signal files and you need to decode them into per-read nucleotide sequences (FASTQ) rather than working from pre-base-called reads.

name: fasta-reference-coordinate-computation
description: Use when direct-BSP or cloning-BSP reads (.ab1 trace files) must be mapped onto a .fasta reference template so each read cytosine receives a genomic coordinate and per-CpG methylation levels can be tallied.

name: fasta-reference-sequence-alignment-for-cpg-mapping
description: Use when analyzing direct-BSP or cloning-BSP data from raw Sanger .ab1 trace files that must be trimmed, matched to a .fasta reference sequence, and converted into per-CpG methylation percentages for one or more sample groups.

name: fasta-sequence-parsing
description: Use when the input is a FASTA file of DNA enhancer sequences (training or independent test set) that must be parsed per-record before feature extraction with dna2vec or motif PWM scanning.

name: fastq-adapter-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw cfMeDIP-seq (or MeDIP-seq) FASTQ files enter a pipeline and need adapter/quality trimming plus QC, especially when the library may or may not carry UMI or spike-in sequences configured via a YAML file.

name: fastq-dataset-generation
description: Use when controlled synthetic FASTQ inputs are needed to benchmark bisulfite aligners under known error rates, and ground-truth read counts and lengths must be exactly reproducible.

name: fastq-header-sequence-extraction
description: Use when you need to run or reproduce a minimal Watchdog workflow that extracts read headers and sequence subsets from compressed FASTQ files, or when benchmarking Watchdog's resource footprint on a small test dataset.

name: fastq-paired-end-read-processing
description: Use when raw paired-end ChIA-PET FASTQ files (e.g. bridge-linker protocol data such as GSE72816/GSM970213) must be stripped of the 5' bridge linker before read alignment.

name: fastq-quality-control
description: Use when raw FASTQ files (e.g. truncated H3K4me3 ChIPseq or RNAseq reads from mouse embryonic stem cells) need pre-alignment quality assessment with per-cycle quality, base composition, k-mer and read-length reports.

name: fastq-quality-metrics-computation
description: Use when short-read sequencing data are supplied as FASTQ files and per-cycle/per-read quality summaries must be computed and visually inspected, especially across many files in one report.

name: fastq-read-alignment-quality-assessment
description: Use when starting from raw ChIP-seq or DNase-seq FASTQ (treatment and control) and you need aligned BAMs plus early QC metrics (read quality, GC content, library complexity PBC, fragment size) before peak calling.

name: fastq-read-output-generation
description: Use when the input is raw nanopore FAST5 signal reads and the goal is base-calling each read into a nucleotide sequence collected in a single FASTQ file, without prior signal segmentation.

name: fastqc-read-quality-reporting
description: Use when raw cfMeDIP-seq FASTQ files (single-end or paired-end, with or without UMI/spike-in sequences) need adapter and low-quality base trimming plus per-sample QC reports, and UMI-containing libraries must be filtered before trimming.

name: fastqc-sequence-quality-evaluation
description: Use when raw FASTQ files from ChIP-seq or DNase-seq experiments need sequence-quality screening, and when new samples must be compared against cumulative historical quality distributions (FastQC score >25, uniquely mapped ratio >0.5, PBC >0.8).

name: fdr-based-loop-strength-ranking
description: Use when SnapHiC loop calls in *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe files must be counted or ranked with fdr_dist as the loop-strength measure — e.g. the 10–742-cell mES subsampling loop-count benchmark or symmetric reproducibility between split 371-cell replicate halves.

name: fdr-corrected-multiple-testing-in-hic
description: Use when calling significant differential compartments across two or more Hi-C contact maps and thousands of genomic bins must be tested, so per-bin chi-square p-values need multiple-testing correction at a target FDR (e.g. FDR10).

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many parallel hypothesis tests are performed (e.g., limma DE tests across 69 SCNAs or hypergeometric enrichment of gene sets) and per-test p-values must be adjusted to FDR before calling significant genes or pathways.

name: fdr-thresholded-loop-count-reproducibility-checking
description: Use when a ChIA-PET loop-calling result (MICC FDR-filtered interactions) must be reproduced against a published interaction count and validated by anchor ChIP-seq co-occupancy.

name: feature-matrix-assembly-for-classification
description: Use when raw 41-nt DNA 6mA candidate sequences (positive/negative FASTA sets) must be converted into a numeric feature matrix to train or test a machine-learning classifier.

name: feature-trend-filtering
description: Use when a normalized feature-by-donor abundance matrix (peaks/genes vs. adult donors aged 22–93) must be scanned for features whose abundance changes systematically with donor age, separating true longitudinal trends from random fluctuation.

name: fiedler-vector-allele-partitioning
description: Use when assembling diploid haplotypes (SIH) from WGS, Hi-C, 10X linked-reads, PacBio SMRT or ONT fragment files plus a bgzipped, tabix-indexed VCF, and you want a fast spectral alternative to MEC/max-cut optimization.

name: file-pattern-path-enumeration
description: Use when a Watchdog XML task must be replicated over a folder or file pattern, so one subtask instance is created per matching path with placeholders substituted.

name: fimo-motif-scanning
description: Use when you have FASTA sequences for two sets of genomic anchors (e.g., loop endpoints from a bedpe) and need strand-resolved motif occurrences to classify pairwise motif orientation.

name: fimo-motif-scanning
description: Use when you have CRE coordinate BED files (chromosome, start, stop, condition) and need motif occurrence annotations from known position weight matrices to build motif-count features for a classifier.

name: finetuned-foundation-model-inference
description: Use when evaluating whether pre-trained DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus variants) capture long-range genomic dependencies on tasks like contact map prediction, eQTL, enhancer-target gene, or regulatory sequence activity prediction.

name: fisher-combined-probability-calculation
description: Use when building enhancer-target interaction features from multi-cell-type activity data and you need a dataset-independent score contrasting gene expression between enhancer-active and enhancer-inactive cell types.

name: fisher-combined-pvalue-across-bandwidths
description: Use when temporal genomic/epigenomic series (e.g., PBMC ATAC-seq/RNA-seq features across donor ages 22–93) must be scanned for abrupt age-related change points rather than gradual trends, and per-age significance must be robust to window-size choice.

name: fisher-exact-contingency-testing
description: Use when you need to test enrichment of one genomic gene/region set (e.g. histoneHMM differential modification calls) against another (e.g. DESeq-derived DE genes) with a 2x2 contingency table and exact test P-value.

name: fisher-exact-driver-enrichment-testing
description: Use when validating a CITRUS attention-weight output (attn_wt) by asking if highly attended genes are enriched for known cancer drivers (e.g., IntOGen), or when quantifying overlap/enrichment of two gene/TF sets via Fisher's exact test.

name: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing
description: Use when validating that a ranked list of predicted cis driver genes (e.g., Rank-1 mediators from iEDGE mediation output) is significantly enriched for known driver genes from curated compendia such as COSMIC CGC, UniProt, OMIM, or TUSON.

name: fisher-exact-overrepresentation-testing
description: Use when you have a ranked list of TR gene symbols from BIT (e.g., mm10_RUNX1_rank_table.csv) and need to test whether the top-ranked TRs are enriched for GO biological processes relevant to the perturbed or analyzed biological context.

name: fisher-exact-test-differential-binding
description: Use when you have cell-by-peak AnnData matrices from CC qbed insertions in two sample groups and need condition-biased binding sites plus peak–gene concordance P-values.

name: fisher-exact-test-motif-significance
description: Use when you have DiNAMO MI-ranked IUPAC motif candidates with per-motif contingency tables (presence/absence counts in signal and control FASTA datasets) and need significance-filtered over-represented motifs.

name: fisher-exact-test-overrepresentation-interpretation
description: Use when a candidate motif set (e.g., DiNAMO IUPAC lattice nodes) must be statistically filtered for over-representation in a positive (signal.fa) versus negative (control.fa) dataset with multiple-testing correction.

name: fishers-exact-proportion-testing
description: Use when two discrete cell samples have been clustered (e.g. k=5 ChromSCape clusters) and you need a significance test that the proportion of cells falling in a target cluster differs between the samples.

name: fit-hic-baseline-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating a Hi-C/HiChIP normalization-and-significance method against an established baseline (Fit-Hi-C) on replicate data, using reproducible-contact overlap and ROC AUC (~0.85 expected) as acceptance criteria.

name: fit-hic-distance-dependent-background-modeling
description: Use when calling significant chromatin interactions from a Hi-C matrix with an enrichment-based method to benchmark against Peakachu/HiCCUPS, or when a distance-dependent background null is needed for interaction significance.

name: five-fold-cross-validation-model-training
description: Use when labeled noncoding sindels from cis-eQTL analyses across 44 GTEx tissues are available as positive/negative indel position files and a model's tissue-specific prediction performance (AUROC/AUPRC) must be estimated via 5-fold cross-validation under different feature sets.

name: five-fold-iterative-cross-validation
description: Use when training/evaluating a cell-specific enhancer predictor on the Enhancer-IF benchmark (eight human cell lines, per-cell-line train FASTA plus independent test FASTA) and you need cross-validated training with head-to-head comparison on five metrics.

name: flow-cytometry-cell-population-analysis
description: Use when per-donor flow-cytometry population proportion data are paired with donor age and sex metadata and the goal is to test which cell-type proportions change with age and differ between men and women (e.g., around an age-65 cutoff).

name: flow-cytometry-prevalence-comparison
description: Use when methylation-based deconvolution prevalence estimates (e.g. from DXM) must be experimentally validated against independently sorted cell populations such as FACS-derived CD4+ T and CD19+ B cell fractions.

name: focal-loss-deep-learning-model-training
description: Use when training a deep learning enhancer predictor on imbalanced FASTA-encoded DNA sequence data (e.g., the eight cell lines in the Enhancer-IF benchmark with 'data/train/${cell_line}.fasta' and '${cell_line}_y_train.txt' labels), or when reproducing Enhancer-MDLF vs Enhancer-IF comparisons.

name: focal-loss-implementation
description: Use when training GILoop (or a similar dual-branch GCN + U-Net loop caller) on Hi-C cis-contact maps where loop pixels are vastly outnumbered by non-loop pixels, so plain cross-entropy over-weights easy negatives.

name: footnoted-qualifier-annotation
description: Decision support for comparing workflow management systems across setup, workflow design, workflow execution, and integration categories when the source figure attaches footnotes to individual feature cells.

name: forward-reverse-strand-methylation-parsing
description: Use when analyzing direct-BSP .ab1 Sanger trace files to quantify CpG methylation at a specific region, and per-site methylation percentages must be derived from dye-signal peak heights at forward (C/T) or reverse (G/A) positions.

name: four-letter-versus-three-letter-mapping-benchmarking
description: Use when a TAPS or 5hmC-CATCH dataset is available and a decision is needed between Msuite's 4-letter mode (faster, exploits higher nucleotide complexity) and the conventional 3-letter mode used by Bismark/BWA-meth.

name: fowlkes-mallows-cluster-similarity-scoring
description: Use when comparing two partitions of the same genomic bins (e.g., predicted TAD calls vs. ground-truth TADs from simulated Hi-C datasets such as the Wang et al. IMR-90 noise series) to produce a similarity score per method per noise level.

name: fragment-bias-correction
description: Use when estimating transcript expression from RNA-Seq alignments (SAM/BAM) whose library preparation (NSR priming, WT SOLiD, strand-specific protocols, single- or paired-end) induces non-uniform fragment distribution and quantification bias.

name: fragment-end-linear-down-weighting
description: Use when reconstructing coverage profiles from directionally extended short ChIP-Seq reads and fragment sizes are only known within a size-selection range (e.g. 175-225 bp), so HDF ends are uncertain.

name: fragment-extraction-from-aligned-reads
description: Use when sorted BAMs aligned with BWA-MEM (short reads) or minimap2 (long reads) and a bgzipped, indexed variant VCF are ready, and platform-specific fragment files must be produced as input to haplotype phasing tools.

name: fragment-file-parsing
description: Use when you have a fragment file (from 10X/Hi-C linked reads, paired-end NGS, PacBio SMRT or ONT data) plus a VCF of heterozygous variants and need to build SpecHap's linkage graph for spectral-based haplotype assembly.

name: fragment-midpoint-signal-aggregation
description: Use when paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq fragment alignments (BAM) must be classified by insert size and converted into single-nucleotide-resolution midpoint count tracks (bedGraph) to feed RoboCOP's HMM.

name: fragment-size-filtering-chipseq
description: Use when mapped BAM alignments from a NEAT ChIPseq or RNAseq pipeline need fragment-size bounds and duplicate-read handling applied before peakcalling, per parameters set in AdvancedSettings.txt.

name: fragment-size-ratio-computation
description: Use when processing paired-end cfMeDIP-seq BAMs within MEDIPIPE's alignment/QC module and you need insert-size distributions and fragmentation-ratio QC tables from duplicate-removed alignments.

name: fragment-size-read-shifting
description: Use when calling broad ChIP-seq domains (e.g. H3K27me3/H3K9me3) with RECOGNICER from BED-format mapped reads and you must set or sensitivity-test the fragment-size shift and window-size parameters.

name: frip-peak-count-association-analysis
description: Use when you have per-sample ChIP-seq/DNase-seq QC metrics (FRiP, peak number, fragment size, PBC) and need to test whether metric associations hold within literature-based assay categories rather than globally.

name: frip-score-calculation-on-subsampled-bams
description: Use when QC of ChIP-seq replicates requires FRiP scores: MACS2 narrow/broad peaks are available and read enrichment in peaks must be quantified on equally subsampled BAMs.

name: frip-score-computation
description: Use when you need a quality/robustness metric for broad-domain ChIP-seq calls — e.g. verifying that total aggregate domain length and FRIP remain invariant under sequencing-depth downsampling (17.23M → 4M reads) of H3K27me3 data.

name: frip-score-thresholding
description: Use when a ChIP-seq or DNase-seq sample needs a per-sample enrichment QC score, or when deciding whether a 1% FRiP threshold is an appropriate pass/fail criterion for ChIP versus input control samples.

name: functional-enrichment-analysis-go-terms
description: Use when you have a deduplicated list of gene IDs linked to a transcription factor's binding regions (e.g. from EpiRegio Region Query of ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks) and want to identify enriched GO terms or KEGG pathways explaining the TF's function.

name: functional-impact-score-adjustment-of-driver-calls
description: Use when you already have DriverPower burden-test-only calls and per-element functional impact scores (e.g. averaged per-mutation CADD PHRED per binID) and want to re-rank/infer drivers with functional adjustment to boost precision.

name: functional-variant-annotation-annovar
description: Use when non-coding SNVs must be converted from VCF/BED coordinates into a per-variant functional feature matrix to train or apply a brain-disorder variant prioritization score like ncDeepBrain.

name: g-quadruplex-genomic-window-annotation
description: Use when nanopore (FAST5/Albacore/Tombo) data for NA12878 must be annotated with G4 motif windows and per-window translocation signals, or when called G4 novelties need Quadron weak/strong stability labels.

name: g-quadruplex-signature-modeling
description: Use when benchmarking non-B DNA detection from ONT translocation times and experimentally-derived G4/STR windows are unavailable or insufficient — synthetic TT datasets with known labels and controlled non-B-to-B ratios (0.05/0.1/0.25) are needed.

name: g4-seq-mismatch-score-interpretation
description: Use when you have G4 novelty loci called by one or more novelty detection methods over NA12878 nanopore windows and need to characterize whether each called G4 is weakly or strongly stable via Quadron G4 stability scores.

name: gae-architecture-hyperparameter-sweep
description: Use when training a GAE on Hi-C contact matrices and you must choose network depth, hidden_dim, and output embedding dimension by comparing downstream TAD-calling quality (FMS/RI) across variants.

name: gam-variance-computation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing algorithms for computing standard errors or position-wise variances of fitted generalized additive models (GAMs), especially tiled genome-wide GenoGAM fits where scalability in parameters per tile matters.

name: gamma-mixture-distribution-fitting
description: Use when building expression probability priors from scRNA-seq count matrices for scPower power analysis, i.e. when per-gene negative-binomial means must be summarized into a fitted distribution of expression means per read depth.

name: gamma-mixture-expression-prior-application
description: Use when you have a UMI count matrix with cell-type annotations and need to predict (or validate) the number of detectable genes per cell type as a function of cells per cell type and transcriptome-mapped read depth.

name: gapped-kmer-svm-sequence-model-training
description: Use when you have fine-mapped, reproducible enriched CLIP windows from Skipper and need sequence-driven models to predict how SNVs change transcription/translation factor binding at occupied sites.

name: gata1-motif-enrichment-visualization
description: Use when you need to test whether a transcription factor motif (e.g. GATA1) is enriched at specific positions relative to an anchor point such as ChIP-seq peak summits, using score-continuum-ranked sequences.

name: gata1-tal1-motif-spacing-analysis
description: Use when testing whether cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility associates with the spacing of a co-occurring TF motif (e.g. SCL/bHLH) relative to an anchor motif (e.g. GATA1) in scored centered sequences.

name: gaussian-copula-bivariate-emission-construction
description: Use when comparing two ChIP-seq samples of broad histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3/H3K9me3) and you need the bivariate emission density behind histoneHMM's three-state differential classifications from binned bivariate read counts.

name: gaussian-mixture-clustering-cnv
description: Use when binned scATAC-seq accessibility data must be decomposed into per-cell copy-number states using Gaussian mixture modeling, e.g. with Copy-scAT's clusterCNV/Mclust after collapseChrom3N arm-level summarization.

name: gaussian-mixture-prior-initialization
description: Use when implementing or reproducing SCALE's VAE+GMM architecture on scATAC-seq data (e.g. Forebrain.h5ad peak-by-barcode matrix) and a tight posterior estimate over latent features is needed for clustering.

name: gbm-model-prediction-genomic-elements
description: Use when you have a pre-trained DriverPower GBM BMR model and need to predict background mutation rates for new test elements (e.g., TCGA WES data sharing no samples with the PCAWG training set).

name: gc-bias-correction-of-accessibility-peaks
description: Use when computing chromVAR motif deviation scores from scATAC-seq peak counts: getBackgroundPeaks and computeDeviations require a 'bias' rowData column derived from peak GC content to control for technical biases.

name: gc-content-and-skew-calculation
description: Use when you have genomic region sets (e.g. HOT vs COLD intervals) in FASTA or BED+reference form and need sequence-composition features (GC content, GC skew, CpG O/E, k-mer frequencies) for classification.

name: gc-content-bias-correlation
description: Use when comparing bias correction across organisms or protocols to decide whether GC normalization suffices as a bias proxy, or when diagnosing whether observed expression shifts in RNA-Seq track transcript GC content.

name: gc-decile-stratified-parameter-estimation
description: Use when calling RNA-binding sites from CLIP/eCLIP data by testing tiled transcriptomic windows for IP-over-input enrichment and you need GC-bias-aware, overdispersion-calibrated nulls rather than peak calling.

name: gc-matched-background-sampling
description: Use when TFBS motif instances from CNN motif detectors must be retained by statistical significance rather than a subjective signal cutoff — i.e., when per-motif occurrence probabilities from GC-matched 101-bp background bins are needed to compute binomial P-values.

name: gcn-graph-based-loop-classifier-training
description: Use when a Hi-C cis-contact map must be encoded as a graph (nodes/edges weighted by contact counts) to train or evaluate a graph-only CTCF loop-calling classifier, e.g. as a uni-modal baseline for view-complementarity tests.

name: gcn-loop-calling-inference
description: Use when evaluating how a graph-based loop caller's PR-AUC and smoothness (MAD) change across Hi-C sequencing depths, or when comparing graph-view vs image-view branch robustness on downsampled contact maps.
