name: genbank-annotation-matching
description: Use when GEO series expression tables must be anchored to official gene annotations: you have a GenBank .gbff for the organism and GEOparse-organized per-series tables whose gene identifiers need to be matched, filtered, and annotated before joining.

name: genbank-genome-library-construction
description: Use when you have a GenBank file for a target genome (e.g. R. sphaeroides NC_007493.2) and a tab-delimited sites file of genomic positions, and need to extract coordinate-windowed sequences into a Delila book artifact for motif construction.

name: genbank-sequence-library-generation
description: Use when running Delila-PY on a new organism: you have an NCBI GenBank file (e.g., NC_007493.2 for R. sphaeroides) and must create the Delila libraries that the delila program consumes to build a book of sequences.

name: gencode-annotation-parsing
description: Use when a genomic interval catalog (e.g., eccDNAs from AmpliconArchitect) must be intersected with GENCODE gene annotations to assign overlapping genes, with per-pair overlap ratios quantifying reciprocal coverage.

name: gencode-gene-annotation-filtering
description: Use when a strand-asymmetry or motif-orientation analysis needs strand-annotated, protein-coding gene regions (e.g. GENCODE v33) formatted as BED input for Asymmetron's contained_asymmetries.

name: gencode-transcript-annotation-harmonization
description: Use when harmonizing lncRNA identifiers and sequences across multiple published RNA:DNA interaction datasets (ChIRP-seq, ChOP-seq, CHART-seq, RAP-seq) prior to peak calling or benchmarking, so all entries share one gene-symbol and transcript reference.

name: gene-annotation-column-preservation
description: Use when mean-centering or otherwise transforming a COnTORT-style expression matrix where the first five columns are GenBank annotations and must survive transformation unchanged, including 'N/A' blanks.

name: gene-annotation-expression-matching
description: Use when normalizing expression data from multiple GEO series for one organism: expression rows must be filtered to genes present in a GenBank annotation file and joined across experiments by locus tag/gene name.

name: gene-annotation-strand-orientation-mapping
description: Use when you have strand-annotated BED files of motifs (e.g. TFBSs) and gene regions and need to test whether motif orientation is biased relative to transcriptional direction within transcribed regions.

name: gene-dosage-sensitivity-scoring
description: Use when annotating genes with binary LOF/GOF dosage-sensitivity scores for SV pathogenicity prediction, especially when sex-chromosome genes lack ClinGen TS scores and need an HI-based proxy.

name: gene-expression-data-simulation
description: Use when you need to benchmark a statistical mediation test or prioritize candidate driver genes: simulate gene expression with known mediated vs. independent cis-trans pairs before running the test.

name: gene-expression-imputation-from-accessibility
description: Use when you have a scATAC-seq snap object plus matched scRNA-seq expression data and need to link distal enhancer peaks to their putative target genes, or to rank enhancer–gene associations for benchmarking against eQTLs.

name: gene-expression-matrix-mean-centering
description: Use when compiling multiple NCBI GEO series into one expression matrix and you need to remove per-experiment offsets so values from different GSE studies are comparable before joining or downstream correlation analysis.

name: gene-expression-matrix-processing
description: Use when a raw numeric expression matrix (rows = features/genes, columns = samples) contains missing values, outliers, or low-variance rows and must be prepared for feature selection and subgroup classification.

name: gene-expression-median-stratification
description: Use when you have per-sample gene expression values (e.g., TCGA RNA data) matched to clinical survival metadata and need binary high/low expression groups for log-rank/KM prognosis testing of an eccDNA gene.

name: gene-expression-methylation-integration
description: Use when integrating matched transcriptomic and epigenomic (methylation) p-value data to score genes, detect dysregulated network modules, or compare module-detection methods such as SMITE and FEM.

name: gene-expression-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when a trained model predicts tumor gene expression from somatic alterations and you must quantify held-out test-set accuracy (predicted vs measured GEP) and compare against baselines.

name: gene-expression-preprocessing-and-imputation
description: Use when a raw gene expression matrix (e.g. from golubEsets Bioconductor data) contains missing values, outlier or sub-1 expression values, or low-variance rows that would break consensus partitioning.

name: gene-expression-quantification
description: Use when raw RNA-seq reads have been mapped to a reference genome (BAM produced via ContextMap 2 and samtools) and per-gene read counts are needed as input for differential expression analysis.

name: gene-expression-repression-annotation
description: Use when evaluating H3K27me3 (or other repressive-mark) ChIP-seq domain calls against functional ground truth: you have matched expression profiles for the same cell types and need per-cell-type sets of repressed genes to compute gene-body coverage fractions.

name: gene-expression-subgroup-clustering
description: Use when a high-dimensional gene-expression matrix (e.g. TCGA GBM from gdc.cancer.gov/about-data/publications/gbm_exp) must be stratified into stable molecular subgroups and the effect of resampling count on consensus stability must be quantified.

name: gene-expression-time-series-smoothing
description: Use when you have a measured gene-expression time series (e.g. GSE6865, GDS38, GSE44415) that must be converted into continuous smooth curves prior to ODE model fitting or regulon scoring.

name: gene-identifier-mapping-for-enrichment
description: Use when BIT output rank tables (e.g., mm10_RUNX1_rank_table.csv) contain TR gene symbols but the downstream enrichment tool requires Entrez IDs, such as clusterProfiler::enrichGO.

name: gene-identifier-mapping-for-rem-retrieval
description: Use when you have a gene list (e.g. DE genes from Seurat FindAllMarkers) and need the REMs associated to those genes, with cell type/tissue-specific filtering via EpiRegio.

name: gene-level-alignment-score-aggregation
description: Use when chromatin state sequences of thousands of protein-coding genes must be compared across two sample groups (e.g. male vs female NIH Roadmap epigenomes) to produce per-gene groups of EpiAlign alignment scores and a ranked list of differentially aligned genes.

name: gene-level-p-value-reproduction
description: Use when validating DriverPower-exclusive non-coding driver candidates by testing whether genes linked to mutated candidate elements show differential expression after correcting for copy number (SCNA) and tissue type.

name: gene-ontology-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have per-cluster up-/down-regulated gene lists from one-vs-rest SAM differential expression and need GO terms explaining the biology of each cluster.

name: gene-ontology-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a BIT output rank table (e.g., mm10_RUNX1_rank_table.csv) of TRs ranked by BIT score from perturbation, cancer-type, or cell-type-specific epigenomic query regions and need to test GO BP enrichment of the top candidates.

name: gene-ontology-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when you have a ranked list of genes from EpiAlign differential alignment (Wilcoxon P-values comparing within-tissue vs cross-tissue alignment scores) and need functional interpretation via GO terms or validation against known tissue-specific gene labels.

name: gene-ontology-enrichment-of-sub-compartments
description: Use when genes have been assigned to CscoreTool-M sub-compartments (e.g., C10_2 or C10_1 from a 10-sub-compartment run on Hi-C data) and you need to test whether these sub-compartments are enriched for housekeeping or cell-type-specific biological functions.

name: gene-overlap-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have two gene/region sets (e.g., differentially modified regions from ChIP-seq and differentially expressed genes from RNA-seq) mapped to a common identifier and need to quantify overlap significance and GO enrichment.

name: gene-pathomechanism-interpretation
description: Use when patient SVs (inversions, translocations, deletions, duplications) in hg19 coordinates need candidate causative genes and coding or long-range pathomechanisms assigned in a phenotype-specific cellular context.

name: gene-peak-pair-association-modeling
description: Use when you have a SnapATAC snap object for scATAC-seq cells plus matched scRNA-seq expression and need to connect distal accessible peaks to putative target genes, e.g. building a cis-regulatory network from the 10X_PBMC_15K PBMC dataset.

name: gene-phenotype-annotation-mapping
description: Use when a candidate gene must be scored for its association with a structural-variant-associated phenotype group (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular) using HPO/MPO gene-phenotype annotations.

name: gene-prioritization-deep-learning
description: Use when you have non-coding variants already scored by a brain-variant prioritizer (ncDeepBrain) and need to assign per-gene susceptibility probabilities by linking variants to genes and training a deep network on gene-level features.

name: gene-ranking-comparison-across-tools
description: Use when a set of SVs with known disease-causative genes (positive controls) must be scored by multiple pathogenicity classifiers and ranked-gene agreement between tools (e.g. POSTRE vs TADEUS2) quantified.

name: gene-region-alignment-score-ranking
description: Use when a query gene's chromatin state sequence must be compared against every protein-coding gene region in one Roadmap/ChromHMM-annotated sample to produce a ranked local-alignment score table identifying the -matching gene region.

name: gene-regulatory-network-method-comparison
description: Use when validating a gene regulatory network inference method on time-course expression data against a curated reference regulon set, especially to compare two methods and a random baseline per transcription factor.

name: gene-regulatory-network-table-export
description: Use when a time-series expression dataset (e.g., mouse liver regeneration GSE95135) has been mined with TSMiner and you need machine-readable tables of time-specific activators/repressors and their interacting KEGG pathways.

name: gene-regulatory-ode-parameter-fitting
description: Use when fitting gene-regulator ODE parameters to smoothed time-course expression profiles (e.g. SigB regulon targets) and you need to compare regularized vs. unregularized fits or enforce biologically interpretable parameter bounds.

name: gene-score-matrix-processing
description: Use when input is scATAC-seq raw data (fragment file or bam file) or gene score matrices, and you need to build Cellcano-ready reference/target matrices with F-test-selected features before supervised celltyping.

name: gene-score-vs-bin-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when evaluating which scATAC-seq input representation (ArchR-derived gene scores vs. 500-bp fixed-size bin counts) yields better Cellcano celltype prediction accuracy across benchmark tasks, especially mouse brain reference-target pairs from Fig 2.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when genes must be ranked by epigenomic signal (e.g. RNAP2 or H3K4me3 ChIP-seq prevalence) within chromosome clusters such as BHi-Cect bottom enclaves, and tested for GO-term enrichment via GSEA with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction.

name: gene-set-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when you have a BED list of ChIP-seq peaks (e.g. bivalent H3K4me3+/H3K27me3+ peaks in mESCs) and need to identify enriched biological functions such as developmental GO categories.

name: gene-set-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have two or more differential-expression-derived gene lists (e.g., H-NS regulons from GSE136050 RNA-seq and a published 308-gene LuxR regulon) and need to compute and validate their overlap count.

name: generalized-linear-model-regression
description: Use when you have per-donor flow cytometry cell population proportion data plus donor metadata (continuous age, sex) and need to quantify which factor — age, sex, or their interaction — is most strongly associated with each PBMC cell subset.

name: generalized-poisson-emission-density-estimation
description: Use when modeling ChIP-Seq HDF per-bin count data whose enriched-state distribution is overdispersed relative to Poisson and whose background contains excess zeros, requiring GP/ZIP emissions for HMM-based bin classification.

name: genome-assembly-liftover-feature-harmonization
description: Use when benchmark pairs or annotations are given on an older assembly (e.g. hg19 BENGI) but features were computed on a newer one (hg38 cCREs-ELS/GENCODE v40), requiring coordinate conversion and per-pair feature averaging before cross-method comparison.

name: genome-assembly-polishing
description: Use when the goal is to regenerate or replicate a published long-read (Oxford Nanopore) genome assembly pipeline from a released repository, specifically the polished E. coli assembly from the 2015 Nature Methods nanopore article.

name: genome-browser-track-retrieval
description: Use when a SeqCode command (e.g. scorePhastCons, produceTSSplots) requires the chromInfo, refGene, or a conservation track for a specific assembly (e.g. mouse mm9) that must first be downloaded and uncompressed from UCSC.

name: genome-build-correspondence-human-mouse
description: Use when encoding enhancer DNA sequences (SEs/TEs) into dna2vec feature vectors and you must decide which pre-trained embedding matrix (human hg19 vs mouse mm9) corresponds to each cell-line dataset.

name: genome-chromosome-coordinate-segmentation
description: Use when multiple ChIP-seq samples with spike-in chromatin must be compared genome-wide and a common fixed-size bin grid (e.g. 1000-bp bins of hg19 and FLY-suffixed dm3 from ChromInfo.txt) is needed before per-bin counting and normalization.

name: genome-index-building
description: Use when preparing a reference genome (e.g., hg19/hg38, mm9/mm10 as multi-fasta or per-chromosome directory) before running Msuite alignment or the CT/GA-rich region benchmark, so converted indices exist for 3-letter or 4-letter TAPS/BS modes.

name: genome-index-preparation-three-letter-conversion
description: Use when aligning bisulfite-treated reads (e.g. WGBS FASTQ against hg19) with BiSpark, since the 'three-letter' aligner requires a pre-converted, Bowtie2-indexed reference stored in HDFS before alignment can start.

name: genome-tiling-chunk-overhang-configuration
description: Use when preparing a ChIP-Seq count dataset for genome-wide GAM fitting with GenoGAM, i.e. when BAM alignments must be tiled into overlapping intervals of fixed chunkSize/overhangSize and written to an HDF5 backend.

name: genome-wide-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have CscoreTool-M *_cscore.txt outputs and a reference set of compartment/sub-compartment scores for the same 500kb hg38 windows and need a genome-wide Pearson correlation to judge inference accuracy or depth robustness.

name: genome-wide-differential-region-validation
description: Use when reproducing or validating published genome-wide differential ChIP-seq region calls for broad histone marks (e.g., H3K9me3/H3K27me3) with histoneHMM and a quantitative target such as total differential Mb or genome fraction.

name: genome-wide-gam-smoothing-fit
description: Use when you need base-level smoothing and significance/peak calls for ChIP-Seq protein-DNA occupancy across whole chromosomes or gigabase-scale genomes (e.g., TF binding, genotype contrasts) without ad-hoc binning or windowing.

name: genome-wide-occupancy-profile-scoring
description: Use when comparing TF binding site predictions from chromatin occupancy models (RoboCOP, COMPETE, MACS2+FIMO/FIMO baselines) against ChIP-chip, ChIP-exo, or ORGANIC annotations to quantify and rank method accuracy.

name: genome-wide-signal-binning
description: Use when filtered .bam/.bai alignments from a ChIPseq/RNAseq pipeline must be converted into compressed genome-browser tracks (.wig/.bigwig) or compact GRanges objects for visualization and downstream analysis.

name: genome-wide-tfbs-prediction-scanning
description: Use when an in vitro trained TF affinity model (e.g. DNAffinity on gcPBM data for CBF1) must be applied genome-wide to predict in vivo binding sites and validated against exo peak calls.

name: genomic-bed-data-loading
description: Use when reproducing a DNALONGBENCH long-range task (eQTL, RSAP, TISP, contact map, enhancer-target gene) and raw bed-file data downloaded from a Dataverse DOI must be converted into train/valid/test loaders for model training and inference.

name: genomic-bed-file-strand-annotation
description: Use when strand-oriented genomic features (e.g. GENCODE v33 genes, PolyASite PAS clusters, UCSC tfbsConsSites TFBSs, JASPAR/FIMO motif tracks) must be converted into 4-column BED files before running Asymmetron asymmetry analyses.

name: genomic-bin-assignment-from-chromosome-sizes
description: Use when a PET/interaction bedpe file must be aggregated into a fixed-bin (e.g. 10 kb) 2D contact map whose bin grid is bounded by a chromosome sizes file such as chrom_hg19.sizes.

name: genomic-bin-count-aggregation
description: Use when raw single-cell ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq reads (FASTQ→BAM/BED) or per-cell alignment files must be converted into a cell-by-region count matrix binned across the genome for downstream clustering.

name: genomic-bin-labeling
description: Use when you already have per-bin node embeddings from a GAE trained on 400×400 Hi-C submatrices and need an unsupervised cluster label per genomic bin to delineate TAD boundaries.

name: genomic-bin-read-counting
description: Use when aligned ChIP-seq BAM files for experimental and spike-in genomes must be converted into genome-wide binned read-count tables (e.g. chromosome-start-end-count rows at 1-kbp resolution) before cross-condition normalization.

name: genomic-bin-segmentation
description: Use when preparing a spikChIP or similar spike-in ChIP-seq pipeline: before counting reads per bin or classifying bins as peaks/background, the sample and spike-in genomes must be divided into fixed-size bins from a ChromInfo chromosome list.

name: genomic-binning-read-counting
description: Use when preparing BAM/Bed ChIP-seq alignments of broad histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) as fixed-width binned read counts before HMM-based modification or differential-modification calling.

name: genomic-blacklist-filtering
description: Use when building a DiffBind workflow on ATAC-seq or ChIP-seq peaks (e.g., mouse/mm10 cKO-vs-WT samples) before counting reads over consensus peaks, to exclude ENCODE blacklist artifact regions from downstream DAR generation.

name: genomic-blacklist-region-filtering
description: Use when preparing narrowPeak/BED peak files (ChIP-seq, CUT&Tag, CUT&Run, ATAC-seq, DNase-seq) for cross-dataset comparison or QC, so that artifactual peaks in ENCODE blacklisted regions (hg19/hg38) do not bias overlap statistics, correlation plots, or ChromHMM/ChIPseeker annotations.

name: genomic-coordinate-distance-matching
description: Use when validating a coordinate-level genome-wide prediction (e.g. called nucleosome dyads) against high-precision reference annotations, and you need a distance-thresholded precision-recall curve.

name: genomic-coordinate-file-formatting
description: Use when you have per-genomic-bin cluster labels (e.g., HDBSCAN output from TOAST embeddings) and must delineate contiguous same-label regions into a TAD boundary coordinate file at a stated matrix resolution.

name: genomic-coordinate-sorting
description: Use when a fragment file produced by ExtractHair (modified from HapCUT2) must be sorted consistently with VCF variant order before SpecHap linkage-graph construction or haplotype phasing.

name: genomic-correlation-decay-visualization
description: Use when integrating epigenomic p-values (e.g., DNA methylation) whose assay sites are spatially non-independent, and you need to quantify or visualize how correlation between adjacent CpG p-values decays with genomic distance before combining p-values.

name: genomic-count-matrix-construction
description: Use when raw ChIP-Seq BAM alignments plus an experiment design file must be converted into a tiled, normalized count matrix too large for memory, as preprocessing before GAM model fitting.

name: genomic-coverage-track-generation
description: Use when paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq BAM alignments must be converted into fragment-length-classified, midpoint-aggregated bedGraph count tracks to serve as HMM observables for chromatin occupancy profiling.

name: genomic-data-train-valid-test-splitting
description: Use when raw task data downloaded for a DNALONGBENCH task must be partitioned and serialized into train*/valid*/test*.tfr files so downstream loaders and model training consume consistent splits.

name: genomic-distance-background-modeling
description: Use when distance-normalized Hi-C or pcHi-C contact tables (covNorm normDistance output) need per-contact significance scores (p-value and FDR) so that reproducible significant long-range interactions can be detected.

name: genomic-distance-binning-analysis
description: Use when coverage-normalized Hi-C or pcHi-C fragment-pair tables (Rij residuals with cov_frag1, cov_frag2, freq, dist columns) need distance-dependent background removal before calling significant long-range interactions.

name: genomic-distance-normalization-of-contact-probabilities
description: Use when calling chromatin loop candidates from single-cell Hi-C contact matrices at 10-kb bin resolution and you need to control for the monotonic distance decay of contact probability before declaring a bin pair significant.

name: genomic-distance-threshold-filtering
description: Use when preparing Hi-C fragment files for haplotype assembly with SpecHap and you need to drop read pairs spanning more than 40 Mbp to avoid linkages with elevated trans interaction error rates.

name: genomic-domain-boundary-refinement
description: Use when calling broad ChIP-seq enrichment domains (e.g., H3K27me3/H3K9me3, kb-to-Mb) and you must convert multi-scale coarse-grained '1' blocks into precisely bounded candidate domains prior to Poisson/FDR significance assessment.

name: genomic-enhancer-prediction
description: Use when the goal is to classify genomic regions as enhancers from matched ChIP-seq (H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K27ac) and DNase-seq datasets, e.g. reproducing enhancer catalogs in human cell lines like HCT116 or HeLa.

name: genomic-feature-collinearity-diagnostics
description: Use when a multi-score genomic feature table (e.g., variant scores from multiple predictors plus epigenomic annotations) must be checked for pairwise redundancy/collinearity before feeding features into an integrative model such as ncDeepBrain.

name: genomic-feature-engineering-from-chromatin-signals
description: Use when genomic elements (candidate enhancers vs promoters) must be converted into numeric features from ChIP-seq/DNase-seq bedGraph signals to train or apply an enhancer-prediction classifier.

name: genomic-feature-importance-ranking
description: Use when you have labeled genomic interval sets (e.g. HOT vs COLD regions) with coordinates and reference genome sequences, and need to rank sequence or genomic features by predictive importance.

name: genomic-feature-interval-derivation
description: Use when you have a UCSC refGene.txt transcript annotation file plus chromInfo.txt for a genome assembly and need BED-like coordinate sets per feature class to feed feature-level analyses (e.g. scorePhastCons conservation scores).

name: genomic-feature-missingness-statistics
description: Use when preparing variant-prioritization training matrices from ANNOVAR-annotated score columns (DANN, CADD, EIGEN, GWAVA, FATHMM) and you need to quantify per-score missingness before/after bPCA imputation.

name: genomic-feature-size-distribution-statistics
description: Use when a catalog of genomic features (e.g. eccDNAs from WGS analysis plus literature curation) must be reduced to headline distribution statistics — total/provenance counts, mean/median feature size, per-feature segment counts, and copy numbers — for reproducibility checks.

name: genomic-graph-representation-construction
description: Use when input is a tab-separated N×N intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact matrix (e.g. dumped from .hic data via juicer_tools) and the goal is to represent genomic bins as graph nodes for GAE-based feature learning or clustering.

name: genomic-indel-feature-preparation
description: Use when building supervised predictors for non-coding small indels (sindels) that need both generic functional annotations and tissue-specific epigenomic sequence-derived features, e.g. replicating the TIVAN-indel feature-set ablation.

name: genomic-interaction-table-processing
description: Use when input is a tab-delimited Hi-C or capture Hi-C fragment-pair table (frag1, frag2, cov_frag1, cov_frag2, freq, dist) and the goal is to remove coverage-driven ligation bias from raw interaction frequencies before distance normalization or contact calling.

name: genomic-interval-aggregation
description: Use when a broad-domain ChIP-seq analysis needs mapped BED reads binned into fixed windows (e.g., 200 bp) with 5'-end shifting (e.g., 75 bp for 150 bp fragments) before multi-scale enrichment detection.

name: genomic-interval-anchoring-quantification
description: Use when you have a set of called TAD boundaries (start bin, start location, end bin, end location) plus genomic peak/interval files (narrowPeak BED, enhancer/promoter BED) and need anchoring ratios per regulatory factor.

name: genomic-interval-binning-and-visualization
description: Reference for converting significant ChIA-PET loop calls (bedpe) into a 10 kb-binned contact matrix and visually comparing it against Hi-C data at loop anchors.

name: genomic-interval-chain-liftover
description: Use when lifting non-coding regulatory regions (peaks, GWAS SNP loci) between species with a UCSC chain file and candidates must be ranked by functional (epigenomic/motif) similarity rather than position alone.

name: genomic-interval-coordinate-handling
description: Use when you must convert ENCODE/modENCODE narrowPeak ChIP-seq peak files into per-genome interval tracks (e.g. HOT regions) by tallying peak-summit coordinates over sliding genomic windows.

name: genomic-interval-coverage-calculation
description: Use when you need to quantify how completely called broad ChIP-seq domains (e.g., ENCODE broadPeak-format H3K27me3 domains) cover annotated gene bodies of repressed genes across multiple methods or samples.

name: genomic-interval-distance-matching
description: Use when processed ChIP-seq peak interval files (e.g. MACS2 LuxR and H-NS peaks from GEO GSE136191/GSE136050) must be intersected or distance-matched, such as counting co-occupied LuxR/H-NS loci per strain or flagging H-NS doublets within 1 kb of a LuxR peak.

name: genomic-interval-extension-and-merging
description: Use when raw ChIP-seq/DNase narrow-peak BED files (chrom, start, end) must be converted into fixed-width genomic training windows with a fixed CNN input size and no redundant overlap before training.

name: genomic-interval-extraction-from-gene-annotation
description: Use when you need to obtain concrete genomic coordinates from a gene annotation table (UCSC knownGenes track) to define fixed-length regions — e.g. 2 kb windows spanning TSS and first splicing site — on which ChIP-Seq enrichment profiles will be extracted.

name: genomic-interval-granges-manipulation
description: Use when coordinate-based query regions (e.g., fine-mapped BMD GWAS SNPs at PIP ≥0.001, or epigenome peak sets) must be loaded as genomic intervals in R and lifted over between hg38 and mm10 via a UCSC chain file.

name: genomic-interval-intersection
description: Use when a set of predicted regulatory element coordinates (e.g. scATAC-seq candidate CREs) needs to be intersected with a reference table of experimentally validated enhancers to annotate functional status per region.

name: genomic-interval-intersection-computation
description: Use when scoring ChIP-seq peak calls against ENCODE union DHS regions to compute per-sample overlap ratios, or when grouping overlap ratios by histone mark / factor category to build a quality atlas distribution.

name: genomic-interval-intersection-with-bedtools
description: Use when ChIA-PIPE has produced peak-supported loops (PET count >= 3) with unique loop IDs from RNAPII ChIA-PET data and you must annotate each loop as E-P, P-P, or neither using enhancer/promoter BED annotations.

name: genomic-interval-length-filtering
description: Use when you have per-bin labels (e.g., HDBSCAN clusters on Hi-C genomic bins at 50/25/5 Kb resolution) and need contiguous same-label regions filtered by a genomic length threshold to define TAD boundaries.

name: genomic-interval-merging
description: Use when peak- or loop-supported genomic intervals must be collapsed into contiguous domains, e.g., deriving CCDs from ChIA-PIPE CTCF loop BED output where overlapping/adjacent loops define continuous coverage.

name: genomic-interval-operations
description: Use when genomic intervals (e.g., ATAC-seq or ChIP-seq peak BED regions) in one genome assembly (hg38, mm10, rn6) must be lifted over, partitioned by mapping multiplicity, or compared against intervals in another species using UCSC chain files and GRanges.

name: genomic-interval-overlap-analysis
description: Use when comparing peak/enriched-window calls from multiple CLIP-seq analysis methods run on the same matched IP-and-input eCLIP replicates, and you need per-RBP counts of shared vs. unique binding sites via interval intersection.

name: genomic-interval-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have strand-annotated BED files of motifs (e.g. PolyASite signals, RepeatMasker Alu elements, TFBSs) and regions (e.g. GENCODE protein-coding genes) and want to test whether motif orientation is biased relative to regions.

name: genomic-interval-overlap-annotation
description: Use when per-region feature values (e.g. enhancer/promoter probabilities from bin-level tracks) must be transferred onto annotated genomic intervals (cCRE-ELS, TSSs) as input features for downstream ET-pair classification.

name: genomic-interval-overlap-comparison
description: Use when you have two BED-format peak lists for different histone marks or features and need to partition their union into overlapping vs. non-overlapping classes (e.g. H3K4me3+/H3K27me3– bivalent analysis).

name: genomic-interval-overlap-filtering
description: Use when you have per-replicate significant interaction/loop calls (e.g., FitHiC at FDR < 0.05, HiCCUPS or Mustache loops) and a list of significant differential compartment bins (e.g., RefineY_Rconf90_FDR10), and need only the interactions anchored in those bins.

name: genomic-interval-overlap-matching
description: Use when comparing loop-calling results (bedpe anchor coordinates) against a curated reference interaction set and you need TP/FP/FN counts, precision, recall, and F1 per method and per subsampling level.

name: genomic-interval-overlap-merging
description: Use when you have sorted, coordinate-anchored genomic intervals (e.g. REM BED records with chr, start, end) and need to collapse overlaps/adjacencies into clusters and quantify their span and multiplicity.

name: genomic-interval-overlap-quantification
description: Use when two or more sets of genomic intervals (e.g. DMRs from different callers, i-DMRs vs reference regions) must be intersected to compute overlap fractions, or when CpG-level methylation records need region names from a BED annotation file before running DXM.

name: genomic-interval-overlap-quantification
description: Use when you have BHi-Cect cluster/loci assignments and coordinate-based epigenomic annotation tracks, and need per-enclave overlap counts and enrichment values to test how activity varies with nestedness along the BPT.

name: genomic-interval-processing
description: Use when the task requires comparing, merging, or signal-quantifying genomic intervals, e.g. calling CC peaks from qbed insertions, annotating peaks, or computing ChIP-seq signal under called peaks.

name: genomic-interval-promoter-assignment
description: Use when you have a set of ChIP-seq peak intervals (e.g., MACs2 output for two regulators) plus RNA-seq differential expression calls, and you need to assign peaks to promoters/ORFs and count co-regulated, co-occupied loci.

name: genomic-landmark-position-histogramming
description: Use when evaluating whether a DTW-based clustering/alignment of epigenomic peak regions has sharpened the positions of annotated genomic landmarks (TSS, FSS) within each cluster.

name: genomic-locus-to-cluster-mapping
description: Use when a BHi-Cect tree output (nested cluster list / named loci lists) must be joined with gene coordinates and per-locus ChIP-seq signal (e.g. RNAP2 in IMR90, H3K4me3 in K562) to produce per-enclave gene rankings for enrichment analysis.

name: genomic-mappability-and-blacklist-filtering
description: Use when running SnapHiC (or similar loop-calling pipelines) on scHi-C/sn-m3C-seq contact files and you must restrict loop candidate calling to bins with adequate mappability, excluding ENCODE blacklist overlaps.

name: genomic-matrix-missing-value-filtering
description: Use when a raw numeric expression/methylation matrix destined for cola consensus partitioning contains missing values, extreme outliers, or rows with very small variance that would distort row-wise scaling and feature selection.

name: genomic-negative-region-sampling
description: Use when building a positive/negative benchmark for genomic prediction tools (e.g. 3plex TPX scoring): you have experimentally derived peak sets (IDR, Overlap q<0.

name: genomic-overlap-strand-assignment
description: Use when a BED feature set lacks strand annotation but an overlapping strand-assigned feature set exists (e.g., orienting hg38 CTCF ChIP-seq peaks using MA0139.1 CTCF motif occurrences) prior to strand asymmetry analysis.

name: genomic-position-file-parsing
description: Use when constructing Delila-PY inputs: you have ChIP-seq/ChIP-chip peak centers or transcription start sites and need to encode each location with chromosome, strand, and base position, then define -l/-r boundaries for motif extraction.

name: genomic-range-block-bootstrap
description: Use when testing enrichment or correlation of genomic ranges (e.g. caQTL peaks vs GWAS SNPs, DEG vs differential accessibility peaks, CRE-gene correlations across pseudo-bulk cell types) against a null and conventional shuffling is at risk of an overly narrow null distribution.

name: genomic-range-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when testing enrichment of overlaps between genomic range sets (e.g. caQTL SNPs vs chromatin accessibility peaks, or DEGs vs DA peaks) and when permutation-based nulls seem too narrow or thresholds need optimization.

name: genomic-range-overlap-statistics
description: Use when testing whether an observed overlap between two genomic range sets (e.g. caQTL/SNP sets and peaks, or CREs and genes) is significant relative to a null that accounts for genomic structure, using GRanges objects in R/Bioconductor.

name: genomic-range-simulation-under-null
description: Use when testing overlap/enrichment between two genomic range sets (e.g. caQTLs vs GWAS SNPs, CREs vs genes) and a properly calibrated null is needed, especially when local genomic correlation structure must be preserved.

name: genomic-region-bed-interval-handling
description: Use when you need read-level methylation linkage (phase) information within defined genomic intervals from MethylC-seq/Bismark alignments, e.g. to test whether methylation differences occur in a nonrandom pattern.

name: genomic-region-blacklist-filtering
description: Reference for removing non-informative or artifact-prone regions (sex chromosomes, chrM, ENCODE blacklist) from bin-sample methylation quantification matrices before downstream group/batch comparisons.

name: genomic-region-coordinate-aggregation
description: Use when individual-CpG methylation count tables (e.g. Bismark-derived .cov files with methylated/unmethylated counts per site) must be collapsed into genomic regions before differential methylation testing.

name: genomic-region-overlap-querying
description: Use when you have TF binding locations (e.g. an ENCODE ChIP-seq peak BED file) and need to find which EpiRegio REMs overlap them and which target genes those REMs are associated with.

name: genomic-region-promoter-intergenic-intragenic-assignment
description: Use when BED peak lists (e.g. MACS-called H3K4me3, H3K27me3, or bivalent peaks) must be classified into promoter, intergenic, or intragenic features using a RefSeq refGene annotation for a genome assembly such as mouse mm9.

name: genomic-region-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when testing whether a genomic feature (R-loops, G-quadruplexes, GC/CpG content) is enriched on HOT region coordinates relative to control regions binned by TF occupancy percentiles.

name: genomic-region-set-processing
description: Use when you hold a set of chromosome coordinates from epigenomic profiling (e.g., ATAC-seq DAR peaks called by MACS2 or DiffBind) and need to identify transcriptional regulators for that region set via BIT.

name: genomic-region-shuffling-negative-control
description: Use when benchmarking TPX-prediction software (3plex, Triplexator, TriplexAligner, fasim-LongTarget) and a matched randomised genomic negative set is needed to compute ROC AUCs against experimentally derived positive peaks.

name: genomic-region-span-verification
description: Use when a published pipeline reports a total differential-region span (e.g. Mb or % of genome) and you must reproduce the pipeline and confirm your summed call-set span matches that value.

name: genomic-region-subsetting-of-hic-data
description: Use when Microcket-generated .hic contact-matrix files (e.g., QSC and FISC Hi-C replicates) must be visualized as contact maps for specific regions, resolutions, and downstream comparative analyses.

name: genomic-region-to-ctx-region-mapping
description: Use when binarized topic or cluster region sets from single-cell ATAC-seq (e.g. cisTopic topics) must be converted to the region identifiers of a cistarget/RcisTarget database (e.g. hg19-regions-9species) before running motif enrichment.

name: genomic-scaling-benchmark-profiling
description: Use when evaluating whether a tiled/smoothed genome-wide model implementation's runtime and memory footprint scale linearly with parameters per tile, or when reproducing version-to-version speedup benchmarks (e.g. 2-3 orders of magnitude).

name: genomic-sequence-anchor-alignment
description: Use when sequences are centered on an anchor point (e.g. TSS) with a continuous per-sequence score, and the goal is to find motif positions whose occurrence correlates with that score.

name: genomic-sequence-data-preparation
description: Use when a training run for deepC (or a similar sequence-based chromatin interaction model) needs genome sequence windows plus 5 kb Hi-C skeleton targets assembled from raw genome assemblies, BED intervals, and Hi-C contact data.

name: genomic-sequence-extraction-around-anchor-motifs
description: Use when a positional motif enrichment analysis (e.g. MEPP) requires centered sequences around anchors such as deduplicated, RepeatMasker-filtered motif sites, TSSs, or cleavage sites, with a score attached per sequence.

name: genomic-sequence-feature-encoding
description: Use when raw enhancer FASTA sequences (e.g. data/train/NHLF.fasta) must be converted into fixed-dimensional numeric vectors before training or predicting with a deep learning model such as Enhancer-MDLF.

name: genomic-sequence-motif-scanning
description: Use when you have scored sequences (e.g. ATAC-seq log2 fold-change scores on ±100 bp windows around a GATA1 motif) in FASTA with score headers and need to locate occurrences of known motifs from a fixed JASPAR/HOMER library for positional enrichment analysis.

name: genomic-subgroup-classification
description: Use when given a high-dimensional gene expression or methylation matrix (rows = features, columns = samples) and the goal is to assign samples to molecular subgroups without known labels.

name: genomic-tile-standard-error-computation
description: Use when you need pointwise standard errors or variance of GAM smooth estimates for base-level significance testing in GenoGAM tile fits, where the penalized Hessian is large and sparse so a full inverse is infeasible.

name: genomic-tiled-model-fitting
description: Use when base-level ChIP-Seq count data along large chromosomes must be modeled with smooth functions genome-wide, and a full-genome GAM fit is intractable without tiling and sparse-matrix parameter fitting.

name: genomic-track-file-compression
description: Use when filtered .bam/.bai alignments from a ChIPseq or RNAseq pipeline must be converted into genome-browser track files (wig/bigwig) or compact GRanges objects for visualization and downstream analysis.

name: genomic-track-prediction-across-species
description: Use when reproducing or extending the RSAP PCC benchmark table in DNALONGBENCH, i.e., when fine-tuned DNA foundation models must be evaluated against expert and CNN baselines on human and mouse regulatory activity tracks.

name: genomic-variant-dataset-curation
description: Use when building a supervised deep learning training set of non-coding variants requiring curated positive (dsQTL, eQTL, HGMD) and frequency-matched negative SNPs, as for ncDeepBrain.

name: genomic-window-tiling
description: Use when generating fixed candidate binding-site windows over GENCODE/Ensembl GFF annotations for CLIP-seq analysis (Skipper-style), replacing peak calling with annotation-aware tiling.

name: genomicranges-overlap-annotation
description: Use when a benchmark asks whether independently called differential ChIP-seq regions (e.g. from histoneHMM, Diffreps, Chipdiff, Rseg) overlap a set of experimentally validated coordinates like qPCR-surveyed regions.

name: geo-and-4dn-hic-data-retrieval
description: Use when a transfer-learning or cross-cell-type loop-calling study requires source/target human Hi-C contact maps, and the target cell line (e.g. K562, HeLa-S3) data must be obtained from GEO or 4DN accessions before GILoop inference.

name: geo-chipseq-data-acquisition
description: Use when a comparative ChIP-seq analysis requires raw reads from GEO (sample plus spike-in chromatin controls) that must be mapped and peak-called before running a normalization method like spikChIP, ChIP-Rx or tag removal.

name: geo-chipseq-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a reproduction task cites specific GEO accessions (e.g. GSM2098958 H3K4me3 mESC, GSM2645501 MLL2 WT) and the raw FASTQ files, mapped BAMs, or BED peak lists must be fetched from NCBI GEO before analysis can begin.

name: geo-chipseq-raw-data-retrieval
description: Use when a downstream module requires raw ChIP-seq reads rather than processed peaks — e.g. deriving H3K27me3 domain-breadth cutoffs per cell type from GEO/SRA accessions with matched input controls.

name: geo-dataset-acquisition-and-preprocessing
description: Use when a replication or comparison task requires downloading a public ChIP-Seq dataset with matched treated and control runs and formatting short reads (BED/ELAND, single- or pair-end) for HPeak-style peak calling.

name: geo-fastq-data-retrieval
description: Use when a spikChIP-style spike-in ChIP-seq analysis needs its starting raw data: GEO accessions such as GSE60104 must be resolved to per-sample FASTQ files (Jurkat_K79 0–100% spike-in fractions) before any mapping with Bowtie can begin.

name: geo-fastq-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis starts from a published GEO accession (e.g. GSE136050) and requires the raw FASTQ files of ChIP-seq IP samples to reproduce published peak counts such as 506 LuxR or 237/302 H-NS peaks.

name: geo-raw-sequencing-data-retrieval
description: Use when starting from a list of GEO accession datasets (e.g., ChIP-seq or DNase-seq studies) and raw FASTQ files for treatment and control samples are needed as pipeline input.

name: geo-rnaseq-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a paper's RNA-seq differential expression claims must be reproduced or re-analyzed and the reads are deposited under a named GEO accession (e.g. GSE136191) with companion scripts on GitHub.

name: geodata-fastq-retrieval
description: Use when a methylation-analysis reproduction task requires the raw sequencing reads of a published dataset identified by a GEO accession (e.g., GSE129673 for TAPS murine ESCs) before alignment or methylation calling can begin.

name: gff-transcript-partitioning
description: Use when you need fixed genomic windows for CLIP-seq binding-site testing over annotated transcripts (e.g., GENCODE GFF3 for Skipper) instead of peak calling, ensuring no window spans intron/exon or gene boundaries.

name: gibbs-sampler-convergence-assessment
description: Use when runModels has built several LDA models (e.g. 2–40 topics) on single-cell ATAC-seq data and you must verify the log-likelihood stabilized after burnin and pick the model.

name: glm-vs-gbm-predictive-metrics-comparison
description: Use when fitting DriverPower BMR background models and needing to decide between the GLM and GBM methods, or when reproducing the paper's finding that GBM outperforms GLM in low mutational burden tumour cohorts.

name: go-term-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a BED list of bivalent (H3K4me3+/H3K27me3+) peaks in mESCs and need to assign them to nearby genes and test whether the resulting gene list is enriched for development-related GO terms.

name: go-term-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a collection of region sets (e.g. binarized cisTopics from scATAC-seq) and need per-set GO functional annotation via rGREAT, or when you need to identify which topics lack cell-type-signature enrichment.

name: go-term-enrichment-statistics
description: Use when you have a list of differentially modified genomic regions from a ChIP-seq differential caller and a list of differentially expressed genes, and you need to test overlap significance and GO term enrichment of the shared genes.

name: gold-standard-target-task-evaluation
description: Use when comparing supervised scATAC-seq celltyping methods on tasks whose target dataset carries FACS-sorted gold-standard cell labels (human PBMCs), or when validating reported benchmark accuracies against the paper's Source Data.

name: goodness-of-fit-metrics-computation-rss-msep
description: Use when benchmarking calibration models for methylation standard-control data (known AMP percentages such as 0/25/50/75/100%) and you need in-sample fit (RSS) plus leave-one-out predictive measures (MSEP, CV-index).

name: goodness-of-fit-rank-comparison
description: Use when ChIP-Seq HDF counts per 25 bp bin must be assigned a probability model, and competing discrete distributions need to be fitted and ranked (e.g. GP vs. Poisson vs. NB) via AIC/log-likelihood.

name: gpu-accelerated-deep-learning-inference
description: Use when a trained deep learning model must be applied to thousands of inputs (e.g. ~96,805 genomic elements in a deletion screen) and CPU inference would be prohibitively slow.

name: gradient-based-saliency-score-computation
description: Use when you have a trained deepC checkpoint (e.g. GM12878) and hg19 sequence, and need a non-negative per-base track of sequence importance underlying predicted chromatin interactions.

name: gradient-boosted-tree-classifier-training
description: Use when you have per-sequence motif count matrices (e.g., from FIMO scans against gimme.vertebrate.v5.0.meme) and labeled CRE sets (chromosome, start, stop, condition) and need to train binary or multiclass classifiers for context-specific regulatory elements.

name: gradient-boosted-tree-interpretation
description: Use when you have a trained motif-count classifier (e.g., XGBoost on FIMO-derived motif counts) and need per-feature SHAP attributions to rank motifs and link them to lineage-specific TFs.

name: gradient-boosted-tree-model-application
description: Use when you need to classify context-specific cis-regulatory elements from sequence using motif-count features with a tree ensemble (XGBoost), e.g. distinguishing cardiomyocyte vs erythroid CREs or transferring models across species.

name: gradient-boosted-tree-modeling-xgboost
description: Use when a tabular sgRNA feature matrix (one-hot encoded sequences plus epigenetic features like nucleosome positioning, ATAC-seq accessibility, DNA methylation, RNA expression) needs both activity prediction and feature-importance interpretation via Tree SHAP.

name: gradient-boosting-classifier-reimplementation
description: Use when benchmarking a new enhancer-target prediction method against TargetFinder or Random Forest baselines and you need identically parameterized GBM/RF comparisons on BENGI All-Pairs.Natural-Ratio datasets with AUPRC/F1 outputs.

name: gradient-boosting-enhancer-target-prediction
description: Use when you need to classify candidate enhancer-target (cCRE-ELS to gene) pairs as interacting or not in a specific cell type from user-supplied histone ChIP-seq BAM files and RNA-seq TPM values, without needing massive interaction datasets.

name: gradient-boosting-kfold-cross-validation
description: Use when building a DriverPower background mutation rate model from genomic features and wanting a flexible non-linear learner (XGBoost GBM) whose performance should be compared against, or substituted for, the GLM default — especially for low mutational burden cohorts.

name: gradient-boosting-model-ablation
description: Use when you must quantify whether a feature group — e.g., the four regulatory-density window features — adds predictive signal to a gradient-boosted enhancer-target classifier by comparing full vs RD-ablated models.

name: gradient-boosting-mutational-burden-regression
description: Use when somatic mutation counts (nMut, nSample, length) per genomic element must be modelled as a function of genomic features to estimate expected background mutation burden before driver significance testing.

name: granges-interval-overlap-operations
description: Use when you have a named group of replicate peak files (e.g. GRanges/BED H3K27ac datasets such as CUT&Tag CnT_H3K27ac and CUT&Run CnR_H3K27ac) and need a single consensus GRanges peak set.

name: granges-object-generation
description: Use when a ChIPseq or RNAseq pipeline stage must hand off filtered bam alignments into R/Bioconductor for metagenomic or DEG analysis, and bam files are too large to manipulate or share.

name: granges-object-manipulation-in-r
description: Use when genomic features (SNP/caQTL ranges, peaks, a genome segmentation) must be represented as GRanges and block-bootstrapped with bootRanges to build null ranges for overlap enrichment analysis.

name: granges-preprocessing-and-segmentation
description: Use when the task is building GRanges objects for observed range sets (e.g. caQTL peaks, GWAS SNPs) and genome segmentation needed as input to bootRanges' segmented block bootstrap for enrichment testing.

name: graph-adjacency-construction-from-contact-matrix
description: Use when a Hi-C intra-chromosomal contact map (KR-normalized, O/E transformed) must be converted into graph-view training samples — e.g., paired adjacency matrices and image patches for training a dual-branch model like GILoop.

name: graph-autoencoder-embedding-training
description: Use when an NxN intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact matrix needs conversion into low-dimensional node features for unsupervised TAD identification, e.g. inputs dumped from .hic files at 50 Kb, 25 Kb, or 5 Kb resolution.

name: graph-neural-network-architecture-implementation
description: Use when reimplementing or retraining the GILoop dual-branch GCN + U-Net loop-calling architecture on Hi-C cis-contact maps, or porting the fused model to new cell lines.

name: graph-neural-network-pretraining
description: Use when Hi-C contact matrices at multiple sequencing depths (e.g. 10%-downsampled and full-depth GM12878 maps) are available and a dual-branch CTCF loop caller should be trained to exploit per-branch matrix-density preferences.

name: graph-neural-network-training-on-hic-data
description: Use when calling CTCF-mediated chromatin loops from Hi-C contact maps, especially when the library is low-depth or downsampled (e.g. 1.5%, ~39 million cis-reads) and single-view loop callers (image- or graph-only) lose PR-AUC.

name: great-genomic-region-enrichment
description: Use when a set of genomic regions (e.g. binarized cisTopics from single-cell ATAC-seq on hg19) needs GO functional annotation, or when interpreting which topics correspond to promoters vs cell-type-specific enhancers.

name: greedy-peak-extension-algorithm-implementation
description: Use when calling TF binding sites from Calling Cards qbed/ccf insertion data (e.g. Brd4 K562, GSE148448) and a fast, single-pass greedy extension peak caller with Poisson significance promotion is needed.

name: ground-truth-loop-set-intersection
description: Use when benchmarking a chromatin loop caller (e.g., GILoop vs Peakachu) on deep Hi-C data and an unbiased, stringent ground-truth loop set must be derived from consensus of independent callers.

name: grouped-sample-methylation-comparison
description: Use when individually analyzed BSP samples (from .ab1 traces) must be gathered into groups to compare CpG methylation and assign per-clone statuses (0–20% unmethylated, 80–100% methylated) in ABSP.

name: gsc-permutation-shuffling-benchmark
description: Use when a genomic overlap/enrichment analysis requires genome-scale null range sets and runtime is a bottleneck, or when benchmarking shuffling (GSC) versus block bootstrap (bootRanges) approaches on ChIP-seq peak sets.

name: gwas-snp-cross-species-liftover
description: Use when fine-mapped human GWAS SNP coordinates (e.g., PIP ≥ 0.1 or PIP ≥ 0.001 fine-mapping outputs) need to be mapped to candidate orthologous regulatory regions in a model organism genome such as mm10.

name: gwas-variant-dataset-preparation
description: Use when preparing a training set of SNPs annotated with multiple variant-prioritization scores (EIGEN, CADD, DANN, GWAVA, FATHMM, GNOMAD, eQTLs, histone marks) and you must check collinearity/redundancy before integrating scores.

name: gwas-variant-target-gene-prediction
description: Use when you have enhancer-annotated noncoding GWAS SNP coordinates and cell type-specific chromatin loop files (*.postprocessed.summits.bedpe) and need SNP-gene linkages.

name: gwas-variant-tissue-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a set of disease-associated non-coding SNPs for one or more traits and need to determine whether their predicted chromatin impact concentrates in the biologically relevant tissue (e.g. immune variants in intestine/colon, neurodegenerative variants in brain/spinal cord).

name: gzip-compressed-fastq-handling
description: Use when a workflow must extract information from gzip-compressed FASTQ files using basic UNIX tools — e.g., decompress FASTQ, pull read headers and a few sequences per file, then recompress and merge results.

name: h3k27ac-bigwig-enhancer-activity-quantification
description: Use when you have enhancer interval BED coordinates (e.g. from rearranged regulatory domains) plus control and patient/condition H3K27ac bigWig tracks for a phenotype-matched cell type and need per-enhancer mean activity values to score enhancer gain/loss.

name: h3k27me3-broad-peak-calling
description: Use when building a cell type-specific H3K27me3/polycomb domain annotation from public ChIP-seq (FASTQ from GEO/SRA), especially to compute POSTRE's binary per-gene polycombScore.

name: h3k27me3-tumor-microenvironment-analysis
description: Use when analyzing sparse single-cell H3K27me3 scChIP-seq count matrices from mixed PDX tumor micro-environment samples to identify chromatin-defined subpopulations and subtype-specific stromal cells.

name: half-linker-chia-pet-read-processing
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads from a half-linker (short-read) ChIA-PET experiment must be converted into significant chromatin loops, requiring linker trimming, bwa alignment, PET filtering, duplicate removal, peak calling and MICC significance testing.

name: haplotype-assembly-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing phasing algorithms' runtime, memory, and accuracy across NGS, 10x linked-read, Hi-C, PacBio SMRT or ONT data, or when reproducing a haplotype assembly benchmark table for samples like NA12878/NA19240/HG00403.

name: haplotype-specific-loop-summit-identification
description: Use when per-haplotype (e.g., CAST vs 129) chromatin loops such as the Sox2 promoter-super-enhancer contact must be called from allele-resolved multiplexed DNA FISH 3D coordinates at 5 Kb bins.

name: hardy-weinberg-genotype-simulation
description: Use when a power or association analysis needs simulated genotype covariates for a reference sample set — e.g. scPower's simulation eQTL power for small-mean genes requires HWE-drawn SNP genotypes paired with negative binomial pseudobulk counts.

name: harmony-batch-effect-correction
description: Use when a scATAC-seq (or scRNA-seq) dataset combines cells from multiple samples/preparations and sample-to-sample technical variability could dominate the low-dimensional embedding, driving clustering to separate batches rather than cell types.

name: hash-partitioning-load-balancing
description: Decision support for choosing between BiSpark --testmode plain and balancing when scaling bisulfite read alignment across 10-, 20-, or 40-node Spark/HDFS clusters and throughput is limited by the slowest node.

name: hashtable-kmer-count-lookup
description: Use when performing exhaustive, restriction-free motif discovery over DNA sequences where degenerate IUPAC motifs must be built from exact constituent instances, requiring per-L-mer occurrence counts in signal and control files.

name: hdbscan-density-clustering
description: Use when you have low-dimensional node embeddings (e.g. 16-dim from a 2-layer GAE with hidden_dim=64) per genomic bin and need unsupervised, density-adaptive labels without specifying k a priori.

name: hdf-bin-count-generation
description: Use when raw ChIP-Seq short reads (BED/ELAND, single- or pair-end) must be converted into per-bin HDF counts to build a genome-wide coverage profile for peak calling or count-distribution modeling.

name: hdf5-backed-genomic-data-import
description: Use when raw ChIP-Seq BAM alignments and an experimentDesign.txt must be converted into tiled count data for GenoGAM model fitting and the dataset is too large to hold in memory, requiring the HDF5 backend.

name: hdf5-out-of-memory-data-handling
description: Use when fitting genome-wide generalized additive models on gigabase-scale ChIP-Seq data where the count matrix exceeds available RAM, and out-of-core processing with low I/O overhead is required.

name: hdfs-distributed-data-management
description: Use when running BiSpark or a similar Spark/Hadoop pipeline over large FASTQ/A read sets (e.g. GSE80911 WGBS data at 10M-200M reads) where reference indices and inputs must be accessible from every slave node.

name: healthy-cohort-sv-specificity-benchmarking
description: Use when validating the specificity of an SV pathogenicity classifier: SV sets from healthy individuals (e.g. gnomAD) should yield predominantly non-pathogenic calls, so a low non-pathogenic rate flags poor Type-1 error control.

name: held-out-classification-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a trained sequence-based classifier (e.g. BOM/XGBoost on motif counts) must be scored on a held-out test set of labeled CRE sequences, and per-class and aggregate performance metrics are needed for validation.

name: held-out-test-set-performance-evaluation
description: Use when replicating CITRUS's performance comparison: you have output_dataset_CITRUS.pkl with test-set predictions and need Spearman/MSE metrics versus the affinity regression baseline.

name: hg19-dm3-genome-coordinate-handling
description: Use when a ChIP-seq spike-in workflow must process reads and bins over two different genome assemblies (e.g. human hg19 sample plus fruit fly dm3 spike-in) and requires consistent bin segmentation and BAM read totals for both.

name: hg19-motif-ranking-database-usage
description: Use when binarized cisTopic topic regions from a human (hg19) single-cell ATAC-seq dataset must be annotated with enriched TF motifs to identify master regulators per topic.

name: hi-c-compartment-dynamics-interpretation
description: Use when you have compartment scores (e.g., 100 kb bin PCA scores) for three or more ordered Hi-C time points and need to cluster bins by their relative trajectory across the full time course instead of comparing single stage transitions.

name: hi-c-coverage-bias-normalization
description: Use when cis-interaction fragment-pair tables (frag1, frag2, cov_frag1, cov_frag2, freq, dist) at ~40 kb resolution show coverage-dependent ligation bias and you need coverage-normalized interaction frequencies or reproducible replicates.

name: hi-c-enclave-hierarchy-annotation
description: Use when a BHi-Cect output (nested tree list plus named per-cluster locus list) needs nestedness scoring and enrichment against epigenomic tracks to test whether nesting along the BPT relates to chromatin activity.

name: hi-c-input-table-preprocessing
description: Use when raw Hi-C or pcHi-C feature tables (e.g. GM19204.chr17.cis.feature.gz with columns frag1, frag2, cov_frag1, cov_frag2, freq, dist) must be cleaned before normalization or reproducibility scoring.

name: hi-c-interaction-modeling
description: Use when fitting a generative model of Hi-C interaction counts (e.g. CscoreTool-M) where expected counts Fij must incorporate Rabl-position effects, bias factors, and per-window sub-compartment probabilities, and the likelihood of observed trans reads is needed.

name: hi-c-loop-calling-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing a Hi-C loop caller (e.g., GILoop) against machine-learning baselines like Peakachu on matched contact maps, requiring PR-AUC, APA enrichment, and loop-recovery evaluation against a ground-truth loop set.

name: hi-c-reproducibility-scoring-hic-spector
description: Use when you have cis-interaction contact maps of two biological replicates (e.g., 40 kb-resolution chr17 maps) and need to quantify and compare how well normalization methods (covNorm, ICE, KR, SCN) improve replicate reproducibility.

name: hi-c-significant-contact-calling
description: Use when you have covNorm distance-normalized contact tables (frag1/frag2, cov, freq, dist) and need p-value/FDR-based significant long-range interaction calling.

name: hi-c-trans-interaction-simulation-from-compartment-model
description: Use when validating that a sub-compartment inference method recovers known compartment scores from simulated Hi-C trans-interaction data, or when testing how low sequencing depth can go before inference degrades.

name: hic-cluster-loci-annotation
description: Use when BHi-Cect spectral clustering of IMR90 (or similar) Hi-C data has produced a tree of enclaves plus a named list of loci per cluster, and you need to relate enclave regulatory content to ChIP-seq data (e.g. ten TFs) via contingency-table analysis.

name: hic-compartment-calling
description: Use when you need genome-wide A/B compartment scores from one or more Hi-C contact maps (bulk, pseudo-replicate, or pseudo-bulk single-cell) at resolutions from 100 kb down to 5-10 kb, or comparable scores across replicates/conditions.

name: hic-compartment-score-quantile-normalization-across-replicates
description: Use when comparing Hi-C compartment scores (e.g., PC1 at 100 kb bins) across two or more conditions or replicates (e.g., mouse ESC vs NPC) so scores are on a common scale before significance testing.

name: hic-contact-map-downsampling
description: Use when you have replicated pairwise Hi-C contact maps (e.g., ESC vs NPC at 100 kb) with known full-depth dcHiC calls and need to determine the minimum sequencing depth at which differential compartments remain recoverable.

name: hic-contact-map-downsampling-and-realignment
description: Use when a deeply sequenced Hi-C dataset must be reduced to controlled sequencing-depth levels to test how data depth affects a structure-prediction or interaction-detection model.

name: hic-contact-map-loading-and-normalization
description: Use when raw Hi-C contact maps (.cool files or Juicer dump text) must be loaded, KR-normalized, converted to O/E matrices, and sequencedepth-aligned before patch sampling or loop calling.

name: hic-contact-map-loop-prediction
description: Use when you have a .cool/.hic genome-wide contact map at ~10 kb resolution plus a bedpe positive training set from an orthogonal assay (ChIA-PET, HiChIP, Capture Hi-C) and need supervised chromatin loop predictions.

name: hic-contact-map-percentile-normalization
description: Use when raw Hi-C contact frequency matrices (e.g. KR-normalized 5 kb bins) must be converted into distance-aware, percentile-binned skeleton labels to train or run inference with deepC.

name: hic-contact-map-preprocessing
description: Use when raw Hi-C matrices from new cell types must be reformatted into the DNALONGBENCH/Akita 448x448 contact map .tfr format so that load_data(task_name='contact_map_prediction') can consume them.

name: hic-contact-map-reproducibility-scoring
description: Use when you have two 40 kb-resolution Hi-C contact maps (e.g., biological replicates, normalized vs reference, or downsampled vs full data) and need a single reproducibility score to compare normalization methods or sequencing-depth robustness.

name: hic-contact-map-target-processing
description: Use when raw Hi-C contact matrices must be converted into fixed-resolution (5 kb skeleton) binned interaction targets to train a sequence-based chromatin interaction predictor such as deepC.

name: hic-contact-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have a PCR-duplicate-removed ChIA-PET bedpe file (e.g. prefixname.rmdup.bedpe) and need a genome-binned 2D contact map for visualization instead of, or in addition to, loop calls.

name: hic-contact-matrix-downsampling
description: Use when benchmarking loop callers across sequencing depths, training GILoop branches at their preferred matrix density (GCN at 10%, U-Net at full depth), or testing robustness of CTCF loop calling on sparse Hi-C libraries.

name: hic-contact-matrix-graph-modeling
description: Use when raw (non-imputed) bulk or single-cell Hi-C contact matrices must be converted into weighted-graph inputs for structural-entropy-based TLD/TAD prediction, including sparse single-cell data.

name: hic-contact-matrix-noise-perturbation
description: Use when benchmarking TAD/TLD predictors for robustness on sparse Hi-C data, e.g., single-cell-level downsampled bulk Hi-C matrices (0.025% sampling rate, 40 kb binsize), by comparing predictions on noisy vs. original matrices.

name: hic-contact-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when raw .hic files (e.g., GM12878 accession 4DNFI1UEG1HD from 4DN/GSE63525) must be dumped into NxN KR-normalized matrices and chunked into 400x400 submatrices before GAE-based TAD calling.

name: hic-contact-matrix-tld-detection
description: Use when input is a raw intra-chromosome Hi-C contact matrix (n×n or sparse edge format) from bulk or single-cell data and hierarchical TAD/TLD boundaries must be predicted, especially for sparse scHi-C where imputation is undesirable.

name: hic-contact-normalization
description: Use when raw Hi-C or capture Hi-C fragment-pair tables (frag1, frag2, cov_frag1, cov_frag2, freq, dist) need bias removal, distance-background normalization, or significance calling of cis long-range contacts.

name: hic-differential-interaction-testing
description: Use when comparing Hi-C datasets (e.g., ESC vs NPC) and you need loop-level differences, not just compartment-level calls, specifically for interactions anchored in bins flagged as significant differential compartments.

name: hic-distance-dependent-background-normalization
description: Use when you have coverage-normalized Hi-C fragment-pair tables (bias-removed residuals with freq and dist columns) and need to remove the genomic distance-dependent background to obtain distance-normalized interaction frequencies.

name: hic-distance-normalization-to-correlation-matrices
description: Use when raw chromosome-wise Hi-C contact maps (up to 10 kb resolution) must be prepared for PCA/SVD compartment calling, so that distance-decay effects are removed before eigen-decomposition.

name: hic-fastq-adapter-trimming
description: Use when paired-end Hi-C (or Micro-C/ChIA-PET) FASTQ files must be adapter- and quality-trimmed before alignment, e.g. at the start of a Microcket run on MuSC Hi-C libraries from GSE189841.

name: hic-fragment-filtering
description: Use when preparing Hi-C fragment files (e.g. from extractHAIRS --hic 1) for haplotype assembly and you need to drop putative trans-homolog linkage errors before phasing with SpecHap.

name: hic-graph-embedding-analysis
description: Use when you have low-dimensional node embeddings (e.g., 16-dim GAE output from 400x400 Hi-C submatrices) and must assign a density-based cluster label to every genomic bin without specifying the number of clusters.

name: hic-matrix-resolution-to-bin-length-conversion
description: Use when you have per-bin cluster labels from an N×N intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact matrix and need to delineate TAD boundaries as genomic intervals for downstream visualization or evaluation.

name: hic-matrix-visualization-compatibility
description: Use when a ChIA-PET bedpe interaction file (e.g. in.rmDup.bedpe) needs to be binned into a genome-wide 2D contact matrix for heatmap-style visualization with Hi-C tools such as HiCPlotter.

name: hic-patch-sampling-and-tiling
description: Use when preparing Hi-C cis-contact matrices as training inputs for dual-branch loop callers like GILoop, i.e. when a contact map must be converted into paired image-view patches and graph-view adjacency samples.

name: hic-read-depth-downsampling
description: Use when you need to determine how many Hi-C sub-compartments are statistically supported at reduced sequencing depth, or to test the robustness of sub-compartment inference to read-depth reduction by sweeping N_subcompartment and comparing AIC minima.

name: hic-sub-compartment-model-order-sweep
description: Use when you must choose how many sub-compartments CscoreTool-M should infer for a Hi-C dataset at 100 kb resolution, e.g. testing 0.1x/0.01x down-sampled GM12878 contacts against candidate compartment counts.

name: hic-subcompartment-probabilistic-inference
description: Use when Hi-C interaction summary data (HOMER HiCsummary format) must be segmented into more than the canonical A/B compartments — e.g. inferring 5–10 sub-compartments, quantifying cell-population heterogeneity, or deconvolving mixed cell-type samples into cell-type-specific profiles.

name: hic-valid-pairs-filtering-statistics
description: Use when paired-end Hi-C (or Micro-C/ChIA-PET) FASTQ libraries need alignment, valid-pair filtering, and QC statistics comparable to Table 1 alignment rates, e.g. replicating MuSC Hi-C stats from GSE189841.

name: hiccups-local-poisson-background-loop-detection
description: Use when you have a high-resolution (e.g., 10 kb) normalized Hi-C matrix in .hic or .cool format and need to call statistically enriched loop pixels with a local Poisson background model, or when benchmarking loop callers against each other.

name: hichip-plac-seq-pseudolinker-handling
description: Use when processing paired-end HiChIP or PLAC-seq FASTQ data whose junction sequence between the two genomic tags differs from the ChIA-PET bridge linker and needs assay-aware linker scanning before mapping.

name: hidden-markov-model-implementation
description: Use when you need to build or reimplement an HMM/state-space model that jointly scores nucleosome and transcription factor occupancy genome-wide from paired-end MNase-seq and/or ATAC-seq data plus genomic sequence.

name: hidden-markov-model-occupancy-inference
description: Use when you have paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq reads plus genome sequence for S. cerevisiae and need probabilistic nucleosome/TF occupancy scores or dyad positions across the genome.

name: hidden-markov-model-viterbi-implementation
description: Use when short-read ChIP-Seq coverage has been binned (e.g., 25 bp HDF counts) and consecutive bins must be statistically classified into enriched vs. background states with a probability model that explicitly captures overdispersion and excess zeros.

name: hierarchical-chromosome-cluster-functional-annotation
description: Use when you have a BHi-Cect nested cluster list plus ChIP-seq tracks and want to know which GO biological functions are enriched among genes whose loci fall into specific bottom enclaves.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-epigenomic-profiles
description: Use when a sparse single-cell count matrix (scChIP-seq/scATAC-seq bins or peaks) with known or hypothesized sub-populations must be grouped via hierarchical clustering on a PCA/feature-space embedding and quantitatively benchmarked by ARI.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-pwm-motifs
description: Use when a large set of predicted sequence motifs (e.g. DESSO motifs from 690 ENCODE ChIP-seq datasets) must be de-duplicated into representative motifs and classified as matching documented JASPAR/TRANSFAC motifs or as novel.

name: hierarchical-dendrogram-cutting
description: Use when a dendrogram from complete-linkage agglomerative clustering of DTW-aligned peak profiles must be cut into clusters whose count reflects true underlying patterns or is chosen interactively near the leaves.

name: hierarchical-density-noise-handling
description: Use when you have a dense node-embedding matrix (e.g. 16-dim per bin from a GAE encoder) and need per-point cluster labels without pre-specifying the number of clusters, including density-varying structure and noise points.

name: hierarchical-drug-clustering-ward-d
description: Use when you need to organize drugs by similarity of their RePhine TR response signatures and validate that drugs with the same mechanism of action (e.g., MEK, RAF, EGFR inhibitors) co-cluster.

name: hierarchical-nestedness-scoring
description: Use when you already have a BHi-Cect tree (nested list plus named locus-per-cluster list) and need to quantify each cluster's nested position and test whether nesting within global clusters associates with epigenomic activity (DNase, LAD, ChromHMM, CAGE, RNA-seq, TF, RNAP2, CTCF/RAD21/CHD1).

name: histone-mark-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have mESC (or analogous) ChIP-seq BAM files for chromatin marks plus ranked RNA-seq expression data and need to test whether mark signal correlates with gene expression groups (high/moderate/silent).

name: histone-mark-odds-ratio-computation
description: Use when you have two sets of genomic intervals (e.g., true vs predicted regulatory indels) plus interval annotations for chromatin interactions or histone marks and need per-feature enrichment odds ratios.

name: histone-mark-quality-metric-stratification
description: Use when you need to compute the fraction of narrowPeak peaks falling in ENCODE union DHS regions per ChIP-seq sample and compare overlap-ratio distributions across histone mark/factor categories as a QC stratification.

name: histone-modification-chipseq-data-processing
description: Use when processing ChIP-Seq BED files of histone modifications (e.g., H3K4me3, H3K27me3) to call enriched regions with HPeak and to assess whether different peak-calling algorithms produce overlapping peak sets.

name: histone-modification-differential-region-calling
description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq profiles of broad diffuse histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3, H3K36me3, H3K79me2) between two samples/cell lines and peak-style callers would yield false positives/negatives.

name: histone-modification-em-mixture-fitting
description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq profiles of broad histone modifications (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) between two samples to call modified or differentially modified regions, and peak-style callers would misclassify diffuse signals.

name: histone-modification-peak-calling-comparison
description: Use when a qPCR-validated or otherwise gold-standard ChIP-seq dataset of a broad histone mark (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) is available and you need to quantify which peak caller detects modified versus unmodified regions via sensitivity-specificity/ROC analysis.

name: histone-modification-peak-profile-processing
description: Use when benchmarking peak-shape clustering or alignment methods and you need ground-truth-labelled synthetic peak profiles derived from real ChIP-Seq (e.g. ENCODE H3K4me3 K562) seed regions with known cluster-of-origin labels.

name: histone-modification-peak-set-processing
description: Use when you have two BED-format ChIP-seq peak lists (chromosome, start, end) for different histone marks and need to partition their union into mark-specific and overlapping classes (e.g. active/bivalent/silent promoters).

name: histone-modification-state-structure-verification
description: Use when reproducing or auditing histoneHMM's emission model: you have binned bivariate ChIP-seq read counts from two samples (e.g. BN vs SHR) and need to verify the four-component copula fit yields coherent modified/unmodified/differential state classes.

name: historical-qc-atlas-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a new ChIP-seq or DNase-seq sample needs QC assessment against historical public data, or when validating whether read-layer metrics (FastQC score, mapped ratio, PBC) are assay-type independent.

name: hmm-based-enriched-region-detection
description: Use when calling protein-DNA binding sites from ChIP-Seq BED or ELAND read files (single-end or paired-end), especially when reproducing HPeak peak counts or comparing peak callers on datasets such as STAT1, NRSF, H3K4me3, or H3K27me3.

name: hmm-based-occupancy-modeling
description: Use when you have paired-end MNase-seq and/or ATAC-seq data plus genome sequence and need probabilistic genome-wide occupancy profiles of nucleosomes and DNA-binding factors, especially to benchmark against NucleoATAC, DANPOS2, or MACS2+FIMO.

name: hmm-coverage-profile-modeling
description: Use when calling protein-DNA binding peaks from short-read ChIP-Seq data with explicit statistical modeling of sequencing noise, or when reproducing HPeak peak counts and motif-enrichment comparisons against other peak-callers on datasets like the NRSF ChIP-Seq data.

name: hmm-differential-call-post-processing
