description: Use when you have histoneHMM differential calls for a broad histone mark (e.g. H3K9me3 female-vs-mouse male) and need to evaluate them against a defined gene set by base-pair and gene-count overlap.

name: hmm-initialization-from-summary-statistics
description: Use when calling ChIP-Seq peaks with a two-state HMM over 25 bp HDF coverage bins and you need defensible starting values for transition and GP/ZIP emission parameters prior to Viterbi refinement.

name: hmm-posterior-decoding-forward-backward
description: Use when you need probabilistic, per-genomic-region classifications of ChIP-seq enrichment for broad histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) rather than binary peak calls, in one- or two-sample comparisons.

name: hns-doublet-peak-detection
description: Use when ChIP-seq peak coordinates need to be scanned for paired peaks (doublets) with an intervening trough, or when relating doublet peaks to a second transcription factor's ChIP-seq binding sites within a fixed genomic distance.

name: hns-nucleation-site-prediction
description: Use when a promoter or intergenic FASTA must be scanned for H-NS nucleation motifs to test whether H-NS binding sites overlap established LuxR binding sites, as for PluxCDABE.

name: hns-silencing-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when reproducing the H-NS regulon from V. harveyi RNA-seq data: raw FASTQ in GEO (e.g. GSE136191), strains wild-type/Δhns/ΔluxR/ΔluxR Δhns, and the goal is gene counts regulated by H-NS including luxCDABE recovery.

name: holdout-chromosome-pearson-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a retrained deepC model (e.g. trained on 1B/100M/10M downsampled GSE63525 GM12878 Hi-C) must be quantitatively evaluated on held-out chromosomes 16 and 17 via predicted-vs-observed Pearson correlation.

name: holm-bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many candidate motifs (e.g., DiNAMO lattice nodes scored by mutual information) each yield a raw 2x2 contingency-table P-value that must be jointly corrected before applying a significance threshold.

name: homer-known-motif-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when scATAC-seq clusters (e.g., Leiden assignments from SCALE on a Breast_Tumor.h5ad dataset) need functional interpretation through motif enrichment in cluster-specific open chromatin peaks.

name: hoogsteen-triplex-sequence-scanning
description: Use when the goal is to predict RNA:DNA:DNA triple-helix interactions in silico from an ssRNA transcript (FASTA) and a set of dsDNA regulatory regions (multi-FASTA), e.g. lncRNA-to-promoter binding screens.

name: hot-region-control-matching-by-tf-occupancy
description: Use when comparing a genomic signal track (e.g. G4-ChIP-seq IP vs input/control) over HOT regions and you need control intervals matched on the number of overlapping TF ChIP-seq peaks to separate feature-specific signal from hyper-ChIPable occupancy effects.

name: hot-region-percentile-threshold-calling
description: Use when you need to define or reproduce HOT regions computationally from many TF ChIP-seq narrowPeak peak files (e.g. ENCODE/modENCODE) for a genome like hg19, mm9, dm3 or ce10 using summit-density percentile thresholding.

name: hpc-cluster-job-submission
description: Use when a ChIA-PIPE (or similar) pipeline run is too large for an interactive shell — e.g., 200–400 million read-pair libraries from ENCODE4/4DN — and a PBS-scheduler cluster is available.

name: hpc-cluster-parallel-scheduling
description: Use when running MEDIPIPE's Snakemake Snakefile over many cfMeDIP-seq FASTQ samples on a cluster (e.g. SLURM) or stand-alone machine, and per-sample Conda environments must be auto-deployed for parallel execution.

name: ht-selex-affinity-regression
description: Use when HT-SELEX per-cycle enrichment files (proteins/{protein}/{cycle}.txt, e.g. from ENA PRJEB14744 or PRJEB29730) are available and per-TF k-mer binding affinities must be predicted or benchmarked.

name: ht-selex-cross-cycle-enrichment-correlation-analysis
description: Use when running selex_regressor.py (DNAffinity) across multiple HT-SELEX cycles and you need to detect/remove cases whose enrichment between cycles is inconsistent before training or evaluating the regressor.

name: ht-selex-enrichment-data-preparation
description: Use when input HT-SELEX data must be converted into per-cycle enrichment files (proteins/{protein}/{cycle}.txt) for regressor training, and inconsistent enrichment cases across cycles need to be filtered out before feature extraction.

name: human-mouse-orthology-phenotype-integration
description: Use when a candidate gene list must be linked to a congenital-abnormality phenotype group and scored for human or mouse gene-phenotype support, e.g. to build POSTRE's genePhenoScore table from hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype.txt, mp.obo and HMD_HumanPhenotype.rpt.

name: hypergeometric-driver-gene-enrichment-testing
description: Use when a ranked candidate driver list (e.g., iEDGE Rank-1 cis genes) must be tested for significant overlap with known cancer driver databases to validate a mediation/differential-expression prioritization.

name: hypergeometric-gene-set-overrepresentation-analysis
description: Use when you have per-cluster differentially enriched regions from single-cell ChIP/epigenomic data (e.g. H3K27me3 scChIP-seq) and need pathway-level interpretation by gene-set over-representation.

name: hypergeometric-pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have pruned lists of significant cis/trans gene sets from iEDGE differential expression and mediation analysis and need to identify recurrently enriched MSigDB pathways across multiple alterations (e.g., TCGA BRCA SCNAs).

name: idr-reproducibility-filtering
description: Use when building a gold-standard set of experimentally determined lncRNA:DNA binding sites from raw fastq files with replicate structure (even/odd probe sets), where reproducible peaks are needed as positives for prediction benchmarks.

name: image-based-loop-prediction-model-training
description: Use when you need to train or reproduce a loop-calling model on Hi-C cis-contact maps represented as image patches (KR-normalized O/E matrices or .cool input), including low-depth downsampled runs.

name: imbalanced-class-resampling
description: Use when building a supervised classifier (e.g. a Keras/TensorFlow variant-scoring network) from a training set where positives are orders of magnitude rarer than negatives — in iMEGES, 574 dsQTL positives vs 27,735 negatives — so the sigmoid output is not dominated by the majority class.

name: imbalanced-dataset-resampling-with-rose
description: Use when training or evaluating a variant/gene classifier on datasets with extreme positive-to-negative imbalance (e.g., PGC schizophrenia GWAS-derived sets with hundreds of positives and tens of thousands of negatives), prior to fitting the model and computing ROC/AUC.

name: immune-and-epithelial-motif-interpretation
description: Use when you have cluster assignments from scATAC-seq data (e.g. SCALE Leiden clusters on an h5ad like Breast_Tumor.h5ad) and need to assign biological identity to clusters via enriched TF binding motifs in type-specific peaks.

name: immune-cell-subset-statistical-testing
description: Use when you have per-donor cell population proportions (flow cytometry) plus donor metadata (continuous age, sex) and need to test which factor—age, sex, or their interaction—is most strongly associated with each cell subset.

name: immune-response-cascade-reconstruction
description: Use when time-series RNA-seq expression data plus TF–gene interactions and pathway gene sets are available and the goal is to identify TFs regulating pathway cascades at specific time points.

name: imprinted-dmr-allele-specific-methylation-calling
description: Use when bisulfite sequencing data (bismark/bsmap/biscuit .cov output) must be tested for allele-specific methylation at imprinted DMRs or X-linked CGIs, e.g. detecting state-dependent imprinting loss in naive ES cells.

name: imprinted-locus-methylation-interpretation
description: Use when a WGBS/bisulfite-seq dataset must be interpreted at a known imprinted or allele-specifically methylated locus, and per-read methylation phased by a heterozygous SNP genotype is needed.

name: imprinting-dmr-methylation-analysis
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon/pyrosequencing methylation data for an imprinted DMR (e.g. KCNQ1OT1, H19/IGF2) include standard controls (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) plus case/control samples and you must correct PCR bias and call hyper/hypo-methylated cases.

name: imprinting-locus-allele-specific-loop-interpretation
description: Use when a deduplicated ChIA-PET bedpe (e.g., GM12878 CTCF) is available together with phased heterozygous genotypes, and the goal is to determine which chromatin loops at an imprinted locus are maternal- versus paternal-specific.

name: imputation-method-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether an imputation method recovers cell-type-specific signal in sparse scATAC-seq data, e.g. comparing SCALE's adata.obsm['imputed'] matrix against scImpute, SAVER, MAGIC or scVI via meta-cell correlation.

name: imputed-accessibility-matrix-handling
description: Use when a raw, sparse scATAC-seq peak matrix has been denoised with SCALE and the task requires the numerical imputed matrix (adata.obsm['imputed']) as input to downstream tools like chromVAR.

name: in-silico-cell-mixing-assembly
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell epigenomic clustering methods on scChIP-seq/scATAC-seq data where no natural labels exist and a ground-truth cell-type mix with known labels is required to compute ARIs.

name: in-silico-deletion-perturbation-prediction
description: Use when you need to rank functional genomic elements (CTF sites, promoters, enhancers) by their predicted impact on chromatin interactions, i.e. identify which elements underlie genome folding patterns from sequence.

name: in-silico-gene-knockout-perturbation
description: Use when you have a trained CITRUS model output (hid_tmr TF activities), a binary SGA alteration matrix, and want to predict which TFs are associated with specific somatic alterations per cancer type.

name: in-silico-mixture-generation-from-reference-profiles
description: Use when benchmarking a methylation deconvolution tool (e.g., DXM) and ground-truth subpopulation profiles and prevalences are needed that cannot be obtained from real mixed samples.

name: in-silico-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking methylation read aligners (e.g., Msuite vs Bismark vs BWA-meth) on ground-truth data, or when stratifying mapping performance by region composition such as CT/GA-rich bins.

name: in-silico-saturated-mutagenesis-analysis
description: Use when you need to dissect which bases and sequence motifs around a non-coding SNP drive a predicted chromatin activity change (e.g., transcription factor binding) for a single variant, at single-base resolution.

name: indel-training-data-preparation
description: Use when building a supervised nc-sindel classifier for tissue-specific regulatory indels and you need to convert indel position/ref/alt files into a CADD + DanQ multi-omics feature table for model training.

name: information-content-heterogeneity-quantification
description: Use when you have CscoreTool-M *_cscore.txt probability outputs and need to measure how heterogeneous sub-compartment localization is across cells, e.g. comparing proliferating vs terminally differentiated cells or G1 vs S/G2 stages.

name: information-content-motif-filtering
description: Use when filtering CNN-derived motif detectors and their TFBS candidate sets from DESSO predict.py output, to discard weak or degenerate motifs before downstream motif comparison or TFBS calling.

name: inla-approximate-bayesian-inference
description: Use when calibrating observed/apparent methylation levels from bisulfite amplicon sequencing of standard controls (known AMP percentages) across multiple CpGs in a CGI or DMR, and a joint Bayesian model with latent Gaussian field inference is needed.

name: insert-size-metrics-profiling
description: Use when processing paired-end cfMeDIP-seq (or cfDNA) BAM alignments within a Snakemake QC pipeline and you need fragment-size distributions and windowed short/long fragmentation ratios as quality-control metrics.

name: interactive-html-qc-report-generation
description: Use when a cfMeDIP-seq (or MeDIP-seq) pipeline has produced per-sample QC outputs (FASTQC, SAMtools, Picard, MEDIPS reports) and they must be aggregated into one interactive HTML summary across samples, groups, or batches.

name: interactive-html-report-generation
description: Use when comparing multiple epigenomic peak files (e.g. ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq, or CUT&Tag/CUT&Run vs ENCODE ChIP-seq H3K27ac reference) and you need QC, overlap statistics, and functional annotation collated in one report.

name: interactive-network-visualization-exploration
description: Use when a time-series regulatory network has been constructed in TSMiner and you need to visually navigate time-specific network maps to identify which TFs interact with pathways and quantify overlaps between pathway-connected TF sets.

name: intrasample-differential-methylation-region-calling
description: Use when dxm_solveMethylation has reconstructed 1- and 2-subpopulation methylation profiles for a heterogeneous bisulfite sequencing sample (eRRBS or Agilent Methyl-Seq BED-like input) and you need per-region i-DMRs, e.g., promoter-level subclonal heterogeneity counts to relate to DLBCL relapse.

name: inverse-normal-transformation-of-pvalues
description: Use when combining non-independent p-values (e.g. correlated methylation promoter/track p-values within a genomic interval) and you need a valid Stouffer-style combination: convert p to Z with qnorm(1 - p/2), then decorrelate using the Cholesky factor of Sigma.

name: ip-control-log2-ratio-computation
description: Use when testing whether a defined region set (e.g., HOT regions) is enriched for R-loops by comparing DRIP-seq IP coverage against RNaseH-treated or mock controls over occupancy-matched control regions.

name: irefweb-interaction-curation
description: Use when assessing whether proteins of interest (e.g. a set of 165 transcription factors occupying HOT regions) can perform a function directly or through direct physical interaction partners, using iRefWeb interaction data joined with a protein-domain scan.

name: iterative-motif-masking-significance-thresholding
description: Use when RIMS-seq Read1/Read2 mpileup files contain C-to-T (and G-to-A) positions and you must de novo identify enriched methylated motifs without a known motif, validating against an expected motif such as CCWGG.

name: iupac-degenerate-motif-discovery
description: Use when a pair of positive (signal.fa) and negative (control.fa) DNA FASTA files is available and the goal is to recover over-represented degenerate IUPAC motifs, e.g. ChIP-seq peak TF binding sites or motifs inducing systematic sequencing errors.

name: iupac-lattice-construction
description: Use when you need to enumerate all degenerate IUPAC motifs of a given length L (e.g., 6-mers for TFBS discovery) from counted L-mers of DNA sequences, ensuring no candidate motif is missed.

name: iupac-motif-lattice-simplification
description: Use when you have an IUPAC motif lattice built from a positive and a negative FASTA dataset and need to score, rank, and prune over-represented degenerate motifs without bias toward occurrence count.

name: jaccard-kernel-computation-single-cell
description: Use when scATAC-seq data must be clustered without predefined peaks: cell-by-bin count matrices (e.g. 5-kb bins in a .snap file) need conversion to a pair-wise cell similarity kernel for dimensionality reduction.

name: jaccard-similarity-cluster-comparison
description: Use when two clustering solutions (e.g., SRIQ vs consensus clustering) exist on the same sample set and you need a quantitative, per-K similarity metric for the derived cluster partitions.

name: jaccard-similarity-computation
description: Use when you have ranked TR output tables from multiple TR identification methods applied to the same epigenomic query region sets and need to quantify overlap of their top-ranked predictions.

name: jaccard-similarity-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when clustering sparse single-cell ATAC-seq profiles without population-level peak calls: raw cell-by-bin (5kb/10kb) accessibility matrices or .snap AM matrices need a cell-level embedding before Leiden clustering.

name: jaspar-motif-loci-handling
description: Use when strand asymmetry analysis needs strand-annotated transcription factor binding site loci, e.g. obtaining CTCF (MA0139.1) motif occurrences on hg38 as BED records with '+'/'-' strand signs to orient ChIP-seq peaks or mutations.

name: jaspar-pwm-based-motif-matching
description: Use when testing the loop-extrusion convergent-orientation rule at two-anchor loop calls: you need CTCF motif occurrence and strand per anchor to classify each loop as convergent, tandem, or divergent against a reference genome such as mm10.

name: java-application-execution-and-configuration
description: Use when a scientific workflow requires running a packaged Java tool (e.g. TSMiner.jar) that needs Java 1.5+, a 1024 MB heap, and manual-specified input/parameter files on a platform-independent system.

name: java-command-line-workflow-execution
description: Use when a multi-step analysis must be executed from a Java command line as an XML-defined workflow with task dependencies, custom success verification, and manual error intervention (release/restart/skip/resolve).

name: java-plugin-api-extension
description: Use when a Watchdog workflow must dispatch tasks to an execution environment not covered by the built-in local, remote SSH, or DRMAA/Slurm executors — e.g. a cloud computing service that does not allow SSH access.

name: joint-cpg-dmr-calibration-modeling
description: Use when calibrating bisulfite amplicon methylation levels across all CpGs in a CGI or DMR and needing to choose among MethylCal's four candidate random-effects models (M1–M4) per assay via the Deviance Information Criterion.

name: joint-probability-estimation
description: Use when each candidate degenerate IUPAC motif carries a 2x2 contingency table (a,b,c,d counts in positive/negative datasets) and you need an occurrence-count-independent score such as MI for ranking or lattice simplification.

name: joint-tsne-embedding-visualization
description: Use when a scATAC-seq embedding (e.g., SnapATAC t-SNE) must be overlaid with cell-type identities predicted by integrating a scRNA-seq reference, to visualize cluster separation or validate label transfer.

name: juicer-hiccups-loop-detection
description: Use when calling or benchmarking chromatin loops from pooled scHi-C contact matrices: run Juicer HiCCUPS on .hic files built from ~371-cell mESC halves at 10KB resolution under both default and optimal parameters, then score replicate overlap against SnapHiC.

name: juicer-pre-hic-conversion
description: Use when a deduplicated PET alignment BAM (unique alignments, MAPQ >= 30, nonredundant PETs) must be rendered as browser-viewable chromatin interaction heat maps in Juicebox.js or HiGlass.

name: k-fold-cross-validation-model-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking regression or classification models on sgRNA screening datasets (e.g., 111,682 sgRNAs x 520 genes) and you need held-out performance estimates comparable across models via cross-validated metrics.

name: k-fold-cross-validation-model-fitting
description: Use when training a DriverPower BMR model on per-element response tables (nMut, nSample, length) with an HDF5 feature matrix of 1373 genomic features and you need a nonlinear, cross-validated fit whose generalization you will assess on held-out test elements.

name: kaplan-meier-survival-curve-estimation
description: Use when you have cancer patient clinical survival data (time, vital status) plus gene expression (e.g., TCGA expression for an eccDNA gene like EGFR) and need to test whether expression level stratification predicts prognosis.

name: kegg-pathway-annotation-mapping
description: Use when a time-series gene expression analysis needs pathway-level interpretation of TF–target networks, and KEGG/Reactome/GO gene-set files must be joined to genes and TFs to identify pathway–regulator interactions.

name: kegg-pathway-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when you have a deduplicated list of gene IDs linked to a TF's binding regions (e.g., from a Region Query of ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks) and need pathway-level interpretation such as KEGG disease pathways.

name: keras-cnn-model-training
description: Use when the input is a dna2vec-encoded SE/TE feature matrix (e.g. ./data/mESC) and a trained super-enhancer vs typical-enhancer classifier is needed, using learning_rate=0.001 and epochs=80.

name: kmeans-clustering-ami-evaluation
description: Use when single-cell TLD or chromatin-domain feature matrices (e.g., TF-IDF/SVD embeddings of deDoc2 TLD predictions) need to be clustered and quantitatively scored against known cell-type labels via adjusted mutual information.

name: kmeans-trajectory-clustering
description: Use when a normalized feature-by-donor abundance matrix (peaks or genes) has samples ordered by age and you need to detect and classify features showing genuine monotonic or non-monotonic temporal trends over adult lifespan.

name: kmer-feature-extraction-from-dna-physical-properties
description: Use when raw k-mer/sequence-affinity data (e.g. HT-SELEX cycle files, PBM intensity tables) must be converted into physicochemical feature vectors before training an ML affinity regressor.

name: kmer-frequency-computation
description: Use when you have a set of labeled genomic regions (e.g. HOT vs COLD from ChIP-seq analysis) and need sequence-derived features — k-mer frequencies, GC content, CpG O/E ratio — for a classifier or feature-importance analysis.

name: kmer-svm-classifier-training
description: Use when benchmarking sequence-based classifiers on binary CRE-vs-background tasks (e.g., mouse E8.25 distal CREs) and a k-mer kernel SVM baseline such as LS-GKM is required.

name: kmer-undersampling-for-affinity-training-sets
description: Use when preparing uPBM training data for DNAffinity's random-forest regressor: 35-mer affinities are dominated by weak binders and the PWM-defined high-affinity motif must be emphasized (10x weight) after MEME-based trimming.

name: kmer-variability-deviation-analysis
description: Use when scATAC-seq/DNase counts in peaks vary between cells or samples and de novo motif discovery is the goal: rank bias-corrected k-mer deviations by covariance, assemble PWMs with assembleKmers, then match to JASPAR via pwmDistance.

name: knn-missing-value-imputation
description: Use when an input gene-expression or methylation matrix (e.g., from golubEsets, ALL, or recount2) contains missing values (NAs) that must be filled before feature selection and consensus partitioning.

name: knowledge-distillation-model-training
description: Use when a first-round MLP has already predicted cell types in a target scATAC-seq gene score matrix and you need to retrain on low-entropy anchor cells to classify the remaining non-anchor cells.

name: knowledge-distillation-pseudolabel-celltyping
description: Use when annotating scATAC-seq cells with an scATAC-seq reference: gene score matrices (e.g., from ArchR) exist for both reference and target, and two-round prediction with entropy-based anchor selection is feasible (default when target has > 1,000 cells).

name: known-transcription-factor-recovery-benchmarking
description: Use when a time-series regulatory-network tool must be benchmarked on recovery of a curated list of known TFs, requiring matched runs, P-value cut-offs (0.01/0.05), unique-hit tallies, and ROC/AUC analysis.

name: kolmogorov-smirnov-distribution-comparison
description: Use when two sets of network modules each carry per-gene significance/score values and the question is whether one method's modules are enriched for high-scoring genes relative to the other (KS p-value comparison).

name: kolmogorov-smirnov-pancancer-enrichment-aggregation
description: Use when replicating the pan-cancer iEDGE evaluation: per-type Rank-1 cis driver lists are available and you must test known-driver enrichment per cancer type and then assess aggregate significance (15/19 types FDR<0.05, KS p=2.5e-13).

name: kr-normalized-hic-data-handling
description: Use when raw KR-normalized Hi-C contact frequency matrices must be converted into the discrete 1-10 percentile skeleton tags deepC needs for training or prediction input.

name: lamin-b1-chromatin-association-analysis
description: Use when you need to validate A/B compartment score tracks (e.g., dcHiC PC1 scores at 100 kb) against an orthogonal Lamin B1 DamID/Data signal track via genome-wide Pearson correlation, or to benchmark concordance between compartment-calling methods.

name: lamina-associated-domain-correlation-analysis
description: Use when Hi-C-derived sub-compartment scores (e.g. CscoreTool-M *_cscore.txt outputs) need to be linked genome-wide to lamina-associated domains such as early-G1 cTSA-seq LAD maps (GSE224282) to test which sub-compartment corresponds to lamina-proximal chromatin.

name: lda-collapsed-gibbs-sampler-execution
description: Use when a cisTopic object holding a binarized accessibility matrix (e.g. 5,335 PBMC cells × ~97k regions) is ready and a sweep of LDA topic models across a topic-number grid is required for subsequent model selection.

name: lda-log-likelihood-comparison
description: Use when cisTopic has fitted multiple LDA models (e.g. 2–40 topics via runModels) on single-cell ATAC-seq data and you must pick one optimal topic number for downstream cell-state and cis-regulatory topic analysis.

name: leave-one-out-cross-validation
description: Use when benchmarking cross-species regulatory-element mapping accuracy with matched orthologous functional genomic datasets (e.g. 67 matched human-mouse ENCODE ChIP-seq/DNase-seq sets), where each dataset must be held out in turn.

name: leave-one-out-cross-validation-of-calibration-models
description: Use when you have calibration data on standard controls of known methylation percentage (e.g. 0–100% AMP dilutions) measured across multiple CpGs and need to compare predictive performance of competing calibration models per assay.

name: leiden-clustering-of-single-cell-data
description: Use when a snap-format scATAC-seq dataset has been filtered and dimensionality-reduced (e.g. via runDimReduct on the Jaccard-normalized cell-by-bin matrix) and you need unsupervised cell-type clustering without prior peak annotation.

name: liftover-genomic-coordinate-mapping
description: Use when motif-based (BOM) predictions transfer across species and you need to quantify how many predicted CREs lack detectable cross-species sequence alignment, as in mouse-trained models tested on human fetal CREs.

name: liftover-mapping-rate-precision-comparison
description: Use when fine-mapped SNP coordinates (e.g., hg38 GWAS SNPs) must be lifted to another genome (e.g., mouse mm10) and a head-to-head mapping-rate vs. precision comparison of UCSC liftOver and AdaLiftOver is needed.

name: liftover-precision-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing cross-species regulatory-element mapping precision of AdaLiftOver vs UCSC liftOver, or when validating liftOver-based SNP-to-gene mappings against a known positive-control gene list such as BMD genes.

name: likelihood-ratio-test-gene-set-partitioning
description: Use when a time-series expression matrix must be split into bifurcation groups to define candidate branching points of a tree-structure (input-output hidden Markov) model prior to Baum-Welch training, as in TSMiner's LR mouse liver regeneration RNA-seq analysis.

name: likelihood-ratio-testing
description: Use when testing whether a candidate driver element's target gene is differentially expressed between samples mutated in that element and wild-type samples, while explicitly correcting for somatic copy-number state (SCNA) and tumour tissue label.

name: limma-linear-model-testing
description: Use when paired copy-number/alteration calls (e.g., GISTIC2.0 focal SCNA peaks) and a log2 gene-expression matrix over the same tumor samples must be tested for cis/trans differential expression with limma linear models.

name: line1-strand-and-age-stratification-analysis
description: Use when Skipper has flagged enriched repetitive elements in eCLIP IP-vs-input experiments and you need to characterize binding orientation and evolutionary age of LINE1 elements for specific RBPs such as MATR3 or SAFB2.

name: linear-model-covariate-adjustment
description: Use when evaluating how one prediction parameter (e.g. minimal TPX length 8/10/12/16) affects accuracy (AUC) across multiple conditions, and confounders like peak filtering method or masking covariate must be controlled.

name: linear-regression-gene-expression-modeling
description: Use when you have paired chromatin accessibility (DNase1-seq) and RNA-seq expression data across many samples/cell types and need to identify putative REMs that explain expression variation of specific genes.

name: linkage-graph-construction
description: Use when building the weighted undirected linkage graph that SpecHap needs for spectral haplotype phasing, starting from extractHAIRS fragment files (10X/Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, ONT, paired-end NGS).

name: linkage-graph-spectral-eigendecomposition
description: Use when phasing diploid SNVs from fragment files generated by WGS, Hi-C, 10X linked-reads, PacBio SMRT or Oxford Nanopore data, and you want a spectral graph-theory alternative to MEC/max-cut iterative optimization.

name: linked-read-fragment-filtering
description: Use when phasing 10× linked-read data (e.g. with SpecHap or HapCUT2) and fragments must be filtered so that barcoded fragments spanning distant loci or low-quality reads do not corrupt haplotype blocks.

name: linked-read-methylation-extraction
description: Use when you need read-level methylation linkage (0/1/- encoding per CpG column) across spatially linked CpGs in defined BED regions from Bismark SAM alignments, e.g. to test whether methylation changes reflect altered cellular populations.

name: linker-filtering-qc-count-reporting
description: Use when starting from raw paired-end ChIA-PET FASTQ reads (e.g., LDK0004-ds_*.fastq.gz) and you must detect the bridge linker and categorize read pairs before mapping.

name: linker-mismatch-sensitivity-benchmarking
description: Use when processing bridge-linker ChIA-PET FASTQ reads and you must quantify how much PET rescue a fuzzy linker search (e.g., -e 1 vs -e 0) yields before fixing the trimming stringency.

name: literature-curated-data-harmonization
description: Use when building or reproducing an integrated catalog that combines pipeline-derived records with literature-curation records and you must reconcile provenance and emit aggregate statistics.

name: literature-marker-gene-curation
description: Use when building or extending a cell taxonomy reference database of literature-curated marker genes (like CellMatch) to support automatic cluster annotation in scRNA-seq pipelines such as scCATCH.

name: liver-regeneration-case-analysis-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing the TSMiner mouse LR case analysis (GSE95135 partial hepatectomy RNA-seq) or when rebuilding the text-mined reference sets of 113 LR-associated TFs and 58 KEGG pathways for sensitivity evaluation.

name: lncrna-binding-site-analysis
description: Use when comparing TPX prediction scoring functions (e.g. Triplexator potential match-count vs thermal stability) for lncRNA binding sites, or when validating that a stability-based TPX score discriminates experimentally supported peaks from matched genomic negatives.

name: lncrna-genomic-triplex-prediction
description: Use when predicting RNA:DNA:DNA triplex interactions between an lncRNA transcript (ssRNA FASTA) and genomic/promoter regions (dsDNA multi-FASTA), needing Hoogsteen-rule scanning, RNA secondary-structure masking, and thermal-stability scoring.

name: lncrna-tpx-evidence-classification
description: Use when lncRNAs have experimentally determined genomic binding sites (e.g. ChIRP/CHART/RADICL-seq peaks) but no prior triplex-mechanism evidence, and the goal is to quantify statistical support for DNA binding via TPX formation.

name: lncrna-transcript-sequence-retrieval
description: Use when a study needs canonical lncRNA transcript sequences (e.g. the 7 TPX-validated lncRNAs MEG3, Meg3, lncSmad7, NEAT1, TERC, CDKN2B-AS1) from a fixed annotation release before running sequence-based prediction tools.

name: local-correlation-structure-preservation
description: Use when testing enrichment or overlap of genomic ranges (e.g. caQTLs/SNPs, CREs, ATAC peaks) against a segmentation where naive shuffling would overstate significance due to spatial correlation.

name: local-regression-signal-correction
description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq conditions (e.g. GSK126-treated H3K27me3, fulvestrant ER, EPZ5676 H3K79me2 series) where spike-in ChIP-Rx or tag removal normalization overcorrects background signal between conditions.

name: loci-significance-testing
description: Use when RRBS-derived per-locus epiallele frequency vectors (phi_s from bed_marginal) are available for matched normal and multi-region tumour samples and the goal is to find loci whose epiallele composition differs significantly between normal and cancer tissue.

name: locus-tag-join-annotation-integration
description: Use when bulk-downloaded GEO series expression data must be keyed to an organism's gene annotations via locus tags before downstream joins, correlation, or cross-experiment comparison.

name: loess-smoothing-of-pvalue-curves
description: Use when moving-window age-comparison tests (e.g., MANOVA on windowed profiles) yield noisy per-age p-value curves that must be smoothed across several bandwidths and combined before calling breakpoint ages.

name: log-count-linear-regression-eqtl-testing
description: Use when estimating eQTL detection power for low-expressed genes (pseudobulk mean < 5) where scPower's analytic eQTL power is inaccurate, or when validating analytic power with empirical simulation.

name: log-log-scaling-slope-analysis
description: Use when comparing two algorithms' runtime/memory behavior across increasing problem sizes and you need empirical complexity estimates (log-log slopes) plus speedup ratios at matched sizes to validate complexity claims.

name: log-rank-significance-testing
description: Use when two patient groups (e.g., high vs low EGFR expression in TCGA-LGG) have overall survival time and vital status, and you must test survival differences with a log-rank test.

name: logfc-threshold-optimization
description: Use when differential accessibility peaks and differential expression gene sets need objective significance thresholds for enrichment analysis, rather than arbitrary logFC or P-value cutoffs.

name: logistic-probability-aggregation-of-feature-similarities
description: Use when candidate target regions have already been generated by adaptive liftOver and both epigenomic signal similarities (from matched orthologous ENCODE ChIP-seq/DNase-seq datasets) and sequence grammar similarities (motif scanning with jaspar_pfm_list) are available to be scored and filtered.

name: logistic-regression-parameter-training
description: Use when mapping epigenome peaks for a model organism other than mouse (e.g., rat) with no pre-fit parameters, or when refitting parameters on labeled data from a specific tissue/experiment.

name: long-range-dna-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing fine-tuned DNA foundation models against task-specific expert models on genomic prediction tasks with long-range dependencies (e.g., TISP, contact map prediction, eQTL, enhancer-target gene, regulatory sequence activity), or when reproducing PCC/SCC/AUROC benchmark tables.

name: long-range-genomic-dependency-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing fine-tuned DNA foundation models against task-specific expert architectures on genomic prediction tasks whose input sequences span long ranges (up to 1,000,000 bp), e.g. eQTL binary classification over 450,000-bp inputs.

name: long-range-genomic-sequence-modeling
description: Use when evaluating or comparing sequence models on genomic prediction tasks with long-range dependencies (e.g., enhancer-target gene prediction, eQTL, contact map), or when deciding whether a DNA foundation model can replace a task-specific expert model.

name: long-range-regulatory-mechanism-annotation
description: Use when a structural variant from a congenital abnormality patient lacks a coding explanation and you need to identify the affected gene via a long-range regulatory mechanism in a phenotype-matched cell type.

name: long-read-fragment-extraction-pacbio
description: Use when preparing PacBio SMRT (or other long-read) BAM alignments plus a position-sorted, bgzipped VCF as input for diploid haplotype phasing with SpecHap; the phaser consumes fragments, not alignments.

name: long-read-fragment-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing Hi-C proximity-ligation read data for diploid haplotype assembly with SpecHap, and trans-homolog interactions (inferred insertion > 40 Mbp) must be removed from fragment input.

name: long-read-genome-assembly
description: Use when the goal is to regenerate or produce a polished genome assembly from nanopore long reads (optionally with Illumina short reads for correction/polishing) using a reproducible, end-to-end pipeline.

name: long-read-haplotype-assembly
description: Use when you have a bgzipped, tabix-indexed VCF plus a sorted fragment file (10X/Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, ONT, or paired-end NGS) and need fast, memory-efficient diploid phasing, especially for error-prone third-generation long reads.

name: long-read-phasing-workflow-configuration
description: Use when phasing diploid individuals from PacBio SMRT, ONT, Hi-C, 10x linked-reads, or paired-end NGS data and you need to build SpecHap, extract fragments with ExtractHair, and run the phaser on position-sorted bgzipped VCF plus fragment files.

name: loocv-classification-performance-evaluation
description: Use when validating AdaLiftOver's candidate target region scoring on a repertoire of matched cross-species epigenome datasets (e.

name: loop-anchor-enclave-co-membership-quantification
description: Use when comparing how well a chromosome clustering scheme (e.g., BHi-Cect bottom enclaves) versus TAD segmentations contains pairs of DNA loop anchor sites from Hi-C data at a fixed binning resolution.

name: loop-anchor-overlap-verification
description: Use when SnapFISH loop summits have been called from chromatin tracing data and must be validated against known anchors (e.g., Sox2 promoter-super-enhancer) within a 10 Kb tolerance.

name: loop-benchmark-against-hic-reference-datasets
description: Use when a newly called loop list from chromatin tracing/imaging data must be validated against HiCCUPS loop anchors from bulk Hi-C at matched resolution (e.g., 10 Kb or 25 Kb), or when precision/recall/F1 of a loop caller are needed.

name: loop-calling-statistical-background-testing
description: Use when calling de novo chromatin loops from imaging-based chromatin tracing data (e.g., ORCA, multiplexed DNA FISH 3D coordinates in nm) where count-based proximity-ligation loop callers are not applicable.

name: loop-false-positive-assessment
description: Use when chromatin tracing 3D coordinate data has heterogeneous per-segment detection efficiency and you need to test whether a loop caller (SnapFISH) reports spurious loops in low-efficiency subsets.

name: loop-set-overlap-reproducibility-analysis
description: Use when comparing the reproducibility of two loop-calling methods or parameter settings on scHi-C data: split per-cell contact files into disjoint replicate halves, call loops per half, and quantify symmetric loop-set overlap.

name: loop-set-overlap-validation-analysis
description: Use when loops predicted from a non-Hi-C contact map (e.g., Micro-C H1-ESC or GM12878 DNA SPRITE coolers) must be benchmarked by their concordance with an independent Hi-C-derived loop set.

name: louvain-graph-clustering
description: Use when single-cell ATAC-seq cells need to be grouped into clusters (e.g., to produce per-cluster consensus CNV genotypes with Copy-scAT's smoothClusters, or to define subpopulations prior to downstream smoothing/filtering).

name: low-information-sequence-filtering
description: Use when running the Delila-PY pipeline and, after cycle 1's malign/malin alignment, some input sequences from the ChIP-derived sites file show information content of 0 bits or less, contaminating the motif with non-matching sequences.

name: low-variance-row-removal
description: Use when a numeric feature-by-sample matrix (gene expression, methylation) feeds into consensus partitioning and rows with near-constant values across samples would distort row scoring, scaling, or clustering.

name: lps-stimulated-bmdm-dataset-comparison
description: Use when comparing motif positional enrichment across multiple genomics assays (csRNA-seq, ATAC-seq, MNase-seq) of a differential stimulation response (e.g. LPS vs resting BMDMs), or when validating cross-assay concordance of TF motif positional profiles.

name: luxr-hns-overlap-analysis
description: Use when quantifying LuxR/H-NS binding overlap — genome-wide from ChIP-seq peaks (506 LuxR, 302 H-NS MACS2 peaks) or promoter-level via FIMO motif scanning (e.g. luxCDABE promoter, H-NS motif TCGATAAATT).

name: m5c-methylation-motif-discovery
description: Use when RIMS-seq paired-end Illumina reads of a bacterial strain need de novo m5C methylase motif discovery, especially when multiple methylases (e.g. A. calcoaceticus) or dcm motifs (E. coli K12 CCWGG) are expected.

name: machine-learning-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when a paper reports classifier or feature-subset performance metrics (e.g. AUC values per feature combination) and the goal is to re-run the released code/data to verify those numbers.

name: macs2-chip-seq-peak-calling
description: Use when processing deduplicated ChIA-PET bedpe/PET data through the ChIA-PET2 pipeline and ChIP-seq-like anchor peaks must be defined before interaction (loop) calling.

name: macs2-fimo-baseline-pipeline-construction
description: Use when benchmarking a chromatin occupancy or TF binding site prediction method and a simple peak/footprint-then-motif-scan baseline is needed for comparison against ChIP-chip/ChIP-exo/ORGANIC ground truth annotations.

name: macs2-log2fc-peak-scoring
description: Use when you have ChIP-seq peak calls and summit-centered sequences (e.g. ±200 bp around MACS2 summits) and need a per-sequence continuous score to drive MEPP positional enrichment analysis.

name: macs2-peak-calling
description: Use when ChIP-seq reads are already mapped to BAMs and QC requires MACS2 peak calls (narrow mode for TFs/active marks, broad for histone marks) to drive FRiP, replicate overlap, and annotation metrics.

name: macs2-peak-calling-from-pseudobulk-signal
description: Use when you have cluster (or cell-type) assignments from single-cell ATAC-seq fragments and need a genome-wide set of candidate accessible peaks that captures cell-type-specific accessibility beyond what bulk peak calls detect.

name: mahalanobis-distance-outlier-detection
description: Use when you must call statistically significant compartment differences between two or more Hi-C contact maps — including changes within the same A or B compartment type that standard PCA-on-each-map analysis cannot detect.

name: mahalanobis-distance-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing compartment scores of 100 kb (or finer, down to 10 kb) genomic bins across two or more replicate-grouped Hi-C contact maps (e.g., mouse ESC vs NPC) and needing statistically significant differential compartment calls.

name: mann-whitney-u-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing two independent per-TF score distributions (e.g., AUPR across 150 TFs for two binding-prediction methods) and a non-parametric significance assessment of their difference is required.

name: manova-pvalue-testing
description: Use when an ordered age/time series (e.g., PBMC ATAC/RNA peak-cluster trajectories across ages 22–93) must be scanned for abrupt change points rather than gradual trends, and per-age p-values for the before-vs-after difference are needed.

name: mapping-efficiency-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when aligner performance on bisulfite or bisulfite-free (TAPS) methylation reads must be quantified and compared in speed, memory, mapping efficiency, and accuracy.

name: mapping-efficiency-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing aligners for bisulfite-free (e.g., TAPS) methylation data on reads from CT/GA-rich regions, where C-to-T conversion erases strand information and 3-letter mapping loses efficiency.

name: mapping-quality-metric-computation
description: Use when you have simulated bisulfite-seq reads (e.g., Sherman FASTQ with embedded original positions) plus a filtered alignment (SAM), and need to quantify mappability, sensitivity, precision, and accuracy per error rate.

name: mapping-quality-threshold-filtering
description: Use when phasing 10x linked-reads with SpecHap/HapCUT2 and fragments from different DNA molecules share the same barcode, inflating spurious linkage between distant variants.

name: mapq-threshold-filtering
description: Use when ChIA-PET (or HiChIP/PLAC-seq) read pairs have been linker-filtered and aligned with the hybrid BWA-ALN/BWA-MEM strategy, and analysis-ready unique, nonredundant PETs must be selected for peak/loop calling.

name: marker-gene-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when an scATAC-seq/snap object has been clustered (e.g. Leiden clusters in SnapATAC) and each numeric cluster needs a cell-type label based on marker-gene accessibility or motif activity.

name: mart-regression-model-training
description: Use when reproducing the mseq learned-feature baseline or training a MART regression to model RNA-Seq fragment bias: you have Bowtie alignments to a transcriptome plus transcript FASTA and need uncorrected vs corrected expression estimates validated against qRT-PCR.

name: maven-build-management
description: Use when a new Watchdog executor plugin has been written in Java (e.g., a cloud executor without SSH) and the modified source must be compiled into runnable jar files for the watchdog.sh command-line tool.

name: mclust-model-based-clustering-of-maxima
description: Use when temporal aging series (e.g., PBMC ATAC-seq/RNA-seq profiles across ages 22–93) yield per-age p-value maxima that must be grouped into discrete breakpoint ages, with positive-control breakpoints expected near 40 and 65 years.

name: md-derived-dna-shape-parameter-lookup
description: Use when converting raw DNA sequence files (uPBM, HT-SELEX, or gcPBM) into physics-based features — tetramer counts, BigNASim MD-derived bps geometry/stiffness, and base-step electrostatic codes — for binding-affinity prediction.

name: mean-average-distance-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating loop-anchor localization accuracy of a GILoop GCN-branch model on downsampled Hi-C contact maps, or when reproducing the Figure 5 trend showing MAD tracking GCN PR-AUC as depth decreases toward the 260-million-read optimum.

name: mean-centered-transcriptomic-data-handling
description: Use when you have a COnTORT_organized_transcriptomic_data.txt matrix (5 annotation columns + mean-centered experiment columns) and need to correlate gene expression across diverse GEO data sets to rank co-expressed gene pairs.

name: mean-reciprocal-rank-computation
description: Use when comparing ranked TR output from two or more TR-identification methods against a known ground-truth set of perturbed TRs (e.g., CTCF, ZBTB7A, FOXA2, RUNX1, BCL11B) and a single ranking-based metric such as MRR is needed, as in reproducing Fig. 3f of the BIT paper.

name: mechanism-of-action-cluster-validation
description: Use when you need to reproduce or validate drug clustering by mechanism of action from RePhine -Log10(uniP) TR signature matrices built on CCLE pharmacogenomic data and ENCODE ChIP-seq regulatory potential scores.

name: meme-format-motif-output
description: Use when DiNAMO has finished filtering over-represented IUPAC motifs and you must emit them in MEME format for downstream tools, validation, or JASPAR matrix comparison.

name: mental-disorder-gene-scoring-integration
description: Use when prioritizing mutated genes from whole-genome/exome sequencing of a personal genome for mental disorders, after non-coding variants have been scored (ncDeepBrain) and need to be linked to genes and integrated with gene-level features.

name: meta-cell-correlation-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantify whether an imputed or denoised single-cell matrix (e.g. SCALE's obsm['imputed'] scATAC-seq peaks) recovers cluster-specific signal, by Pearson-correlating each cell against per-cluster meta-cells.

name: method-performance-comparison-tabulation
description: Use when a newly proposed computational method's identification performance must be quantified against established baselines under controlled perturbations like added noise or spurious-correlation confounders.

name: methylated-core-signature-extraction
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon-seq epihaplotype tables are available and the goal is to identify stable phased mCpG combinations (methylated cores) marking epiallele families, or to compute clonality/stability indices revealing dominant epiallele families in complex DNA populations.

name: methylated-motif-discovery-from-c-to-t-deamination
description: Use when RIMS-seq reads must yield m5C methylase specificities without prior knowledge of the methylome — e.g. mapping A. calcoaceticus reads to a de novo SPAdes assembly to recover motifs like GATC and CGCG with MosDi significance thresholds.

name: methylation-alignment-mode-comparison
description: Use when comparing DNA methylation read aligners (4-letter vs 3-letter) on TAPS/bisulfite-free reads, especially for CT/GA-rich regions where 3-letter C->T conversion collapses mapping power.

name: methylation-array-probe-preprocessing
description: Use when the input is a raw Illumina 450K methylation beta-value matrix (probes x samples, e.g. from GEO GSE36278) containing sex-chromosome probes, SNP-overlapping probes, missing values, outliers, and low-variance rows prior to cola consensus partitioning.

name: methylation-calibration-curve-fitting
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon/pyrosequencing data include standard controls with known methylation percentages (e.g. AMP = 0/25/50/75/100%) and apparent post-PCR methylation levels per CpG need bias-corrected calibration curves.

name: methylation-core-cross-tool-comparison
description: Use when bisulfite sequencing reads (e.g. FASTA epiallele tables from DDO1/DAO amplicons) have been processed with both single-epiallele tools and MethCoresProfiler, and the goal is to demonstrate that epiallele frequency distributions alone miss stable methylation cores.

name: methylation-core-significance-testing-chi-square
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon data (paired-end FASTQ, e.g. ENA PRJEB28662) has been reduced to binary epihaplotype tables of mCpG configurations and the goal is to detect stable phased mCpG combinations and trace epiallele families in complex DNA populations.

name: methylation-core-statistical-annotation
description: Use when amplicon bisulfite reads have been converted to binary epihaplotype matrices of phased CpG methylation states and the goal is to extract significant mCpG combinations, cores, clonality/entanglement indices, or track epiallele families across cell types or time points.

name: methylation-count-table-validation
description: Use when reconstructing or testing the methylation-count extraction step of a MethylC-seq pipeline and confirming that output tables match a reference implementation, including CpG sites absent from the reference genome.

name: methylation-density-comparison-analysis
description: Use when you have Msuite methylation-call outputs (CpG/CpH meth.call files) from simulated benchmark reads with known preset methylation densities and need to quantify call accuracy per cytosine context.

name: methylation-group-comparison-statistics
description: Use when ab1 bisulfite sequencing PCR reads have already been individually analyzed for CpG methylation and you need to compare methylation percentages between sample groups (e.g. high- vs low-methylated DNA controls) with plots and significance tests.

name: methylation-hidden-markov-state-modeling
description: Use when bisulfite sequencing data from a heterogeneous sample must be deconvolved into major allelic subpopulation methylation profiles over user-defined regions, without prior knowledge of subpopulation count.

name: methylation-level-correction-evaluation
description: Use when observed bisulfite amplicon/pyrosequencing methylation percentages in case and control samples need PCR-bias correction, and the stability or concordance of the resulting hyper/hypomethylation classifications must be assessed.

name: methylation-level-numerical-inversion
description: Use when fitted MethylCal INLA calibration models and formatted BWS-style methylation data are available and the apparent methylation level of case/control samples must be converted back to a corrected methylation degree per CpG-AMP combination.

name: methylation-matrix-aggregation-across-samples
description: Use when a completed per-sample (cf)MeDIP-seq methylation quantification run must be combined across many samples, groups, or batches into genome-bin x sample matrices with standardized region filtering and region-queryable output.

name: methylation-profile-significance-plotting
description: Use when individually analyzed bisulfite sequencing PCR (.ab1 trace) samples must be gathered into groups (e.g. high- vs low-methylated DNA) and compared with t-tests plus per-CpG significance-annotated profile plots.

name: methylation-quantification-from-enrichment-data
description: Use when you have cfMeDIP-seq (or MeDIP-seq) aligned enrichment data from raw FASTQs and need per-sample methylation quantification plus aggregated, filtered bin-by-sample methylation matrices across a cohort.

name: methylation-standard-control-calibration
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon sequencing standard controls with known methylation percentages (e.g. 0/25/50/75/100% BWS or 0/12.5/25/37.5/50/62.5/87.5/100% Celiac) are available and you must pick the MethylCal model specification per assay.

name: methylation-subpopulation-deconvolution
description: Use when bisulfite sequencing data (eRRBS, Methyl-Seq) come from a heterogeneous sample and you need to infer the number of major subpopulations, their methylation profiles, or intrasample DMRs.

name: methylation-variability-quantification
description: Use when comparing methylation dynamics of a region set (e.g., HOT regions) against CpG islands across multiple cell types using WGBS methylation calls and BED-style interval files.

name: methylc-seq-alignment-processing
description: Use when raw FASTQ or Bismark BAM/SAM alignments from a bisulfite-sequencing run (e.g. IMR90/H1 MethylC-seq) must be converted to per-CpG methylated/unmethylated count tables or region-linked methylation strings.

name: methylc-seq-region-dmr-identification
description: Use when you have per-sample clustered-region methylation counts (combined.csv with chr, start, end, CpG and per-sample total/methylated count columns) from two or more sample groups and need to call DMRs between groups.

name: microarray-rnaseq-matrix-preprocessing
description: Reference for cleaning raw gene-expression matrices (missing values, outliers, low-variance rows) before consensus partitioning or benchmarking clustering methods.

name: missing-data-imputation-bpca
description: Use when iMEGES variant or gene feature matrices contain missing continuous predictor scores (e.g. DANN, CADD, EIGEN, GWAVA, FATHMM) that must be filled before feeding the deep learning model.

name: mixed-depth-transfer-finetuning
description: Use when training GILoop on GM12878 Hi-C and marginal PR-AUC matters: pre-train each branch at its preferred matrix density (GCN on 10% downsampled, U-Net on full-depth), then jointly fine-tune on the mixed-density set to beat the single-depth 90% baseline (0.3790 vs 0.3718).

name: mlp-architecture-configuration
description: Use when building Cellcano's supervised celltyping models: a first-round MLP on reference gene scores, or a second-round self-KD teacher-student model trained on low-entropy anchor cells to classify remaining non-anchor cells.

name: mlp-training-on-reference-data
description: Use when cell-type labels must be transferred from an scATAC-seq reference gene score matrix (with cell-type metadata) to a target scATAC-seq gene score matrix, and first-round MLP predictions are needed to define anchor cells for two-round prediction.

name: mnase-seq-fragment-length-classification
description: Use when raw paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq alignments (BAM) must be converted into fragment-length-classified midpoint count tracks (bedGraph) to feed a chromatin occupancy model such as RoboCOP.

name: mnase-seq-occupancy-modeling
description: Use when paired-end MNase-seq (or ATAC-seq) data are available and you need genome-wide, single-nucleotide-resolution probabilistic occupancy scores for nucleosomes and DNA-binding factors, e.g. ORC at annotated ACS replication origins.

name: mnase-seq-timecourse-analysis
description: Use when you have paired timepoint MNase-seq (plus matched RNA-seq) data and need to detect stress- or condition-induced nucleosome repositioning, such as +1 dyad shifts at promoters of transcriptionally responsive genes.

name: model-performance-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing a newly trained cell-specific enhancer classifier against a published baseline (e.g. Enhancer-IF) across multiple cell lines, or when quantifying cross-cell-line transferability via per-pair balanced accuracy.

name: model-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a DeepSE model trained on pooled cell-line datasets must be scored on held-out cell lines or on another species' datasets (e.g., hg->mm or mm->hg transfer), and per-cell-line test metrics are needed.

name: modular-ngs-pipeline-scripting
description: Use when a lab must turn raw NGS data (FASTQ from ChIPseq or RNAseq of mouse embryonic stem cells or similar) into reproducible QC, alignment, filtering, peak-calling and signal-track outputs with minimal command-line expertise.

name: modularity-index-calculation
description: Use when scoring the structural quality of predicted TAD/TLD partitions on single-cell Hi-C contact matrices (e.g., Tan GM12878, Nagano mouse ES, Lee PFC datasets), to compare predictors on modularity alongside 2D structural entropy and AMI.

name: module-significance-testing
description: Use when a normalized PvalueAnnotation object holds multiple component scores per gene (e.g. expression plus methylation_promoter/body and h3k4me1) and you need a single per-gene p-value and G statistic to score network modules.

name: monte-carlo-fdr-pvalue-estimation
description: Use when combining non-independent component p-values/scores per gene (e.g. expression plus methylation promoter/body/histone data) and an empirical per-gene p-value is needed because parametric assumptions fail under correlation.

name: monte-carlo-resampling-statistics
description: Use when combining p-values from correlated genomic assays (e.g., methylation p-values from multiple CpGs mapped to one gene) and you need SMITE's MCM correlation-corrected resampling, including characterizing how CpG correlation decays with genomic distance.

name: mosdi-motif-significance-scoring
description: Use when RIMS-seq Read 1/Read 2 mpileup files are available and the goal is to de novo recover m5C methylase motifs with significance scores, with or without a reference genome.

name: motif-center-proximity-statistics
description: Use when ChIP-Seq peaks (called with base-level significance) must be validated against known transcription-factor binding motifs, e.g. measuring how many significant peaks center within 30 bp of the motif center to compare summit-inference accuracy across methods or versions.

name: motif-count-aggregation-across-datasets
description: Use when DESSO shape-motif prediction outputs (DNAShape/CNN/0-3 per-dataset directories) must be tallied into per-shape-type totals and per-dataset presence/absence summaries across many ChIP-seq datasets.

name: motif-count-feature-engineering
description: Use when building cell-type-specific CRE classifiers from four-column BED-like inputs (chromosome, start, stop, condition) and you need interpretable motif-count features rather than k-mer or deep-learning representations.

name: motif-discovery-differential-enrichment
description: Use when you have labeled positive and negative short sequence datasets (e.g., 6 mA sites vs. non-sites) and need enriched motifs as encoded features for a downstream machine-learning classifier.

name: motif-enrichment-analysis-across-peak-callers
description: Use when evaluating one or more ChIP-Seq peak-calling algorithms by the prevalence of expected transcription factor motifs in peak sequences relative to matched control sequences, rather than by sensitivity alone.

name: motif-enrichment-based-tr-ranking
description: Use when a differentially accessible region (DAR) BED file must be scored for candidate TRs by motif enrichment, and per-TR ranks are needed to compute mean reciprocal rank (MRR) in a multi-method benchmark such as Fig. 3f of the BIT paper.

name: motif-enrichment-chi-square-testing
description: Use when comparing motif content of peak sets from different ChIP-Seq peak callers — e.g., testing whether the NRSF motif separates HPeak-unique peaks from peaks unique to PeakFinder, FindPeaks, MACS, SISSRs, CisGenome, or ChIPseeqer.

name: motif-enrichment-verification-across-raw-and-imputed-data
description: Use when a scATAC-seq imputation result (e.g. SCALE --impute output) must be validated by showing downstream chromVAR motif detection improves relative to the raw peak-count matrix.

name: motif-family-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you need to validate called peaks or ChIP-enriched regions by checking enrichment of an expected TF motif family (e.g. STAT) against all vertebrate motif families, or compare motif enrichment across platforms (ChIP-Seq vs ChIP-chip) and peak-rank bins.

name: motif-frequency-summarization
description: Use when you have a set of representative motifs predicted by DESSO from ChIP-seq data and need to determine how many correspond to known JASPAR/TRANSFAC motifs versus undocumented classes.

name: motif-instance-enumeration-across-cutoffs
description: Use when identifying motif instances (TFBSs) from CNN motif detector outputs and you need an objective, statistically grounded cutoff instead of a fixed/subjective signal threshold.

name: motif-log-odds-threshold-calculation
description: Use when a positional motif-enrichment pipeline needs, per JASPAR PWM, a statistically calibrated log-odds cutoff (via MOODS) before scanning scored DNA sequences for motif matches.

name: motif-orientation-pairwise-classification
description: Use when you have a strand-annotated BED file of motif occurrences (e.g. JASPAR MA0139.1 CTCF sites in hg19) and need to test whether nearby consecutive pairs within a distance window show same-strand versus opposite-strand orientation bias.

name: motif-peak-position-identification
description: Use when you have centered genomic sequences (e.g. ±200 bp around TSSs) with a continuous per-sequence score (e.g. log-transformed csRNA-seq coverage) and need to determine the positional dependence of known motifs relative to the anchor point.

name: motif-positional-enrichment-profiling
description: Use when you have a set of genomic sequences centered on a biological anchor (TSS, ChIP/ATAC/MNase peak summit, or a known motif site) plus a continuous score per sequence, and you need to know WHERE a motif enriches relative to that anchor rather than merely whether it is enriched.

name: motif-pwm-feature-extraction
description: Use when enhancer or promoter FASTA sequences must be converted into TFBS motif-frequency features (via PWM scanning) as input to a multi-input deep learning predictor such as Enhancer-MDLF.

name: motif-pwm-instance-scanning
description: Use when you have genomic FASTA sequences (e.g., ATAC-derived distal elements) plus a PWM file such as gimme.vertebrate.v5.0.meme and need per-sequence motif instances/counts for downstream modeling or SRE construction.

name: motif-pwm-sliding-window-scoring
description: Use when raw DNA sequences (e.g. FASTA enhancer sequences per cell line) must be converted into per-motif TFBS count/frequency features for downstream machine learning, and a curated PWM library with p-value thresholds is available.

name: motif-redundancy-deduplication
description: Use when constructing a TF-target gene prior from motif scans of open-chromatin peaks and same-family TFs yield overlapping motif-to-peak sets that would create redundant, correlated rows in the decoder's TF-gene matrix.

name: motif-scanning-of-regulatory-sequences
description: Use when you have genomic intervals (chromosome, start, stop, condition BED-style input) or extracted FASTA of candidate enhancers and need per-sequence TF motif occurrences as features for cell-type-specific CRE classification or cross-species transfer.

name: motif-sequence-truth-matching
description: Use when comparing called-site outputs from CLIP-seq peak callers (Skipper, CLIPper, Piranha) on eCLIP data and an independent motif-, sequence-, or feature-derived positive truth set is available for the assayed RBP.

name: motif-significance-evalue-filtering
description: Use when MEME has discovered candidate motifs from positive vs. negative sequence sets and you must retain only statistically significant motifs (E-value < 0.05) to build per-sample motif score features for a classifier.

name: motif-similarity-clustering
description: Use when a large pool of predicted motifs (e.g. from DESSO predict.py across many ChIP-seq datasets) must be reduced to representative motifs and classified as known versus undocumented.

name: motif-similarity-evaluation-against-jaspar-transfac
description: Use when predicted motifs from a motif-discovery or deep-learning pipeline must be validated or benchmarked against curated motif databases (JASPAR/TRANSFAC) via TOMTOM similarity statistics.

name: motif-variability-quantification
description: Use when you have a sparse scATAC-seq fragment-count matrix over peaks and want to rank motifs/annotations by cell-to-cell accessibility variability with bias correction, or to test whether motif deviations or variability differ between cell-type groups.

name: mouse-brain-prediction-outcome-verification
description: Decision support for choosing between gene scores and 500-bp bin counts as scATAC-seq celltyping input, or when verifying the reported 62/63 mouse brain win count of the Cellcano benchmark before citing or extending it.

name: mpileup-read-pair-splitting
description: Use when paired-end RIMS-seq or adapter-ligated Illumina reads have been mapped to a reference (or SPAdes-assembled) genome and separate Read1/Read2 mpileups are needed for m5C motif discovery.

name: multi-cell-line-dataset-pooling
description: Use when the goal is cross-cell-line generalization of sequence-based SE/TE classification: you have per-cell-line encoded dna2vec feature matrices and want one universal pooled model evaluated on each cell line.

name: multi-compartment-benchmark-validation
description: Use when evaluating whether a Hi-C deconvolution tool can resolve multiple sub-compartments, or when validating that sub-compartments inferred from a mixed cell population correspond to the underlying cell-type-specific models.

name: multi-input-deep-learning-model-training
description: Use when cell-line enhancer FASTA training/test sets with label files are available and pre-extracted dna2vec and motif features exist, and a combined multi-input model must be trained and evaluated on an independent test set.

name: multi-mapping-read-filtering
description: Use when aligning converted methylation reads (3-letter bisulfite or 4-letter TAPS/5hmC-CATCH mode) with Msuite and you must remove ambiguously mapped reads before methylation calling.

name: multi-mapping-repeat-region-binding-analysis
description: Use when testing CLIP-seq/eCLIP data for enrichment at multi-mapping annotated repetitive elements (RepeatMasker), where peak callers fail and RBPs may bind simple repeats such as GU-rich motifs.

name: multi-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a new domain/peak-calling or prediction method needs head-to-head validation against established alternatives on shared real datasets, with a functional readout rather than only internal overlap metrics.

name: multi-method-benchmark-visualization
description: Use when comparing TR-identification methods on the same epigenomic query region sets and a known ground-truth perturbed TR exists, so ranks can be converted into mean reciprocal rank values for head-to-head benchmarking.

name: multi-method-peak-caller-agreement-analysis
description: Use when differential ChIP-seq region calls (e.g. SHR vs BN H3K27me3 on rn4) need validation against qPCR-confirmed loci and against alternative callers' outputs.

name: multi-omics-data-object-construction
description: Use when you have paired sample-level copy-number/epi-DNA alteration calls and matched gene expression matrices and need to package them, with cis gene lists and sample/feature annotations, into the iEDGE object required by run_iEDGE.

name: multi-omics-pvalue-integration
description: Use when combining gene expression p-values with epigenomic modification p-values (promoter methylation, gene-body methylation/hydroxymethylation, enhancer H3K4me1) that are anchored to hg19 TSS coordinates, to obtain per-gene scores and significant subnetwork modules.

name: multi-region-tumour-heterogeneity-comparison
description: Use when you have per-locus epiallele distributions from multiple tumour regions plus matched normal tissue and need a scalar, per-sample measure of epigenetic heterogeneity to compare regions against normal.

name: multi-resolution-genomic-contact-binning
description: Use when you have an analysis-ready, deduplicated ChIA-PET/HiChIP PET BAM (unique alignments, MAPQ >= 30, nonredundant PETs) and need browser-loadable 2D contact maps at multiple resolutions for Juicebox.js or HiGlass.

name: multi-resolution-hic-contact-map-visualization
description: Use when hic contact matrix files from the Microcket pipeline are available and region-specific contact-map heatmaps must be extracted and rendered at multiple resolutions for side-by-side condition comparison.

name: multi-sample-qc-report-aggregation
description: Use when per-sample QC and methylation outputs (FastQC, SAMtools, Picard, MEDIPS/QSEA/MEDStrand quantifications) must be pooled across many samples, groups, or batches into a summarized report and region-queryable aggregated matrices.

name: multi-species-enhancer-benchmarking
description: Use when asked to reproduce or extend classification of cell-type-specific enhancers across species, cell types, or disease states using BED coordinates plus condition labels and the BOM pipeline.

name: multi-topic-grid-model-training
description: Use when a cisTopic object (initialized binary accessibility matrix) is available and multiple LDA models over a grid of topic numbers must be trained to later choose the optimal number of cis-regulatory topics.

name: multiclass-cell-type-classification-from-scatac-distal-elements
description: Use when scATAC-seq peak/CRE data must be assigned to cell types from sequence alone — e.g., multiclass classification of cell-type-specific distal elements or cross-species cell-type assignment using motif counts.

name: multiclass-mcc-evaluation
description: Use when clustering outputs must be scored against known ground-truth class labels (e.g. 5 simulated peak seed patterns of ~100 members each) across a parameter grid, and a single balanced score per condition is needed.

name: multidimensional-epigenomic-track-warping
description: Use when multiple epigenomic tracks (e.g. ChIP-Seq coverage binned into 50 bp windows per peak) must be aligned by shape across peaks without gene annotation or TSS information, as a precursor to hierarchical clustering.

name: multimapper-partitioning
description: Use when you have AdaLiftOver candidate target regions for query peaks and need to separate uniquely mapped regions from multi-mappers, or to test whether epigenomic signal overrides sequence-conservation-based mapping support.

name: multipanel-figure-composition
description: Use when many per-sample QC summaries (e.g., FASTQ per-cycle quality and read-quality distributions) must be arranged into one combined multi-panel plot/report for visual inspection of large sample sets.

name: multiple-alignment-information-maximization
description: Use when you have a delila-generated book of unaligned input sequences and need to find the multiple alignment that maximizes information content before calculating per-sequence information or building a sequence logo.

name: multiple-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction
description: Use when a large family of one-sided Fisher's exact tests (e.g., clusterProfiler::enrichGO GO term enrichment of BIT top-ranked TRs) must be corrected for multiple testing, with terms ranked by BH-adjusted p values at a q-value cutoff of 0.05.

name: multiple-testing-bonferroni-correction
description: Use when calling or powering differential expression / eQTL tests across many genes in scRNA-seq pseudobulk data, where a per-gene threshold must be corrected for the number of expressed genes tested.

name: multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a differential-expression or regression analysis produces thousands of raw p-values (one per gene or TR) and hits must be called with a controlled false-discovery rate, e.g. adjusted p-value < 0.05.

name: multiple-testing-correction-fdr
description: Use when testing many motifs or functional terms simultaneously — e.g. PASTAA on REM sequences ranked by Cell type score, or g:Profiler on ~1,721 ARID3A-associated genes — to control the false discovery rate at BH FDR ≤ 0.05.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when you have per-RBP constraint regressions (mean delta score vs. gnomAD allele-frequency bin) over Skipper enriched windows and must aggregate to RBP-transcript pairs and control the false discovery rate to nominate constrained transcripts.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when a CITRUS in silico knock out or association analysis yields one raw p-value per TF (hundreds of TFs tested simultaneously) and significant TF–alteration or TF-overlap associations must be controlled for multiple testing.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when dcHiC has produced one raw chi-square p-value per genomic bin (from Mahalanobis distance on quantile-normalized compartment scores) or per candidate interaction, and you must call significant differential compartments or interactions at a controlled adjusted-p threshold such as FDR 10%.

name: multiple-testing-qvalue-correction
description: Use when a genome-wide scan (e.g., driverpower infer over eight test element sets: CDS, splice site, 5'-UTR, 3'-UTR, promoter, enhancer, lncRNA, lncRNA promoter) has produced raw p-values that must be converted to q-values before calling driver candidates.

name: multiplet-rate-modeling-10x-genomics
description: Use when planning or costing a 10X droplet scRNA-seq experiment with scPower and you must account for usable cells per lane given multiplet loss as a function of cells loaded per lane.

name: multiplexed-dna-fish-loop-calling
description: Use when analyzing 3D chromatin tracing coordinates (per-cell x/y/z per locus) to call chromatin loops with SnapFISH, or to test how detection-efficiency stratification affects loop-calling sensitivity and false positives.

name: multiqc-report-aggregation
description: Reference for combining multiple per-sample NGS quality-control outputs (FastQC, trimming/mapping stats) from a Nextflow/CIPHER run into one aggregated MultiQC report instead of inspecting each QC file individually.

name: multiscale-genomic-signal-analysis
description: Use when a ChIP-seq signal (e.g. H3K27me3 in human CD4+ T cells, chromosome 1) must be analyzed across multiple length scales to measure how its spatial auto-correlation length evolves under recursive coarse-graining.

name: multivariate-hmm-chromatin-inference
description: Use when paired-end MNase-seq (or ATAC-seq) reads and a reference genome sequence are available and the goal is a probabilistic occupancy landscape of nucleosomes and transcription factors across the genome.

name: multivariate-variance-explained-interpretation
description: Use when you have BHi-Cect's named list of loci per cluster (bottom enclaves) plus ChIP-seq peaks for a set of TFs and need to check whether a low-dimensional CA projection summarizes regulatory regimes across enclaves.

name: mutant-vs-wildtype-binding-comparison
description: Use when eCLIP data exist for both wild-type and missense-mutant versions of an RBP (e.g., RPS19 R62W/R101H) and the goal is to detect altered binding — region-proportion shifts or novel target classes like tRNA loci.

name: mutation-expression-association-testing
description: Use when validating DriverPower-exclusive driver candidates (e.g. SGK1 in Lymph-BNHL, GPR126 in Bladder-TCC enhancer) by asking whether mutated samples show differential gene expression after correcting for copy number and tissue.

name: mutation-status-cell-line-partitioning
description: Use when CCLE mutation annotation and drug-sensitivity (e.g. PLX4720) tables are available and the goal is to test whether a co-mutation class (BRAF + PRC2/H3K27me3 loss) shifts pharmacological response versus a single-mutant baseline.

name: mutual-information-scoring-from-contingency-tables
description: Use when ranking over-represented degenerate IUPAC motifs from a positive/control FASTA pair where occurrence-count-biased statistics would favor long or highly degenerate motifs; each candidate motif has a contingency table of counts (a, b, c, d).

name: n50-mismatch-rate-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing de novo assembly quality (N50, mismatch rate, and related Quast metrics) between a chemically treated read set (e.g. RIMS-seq alkaline-treated) and a standard DNA-seq control to show the treatment preserves assembly metrics.

name: nanopore-event-table-to-translocation-time-conversion
description: Use when you have ONT FAST5 data basecalled with Albacore and need base-level translocation times in seconds — e.g. to build per-window TT quantiles for non-B DNA versus B-DNA comparisons.

name: nanopore-raw-signal-basecalling
