description: Use when you have raw nanopore FAST5 electrolytic-current signal files and need to decode them into per-read nucleotide sequences without prior signal segmentation.

name: nanopore-read-error-correction
description: Use when assembling genomes from noisy Oxford Nanopore long reads and you must choose between correct-then-assemble vs assemble-then-correct correction strategies, or when polishing a draft long-read assembly to final accuracy with Illumina short reads.

name: nanopore-translocation-time-novelty-detection
description: Use when ONT nanopore FAST5 reads (e.g. NA12878 / SRR15058166) must be converted to per-base translocation times and scored for non-B DNA novelty against motif-free B-DNA controls at an FDR-controlled level.

name: narrowpeak-coordinate-preprocessing
description: Use when raw narrow-peak BED files (chrom, start, end) from ENCODE/Roadmap chromatin profiles must be converted into non-redundant, fixed-width 1000 bp input intervals for a Basset/DeepFun CNN training set.

name: narrowpeak-format-parsing
description: Use when the input consists of narrowPeak ChIP-seq peak files and you need peak summit coordinates to build a genome-wide TF-occupancy track or define HOT regions.

name: nearest-gene-peak-annotation
description: Use when you have called Brd4/TF binding peaks (e.g., ~902 peaks from the mouse cortex scCC dataset) and need to assign nearest genes so peaks can later be paired with gene expression via cc.tl.pair_peak_gene_sc.

name: nearest-neighbor-cell-clustering
description: Use when Copy-scAT per-cell CNV assignments are noisy (e.g., sparse scATAC coverage) and you want to smooth them into one consensus chromosome value per cell cluster using Louvain (or k-means) clustering of the accessibility matrix.

name: negative-binomial-count-emission-modeling
description: Use when computing genome-wide chromatin occupancy profiles from paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq fragment data together with nucleotide sequence, and per-factor accessibility counts must be modeled as emission distributions inside an HMM.

name: negative-binomial-count-model-regression
description: Use when modeling base-resolution ChIP-Seq read counts as smooth functions of genomic position with a penalized NB GAM, especially genome-wide where per-tile sparsity must be exploited for tractable fitting.

name: negative-binomial-coverage-bias-correction
description: Use when raw Hi-C/pcHi-C interaction tables (frag1, frag2, coverage values, freq, dist) show coverage-driven bias and you need implicit bias correction before distance normalization or significant interaction calling.

name: negative-binomial-glm-fitting
description: Use when Hi-C or pcHi-C fragment-pair tables (frag1, frag2, cov_frag1, cov_frag2, freq, dist) contain coverage-driven ligation bias that must be estimated and removed before distance normalization or replicate comparison.

name: negative-binomial-pseudobulk-count-simulation
description: Use when analytic power estimates (e.g. from scPower) must be validated against simulated count data, when cross-checking scPower against powsimR/muscat, or when a gene's pseudobulk mean is too small (< 5) for the analytic linear-model eQTL approximation.

name: nested-feature-set-performance-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether adding sequence-derived epigenomic features (reference and/or alternative alleles) to generic functional annotations improves a tissue-specific variant classifier, using AUROC/AUPRC medians across tissues.

name: nested-tld-boundary-specificity-detection
description: Use when single-cell TLD predictions from multiple cell types (e.g., Lee PFC scHi-C cells) are available and the goal is to identify which nested TLD boundaries distinguish specific cell types.

name: nested-tld-hierarchy-assessment
description: Use when single-cell or sparse Hi-C contact matrices must be decomposed into hierarchical TLDs and the hierarchy compared across conditions (e.g., cell-cycle stages G1, early/mid/late S, G2) via modularity and similarity metrics.

name: network-modularity-calculation
description: Use when single-cell Hi-C contact matrices have been partitioned into nested TLDs (e.g., by deDoc2.w/deDoc2.s) and you need a per-cell scalar (modularity Q) to track how TLD hierarchy changes across cell-cycle stages (G1, early/mid/late S, G2) or other groupings.

name: neural-network-convergence-monitoring
description: Use when training the SCALE VAE (encoder 3200-1600-800-400, 10-dimensional latent layer, single-layer decoder) on scATAC-seq count data and you must verify the ELBO decreases and plateaus without divergence before using latent features or cluster assignments.

name: neural-network-sigmoid-classifier-training
description: Use when gene-level feature vectors combining a non-coding variant deep-learning score with gene-based scores must be fused into a per-gene susceptibility probability by a supervised neural network classifier.

name: neural-network-training-configuration
description: Use when training the DeepSE two-layer CNN (Keras) on encoded SE/TE feature vectors for a cell line or species, e.g. via train_specific.py or train_integrative*.py with species hg/mm, learning_rate, and epochs arguments.

name: neural-network-training-with-mse-reconstruction-loss
description: Use when a Hi-C N×N contact matrix must be converted into low-dimensional node embeddings (dim 16) via a graph auto-encoder before unsupervised clustering of genomic bins into TADs.

name: neuron-cell-type-epigenomic-annotation
description: Use when fine-mapped human GWAS SNPs in hg38 must be mapped to the mouse genome and annotated against cell-type-specific chromatin accessible regions (e.g., mouse excitatory vs inhibitory neurons) to test cell-type enrichment.

name: newick-tree-export
description: Use when multi-region tumour epiallele presence/absence profiles (post purity correction) need to be converted into an evolutionary tree relating tumour regions and matched normal tissue.

name: newton-based-maximum-likelihood-parameter-updating
description: Use when fitting CscoreTool-M's probabilistic sub-compartment model (Ci, alpha, beta) to Hi-C interaction data and you need to reproduce or re-implement its non-convex likelihood optimization and convergence loop.

name: newton-raphson-maximum-likelihood-optimization
description: Use when fitting penalized GAM-type regression models (e.g. smooth functions of genomic position s(x) on ChIP-Seq counts) where the Hessian of the penalized negative-binomial likelihood is sparse and a direct sparse solve is preferable to forming the inverse.

name: nextflow-workflow-execution
description: Use when raw single- or pair-ended FASTQ datasets for one or more NGS assays must be processed reproducibly end-to-end via Nextflow, or when comparing pipeline runtime/user-input burden against alternatives.

name: ngs-adapter-trimming-benchmarking
description: Use when choosing between NGS read-trimming or alignment tools (e.g., BBDuk vs cutadapt vs Trimmomatic; BBMap vs BWA vs STAR) and you need speed-vs-accuracy metrics on a common ENCODE FASTQ input.

name: ngs-error-model-parameterization
description: Use when an aligner-evaluation experiment needs synthetic bisulfite-seq FASTQ read sets with a controlled per-base error rate (e.g. 0%, 1%, 2%) and known genomic origin, so mapping quality can be scored against ground truth.

name: ngs-pipeline-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing pipeline runtime and configuration burden across NGS analysis platforms (ChIP-seq/RNA-seq) on the same fastq inputs, or when validating claims that a parallelized workflow outperforms serial competitors.

name: ngs-pipeline-execution-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to measure runtime and output file sizes of an end-to-end NEAT NGS pipeline on truncated ChIPseq/RNAseq test data, or to validate that pipeline completion fits within sequencing-run turnaround limits.

name: ngs-pipeline-module-configuration
description: Use when building or re-running a NEAT NGS project and you must select which pipeline modules (unzip, QC, chiprx, map, filter, peakcalling, cleanfiles, granges) execute and with which user parameters.

name: ngs-read-quality-control
description: Use when raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) enter a Watchdog RNA-seq workflow and their quality must be checked before mapping against the reference genome.

name: ngs-read-quality-visualization
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads (e.g. truncated H3K4me3 ChIPseq or RNAseq data from mouse embryonic stem cells) have been unzipped and registered in Targets.txt and a per-sample sequencing-quality report must be generated before mapping.

name: ngs-short-read-alignment
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads from ChIPseq (e.g. H3K4me3) or RNAseq experiments must be aligned as an automated pipeline step, with per-sample .bam outputs named after the samples in Targets.txt.

name: ngs-workflow-orchestration-nextflow
description: Use when raw single- or pair-ended FASTQ datasets for common NGS assays must be batch-processed into trimmed reads, mapped BAMs, QC reports, and mode-specific outputs (e.g. MACS2 peaks or DE genes) in one reproducible pipeline.

name: noise-and-confounder-scenario-generation
description: Use when stress-testing a TR–drug response identification method under controlled synthetic conditions: you need simulated TR/target expression, drug response, and RP scores with injected noise or spurious (non-TR-mediated) correlations to compare against baseline methods.

name: non-b-dna-motif-window-annotation-hg38
description: Use when ONT re-squiggled per-base translocation times must be assigned to genomic windows — 100 bp windows centered on non-B DNA DB hg38 motifs (G-quadruplex, Z-DNA, STR, A-phased repeat, etc.) plus motif-free B-DNA controls — for TT quantile comparison.

name: non-b-dna-simulation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing non-B DNA detection methods on simulated ONT translocation-time windows across non-B ratios (e.g. 0.05), needing F1 benchmark tables like Fig. 6 / Supp. Table S6.

name: non-coding-variant-score-integration
description: Use when annotating candidate non-coding SNVs with heterogeneous per-variant scores (EIGEN, CADD, DANN, GWAVA, FATHMM, GNOMAD, brain eQTLs, H3K4me3/H3K4me1/H3K27me3/H3K27ac) and needing a single prioritization score.

name: noncoding-variant-functional-annotation
description: Use when you need to prioritize or interpret non-coding GWAS variants by their predicted effect on chromatin accessibility, histone marks, or TF binding in a tissue- or cell type-specific manner at single-nucleotide resolution.

name: normal-tissue-decontamination
description: Use when multi-region tumour RRBS data plus matched normal tissue have been fit with bed_fit and per-locus epiallele distributions phi_s exist, and you need to estimate tumour purity and remove normal-tissue contamination before phylogeny or entropy analyses.

name: normal-wishart-hierarchical-prior-elicitation
description: Use when calibrating observed methylation levels from bisulfite amplicon sequencing standard controls (e.g. AMP = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100)) jointly across all CpGs of a targeted DMR/CGI, and a hierarchical Bayesian random-effects formulation with elicited priors is needed.

name: novel-cpg-site-inclusion
description: Use when post-aligning MethylC-seq reads with Bismark and you need per-CpG methylated/unmethylated counts that capture novel CpG sites introduced by SNPs (e.g., rs11348696), not just reference-genome CpGs.

name: novelty-call-per-method-aggregation
description: Use when you have per-method G4 novelty calls from GoFAE-DND, isolation forest, LOF, or one-class SVM on NA12878 nanopore windows and need to compare how weakly vs strongly stable the called G4s are via Quadron scores.

name: nucleosome-dyad-prediction-from-mnase-seq
description: Use when paired-end MNase-seq data (e.g. S. cerevisiae GSE153609) must be converted into nucleosome dyad positions and occupancy probabilities, and validated against ground-truth dyad annotations.

name: nucleosome-occupancy-filtering-of-predictions
description: Explains and contextualizes predicted TF binding sites that lack experimental support by overlaying them with G1-phase yeast nucleosome occupancy maps, as done for CBF1 false positives from DNAffinity PB-exo/ChIP-exo predictions.

name: nucleosome-occupancy-profiling
description: Use when paired-end MNase-seq (or ATAC-seq) data are available for two or more conditions and the goal is to quantify nucleosome positioning dynamics, such as +1 dyad shifts at promoter NDRs under stress.

name: nucleosome-positioning-aupr-evaluation
description: Use when multiple nucleosome-positioning methods have been run on the same ATAC-seq and/or MNase-seq data and their predicted nucleosome calls must be compared on an identical validation set using AUPR.

name: nucleosome-positioning-benchmarking-against-chemical-cleavage-annotations
description: Use when a genome-wide nucleosome positioning prediction (dyad calls or occupancy-derived dyads) must be validated quantitatively against gold-standard chemical-cleavage dyad annotations, e.g. reproducing Figure 4C.

name: nucleotide-annotation-fraction-quantification
description: Use when reproducing or sanity-checking the motif-scanning sensitivity of a BOM/FIMO CRE classification workflow, e.g. verifying that ~83% of CRE nucleotides are annotated at q<=0.5 before ablation or retraining.

name: nucleotide-chemical-dichotomy-encoding
description: Use when converting fixed-length 41-nt DNA sequences (A/C/G/T) into per-position binary features for the csDMA 6mA classifier, when Motif and Kmer features alone underperform, or when a purely chemical-dichotomy encoding of nucleotides is needed.

name: nucleotide-level-correlation-coefficient-evaluation
description: Use when comparing motif discovery tools (e.g. DiNAMO vs MEME-CHIP, HOMER, Discrover) on data where ground-truth implanted motifs exist and per-nucleotide recovery quality must be quantified.

name: nucleotide-pattern-counting
description: Use when converting labeled DNA sequences (e.g., FASTA of 41-nt 6mA positives/negatives) into a fixed-length numeric feature matrix via k-mer relative-frequency encoding before classifier training.

name: null-distribution-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when testing whether genomic ranges (peaks, QTLs, CREs) show significant enrichment or correlation with features (genes, cell types) and a null that preserves local genomic correlation structure is required.

name: null-distribution-z-score-computation
description: Use when testing enrichment of overlap between two genomic range sets (e.g., ATAC-seq caQTL peaks and GWAS SNPs) and you need to compare block-bootstrap vs. shuffling nulls via z scores of the overlap rate.

name: null-range-generation-for-enrichment-testing
description: Use when testing enrichment/overlap of genomic ranges (e.g. caQTLs, CREs, differential peaks) where naive shuffling or permutation would over-estimate statistical significance due to genomic correlation.

name: numerical-model-implementation
description: Use when implementing or re-deriving a probabilistic model of Hi-C interaction counts that requires a centromere-telomere (Rabl) positional term, bias factors, and sub-compartment probability products feeding a Poisson likelihood.

name: nystrom-approximation-large-scale-simulation
description: Use when the goal is to benchmark or extrapolate dimensionality-reduction scalability of scATAC-seq data beyond the available cell count (e.g., 20k-80k measured cells up to a simulated 1M cells) using the ensemble Nyström approximation.

name: occupancy-class-stratification
description: Use when you have ChIP-seq peak/occupancy data for many transcription factors and need to partition regions into HOT, MILD and COLD percentile classes to test whether apparent high occupancy correlates with control or artifact signal.

name: ode-based-gene-regulation-model-fitting
description: Use when you have a time-course expression dataset (e.g. GSE6865 B. subtilis) plus a candidate regulon list and need to infer direct regulator–target interactions with an ODE model rather than correlation or co-expression methods.

name: ode-model-parameter-fitting
description: Use when inferring regulatory interactions from time-course gene expression data and per-gene ODE parameters (synthesis rate, decay rate, regulator weights) must be fitted to a sigmoidal activation model, e.g. Bacillus subtilis SigA regulon with GSE6865 series.

name: ode-parameter-fitting-simulated-annealing
description: Use when time-course gene expression profiles must be fitted with an ODE regulatory model to decide which candidate gene–regulator interactions are real, as in Genexpi/CyGenexpi regulon inference.

name: oncogene-tumor-suppressor-classification
description: Use when validating a ranked list of predicted cis driver genes (e.g., iEDGE Rank-1 genes from amplifications/deletions) against curated cancer driver compendia to confirm that top-ranked genes are enriched for known oncogenes or tumor suppressors.

name: one-hot-dna-sequence-encoding
description: Use when a neural model such as deepC requires one-hot encoded A/C/G/T input built from hg19 reference sequence over megabase-scale windows, e.g. for saliency scoring or interaction prediction.

name: one-hot-sequence-encoding-for-deep-learning
description: Use when sgRNA sequence data must be converted into fixed-width one-hot channel matrices (e.g. 4 sequence channels over the 40-nt target window) to serve as deep learning input for CRISPR efficiency models.

name: one-hot-sgrna-sequence-encoding
description: Use when raw sgRNA nucleotide sequences must be converted into numeric tensors for the EpiCas-DL CNN (TensorFlow 2.4.1), either as 4×40 sequence-only matrices or stacked into 11×40 sequence-plus-epigenetics inputs.

name: one-sided-fisher-gene-set-enrichment
description: Use when validating a ranked or predicted driver gene list by testing its overlap against a curated functional gene set, e.g., reproducing the P = 3.53e-5 enrichment of BRCA Rank-1 cis genes among amplification-driven dependency genes.

name: one-sided-slope-t-testing
description: Use when you have paired cell-line dependency and copy-number matrices (e.g., DepMap DEMETER2 RNAi scores with CCLE CN) and need to identify genes whose 'essentiality' increases with amplification, e.g., to validate predicted cancer drivers.

name: ont-long-read-data-handling
description: Use when raw nanopore FAST5 electrolytic-current signal files must be decoded to nucleotide sequences without prior segmentation, e.g. reproducing Chiron-style end-to-end deep-learning base-calling.

name: ont-signal-event-segmentation
description: Use when raw ONT FAST5 current signals must be converted into per-base translocation times (seconds per genomic position) for sequencing-speed or non-B DNA structure analyses.

name: ontology-term-graph-traversal
description: Use when a gene set must be linked to broad phenotype categories via ontology annotations, requiring expansion of root terms (e.g. HPO/MPO) into all nested child terms before matching gene annotation files.

name: opencl-gpu-runtime-profiling
description: Use when you must quantify whether a network-inference pipeline is fast enough for repeated runs on commodity hardware, e.g. timing Genexpi's OpenCL GPU core vs TD-Aracne on the SigB and SigR regulon benchmarks.

name: optimal-k-decision-rule-implementation
description: Use when you have per-k consensus partition outputs (individual partitions, consensus partition, sample-sample consensus matrices) from a cola run and need to reconstruct or audit how the k is chosen.

name: optimize-based-root-minimization
description: Use when fitted INLA-based MethylCal calibration models must be inverted numerically to recover corrected methylation degrees from observed apparent methylation levels, because the correction (eq. 10) has no closed-form solution unlike Warnecke's or Moskalev's CPR (eq. 9).

name: orc-origin-binding-analysis
description: Use when paired-end MNase-seq data exist for wild-type versus an orc1-161 (or other ORC-mutant) yeast condition and you need RoboCOP-derived chromatin occupancy evaluated at ACS replication-origin sites.

name: orientation-barplot-visualization
description: Use when an Asymmetron strand-asymmetry analysis has produced per-feature same/opposite counts or ratios (e.g. a tfbs_chipseq_strand_asymmetries.tsv table) and the results need visual comparison across features.

name: orthogonal-binding-site-truth-set-ascertainment
description: Use when benchmarking a CLIP-seq binding-site caller (e.g., Skipper, CLIPper, Piranha) and an independent, biology-grounded positive set exists for an RBP (e.g., chrM binding for FASTKD2/TROVE2, 5' splice sites for PRPF8, GURUG motif for TARDBP, histone stem-loops for SLBP).

name: orthogonal-loop-validation-enrichment-assessment
description: Use when you have a 10 kb-binned .cool/.hic Hi-C matrix (e.g., GM12878) and need to benchmark predicted loops against enrichment-based callers or validate loop sets against orthogonal data such as H3K27ac HiChIP or ENCODE ChIP-Seq peaks.

name: orthologous-promoter-region-verification
description: Use when a GWAS SNP or query regulatory element has been mapped across species (e.g., human hg38 to mouse mm10 via mm10.hg38.r.chain) and you need positive-control verification that a promoter-region SNP maps to the orthologous promoter.

name: orthologous-region-mapping-chip-seq
description: Use when you need to identify orthologous non-coding regulatory elements across species (e.g., human-mouse or rat-human ENCODE ChIP-seq/DNase-seq peaks) and existing sequence-conservation liftOver suffers from multi-mapping, low precision, or low mapping rate.

name: orthologous-regulatory-element-mapping
description: Use when you need to lift over orthologous regulatory elements (TF ChIP-seq, DNase-seq, DNA methylation peaks) between species, e.g. mouse mm10 to human hg38, and reduce multi-mapping with functional-genomic similarity scoring.

name: overdispersion-estimation-from-replicates
description: Use when calling enriched CLIP/eCLIP windows from tiled transcriptomic or repetitive-element windows, where per-window read-start counts in IP and matched input are available and counts are overdispersed and GC-biased.

name: overlap-aware-tpx-merging-and-normalisation
description: Use when raw PATO/3plex TFO:TTS predictions must be consolidated and ranked: overlapping TPXs need merging, and a duplex-length-normalised thermal-stability score is needed for cross-duplex comparison.

name: overlap-rate-variance-estimation
description: Use when quantifying significance of an observed SNP–peak (or range–range) overlap against block-bootstrapped null ranges, i.e. when per-bootstrap overlap rates, their variance, and a z-score are needed.

name: overlap-ratio-computation
description: Use when genomic interval sets (e.g., eccDNA coordinates and GENCODE gene annotations) must be intersected and pairwise overlap fractions computed to decide which genes fall on which eccDNA elements.

name: overlap-statistic-zscore-computation
description: Use when a set of null genomic range iterations (from bootRanges block bootstrap or conventional shuffling) must be converted into an overlap-rate statistic with variance and z-score for false-positive-rate or significance assessment.

name: overlapping-regional-element-clustering-crem
description: Use when StitchIt has produced REMs per gene (from paired DNase1-seq and RNA-seq samples) and you need to consolidate overlapping or directly adjacent REMs into CREMs with unique IDs for database-level annotation or counting.

name: p-value-distribution-normalization
description: Use when integrating p-values/scores from multiple genomic assays whose distributions occupy different ranges — e.g. before SMITE scorePval — and you need scores comparable to a reference (expression) without changing within-feature ranking.

name: p-value-threshold-based-motif-filtering
description: Use when converting cell-line enhancer FASTA sequences (e.g. data/train/NHLF.fasta) into numeric motif features for enhancer prediction, requiring PWM sliding-window scanning with p-value threshold filtering.

name: pac-clustering-stability-evaluation
description: Use when comparing stability of consensus subgroup classifications on a gene expression matrix — e.g., judging whether row sampling outperforms column sampling, or whether ATC/skmeans yields more consistent partitions than alternatives.

name: pac-score-stability-assessment
description: Use when you have per-k consensus partitioning results (individual partitions, consensus partition, sample-sample consensus matrices) and must select the k using cola's PAC-based stability metrics and decision rules.

name: paired-cluster-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when assigning cell identities to pre-computed scRNA-seq clusters and you need marker genes that are specific to one cluster only, avoiding pseudo marker genes upregulated in two or more clusters.

name: paired-cluster-marker-gene-comparison
description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters were annotated with one-against-all marker genes (e.g., Seurat FindAllMarkers) and you need to check whether pseudo markers (genes significantly upregulated in at least two clusters) caused incorrect cell type annotations.

name: paired-end-naming-convention-application
description: Reference for setting up a NEAT project with paired-end sequencing data where reverse-read FASTQ files must be linked to their forward mates inside the centralized Targets.txt file.

name: paired-end-read-alignment-to-reference
description: Use when paired-end RIMS-seq FASTQ reads must be aligned to a reference genome — either user-supplied (option 2) or de novo assembled with SPAdes (option 1) — as a prerequisite for methylase specificity discovery.

name: paired-end-read-pair-categorization
description: Use when raw paired-end ChIA-PET (or HiChIP/PLAC-seq) FASTQ reads must be scanned for the bridge linker junction and partitioned by linker/tag content before read mapping.

name: paired-end-tag-alignment-and-bedpe-construction
description: Use when processing raw ChIA-PET paired-end FASTQ data after linker trimming and you need aligned PETs as deduplicated BEDPE pairs for downstream peak and loop calling.

name: paired-end-tag-fraction-computation
description: Use when processing ChIA-PET fastq data through ChIA-PET2 and you need to quantify per-step PET retention (pre-/post-alignment, post-duplicate-removal, intra-chromosomal >=4 PETs) for quality control.

name: paired-image-graph-training-data-preparation
description: Use when preparing training data for GILoop: the input is a KR-normalized intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact map (or Juicer-dump O/E matrix) and paired image and graph samples are needed for dual-branch loop-calling training.

name: paired-t-test-replicate-statistics
description: Use when eCLIP/skipper reproducible_enriched_windows tables exist for matched WT and mutant replicates and you need to quantify region-proportion shifts (CDS, deep introns) or test differential enrichment (e.g., tRNA loci) with replicate-level statistics.

name: paired-t-test-significance-testing
description: Use when you have per-task performance values (e.g., Accuracy) for two methods evaluated on the same matched set of benchmark tasks and need to show one method's advantage is statistically significant, not just numerically higher.

name: pairwise-co-clustering-matrix-construction
description: Use when two clustering solutions (e.g. SRIQ and consensus clustering) have been derived on the same sample set and you need a per-K quantitative similarity metric between their cluster partitions.

name: pairwise-epigenome-local-alignment
description: Use when two genomic regions are represented as single-track chromatin state sequences (ChromHMM labels) and you need a local alignment score to find which regions/gene bodies are epigenomically similar to a query region.

name: pairwise-group-methylation-comparison
description: Use when you have a clustered-region methylation counts table (combined.csv with chr, start, end, CpG and per-sample -N/-X count columns) and need to identify DMRs between two or more sample groups.

name: pairwise-local-alignment-score-computation
description: Use when the goal is to score similarity between genomic regions represented as chromatin state sequences (e.g. 500 kb Roadmap query regions vs. other regions or randomized negative controls) with a local alignment algorithm.

name: pam-proximal-nucleotide-preference-profiling
description: Use when a trained CRISPR sgRNA-efficiency CNN (EpiCas-DL CRISPRoff/CRISPRa models) needs per-base, per-position attribution to reveal which nucleotide a model favors at PAM-adjacent positions 20/21.

name: pan-cancer-multi-omics-neural-network-training
description: Use when training or reproducing the CITRUS pan-cancer model from somatic alteration matrices, gene expression, and TF-target gene priors, or extracting its held-out test predictions and TF activities.

name: pancancer-tumor-type-structure-visualization
description: Use when you have CITRUS output (output_dataset_CITRUS.pkl with 'hid_tmr', 'tmr', 'can') for 17 TCGA tumor types and want to cluster tumors, render tumor-grouping heatmaps, and test which TFs define each cancer type.

name: parallel-backend-configuration-genomics
description: Use when benchmarking or running a tiled genome-wide GAM fit (GenoGAM 2.0) that benefits from per-tile parallelization, and you need a registered BiocParallel backend plus a per-stage wall-clock breakdown.

name: parallel-cluster-job-submission
description: Use when an R/Bioconductor NGS workflow must process many sample files (e.g., ~100 FASTQ files) faster by parallelizing per-sample steps across multiple cluster cores and quantifying the speedup.

name: parallel-versus-sequential-execution-timing
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking compute-time claims for a TAD-calling or similar pipeline: input is Hi-C contact matrices at multiple resolutions (50 Kb, 25 Kb, 5 Kb) and the goal is to measure and compare sequential vs parallel wall-clock runtime.

name: parameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when validating that a method's scientific conclusions do not depend on its tunable parameters — e.g., sweeping DNA fragment size and window size in RECOGNICER and checking whether total domain length and read counts remain stable.

name: parameter-sweep-comparison-across-tools
description: Use when a published method exposes a discrete structural parameter (e.g., maximum subpaths) whose effect on known-target recovery must be quantified and compared head-to-head with a baseline tool on the same dataset.

name: partial-correlation-covariate-control
description: Use when a scored sequence set (e.g. FASTA with sequence scores in headers) plus a JASPAR motif library must be tested for motif enrichment at each position relative to an anchor (TSS, other motifs) while controlling for GC bias.

name: partial-correlation-drug-response-analysis
description: Use when estimating gene-expression vs drug-response associations from pharmacogenomic data (CCLE-style expression, copy number, mutation, and pharmacology profiles) where CNV effects and confounding mutations (kinase/tumor-suppressor genes) must be adjusted before correlation.

name: partial-svd-compartment-calling-on-filebacked-big-matrices
description: Use when per-sample A/B compartment scores must be computed from Hi-C contact maps (resolutions down to 5-10 kb) and full eigen-decomposition is infeasible due to memory limits on large chromosome matrices.

name: partition-concordance-evaluation
description: Use when choosing the number of resampling repetitions or the sampling type (rows vs columns) for cola consensus partitioning, or when verifying that a discovered subgroup partition is stable rather than an artifact of sampling.

name: partition-jaccard-concordance-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing the number of subgroups k from cola consensus partitioning results, when per-k consensus matrices and partitions are available and a reproducible, threshold-based k-selection rule is needed.

name: partition-size-imbalance-statistics
description: Use when a distributed Spark pipeline (e.g. BiSpark-style bisulfite alignment on WGBS FASTQ reads) shows uneven per-partition loads across executors, and you need to quantify imbalance and verify that hash-based re-partitioning balances record counts.

name: partition-stability-evaluation-1pac
description: Use when consensus clustering has been run with cola (or an equivalent framework) and you must quantify which top-value/partitioning method combination and k yields the most stable sample partitions.

name: pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when comparing a network- or clustering-based method's ability to recover known biological pathways from time-series expression data, requiring sensitivity/AUC benchmarking against curated pathway sets.

name: pathway-geneset-mapping
description: Use when you have a time-series expression matrix, known TF–gene interactions, and pathway gene sets (KEGG/Reactome/GO), and you need to determine which pathways are significantly regulated by TFs activated or repressed at specific time points.

name: pbc-pcr-bottleneck-coefficient-assessment
description: Use when QC'ing ChIP-seq or DNase-seq libraries for sequencing-depth bottlenecking — e.g., checking whether a sample's PBC falls above the atlas-derived 0.8 cutoff or comparing it to historical read-layer metric distributions.

name: pbm-selex-training-data-preparation
description: Use when raw uPBM, gcPBM, or HT-SELEX data must be formatted into DNAffinity's per-protein training files before running upbm_regressor.py, selex_regressor.py, or gcpbm_regressor.py.

name: pc-selection-and-sign-orientation-with-genomic-features
description: Use when computing A/B compartment scores from a Hi-C contact map and you need to decide which eigenvector (PC1 vs PC2) is the compartment component and which sign corresponds to the A-type compartment.

name: pca-based-dimensionality-reduction-of-windowed-profiles
description: Use when each sample contributes a windowed multi-variable profile over age (e.g., epigenomic/ATAC-seq or RNA-seq features in moving windows spanning ~10-20 years) and a multivariate test such as MANOVA needs a compact, low-dimensional representation of each window before testing.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-scchipsq
description: Use when a quality-controlled, sparse scChIP-seq count matrix (e.g. H3K27me3 from PDX tumor micro-environment samples) needs a dense low-dimensional feature space before clustering or 2D visualization.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-single-cell
description: Use when a sparse single-cell epigenomic count matrix (reads-in-peaks scATAC-seq or scChIP-seq bins) has passed QC filtering and normalization and a low-dimensional embedding is needed for clustering or 2D visualization.

name: pca-embedding-of-deviation-scores
description: Use when you need a low-dimensional cell embedding from scATAC-seq accessibility counts for clustering and want to compare it against alternatives such as SnapATAC.

name: pcawg-cohort-driver-result-aggregation
description: Use when comparing called cancer driver elements from DriverPower (or a similar method) against gold-standard gene sets on the same PCAWG cohorts to quantify precision, recall and F1 for coding, splice-site and non-coding discovery.

name: pchi-c-promoter-other-interaction-normalization
description: Use when normalizing pcHi-C replicates into promoter-centered long-range P-O cis-interaction calls, or when benchmarking covNorm's significant interaction calls against a CHiCAGO baseline via ROC AUC and hypergeometric overlap.

name: pcr-duplicate-removal
description: Use when processing methylation-seq alignments (e.g., Msuite SAM output) where PCR over-amplification may inflate read counts; reads sharing identical start/end coordinates and strand must be collapsed before methylation calling.

name: pcr-duplicate-removal-genomic-pets
description: Use when processing ChIA-PET paired-end FASTQ data and identical PETs arising from PCR amplification must be collapsed prior to MACS2 peak calling and MICC2 loop significance estimation.

name: peak-background-region-classification
description: Use when ChIP-seq bins (e.g. 1000-bp from spikChIP/SeqCode binning) must be partitioned into peaks vs background regions to quantify how a normalization strategy (spikChIP, ChIP-Rx, Tag removal) affects enriched vs non-occupied loci.

name: peak-caller-algorithm-dispatch
description: Use when a ChIPseq pipeline must call enrichment peaks from filtered .bam alignments and the peak calling algorithm and its parameters are configured in a centralized NEAT Targets.txt file.

name: peak-caller-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking ChIP-Seq peak callers on one shared treated+control dataset (e.g., NRSF GSE13047 or STAT1) to compare peak counts and TF-motif enrichment across HPeak, PeakFinder, FindPeaks, MACS, SISSRs, CisGenome, and ChIPseeqer.

name: peak-caller-benchmarking
description: Use when multiple CC peak callers are available for qbed input and you must decide which caller to trust, or when reproducing the Pycallingcards Fig. 2c-e accuracy benchmark comparing callers on bulk and single-cell HCT116 datasets.

name: peak-caller-method-comparison
description: Use when comparing differential ChIP-Seq occupancy methods (e.g. GenoGAM vs csaw vs DESeq2) on the same dosage-responsive dataset using ROC/AUC against a quantile-defined gold standard.

name: peak-caller-scaling-visualization
description: Use when comparing computational cost (wall-clock runtime, peak RSS memory) of calling-cards peak callers across a dilution series of qbed datasets with increasing insertion counts (e.g., >5M insertions).

name: peak-calling-algorithm-selection
description: Use when building or editing a NEAT project's Targets.txt for ChIPseq data (e.g. H3K4me3 ChIPseq from mouse embryonic stem cells) and you must choose between MACS and SPP as the peak caller.

name: peak-calling-quality-assessment
description: Use when processing raw ChIP-seq or DNase-seq FASTQ files (treatment and control) and you need per-sample quality metrics to judge whether peak calls are reliable before downstream analysis.

name: peak-centered-metaplot-generation
description: Use when you need a standardized, reproducible averaged profile of sequencing signal (BAM/SAM ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN reads) aggregated around a set of peak centers to compare conditions, such as WT vs KO ChIP levels.

name: peak-file-bed-import-export
description: Use when input consists of peak BED files (e.g. *_peaks.stringent.bed from CUT&Tag/CUT&Run/ChIP-seq) that must be loaded as GRanges for QC/comparison, or when harmonized/lifted intervals must be written back out to a BED file.

name: peak-gene-expression-concordance-analysis
description: Use when you have qbed insertion data from two biological conditions (e.g. male vs female GBM Brd4 single-cell calling cards) plus matched single-cell RNA expression, and need to test concordance of differential binding with nearby gene expression.

name: peak-gene-expression-pairing
description: Use when you have single-cell calling cards insertions (qbed) plus matched scRNA-seq for the same cells and need to identify TF binding peaks whose cell-type-specific binding correlates with expression of nearby genes.

name: peak-length-summary-statistics
description: Use when comparing peak sets from multiple ChIP-seq peak-calling algorithms on histone mark datasets (H3K4me3, H3K27me3) and you need overlap percentages and average peak-length summaries.

name: peak-overlap-analysis-across-algorithms
description: Use when you need to evaluate agreement between different ChIP-Seq peak-calling algorithms on the same dataset, e.g. comparing called peak regions for histone marks like H3K4me3 or H3K27me3 by pairwise overlap percentages.

name: peak-qc-metrics-computation
description: Use when ChIP-seq/CUT&Run/CUT&Tag peak files (e.g. BED narrowPeaks) need QC before cross-sample comparison, specifically quantifying the fraction of peaks falling in ENCODE blacklisted regions.

name: peak-rank-enrichment-stratification
description: Use when comparing peak-calling outputs from ChIP-Seq and ChIP-chip (or across peak callers) and you need rank-resolved evidence that higher-ranked peaks are progressively enriched for the expected TF motif family.

name: peak-region-filtering-by-length-and-count
description: Use when MACS2-called merged peak regions from ChIP-seq marks (e.g. ENCODE K562 H3K4me3 + H3K9ac BAMs) must be filtered by region length in bins and minimum counts/pileup prior to DGW DTW clustering.

name: peak-score-distribution-modelling
description: Use when you have multiple peak files (e.g. CUT&Tag/CUT&Run H3K27ac BED files as GRanges) that should be collapsed into a single consensus peak set, and you must choose between fast overlap-based and distribution-model-based consensus calling.

name: peak-set-non-overlapping-filtering
description: Use when a RangedSummarizedExperiment of ATAC-seq/DNase-seq fragment counts has already been sample-filtered and the peak set still contains peaks with no fragments across samples or overlapping peak intervals that would bias motif accessibility estimates.

name: peak-size-inflection-cutoff-estimation
description: Use when calling broad histone-mark peaks (H3K27me3) and needing a data-driven, cell-type-specific peak-size cutoff to decide which merged peaks count as Polycomb domains over genes.

name: peak-supported-anchor-filtering
description: Use when calling chromatin contact domains (CCDs) from CTCF ChIA-PET loops and you need to restrict the loop set to high-confidence, peak-supported interactions before merging into domain intervals.

name: peak-to-gene-distance-assignment
description: Use when ENCODE ChIP-seq peak BED files for TRs must be converted into gene-level regulatory potential scores via peak-to-TSS distances plus peak signal strength weighting.

name: peak-to-gene-promoter-assignment
description: Use when you have a BED file of called peaks and need a non-redundant gene list for enrichment analysis, by linking each peak to RefSeq genes with a TSS within a promoter window (e.g. 2500 bp).

name: pearson-correlation-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a trained TF-affinity model must be evaluated across experimental platforms (e.g. HT-SELEX training, uPBM testing) and ranked against published predictors via per-TF Pearson correlations.

name: pearson-correlation-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating fine-tuned DNA foundation models on the DNALONGBENCH RSAP regression task and reporting per-sample PCC for Human, Mouse, and average against the expert-model benchmark.

name: pearson-correlation-hierarchical-clustering
description: Use when clustering a log2-transformed, median-centered gene expression matrix (samples × transcripts) with a Pearson-correlation-distance hierarchical method, and when you need stable cluster assignments across K values to compare against an alternative clustering method.

name: pearson-correlation-matrix-computation
description: Use when a feature table of variant-prioritization predictor scores (e.g., the 574 dsQTL-positive and 27,735 negative SNPs of training dataset 1) must be screened for collinearity before feeding scores into ncDeepBrain or gene prioritization.

name: pearson-correlation-model-comparison
description: Use when comparing CNN, HyenaDNA, or Caduceus variants against an expert model on base-pair-resolution regression of transcription initiation signals over 100,000-bp sequences in DNALONGBENCH.

name: pearson-correlation-of-cross-model-scores
description: Use when two sequence-based variant-effect models (e.g. DeepFun and DeepSEA) have been run on the same SNP set and you must quantify per-assay score agreement, such as CTCF, DNase-seq, H3K4me3, or H3K9ac concordance.

name: pearson-correlation-of-crup-probability-tracks
description: Reference for computing or benchmarking the cor_CRUP generic feature (Pearson correlation between summed CRUP-EP and CRUP-PP probability tracks across cell types) when building or ablation-testing ET-interaction feature vectors.

name: pearson-correlation-of-fold-change-signatures
description: Use when two differential analysis results (e.g., young-vs-old log2 fold-change per ATAC-seq peak in men vs women) must be compared on a common feature set to measure how much of the response is shared versus sex- or condition-specific.

name: pearson-correlation-of-genomic-tracks
description: Use when you have CscoreTool-M cscore.txt or cscore.bedgraph sub-compartment probabilities and an independent track (NAD-seq, Lamin-B1 DamID) that can be aggregated over the same 100 kb windows, and you want to quantify agreement.

name: pearson-correlation-outlier-cell-filtering
description: Use when a scChIP-seq or scATAC-seq count matrix has passed read-count QC (e.g. ≥1600 unique reads, top 5% coverage removed) but may still contain isolated low-quality outlier cells before dimensionality reduction and clustering.

name: pearson-correlation-sample-assignment
description: Use when each sample in a log2-transformed, median-centered tumor expression matrix (e.g., the SRIQ '_mc_log2_nz' output) must be labeled with a nearest-centroid TRU/PI/PP call to compare against an independent clustering solution.

name: pearson-logistic-gsea-baseline-execution
description: Use when a new TR–drug response inference method (e.g. RePhine) must be compared fairly against established mRNA- and target-based baselines on the same simulated noise or confounder scenarios.

name: per-base-pair-sensitivity-specificity-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking a peak caller for broad histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3) against a qPCR-validated truth set and needing threshold-free ROC comparison of sensitivity and specificity per base pair.

name: per-base-quality-profiling
description: Use when raw short-read data is supplied as FASTQ files and you need per-cycle quality summaries before or after preprocessing, especially for many samples requiring one combined visual QC report.

name: per-chromosome-genomic-array-io
description: Use when a pipeline needs to persist or reload per-chromosome, binned genomic annotation arrays (e.g. deepC skeleton tags in 1–10 range) from Hi-C contact maps at 5 kb resolution.

name: per-cluster-consensus-cnv-imputation
description: Use when per-cell CNV calls from scATAC-seq data are noisy or sparse and cluster-level consensus genotypes are needed — e.g. after identifyCNVClusters has produced a CNV cluster file and Louvain cell clusters exist.

name: per-experiment-mean-centering
description: Use when combining gene expression values from multiple GEO series into a single matrix and you need to remove per-experiment offset differences, e.g., building COnTORT_organized_transcriptomic_data.txt (mean-centered variant).

name: per-gene-polycomb-repression-binarization
description: Use when a cell type-specific binary annotation of polycomb-repressed genes is needed from H3K27me3 ChIP-seq, e.g. as an epigenetic-state input feature for SV pathogenicity prediction in POSTRE-style analyses.

name: per-gene-score-table-aggregation
description: Use when interval-level ClinGen HI/TS dosage-sensitivity annotations (GRCh37/hg19 BED) must be mapped onto individual genes and reduced to binary per-gene dosage-sensitivity calls for LOF/GOF contexts, or when POSTRE per-SV results need a per-gene aggregated view.

name: per-lineage-count-summarization
description: Use when you have per-cancer-type BIT rank tables and DepMap CRISPR/Cas9 Chronos gene effect data and need per-lineage counts of functionally essential TRs.

name: per-read-methylation-calling
description: Use when bisulfite-treated reads have been aligned with the 'three-letter' approach and you need per-read/per-site methylation states recovered by comparing alignments back to the original (un-converted) reference genome.

name: per-sequence-information-content-interpretation
description: Use when a cycle-2 Delila-PY run has produced per-sequence information content values (bits) and you must decide which sequences are poor matches to keep or drop before regenerating the book with delila.

name: per-task-benchmark-accuracy-aggregation
description: Use when comparing two or more celltyping methods evaluated on the same set of matched tasks (e.g., 50 Cellcano benchmark tasks) and you need a statistical test of whether one method's accuracy advantage is significant.

name: per-tissue-cross-validation-evaluation
description: Use when labeled nc-sindels (cis-eQTL positives vs negatives) must be classified per GTEx tissue and model comparison requires within-tissue AUROC/AUPRC medians across 44 tissues rather than a pooled single-split evaluation.

name: percentile-based-outlier-winsorization
description: Use when a numeric genomic data matrix (e.g. gene expression rows x samples) contains extreme outlier values that could distort row-wise statistics or downstream partitioning, as part of cola's adjust_matrix() cleaning pipeline.

name: percentile-ranking-of-predicted-variant-effects
description: Use when you have deepC-predicted effect sizes for one or more candidate SNPs and need a population-level comparison (percentile) against sampled background SNPs to decide which variant most plausibly perturbs genome folding.

name: periodicity-detection-in-enrichment-profiles
description: Use when you have ChIP-seq-scored DNA sequences centered on an anchor motif (e.g. Nanog motif sites scored by mESC Nanog ChIP-seq signal) and want to test whether a second TF's motif (e.g. Sox2) occurs at periodic, helical-phase offsets rather than at a single fixed spacing.

name: perl-scripting-for-genomics
description: Use when reproducing the LuxR/H-NS ChIP-seq analyses in V. harveyi — counting overlapping peaks, detecting H-NS doublet peaks, or assigning peaks to ORFs — using the Perl scripts from the LuxR_H-NS GitHub repository.

name: permutation-based-alignment-score-normalization
description: Use when computing EpiAlign horizontal alignment scores within an epigenome (e.g. 500 kb regions of a Roadmap sample) and raw Smith-Waterman-style scores must be calibrated against a random background before ranking or clustering.

name: permutation-based-anova-significance-testing
description: Use when you need to establish whether a tuning parameter (e.g. minimal TPX length 8/10/12/16) significantly influences AUC performance, by comparing a full linear model against a nested model without that term via ANOVA and a permutation test.

name: permutation-based-contact-enrichment
description: Use when validating that single-cell chromatin structures (e.g., TLD-cliques from deDoc2 TLD predictions) show genuine inter-TLD contact enrichment beyond what is expected from genomic layout alone.

name: permutation-based-significance-testing
description: Use when regressing CCLE pharmacogenomic drug response (e.g. PLX4720 sensitivity) against regulation-potential (RP) scores of TR targets and you need empirical significance beyond parametric uniP/multiP likelihood-ratio tests.

name: permutation-based-significance-testing
description: Use when a positional enrichment profile (one correlation per heatmap column relative to an anchor point such as a TSS or motif) must carry statistical significance and confidence bands robust to GC bias and spatial autocorrelation.

name: permutation-shuffling-null-generation
description: Use when benchmarking null-range generation for genomic overlap testing: you need a shuffling/permutation baseline null distribution of overlap rates to compare against block bootstrapping (bootRanges) for FPR calibration.

name: permutation-significance-testing
description: Use when a TF–pathway interaction score from time-series expression data needs an empirical significance call: TSMiner derives each block's probability via permutation testing and accepts interactions with score >= 50 and probability >= 50%.

name: perplexity-parameter-tuning-for-tsne
description: Use when visualizing cell-to-cell similarity of single-cell ATAC-seq profiles via chromVAR deviationsTsne and a perplexity must be set for the number of filtered cells (e.g., perplexity = 10 on small filtered sets).

name: pet-count-percentile-filtering
description: Use when calling chromatin contact domains from CTCF ChIA-PET loop-calling output and you need to reduce noisy, low-support loops before merging intervals of continuous loop coverage.

name: pet-deduplication
description: Use when linker-filtered ChIA-PET FASTQ tags must be mapped to a reference genome and deduplicated so that downstream peak calling and loop calling receive only uniquely aligned, nonredundant PETs.

name: pet-duplicate-removal-and-alignment-qc
description: Use when processing raw ChIA-PET FASTQ (bridge-linker or half-linker) data and you need PCR duplicate removal and per-step QC before PET construction, MACS2 peak calling, and MICC loop calling.

name: pet-rescue-count-comparison
description: Use when processing bridge-linker ChIA-PET raw reads and you need to measure the sensitivity gain of linker-searching at 1 allowed mismatch (-e 1) versus the strict 0-mismatch setting (-e 0), expressed as rescued PET counts and valid PET ratio from the trim.stat summaries.

name: pet-to-peak-interaction-mapping
description: Use when aligned, PCR-deduplicated ChIA-PET PETs in bedpe format must be assigned to MACS2-called anchor peak pairs to generate candidate intra-/inter-chromosomal loops.

name: pfam-hmm-domain-scan
description: Use when a research question asks whether a set of transcription factors (e.g. TFs occupying HOT regions) can bind single-stranded DNA directly or through their direct interaction partners, requiring domain-level annotation via PFAM HMMs plus PPI evidence.

name: phage-deamination-treatment-optimization-analysis
description: Use when paired-end RIMS-seq fastq data (e.g. Xp12 phage DNA across 0-14 h / 0.1-0.5 M NaOH treatments) must be converted into a C-to-T deamination rate table or R1/R2 fold-imbalance curve to choose optimal alkaline-treatment conditions.

name: pharmacogenomic-chipseq-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a TR–drug response identification method on synthetic pharmacogenomic/ChIP-seq data, or when evaluating robustness of such methods to added noise or spurious confounder-induced correlations.

name: pharmacogenomic-data-integration
description: Use when you have cell-line pharmacogenomic data (expression, CNV, mutation, drug sensitivity such as CCLE PLX4720 profiles) plus ChIP-seq or RP-score target maps and need to find drug-response TRs while adjusting confounders.

name: phased-methylation-core-identification
description: Use when bisulfite amplicon reads have been converted to a binary epihaplotype matrix and the goal is to identify statistically significant phased mCpG combinations (cores) and track epiallele families across populations.

name: phasing-accuracy-and-runtime-evaluation
description: Use when comparing diploid single-individual haplotyping tools on simulated or real reads (Illumina, 10X, Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, ONT) and you need runtime, memory, and phasing-accuracy tables.

name: phasing-tool-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a large or error-prone long-read dataset (e.g. ~32x PacBio SMRT for a gigantic diploid genome) must be phased and tool scalability in CPU hours and memory must be empirically compared.

name: phastcons-conservation-scoring
description: Use when you need to score evolutionary conservation of genomic regions (e.g. rank candidate regulatory blocks) using a PhastCons multiple-alignment track plus RefSeq annotation, and compare score distributions across feature classes.

name: phenotype-category-annotation
description: Use when preparing SV input for POSTRE and each variant must be tagged with one or more disease-relevant phenotype categories from the seven supported options to drive tissue-specific enhancer/TAD analysis.

name: phenotype-group-term-propagation
description: Use when a candidate gene must be scored for association with an SV-associated phenotype group using HPO (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype.txt) and MPO (mp.obo, HMD_HumanPhenotype.rpt) annotations, as in POSTRE's genePhenoScore module.

name: phenotype-stratified-results-tabulation
description: Use when POSTRE has been run in batch (POSTRE_multiSV or Multiple SV Submission) over an SV set with attached phenotype lists and you must tally pathogenic vs non-pathogenic calls per phenotype association and compute non-pathogenic percentages per mode.

name: phosphoproteomic-tf-list-integration
description: Use when CITRUS ensemble TF activities (hid_tmr) must be validated against independent TF lists, e.g. MCF10A isogenic PIK3CA knock-in phosphoproteomics or AKT1 kinase assay substrate TFs.

name: phred-quality-score-sequence-trimming
description: Use when raw Sanger .ab1 bisulfite sequencing PCR (BSP) trace files must be quality-trimmed before computing CpG methylation percentages, especially when sequences end up too short or low-quality after trimming.

name: pie-chart-distribution-visualization
description: Use when you have BED-format peak lists or genomic coordinate sets (e.g. bivalent vs single-mark ChIP-seq peaks) and need to quantify which genomic features they occupy and plot the distribution as pie charts.

name: pipeline-runtime-measurement
description: Use when quantifying end-to-end runtime and output file sizes of a NEAT NGS analysis on the truncated ChIPseq/RNAseq test datasets, or when validating speed claims for a sequenced run assessment within 24 h.

name: pipeline-runtime-profiling
description: Use when choosing between read-trimming or read-mapping tools for an NGS pipeline and a reproducible comparison of wall-clock runtime plus retained-read yield/mapping accuracy is needed to justify the selection.

name: pipeline-wall-clock-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing runtime efficiency of post-alignment bisulfite methylation pipelines, or when a user needs per-step wall-clock timings for extracting, clustering, and testing CpG methylation counts on large MethylC-seq datasets.

name: poi-position-histogram-quantification
description: Use when you have DGW clustering outputs (config, warping paths, cluster BEDs) plus POI coordinate files and need a quantitative, per-cluster measure of whether warping tightened TSS/FSS alignment.

name: poisson-enrichment-peak-testing
description: Use when Calling Cards qbed/ccf insertions must be tested for significant TF binding enrichment — e.g. after greedy candidate-peak extension, to decide which candidates become CC peaks.

name: poisson-log-likelihood-evaluation
description: Use when modeling trans Hi-C interactions between equal-length genomic windows annotated with Rabl positions (relative centromere-telomere coordinates), or when fitting/evaluating the CscoreTool-M generative model with fitted alpha and beta parameters.

name: poisson-significance-testing-of-insertion-enrichment
description: Use when bulk or single-cell Calling Cards (CC) qbed insertion data must be converted into statistically significant TF binding-site peaks and no ready-made peak set is available.

name: poisson-significance-testing-with-fdr
description: Use when candidate enriched domains (e.g. broad H3K27me3 domains from coarse-graining) must be filtered for statistical significance against a control sample using a local Poisson model with BH FDR correction.

name: pooled-data-hiccups-loop-benchmarking
description: Use when quantifying how chromatin loop recovery scales with scHi-C cell number: per-cell contact files exist at multiple subsample sizes and pooled HiCCUPS loop calls must be compared against SnapHiC.

name: position-specific-probability-matrix-scoring
description: Use when converting MEME-discovered differential motifs around 6mA sites into numeric per-sequence features for a classifier, given a FASTA-like training set of 41-nt positive/negative samples and motif probability matrices.

name: position-weight-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have a GenBank file plus a tab-delimited sites file of genomic positions (e.g., ChIP-seq peak centers or transcription start sites) and need a binding-site logo and PWM.

name: position-weight-matrix-emission-modeling
description: Use when building a chromatin occupancy model that scores TF or nucleosome states from nucleotide sequence alongside accessibility data, and sequence emissions must be probabilistically defined per HMM state.

name: positional-correlation-profiling
description: Use when analyzing scored, anchored DNA sequences (e.g. FASTA headers with sequence scores) and you need position-resolved motif enrichment rather than a single aggregate enrichment score.

name: positional-enrichment-profile-visualization
description: Use when you have centered, scored genomic sequences (e.g., ±200 bp around ChIP-seq or ChIP-nexus peak summits with signal scores) and need to determine at which positions a TF binding motif is enriched relative to the sequence center.

name: positional-motif-heatmap-construction
description: Use when you have scored DNA sequences (FASTA headers of the form '>name score') centered on anchor points and a fixed JASPAR PWM library, and need a motif-by-position heatmap of excess match scores relative to the anchors.

name: positive-negative-variant-labeling
description: Use when constructing supervised training data for non-coding variant prioritization, i.e. pairing known functional/eQTL/disease SNPs (positives) with frequency-matched common background SNVs (negatives) in tab-delimited variant files.

name: posterior-credible-interval-quantification
description: Use when the input is an epigenomic region set (e.g., MACS2/DiffBind-derived ATAC-seq DARs as a BED file) and you need TR ranks with probabilistic uncertainty rather than a frequentist-only enrichment score.

name: posterior-marginalisation-of-read-assignments
description: Use when RRBS reads at a multi-sample locus have been assigned to epialleles by bed_fit and you need per-sample epiallele distributions (phi_s) that account for assignment uncertainty rather than hard MAP read labels.

name: posterior-predictive-outlier-detection
description: Use when calibrating pyrosequenced/amplicon methylation levels with MethylCal and suspect aberrant standard-control observations at some CpG-AMP combinations that would bias the fitted calibration curve.

name: power-grid-visualization
description: Use when scPower's optimize.constant.budget has produced a grid of designs over nCells and readDepth for a fixed budget and you must inspect or communicate which combination maximizes powerDetect.

name: pr-auc-evaluation-of-loop-callers
description: Use when comparing loop-calling models (fused dual-branch vs. single-view U-Net or GCN baselines) on downsampled Hi-C contact maps and reporting robustness as mean PR-AUC, e.g. at the 1.5% (39 million cis-reads) depth.

name: prc2-downregulation-verification
description: Use when validating a predicted transcriptional-regulator/drug-response association (e.g. EZH2/PRC2 loss reducing PLX4720 sensitivity) with independent expression datasets comparing drug-resistant versus drug-sensitive cells.

name: precision-and-true-positive-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare two genomic interval mapping methods on matched orthologous peak sets, evaluating mean precision and true-positive counts against a gold-standard orthologous dataset.

name: precision-benchmark-comparison-across-species
description: Use when mapping regulatory-element intervals (ChIP-seq, DNase-seq, methylation) across species and you need to quantify mapping precision against matched orthologous epigenome datasets, comparing AdaLiftOver with UCSC liftOver baselines.

name: precision-recall-auc-computation
description: Use when comparing loop-calling model performance on imbalanced Hi-C loop-detection tasks (positive loop labels are rare), especially across Hi-C sequencing-depth conditions or between dual-branch GILoop variants where mean PR-AUC (e.g., 0.3790 vs 0.3718) is the reported metric.

name: precision-recall-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a cell-type-specific enhancer-target prediction model against BENGI ground truth, or when quantifying the contribution of a feature group (e.g. regulatory distance) via AUPRC ablation.

name: precision-recall-benchmark-evaluation-of-loop-callers
description: Use when comparing called chromatin loop sets from scHi-C loop-calling tools against a merged bulk-Hi-C/HiChIP reference list to rank methods by precision, recall, and F1 across subsampling levels.

name: precision-recall-curve-analysis
description: Use when comparing loop-calling predictions (e.g., GILoop vs. Peakachu) or evaluating a transferred model on K562/HeLa-S3 Hi-C data, and you need threshold-free precision-recall comparison against a defined ground-truth loop set.

name: precision-recall-curve-computation
description: Use when two or more open-chromatin (or ChIP/CUT&Tag) peak files must be benchmarked against a gold-standard reference peak set, and a precision-recall plot is needed to contrast technologies such as ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq.

name: precision-recall-curve-evaluation
description: Use when you have computationally called nucleosome dyad positions plus independent, high-precision ground-truth dyad annotations (e.g., Brogaard et al. chemical cleavage) and need to quantify positioning accuracy via precision-recall.

name: precision-recall-f1-computation
description: Use when comparing called binding sites from CLIP-seq methods against independently ascertained truth sets (e.g., chrM binding, splice sites, known motifs) to quantify which method recovers true RBP targets .

name: precision-recall-performance-metrics-computation
description: Use when comparing binary enhancer-target (or other paired genomic) interaction classifiers on imbalanced BENGI-style datasets and you need AUPRC/F1 from chromosome-based cross-validated held-out predictions.

name: predicted-versus-observed-model-validation
description: Use when a fitted statistical model (e.g., expression probability priors from a pilot scRNA-seq study) must be shown to generalize to an independent dataset not used for parameter estimation, by regressing predicted against observed counts.

name: prediction-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when a paper reports pathogenicity-prediction success rates for structural variants (e.g. 95% vs 66% across two POSTRE modes) and the goal is to rerun the tool on its released patient SV files to verify the numbers and per-gene calls.

name: prediction-entropy-computation
description: Use when running Cellcano's two-round celltyping on scATAC-seq data and you need to derive anchor cells from first-round MLP prediction probabilities via an entropy quantile cutoff before training the KD model.

name: prediction-score-aggregation
description: Use when a leave-one-out or jackknife evaluation has emitted per-sample prediction scores and you need to aggregate them into a headline metric (e.g., ACC) for comparison against a published baseline.

name: predictive-distribution-region-ranking
description: Use when a fitted cisTopic LDA model (e.g. a 30-topic model on 5,335 PBMC cells) exists and per-cell enrichment of curated epigenomic signatures is needed, requiring cell-specific region rankings as input.

name: pretrained-cnn-variant-scoring
description: Use when a set of non-coding SNP coordinates and alleles needs tissue- or cell type-specific functional impact scores across ENCODE/Roadmap epigenomic tracks, rather than a single pathogenicity score.

name: pretrained-embedding-vectorization
description: Use when raw DNA sequences in FASTA format must be turned into fixed feature-vector inputs for a deep learning model, and a species-matched pre-trained dna2vec embedding matrix (hg19 or mm9) is available.

name: pretrained-model-transfer-across-cell-types
description: Use when you need to predict chromatin loops in a Hi-C contact map without training a new model, by transferring an existing Peakachu model trained in a different cell type or species, and quantifying overlap with cell-type-matched models.

name: pretrained-random-forest-loop-scoring
description: Use when a .cool/.hic Hi-C or HiChIP contact map needs loop calling with a pre-trained Peakachu model, or when an FDR estimate for loop predictions is required via a perturbation expected to abolish loops.

name: primary-peak-ratio-mixed-base-trimming
description: Use when processing .ab1 Sanger chromatogram traces in ABSP whose ends contain mixed-base positions, and the goal is to define trimming boundaries before computing CpG methylation percentages.

name: process-block-instance-enumeration
description: Use when a Watchdog XML workflow task definition contains process blocks (process sequences, folders, or tables) and you need to determine or reconstruct the exact set of expanded subtask instances.

name: promoter-enhancer-discrimination-classification
description: Use when you have promoter and enhancer DNA sequences (e.g. the EPdata folder) and need to test whether a promoter-identification model can classify enhancers as negatives on a count-balanced, cell-line-specific benchmark.

name: promoter-motif-scanning
description: Use when a promoter FASTA must be scanned for putative binding sites of a known motif (e.g., H-NS TCGATAAATT in PluxCDABE) and site coordinates must be compared against established binding-site annotations for overlap.

name: promoter-positive-negative-cluster-visualization
description: Use when you have labeled promoter FASTA-style sequence sets (first half positive, second half negative) per human cell line and need a visual check that fused sequence-encoding features separate the two classes before model training.

name: promoter-probability-derivation
description: Use when computing CENTRE cell-type-specific features for enhancer-target pairs and promoter probabilities (PP_prob_enh, PP_prob_gene) are needed from normalized histone-mark ChIP-seq tracks of the cell type of interest.

name: promoter-region-annotation-overlap
description: Use when methylation callsets (e.g. Bismark .cov output) need unique region identifiers per promoter or CGI before running DXM, or when restricting deconvolution to specific genomic compartments like TSS +/-5kb promoters.

name: promoter-window-definition-from-annotation
description: Use when testing whether sequence- or feature-defined genomic bins (e.g., CT/GA-rich regions from the hg19 multi-fasta) are enriched in promoters, and only a gene-annotation file (RefSeq) is available for locating TSSs.

name: protein-interaction-network-filtering
description: Use when you need to annotate a fixed list of proteins (e.g. 165 human TFs) with a domain-based capability (OB, KH, RRM, sPC4-like ssDNA-binding) propagated one hop through direct physical PPIs, and report the fraction annotated.

name: protein-protein-dna-association-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you have DESSO motif/TFBS predictions and ENCODE ChIP-seq peak files for multiple TFs in one cell line (e.g. the 100 K562 TFs) and want to identify indirect (tethering) TF-DNA binding mechanisms.

name: proximal-motif-pairing-with-bedtools-closest
description: Use when two strand-annotated BED files of genomic elements (e.g. two transcription factor motif sets such as SP1 and YY1 tfbsConsSites) must be paired at a distance range to test strand orientation preferences.

name: pseudo-bulk-schic-development-stage-analysis
description: Use when you have pseudo-bulk single-cell Hi-C maps at multiple developmental time points and need to group genomic bins by dynamic compartmentalization patterns rather than comparing transitions pairwise.

name: pseudo-label-cell-type-classification
description: Use when you have target scATAC-seq gene scores plus first-round MLP predictions with per-cell probabilities, and need to classify non-anchor cells by self-training on confident (low-entropy) pseudo-labeled anchors.

name: pseudo-marker-gene-detection
description: Use when annotating scRNA-seq clusters with Seurat FindAllMarkers (Wilcoxon rank-sum) and you need to flag candidate pseudo markers by comparing against scCATCH paired-comparison gene sets before trusting annotations.

name: pseudobulk-count-aggregation
description: Use when a per-cell UMI/read count matrix plus a cell annotation data frame (donor and cell type per cell) must be converted to donor-by-cell-type pseudobulk matrices to count expressed genes (e.g. count>0 and count>10) for power modelling or model validation.

name: pseudobulk-count-matrix-construction
description: Use when a per-cell count matrix (UMI or read counts) plus donor/sample and cell-type annotations must be aggregated into pseudobulk form to fit expression priors or run pseudobulk-based DEG/eQTL power analysis with scPower.

name: pseudobulk-differential-expression-testing-edger
description: Use when testing differential expression between individuals/groups from single cell RNA-seq UMI count data: the pseudobulk aggregation + edgeR route is the recommended analysis whose power scPower estimates.

name: pseudobulk-negative-binomial-power-modeling
description: Use when planning or optimizing multi-sample scRNA-seq DEG studies: you need power/sample-size/read-depth trade-offs (e.g. cells per cell type vs number of individuals) for a pseudobulk two-group comparison with effect-size and expression priors.

name: pvalue-reproducibility-verification
description: Use when a benchmarking claim of statistical significance over matched tasks (e.g., reported paired t-test p-values on Accuracy) must be independently recomputed and validated against published values.

name: pwm-one-hot-sequence-encoding
description: Use when scored FASTA sequences centered on an anchor (e.g. TSS or motif) must be converted to one-hot tensors and scanned with JASPAR PWMs to produce a motif-by-position heatmap for downstream positional enrichment analysis.

name: pwm-weighted-high-affinity-sequence-annotation
description: Use when preparing uPBM training files (35-mer sequences with experimental affinities, e.g. proteins/{protein}/{protein}_training.txt) for per-TF affinity regression where sequence variability must be reduced and PWM-matching high-affinity k-mers emphasized.

name: pytorch-gcn-model-implementation
description: Use when you need to convert an N×N Hi-C contact matrix into low-dimensional node embeddings (e.g., 16-D per genomic bin) as features for downstream unsupervised clustering of TADs.

name: q-value-threshold-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when you must justify the FIMO q-value cutoff for motif-annotating CRE sequences, or test whether removing overlapping/redundant motif annotations degrades cell-type-specific classification performance.

name: qbed-insertion-data-loading
description: Use when the input is raw Calling Cards sequencing output as qbed/ccf insertion files (e.g. from GEO accessions like GSE148448) or a built-in pycallingcards dataset, and peaks must be called.

name: qbed-insertion-downsampling
description: Use when a qbed file (e.g. >20M PBase Brd4 K562 insertions) must be subsampled to decreasing insertion counts to measure how peak-caller runtime and memory scale with dataset size.

name: qbed-peak-calling-with-cccaller
description: Use when the input is qbed/ccf calling cards insertion data (e.g., Brd4 scCC insertions from GEO) and TF binding sites must be called as peaks for annotation, AnnData construction, or peak-gene pairing.

name: qc-aggregation
description: Use when per-sample peak calls (narrowPeak) and replicate-level QC intermediates must be rolled up into a ChiLin QC JSON and per-mark distributions (e.g., DHS overlap ratios grouped by histone mark type) for atlas-scale comparison.

name: qc-metric-pairwise-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a batch of ChIP-seq/DNase-seq samples has per-sample ChiLin QC JSON outputs and you need to determine which QC metrics covary within each literature-based assay category.

name: qc-metrics-compilation-across-datasets
description: Use when per-sample ChiLin QC JSON outputs (id_fastqc., id_map., id_frag., id_pbc., id_frip., id_macs2., id_rep.) must be aggregated into a dataset-level summary table covering the 17 QC metrics across three QC layers for benchmarking or atlas building.

name: qc-stability-curve-visualization
description: Use when evaluating whether a ChIP-seq QC metric such as FRiP is an artifact of sequencing depth: you have down-sampled BAMs (e.g., 1M, 2M, 4M reads) and want stability curves under two peak-calling settings.

name: qpcr-region-coordinate-lookup
description: Use when benchmarking differential ChIP-seq region callers against a small qPCR-validated ground truth set: you have genomic coordinates of qPCR-tested regions and called-region sets (e.g. BED/GRanges) from histoneHMM, Diffreps, Chipdiff and Rseg to classify as Y/FP/FN.

name: qrt-pcr-correlation-analysis
description: Use when expression estimates from an RNA-Seq method (uncorrected or bias-corrected) must be benchmarked against independently performed qRT-PCR measurements to quantify whether bias correction improved accuracy.

name: qt-clustering-of-transcriptomic-data
description: Use when clustering a gene-by-sample transcriptomic matrix (e.g., FPKM RNA-seq) to discover stable tumor subgroups without predefining the number of clusters K, and when consensus/bootstrap clustering stability is in question.

name: quality-atlas-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when ChIP-seq narrowPeak samples (e.g. from a histone mark atlas) need a QC metric scored against ENCODE union DHS regions, or when reproducing Fig. 5 per-mark DHS overlap distributions.

name: quality-threshold-filtering-of-sequencing-reads
description: Use when processing raw .ab1 BSP trace files where reads must be trimmed of low-quality ends and reads failing bisulfite conversion (non-CpG C-to-T conversion rate below 0.9) must be flagged before CpG methylation computation.

name: quantile-based-cell-filtering
description: Use when a supervised celltyping pipeline has produced first-round per-cell prediction probabilities for scATAC-seq target cells and a confident anchor subset is needed to train a second-round model.

name: quantile-deviation-visualization-across-structure-types
description: Use when you have per-base translocation times from Tombo re-squiggled ONT reads and motif coordinates (e.g. non-B DNA DB hg38 annotations), and need to test which non-B structure classes show significant TT quantile deviations from B-DNA.

name: quantile-normalization-of-compartment-scores
description: Use when compartment scores (PC1/PC2 vectors) have been computed for multiple Hi-C datasets or replicates and must be made comparable across conditions prior to differential compartment analysis.

name: quantile-permutation-pvalue-adjustment
description: Use when combined significance scores from integrating multiple genomic/epigenomic p-value tracks show a spurious increasing trend with the number of component p-values per genomic interval, and the trend must be removed before scoring modules.

name: quasi-poisson-glm-regression
