description: Use when testing whether a candidate driver element's mutation status (MUT) is associated with gene expression while correcting for copy number (SCNA) and tumour-type covariates, from per-sample quantification tables.

name: query-region-window-extension-for-mapping-recovery
description: Use when a query genomic region fails to map directly between species with UCSC liftOver and you need to recover candidate orthologous target regions via local window extension before scoring.

name: quorum-sensing-gene-expression-interpretation
description: Use when RNA-seq read counts from V. harveyi quorum sensing mutants (wild-type, Δhns, ΔluxR, ΔluxR Δhns) must be compared to enumerate H-NS-regulated genes and verify luxCDABE recovery.

name: quorum-sensing-promoter-sequence-analysis
description: Use when a promoter FASTA needs to be scanned for TF binding motifs (e.g., H-NS nucleation sites in luxCDABE) and the predictions must be compared to established binding-site coordinates.

name: r-affy-normalize-loess
description: Use when comparing multiple ChIP-seq experiments with exogenous spike-in chromatin (e.g. human hg19 + fly dm3) and a genome-wide correction that preserves background equilibration is needed rather than a single global scaling factor.

name: r-base-graphics-plotting
description: Use when the task requires summarizing quality and diversity of short reads in FASTQ files as plots — e.g. per-cycle quality scores or read-quality distributions across many samples in one report figure.

name: r-based-methylation-data-table-construction
description: Use when bisulfite sequencing epiallele tables (e.g. DDO1/DAO FASTA-derived EpiHaplotypes) must be compared between single-epiallele frequency tools and MethCoresProfiler core outputs to show single-epiallele methods fail to isolate stable methylation cores.

name: r-bioconductor-programming
description: Use when an analysis must be scripted in R with Bioconductor packages — e.g. loading golubEsets expression matrices, imputing with impute.knn(), or customizing cola's consensus partitioning framework.

name: r-bioconductor-runtime-profiling
description: Use when you must compare runtime of two genomic-range null-generation methods (bootRanges vs GSC) on identical GRanges inputs, e.g. ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks, to quantify a speedup factor on genome-scale statistics.

name: r-bioconductor-workflow-execution
description: Use when many NGS sample files (e.g., ~100 FASTQ files) must be processed through multi-step workflows (alignment, variant/peak calling) in R, or when per-sample parallelization on an HPC cluster is needed to cut runtime.

name: r-bioconductor-workflow-execution
description: Use when annotating cell types of clusters in an scRNA-seq dataset in R, or when reproducing the scCATCH/SingleR/CHETAH performance comparison from the scCATCH_performance_comparison repository.

name: r-bioinformatics-workflow-scripting
description: Use when you have a BIT output rank table (e.g., mm10_RUNX1_rank_table.csv) of TRs ranked from differential accessibility data and need to test whether the top TRs are enriched for GO biological processes relevant to the perturbed context.

name: r-commandline-mixed-step-execution
description: Use when a pipeline must interleave R code steps with external command-line steps (e.g. an R export step followed by gzip/gunzip utilities) and needs to run inside a single reproducible systemPipeR workflow container.

name: r-function-workflow-execution
description: Use when many SVs must be scored for pathogenicity in a scripted, parameterized R (>=3.5.0) pipeline rather than through the Shiny Multiple SV Submission GUI, e.g. batch benchmarking of hg19 SV sets.

name: r-markdown-reproducible-analysis
description: Use when reproducing or re-running the Genexpi evaluation pipeline on time-course expression data (e.g. GSE6865 SigB or GDS38 yeast datasets), since the complete parameterized workflow is shipped as R notebooks in the paper's Additional file 1.

name: r-package-data-workflow
description: Use when raw Hi-C or pcHi-C interaction data is provided as fragment-pair feature tables (frag1/frag2 coordinates, coverages, raw frequencies, distances) and reproducible, coverage-normalized contact maps are needed.

name: r-package-function-implementation
description: Use when you need to reproduce or extend cola's -k selection logic in R code: you have per-k consensus matrices, individual partitions, and consensus partitions and must compute PAC/silhouette/concordance/Jaccard metrics to choose k.

name: r-package-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix with cluster assignments needs automated cell type annotation via an R package pipeline (e.g., scCATCH with CellMatch), following the article's documented function sequence.

name: r-script-peakcaller-integration
description: Use when a NEAT ChIPseq project needs an automated 'peakcalling' module run after filtering, with the algorithm and parameters defined in the centralized Targets.txt configuration file.

name: r-scripted-batch-sv-analysis
description: Use when you need to analyze multiple structural variants (e.g. a patient cohort or benchmark set) with POSTRE beyond the online single-SV interface, by scripting POSTRE_multiSV() in R (>=3.5.0).

name: r-squared-goodness-of-fit-assessment
description: Use when a parametric model (e.g. scPower expression probability model) yields numeric predictions that must be validated against observed values across controlled conditions such as sequencing-depth subsampling of count matrices.

name: r-systempiper-workflow-execution
description: Use when running or reconstructing the QC step of the NEAT NGS pipeline on truncated H3K4me3 ChIPseq or RNAseq FASTQ test data, and per-cycle quality and read-distribution reports are required.

name: random-effects-model-specification-methylation
description: Decision support for choosing among MethylCal's four random-effects model specifications (equations 2-5) for a methylation calibration assay when standard-control data at known methylation percentages are available and goodness-of-fit comparison via DIC is required.

name: random-forest-binding-prediction
description: Use when the goal is to predict or reproduce TF-DNA binding affinities from experimental intensity/enrichment data (gcPBM, uPBM, HT-SELEX) using structural/mechanical DNA features rather than sequence-only models.

name: random-forest-classifier-application
description: Use when genomic bins must be classified as active/primed enhancers from ChIP-seq histone marks and DNase-seq accessibility data, e.g. reproducing enhancer discovery in human cell lines like HCT116 or HeLa.

name: random-forest-cross-validated-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when training a supervised loop-detection model from a 10 kb Hi-C cooler file and a bedpe positive set (e.g., H3K27ac HiChIP), needing per-chromosome models and tuned hyperparameters before scoring pixels.

name: random-forest-cross-validation-evaluation
description: Use when comparing feature subsets or classifiers for DNA 6mA sequence prediction on 41nt sequences and you need cross-validated AUC estimates (e.g. Binary vs Motif+Kmer+Binary) before freezing a feature matrix.

name: random-forest-dna-affinity-regression
description: Use when predicting TF binding affinities from uPBM (35-mer oligos), gcPBM, or HT-SELEX datasets with a random forest over MD-derived DNA shape/flexibility features rather than sequence-only CNNs like DeepBind.

name: random-forest-enhancer-classification
description: Use when labeled enhancer and promoter (non-enhancer) genomic element sets are available with ChIP-seq and DNase-seq signal tracks (e.g. RPM-normalized bedGraph) and the goal is to train, validate, or apply a supervised enhancer-prediction model.

name: random-forest-feature-importance-extraction
description: Use when comparing how training data source (uPBM vs gcPBM vs HT-SELEX) changes the relative importance of DNA feature classes in the DNAffinity random forest regressor, or when auditing which physical parameters drive affinity predictions.

name: random-forest-model-training-hic
description: Use when a 10 kb-binned contact map (.cool or .hic) and a positive interaction list (bedpe from ChIA-PET, HiChIP, or annotated loops) are available and supervised chromatin loop detection is needed.

name: random-forest-model-training-on-3c-derived-interactions
description: Use when you have a 10 kb-binned .cool or .hic Hi-C matrix and a bedpe list of positive interactions (ChIA-PET, HiChIP, Capture Hi-C) and need chromosome-wise random forest models for loop prediction.

name: random-forest-model-training-per-chromosome
description: Use when you have a .cool or .hic genome-wide contact map and an orthogonal positive interaction set (e.g. HiChIP/ChIA-PET bedpe) and need supervised loop classifiers for genome-wide prediction.

name: random-forest-proximity-based-clustering
description: Use when clustering high-dimensional tumor gene expression data (e.g., RNA-seq FPKM matrices) into stable, reproducible subgroups without predefining K, and when consensus clustering overfits due to the curse of dimensionality.

name: random-forest-regressor-training
description: Use when k-mer binding data (e.g. HT-SELEX penultimate-cycle affinities, uPBM/gcPBM intensities) must be converted into per-protein affinity predictions via regression on MD-derived DNA shape features, with R2/Pearson/MSE evaluation.

name: random-forest-tree-number-tuning
description: Use when building the RF component of an iPro-WAEL-style promoter classifier and you need to empirically select the number of trees via cross-validated grid search over promoter training sequences.

name: random-sample-subsetting-of-expression-cohorts
description: Use when assessing how stable an unsupervised clustering solution (e.g., SRIQ K3/K5/K6 on 434 TCGA LUAD samples) is to cohort-size reduction, alongside BagSize reduction tests.

name: random-walk-restart-contact-imputation
description: Use when individual single-cell Hi-C contact files are too sparse for direct loop detection and normalized per-cell contact probabilities at 10-kb resolution must be imputed before statistical testing.

name: random-walk-with-restart-imputation
description: Use when a Hi-C contact matrix is extremely sparse (e.g., 0.025% downsampled or single-cell data) and needs imputation prior to structural-entropy TLD detection.

name: randomized-lasso-feature-selection
description: Use when training a GLM BMR model in DriverPower from high-dimensional genomic feature tables (e.g. train_feature.hdf5 with 1373 features) and a mutation-count response table, to discard uninformative features before fitting.

name: randomized-sequence-negative-control
description: Use when computing horizontal or vertical alignment scores over chromatin state sequences (e.g. EpiAlign on Roadmap 500 kb regions) and raw scores need a null baseline to separate real from randomized signal.

name: range-validation-of-computed-scores
description: Use when computing or consuming EpiRegio Cell type scores from GeneQuery REM tables and you must verify normalization: every score in [-1, 1] and absolute scores per gene per cell type summing to 1.

name: rank1-driver-pruning-fdr-thresholding
description: Use when candidate cis genes from SCNA/gene-expression integrative analysis must be prioritized by their trans mediation signal, and the pruned Rank-1 lists need in silico validation against known driver databases.

name: ranked-transcription-factor-list-overlap-analysis
description: Use when two or more tools output ranked TR lists for the same query region sets (e.g., TR perturbation-derived DARs or cancer-type-specific accessible regions) and you need pairwise top-k list agreement via Jaccard indices.

name: rbp-binding-site-count-aggregation
description: Use when comparing the number of enriched candidate binding sites called by Skipper against Piranha and CLIPper on matched eCLIP replicates, or when benchmarking a new CLIP-seq caller's sensitivity on ENCODE data.

name: rbp-transcript-region-distribution-analysis
description: Use when eCLIP replicates (e.g., WT vs point-mutant RBP) have Skipper reproducible_enriched_windows output and the goal is to compare the fraction of binding windows assigned to transcript regions such as CDS, deep introns, or tRNA loci.

name: rdd-portable-hash-partitioning
description: Use when a Spark RDD pipeline shows imbalanced partition sizes (e.g., after HDFS chunk-boundary loading or post-filtering valid-alignment skew) and you need to quantify and rebalance records-per-partition across executors.

name: read-attribution-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when validating BED (Bayesian Epiallele Detection) on simulated bisulfite-sequencing reads with known epialleles, to measure the fraction of reads attributed to the correct underlying epiallele before trusting model output on real RRBS tumour data.

name: read-depth-sensitivity-assessment
description: Use when you need to determine the minimum sequencing depth required to visualize a ChIP-seq signal, especially to compare sharp histone marks like H3K4me3 against broad domains like H3K36me3.

name: read-depth-subsampling-comparison
description: Use when you have a UMI/read count matrix with donor and cell-type annotations and need to verify that scPower's predicted expressed-gene counts track observed counts across read-depth conditions before trusting power predictions.

name: read-depth-umi-relation-fitting
description: Use when fitting scPower expression priors from pilot data: you have per-matrix mean UMI counts and corresponding cellranger mapped-read counts (e.g. 23130, 17422, 11666, 5859 from full and subsampled PBMC matrices) and need a read-depth-to-UMI curve for power estimation.

name: read-fragment-extraction-from-bam
description: Use when a diploid phasing pipeline needs a fragment file from sequencing reads (WGS paired-end, Hi-C, 10X linked-reads, PacBio SMRT, or ONT) before running SpecHap graph construction.

name: read-length-compatibility-code-patching
description: Use when benchmarking methylPurify against DXM on simulated bisulfite sequencing mixtures whose reads exceed 100 bp, since methylPurify's original code fails without documented code edits.

name: read-mapping-statistics-extraction
description: Decision support for choosing a DNA/RNA read aligner: when you need to compare mappers on the same FASTQ input by unique vs multimapped vs low-quality/unmapped read counts and runtime.

name: read-to-reference-alignment-for-methylation-analysis
description: Use when chromatogram trace reads (.ab1) from direct-BSP or cloning-BSP must be aligned to a reference .fasta to identify non-CpG C/G positions for bisulfite conversion-rate QC and CpG methylation computation.

name: read1-read2-strand-asymmetry-analysis
description: Use when paired-end bacterial sequencing reads from heat-alkaline-treated (RIMS-seq) vs regular DNA-seq libraries must be checked for mate-specific (R1 vs R2) C-to-T elevation in a methylated motif context such as CCWGG.

name: reconstruction-error-novelty-scoring
description: Use when translocation-time windows (B-DNA and candidate non-B) from ONT reads are available and the goal is novelty-based non-B DNA detection with per-window P-values and FDR-controlled calls.

name: recursive-bisection-cluster-nesting-analysis
description: Use when you have a 3-column sparse Hi-C contact matrix (e.g. IMR90) and need a multi-scale, nested partition tree of loci clusters without assuming genomic contiguity.

name: reference-driver-set-curation-cgc
description: Use when comparing driver discovery methods (e.g., DriverPower vs ActiveDriverWGS, ExInAtor, LARVA, MutSig, ncdDetect, oncodriveFML) on the same PCAWG cohorts and you need CGC-anchored precision/recall/F1 metrics.

name: reference-genome-data-preparation
description: Use when setting up ChiLin (or a bwa-based ChIP-seq QC pipeline) for a new species/build and the dependent data in db/ plus a mapped-ready genome index are not yet installed.

name: reference-genome-read-mapping
description: Use when raw sequencing reads (e.g. RNA-seq FASTQ input) must be aligned to a reference genome as an early step of a Watchdog workflow before feature counting or differential expression testing.

name: reference-genome-sequence-preparation
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads must be aligned with BiSpark, or simulated bisulfite reads must be generated, and the reference genome (hg19 Build 37) has not yet been converted, indexed, or placed in HDFS.

name: reference-implementation-output-validation
description: Use when re-implementing or modifying combine_CpG_sites.py and you must prove the new clustered-region table (chr/start/end/CpG plus per-sample -N/-X columns) matches DMRfinder's reference output exactly.

name: reference-vs-variant-interaction-difference-computation
description: Use when fine-mapping candidate regulatory SNPs (e.g. CTCF-site variants such as 17q21 asthma SNPs) to identify which allele most likely alters chromatin architecture, by comparing predicted interaction maps between reference and alternate alleles.

name: refseq-annotation-parsing
description: Use when running SeqCode (or reproducing its workflows) on sequencing data for a genome assembly, since most commands require the chromosome list and RefSeq gene transcript annotation files as inputs.

name: refseq-transcript-annotation-matching
description: Use when you have BED-formatted peak coordinates (e.g. MACS peaks) and need to map them to gene identifiers via RefSeq transcript annotations, e.g. to build target-gene lists for pathway or GO enrichment.

name: region-set-summary-statistics
description: Use when you have CpG-level methylation calls (e.g. Roadmap WGBS) for several cell types plus BED-style genomic interval sets (HOT regions, non-HOT CpG islands) and need per-region and per-set median/IQR methylation summaries.

name: region-to-gene-annotation
description: Use when you have topic-defined region sets (e.g. from binarizecisTopics on a 30-topic PBMC scATAC-seq model) and need per-topic GO term enrichment to functionally characterize topics, such as distinguishing promoter topics from cell-type-specific enhancer topics.

name: region-to-gene-annotation-mapping
description: Use when a cluster-vs-rest differential test has returned significant genomic regions (adj. p-value < 0.01, |fold change| > 1) and you need to convert those regions into gene lists for pathway over-representation analysis.

name: regression-based-tr-activity-inference
description: Use when you have cell-line gene expression, copy number, mutation, and pharmacological sensitivity data plus ChIP-seq (or precomputed RP) targets, and want to infer which transcriptional regulators drive resistance or sensitivity to a specific drug.

name: regression-coefficient-normalization
description: Use when you need to quantify or rank how strongly individual REMs associated to a gene contribute to that gene's expression in a specific cell type, e.g. after a GeneQuery retrieval of regressionCoefficient and DNase1 signal data.

name: regression-model-evaluation-r2
description: Use when a binding-affinity regression model (e.g. DNAffinity on gcPBM/uPBM/HT-SELEX data) needs quantitative validation of prediction quality via R2 on a held-out test partition.

name: regularization-impact-comparison-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether a penalty-based model-selection term (Genexpi's r(β)) improves parameter interpretability without degrading fit quality, by refitting the same genes/regulators with the penalty switched off and on.

name: regularized-maximum-a-posteriori-estimation
description: Use when you have smoothed time-course expression data for a target gene and candidate regulators and need to estimate ODE synthesis/decay/weight parameters while forcing them into biologically interpretable ranges.

name: regulatory-distance-feature-computation
description: Use when building cell-type-specific features for enhancer-target (ET) pairs from H3K27ac/H3K4me1/H3K4me3 ChIP-seq, to quantify regulatory density in the enhancer-promoter interval rather than relying on genomic distance alone.

name: regulatory-element-coordinate-processing
description: Use when you have a set of genomic intervals (REM BED-like records with chr, start, end) and need to group overlapping/adjacent elements into clusters and report cluster-level statistics.

name: regulatory-element-gene-association-query
description: Use when you have TF ChIP-seq peak BED files or a list of differentially expressed genes and need the REMs associated with them, with optional cell-type/tissue filtering.

name: regulatory-element-sequence-extraction
description: Use when an EpiRegio Gene Query result table (CSV of REMs linked to genes of interest, filtered for a cell type/tissue such as 'heart') must be turned into DNA sequences in FASTA format to feed a motif enrichment tool.

name: regulatory-potential-score-calculation
description: Use when ChIP-seq peak BED files with signal enrichment values and gene/TSS annotations must be converted into quantitative TR-target regulatory potential scores for target inference.

name: regulon-dataset-preparation
description: Use when a candidate regulon definition (ChIP-derived, knockout-derived, or literature/database-mined) must be paired with a time-course expression series and preprocessed before network inference.

name: regulon-recovery-benchmarking
description: Use when a candidate regulon (ChIP, knockout, or database-derived) plus a matching expression time series (e.g. GSE6865, GSE44415, GDS38) is available and you need to quantify recovery rate versus a random-profile baseline.

name: rem-clustering-into-crems
description: Use when you have interval-formatted REM/genomic region coordinates (chr, start, end) and need to merge overlapping or adjacent regions into clusters and report aggregate span/size statistics.

name: repeated-random-sampling-of-methylation-reads
description: Use when comparing phased mCpG/epiallele frequencies across bisulfite-sequenced amplicon samples with unequal read depths, where raw frequency comparisons are biased by library size.

name: repeatmasker-repeat-coordinate-extraction
description: Use when an analysis requires strand-annotated genomic coordinates of transposable elements (LINE, SINE, LTR subclasses) from UCSC hg38 RepeatMasker as motif input for interval-overlap or asymmetry tooling.

name: repeatmasker-repetitive-element-filtering
description: Use when preparing centered, score-carrying motif-site sequences (e.g. ±200 bp around Nanog ChIP-seq motif sites) for positional motif enrichment, and repeats must be removed to avoid confounding motif-matching with low-complexity DNA.

name: repeatmasker-transposable-element-annotation-processing
description: Use when a strand-asymmetry or breakpoint-enrichment analysis needs class-filtered, strand-annotated transposable element coordinates from UCSC hg38 rmsk (e.g. LINE/SINE/LTR) to orient mutations or assign background orientation probabilities.

name: rephine-response-signature-computation
description: Use when the goal is to organize anti-cancer drugs (e.g., CCLE compounds) into mechanism-of-action groups from TR-drug response associations, or to reproduce the RePhine drug-cluster dendrogram of Figure 3A.

name: replicate-consistency-assessment-via-peak-overlap-and-correlation
description: Use when QC-ing a ChIP-seq experiment with ≥2 biological replicates and you need to measure agreement before merging BAMs or trusting merged peak calls.

name: replicate-consistency-correlation-analysis
description: Use when two or more ChIP-seq treatment replicates (plus controls) are supplied as FASTQ and the QC goal is to quantify replicate agreement via wiggle correlation and peak overlap before interpreting the experiment.

name: replicate-merging-of-hic-contact-matrices
description: Use when multiple Hi-C replicates (e.g., QSC and FISC MuSC replicates) exist as Microcket-produced .hic files and a per-condition contact matrix/heatmap is needed for specific regions and bin sizes.

name: reporter-assay-outcome-annotation
description: Use when a set of candidate CRE or OCR coordinates must be functionally benchmarked against previously tested enhancers, e.g. intersecting scATAC-seq-derived OCRs with VISTA e11.5 transgenic reporter regions and recovering per-region positive/negative outcomes.

name: reproducible-enriched-window-calling
description: Use when analyzing eCLIP/CLIP-seq replicates to detect RBP binding transcriptome-wide as reproducible enriched windows (with annotation metadata) rather than peaks, especially when repetitive elements or diverse binding modes break peak callers.

name: reproducible-ngs-analysis-execution-in-r
description: Use when the analysis goal is to rapidly run or test a complete NGS workflow in R/Bioconductor — e.g. reproducing a template RNA-Seq analysis from FASTQ inputs through reporting — with logged, reproducible execution.

name: resnik-semantic-similarity-of-go-terms
description: Use when chromosome clusters (e.g. BHi-Cect bottom enclaves from IMR90 Hi-C data) need an ontology-based functional similarity score to correlate against BPT distance or genomic coordinate distance.

name: rest-api-data-retrieval
description: Use when you need programmatic access to EpiRegio's REM data — e.g. regressionCoefficient and per-cell-type DNase1 signal and cell type score values — for a chosen gene identified by an Ensembl ID such as ENSG00000223972.

name: reusable-feature-encoding-module-integration
description: Use when converting 41-nt DNA sequences (FASTA) into the csDMA Binary feature block, or when a feature-encoding routine must live in one shared script (feature_selection.py) that classifier-selection, training, and testing scripts can auto-invoke.

name: rimsseq-vs-dnaseq-assembly-metric-comparison
description: Use when paired-end RIMS-seq reads (e.g. from NCBI BioProject PRJNA706563) must be shown to support de novo genome assembly at quality metrics equivalent to standard Illumina DNA-seq shotgun reads.

name: rloop-drip-seq-enrichment-quantification
description: Use when DRIP-seq IP and control datasets (mock or RNaseH-treated) plus a coordinate set of HOT or occupancy-binned regions are available and the goal is to test RNA-DNA hybrid enrichment per region set.

name: rmarkdown-workflow-step-import
description: Use when a user wants to rapidly test or run an end-to-end NGS analysis (e.g. the RNA-Seq template) with systemPipeR's workflow toolkit starting from an R Markdown template that must be parsed into executable steps.

name: rna-dna-interaction-dataset-curation
description: Use when building a gold-standard benchmark of experimentally validated lncRNA:DNA binding sites from heterogeneous published ChIRP/ChOP/CHART/RAP-seq studies, requiring uniform peak-calling and reproducibility classification.

name: rna-dna-triplex-prediction-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing the prediction accuracy or runtime of triplex-forming lncRNA tools on experimentally validated RNA:DNA peaks and needing a fair, negative-control-based AUC benchmark with resampling-based confidence estimates.

name: rna-essentiality-screen-analysis
description: Use when a ranked list of candidate cis driver genes (e.g., TCGA Rank-1 iEDGE genes) must be validated against DepMap RNAi essentiality screens where dependency scores correlate with copy number amplification.

name: rna-secondary-structure-masking
description: Use when predicting RNA:dsDNA triplex interactions with 3plex/Triplexator-style scanning and you want to exclude ssRNA nucleotides unlikely to be available for Hoogsteen pairing, or when benchmarking whether structure-aware masking improves TPX prediction AUC for lncRNAs with validated binding.

name: rna-seq-bias-quantification
description: Use when RNA-Seq expression estimates (e.g. FPKM from Cufflinks or eXpress) show poor agreement across technical replicate libraries or against qRT-PCR, and sequence/positional fragment bias is suspected as the cause.

name: rna-seq-data-processing-execution
description: Use when raw FASTQ RNA-seq data (e.g. WT versus KO designs from GEO) must be processed end-to-end into QC reports, BAM files, bigWig tracks, and differential gene expression results with a reproducible, low-input pipeline.

name: rna-seq-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when FASTQ RNA-seq reads (with replicates across conditions) must be turned into per-method differential expression result tables and the Watchdog WMS is available, with bwa and ContextMap2 installed and configured.

name: rna-seq-expression-based-gene-stratification
description: Use when you need to partition a gene set into expression-based classes (e.g. three groups of 100 highly/moderately/silently expressed RefSeq genes) from RNA-seq data to relate them to ChIP-seq signal levels.

name: rna-seq-expression-estimation
description: Use when RNA-Seq alignments (SAM) and a reference (FASTA/GTF annotation) must yield expression estimates whose fragment sequence, priming, or position bias is learned from the data rather than assumed uniform, e.g. MAQC HBR or strand-specific SRA020818 yeast libraries.

name: rna-seq-regulon-gene-list-processing
description: Use when two or more differentially expressed gene sets (e.g. H-NS and LuxR regulons from RNA-seq comparisons) must be intersected to count shared regulators/genes, with identifiers harmonized first.

name: rna-seq-short-read-alignment
description: Use when aligning RNA-Seq FASTQ files inside a systemPipeR workflow and you need to choose or benchmark an aligner (Bowtie2/TopHat2 vs HISAT2/Rsubread) or verify near-linear parallel speedup via clusterRun.

name: rna-seq-short-read-alignment
description: Use when FASTQ RNA-Seq reads (single- or paired-end Illumina) must be spliced-aligned to a reference genome before expression estimation, and novel junction discovery should be suppressed in favor of known annotated junctions.

name: rna-seq-tpm-integration
description: Use when computing CENTRE features for enhancer-target pairs and a TPM expression table must be attached to each target gene before calling centrePrediction, or when checking that RNA-seq inputs match CENTRE's expected schema.

name: rna-seq-workflow-environment-generation
description: Use when a user needs to rapidly test or run a complete pre-configured RNA-Seq NGS workflow in R/Bioconductor, from environment generation through execution to HTML scientific reporting.

name: rnaseh-control-selection
description: Use when computing per-region DRIP-seq log2(IP/control) R-loop enrichment over HOT regions or occupancy-binned control regions and a given cell line has no mock control, so the RNaseH-treated DRIP-seq library must serve as control.

name: rnaseq-design-matrix-construction
description: Use when an RNA-seq count matrix covers more than two conditions, multiple factors, batch effects, or a time course, and the default two-group DEG schema cannot express the contrasts of interest.

name: rnaseq-gene-expression-assignment
description: Use when sgRNA or other genomic target sites need continuous epigenetic feature values (RNA expression from RNA-seq/GEO, accessibility from ATACdb, TSS distance) attached per locus before deep learning input.

name: rnaseq-quality-control-assessment
description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files plus a tab-separated CONFIG file (MergeID, SampleID, Path, InputID, Mark) are the input and QC/bias/contamination assessment is needed before DEG analysis.

name: rnaseq-read-quantification
description: Use when processing bulk RNA-seq FASTQ files (single- or pair-ended) through alignment, gene-level counting, and normalization to produce count matrices and DEG tables, or when assessing whether a design beyond two conditions fits CIPHER's expInfo schema.

name: roadmap-epigenome-sample-comparison
description: Use when comparing epigenomic samples (e.g. Roadmap ESC/heart/brain) via ChromHMM chromatin state sequences and needing an order-aware alignment score benchmarked against a frequency-only baseline.

name: robust-covariance-estimation-with-mcd
description: Use when you have compartment scores (PC1/PC2) from multiple Hi-C or pseudo-bulk scHi-C maps and need to test which genomic bins have statistically significant compartmentalization differences without relying on an A/B compartment flip.

name: robust-mahalanobis-anomaly-scoring
description: Use when detecting non-B DNA windows in nanopore translocation-time matrices as a novelty detection problem, or when scoring windows against an empirical null built from B-DNA controls.

name: roc-auc-baseline-comparison
description: Use when a new significant-interaction caller for pcHi-C (or another 'C' technology) needs to be validated by ROC AUC against an established baseline like CHiCAGO, plus replicate-overlap significance testing.

name: roc-auc-binding-site-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify whether a triplex-prediction tool (e.g. 3plex, Triplexator) enriches real RNA:DNA binding peaks over matched negative regions, and to tier lncRNAs by AUC evidence.

name: roc-auc-classification-scoring
description: Use when evaluating binary sgRNA high-activity classifiers (e.g., labeled via phenotype scores below -0.1 or activity scores above 0.75) and you need a threshold-independent ROC-AUC metric to compare prediction models.

name: roc-auc-cross-validation-evaluation
description: Use when binary-classifying sgRNAs as highly active vs. inactive (e.g., phenotype score < −0.1 labeled '1') and you need cross-validated ROC-AUC comparison of a CNN against classical ML baselines on sequence-plus-epigenetic features.

name: roc-auc-curve-analysis
description: Use when comparing how sensitively and accurately multiple methods (e.g., TSMiner vs clustering tools) recover a known positive set of pathways/TFs from time-series expression data, and a negative set can be defined.

name: roc-auc-evaluation-of-genomic-predictions
description: Use when predictions of genomic binding regions must be scored against curated positive peaks and matched negative regions, and you need AUC comparison across parameter settings plus significance testing of parameter effects.

name: roc-auc-evaluation-of-tf-prediction
description: Use when comparing tools that predict transcription factors from time-series expression data (e.g. liver-regeneration RNA-seq) and you must quantify sensitivity/accuracy against a curated list of known TFs.

name: roc-auc-model-evaluation
description: Use when a trained variant- or gene-prioritization classifier (positive disease variants/genes vs. negatives) must be validated, and discriminative performance on held-out or cross-validated test sets must be reported as ROC curves with AUC values.

name: roc-auc-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a statistical test or predictor (e.g., a mediation test) must be validated on simulated data with known true positives/negatives, and you need AUC, sensitivity, and specificity as a function of controlled parameters such as effect strength and sample size.

name: roc-auc-reproducibility-evaluation
description: Use when comparing two or more Hi-C significance-calling or normalization methods on replicate datasets, and you need quantitative reproducibility (replicate overlap fractions) and ROC AUC of significance scores.

name: roc-auc-tool-comparison
description: Use when multiple TPX-prediction tools or scoring functions must be compared quantitatively on the same positive (Top1000 RNA:DNA peaks) and negative (bedtools-shuffled genomic) region sets.

name: roc-auprc-performance-benchmarking
description: Use when predicted functional scores for nc-sindels and gold-standard positive/negative eQTL labels are available and you must compare classifier performance (AUROC/AUPRC) across multiple tissues or cell types.

name: roc-curve-auc-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing differential occupancy / peak-calling methods on a dosage-responsive ChIP-seq benchmark with a gold-standard positive set defined at a signal quantile, and you need ROC curves and AUC-vs-cutoff comparisons.

name: roc-evaluation-against-qpcr-validated-regions
description: Use when a modified-vs-unmodified region caller on broad histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3) must be ranked against competitors using an independent qPCR-validated ground-truth region set rather than simulated data.

name: row-sampling-perturbation-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to justify or tune the number of random samplings (repetitions) in cola consensus partitioning, or to show that a low sampling count already yields a stable partition.

name: row-vs-column-sampling-comparison
description: Use when running cola consensus partitioning on a high-dimensional matrix and you need to decide whether to resample rows or columns during bootstrapping, or to verify that both sampling types yield comparable subgroupings.

name: rpm-normalized-bedgraph-processing
description: Use when starting CIPHER's enhancer-prediction or element-feature computation and you have ENCODE ChIP-seq/DNase-seq data that must be converted to RPM-normalized bedGraph signal tracks before genomic elements are classified.

name: rrbs-epiallele-inference
description: Use when reduced representation bisulfite sequencing (RRBS) read matrices are available for two or more samples (e.g. multi-region tumour regions plus matched normal) and the goal is to infer which epialleles are present at each eligible CpG locus.

name: rrbs-locus-quality-filtering
description: Use when preparing multi-sample RRBS methylation data for epiallele analysis and you need to drop poorly covered or incompletely observed loci (e.g. shallow read depth, few CpGs, sex chromosomes) before fitting epiallele models.

name: rrbs-methylation-data-analysis
description: Use when RRBS reads from multi-region tumour samples plus matched normal tissue have been fitted with bed_fit and per-locus epiallele proportions are needed, purity (rho) must be estimated from the xi density, or tumour profiles must be decontaminated before phylogeny/entropy analysis.

name: runtime-and-memory-profiling
description: Use when a command-line motif discovery tool must be benchmarked for runtime and peak memory on defined FASTA datasets, and results compared to published performance numbers.

name: runtime-and-peak-memory-profiling
description: Use when comparing the computational efficiency of Hi-C compartment-calling methods: wall time and peak memory must be measured per tool across resolutions (10–100 kb) and sequencing depths on identical binned contact maps.

name: runtime-benchmark-decomposition
description: Use when benchmarking a GenoGAM 2.0 genome-wide GAM fit and the goal is a per-stage runtime breakdown (preprocessing vs cross-validation vs fitting) on a specified core count and backend (in-memory vs HDF5).

name: runtime-memory-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing or auditing SCALE's scalability claims on a large scATAC-seq input (e.g. the ~80k-cell mouse_atlas.h5ad), where reported runtime (~1.5 h), memory (~2 GB), and clustering F1 (0.419) must be measured and compared.

name: runtime-memory-measurement-in-r
description: Use when benchmarking runtime and memory footprint of an R model-fitting routine (e.g. genogam() GAM fits) at increasing parameter counts, holding hyperparameters fixed and forcing single-worker execution.

name: runtime-memory-profiling
description: Use when comparing computational cost of peak callers on calling cards data, or when validating that CCcaller delivers ~7-10x speedup over MACCs/ccf_tools on >5M insertion datasets.

name: runtime-memory-scaling-profiling
description: Use when comparing runtime and memory scaling of two alternative implementations of the same computation (e.g. variance/standard-error computation in GAM fits) across increasing problem sizes on a single core.

name: runtime-speedup-benchmarking
description: Use when a paper claims near-linear or 10x/100x speedup for parallel execution of sample-level NGS steps (e.g., short-read alignment over 100 FASTQ files) and the claim needs empirical reproduction.

name: sakoe-chiba-band-constrained-warping
description: Use when aligning two or more epigenomic tracks (or other multivariate time series of binned coverage vectors) by shape similarity, where the warping path must be bounded near the diagonal and strand orientation must be handled.

name: sal-container-workflow-construction
description: Use when a multi-step analysis must be declared, loaded, and run as a reproducible systemPipeR SAL workflow where R steps and command-line steps chain via output-to-input targets (e.g., export -> gzip -> gunzip -> stats).

name: sam-alignment-filtering-and-duplicate-removal
description: Use when processing cfMeDIP-seq (or MeDIP-seq) FASTQ reads into filtered, deduplicated BAM files with QC metrics, especially when libraries may or may not carry UMI barcodes and spike-in controls may be present.

name: sample-count-scaling-analysis
description: Use when a runnable Watchdog workflow XML and an equivalent Snakemake rule chain are available, and the goal is to measure how WMS overhead grows as the number of input samples is scaled across multiple benchmark runs.

name: sample-fastq-data-handling
description: Use when a workflow must process many sample FASTQ files (e.g., RNA-Seq) on a cluster and the goal is to parallelize per-sample steps and measure or achieve near-linear speedup with core count.

name: sample-size-and-cells-per-sample-design-grid-evaluation
description: Use when planning an interindividual single-cell DE (or eQTL) study and you need to pick sample size, cells per cell type, and read depth by comparing power across a design grid rather than guessing a single design.

name: samtools-bam-filtering
description: Use when aligned BAM files from a mapped ChIPseq/RNAseq run must be filtered by fragment-size bounds and duplicate-read policy before peakcalling or downstream normalization.

name: sanger-chromatogram-trace-parsing
description: Use when the input consists of raw Sanger trace files (.ab1) from bisulfite sequencing PCR (BSP) that must be base-called, quality-trimmed, and converted into trimmed sequences before methylation percentage computation.

name: sc-hic-cell-subsample-splitting
description: Use when you have per-cell scHi-C contact files (e.g. 742 mES cells) and need to measure how reproducibly two loop-calling methods or parameter settings recover loops from equally sized cell subsamples.

name: scalability-curve-analysis
description: Use when evaluating a distributed aligner or Spark-based pipeline's scale-out behavior: you have access to clusters of differing node counts (e.g. 10, 20, 40 slaves) and need to quantify throughput gain or loss as nodes are added.

name: scatac-accessibility-matrix-processing
description: Use when a scATAC-seq accessibility matrix clusters primarily by copy number state and you need to test whether CNVs confound clustering: drop CNV-chromosome peaks, recluster, and compare assignments via AMI.

name: scatac-fragment-aggregation-per-cluster
description: Use when you already have single-cell cluster assignments for scATAC-seq data (e.g., from a SnapATAC snap file with barcodes and the FM fragment session) and need to generate pseudo-bulk signal per cluster for peak calling.

name: scatac-fragment-genome-binning
description: Use when raw scATAC-seq fragment files (e.g., cellranger-atac output) must be converted into a per-cell genomic bin count matrix prior to CNV or copy number inference with Copy-scAT.

name: scatac-read-depth-downsampling
description: Use when benchmarking how a scATAC-seq analysis method's cell-type assignments hold up at reduced sequencing depth, or when compiling runtime-vs-cell-count and reproducibility tables (e.g., on the ~81k-cell Cusanovich 13-mouse-tissue atlas).

name: scatac-scrna-integration-label-transfer
description: Use when scATAC-seq cells lack annotations and a matched or related scRNA-seq reference with known cell types is available, e.g. predicting PBMC cell types from a ~10k-cell scRNA reference.

name: scatac-seq-cell-type-prediction
description: Use when both a labeled scATAC-seq reference dataset (gene score matrix + cell-type metadata) and an unlabeled target scATAC-seq dataset are available and per-cell cell-type labels must be transferred without joint reference-target integration.

name: scatac-seq-celltyping-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking cell-typing predictions for scATAC-seq data — e.g., comparing Cellcano's predicted labels against FACS-derived ground truth for a human PBMC target dataset to quantify per-type accuracy.

name: scatac-seq-gene-score-analysis
description: Use when preparing a reference scATAC-seq gene score matrix (with known cell type labels) for supervised celltyping and you must reduce thousands of genes to a compact, informative feature set.

name: scatac-seq-latent-feature-clustering
description: Use when the input is a raw scATAC-seq count matrix (h5ad, txt/tsv/csv, or mtx folder with count/peak/barcode files) and the goal is cell-type clustering, visualization, or denoising/imputation with benchmarked accuracy against scABC, scVI, cisTopic, and SC3.

name: scatac-seq-motif-activity-analysis
description: Use when sparse scATAC-seq peak-by-cell data (h5ad) needs transcription factor motif activity scoring, especially to test whether SCALE-imputed data recovers more cluster-specific motifs than the raw matrix.

name: scatac-seq-peak-dropping-corruption
description: Use when you need to quantify how a scATAC-seq clustering method's accuracy (ARI) degrades as sparsity increases, by simulating missingness through random peak dropping on a labeled dataset such as Forebrain (2088 cells, k=8).

name: scatac-seq-read-downsampling-simulation
description: Use when evaluating scATAC-seq clustering methods for coverage robustness: simulated datasets at graded depths (1,000–10,000 reads/cell) are needed and cell-type recovery is quantified by ARI/NMI against reference labels.

name: scchipseq-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing sub-population identification performance of ChromSCape or scATAC/scChIP-seq methods on count matrices where cell-type ground-truth labels exist and ARI can be computed.

name: scientific-figure-data-extraction
description: Use when a published article presents a qualitative feature comparison as a figure (e.g., Fig. 12 comparing WMSs across setup, workflow design, workflow execution, and integration) that must be reproduced as structured table data with footnote-derived qualifiers intact.

name: scientific-task-formulation
description: Use when a published finding must be turned into a reproducible task: the goal is to re-derive a specific result (e.g. replicate mixing after FastMNN correction without merging resistant-tumor cells) and the source text must be decomposed into datasets, tools, parameters and pass/fail criteria.

name: scrna-seq-cluster-annotation
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices with pre-computed cluster assignments need automatic cell type labels, replacing subjective manual marker-gene annotation with a tissue-specific, evidence-scored reference lookup.

name: scrnaseq-count-matrix-normalization
description: Use when a raw or unnormalized scRNA-seq count matrix from two biological conditions (e.g. treated vs untreated cells) must be normalized in Seurat before calling differentially expressed genes for downstream regulatory-element queries.

name: segmentation-stratified-range-resampling
description: Use when computing enrichment/overlap statistics between genomic query ranges (e.g. caQTLs, DHS peaks) and feature ranges and a null distribution that preserves local genomic correlation structure is needed.

name: selex-cycle-enrichment-consistency-filtering
description: Use when preparing HT-SELEX datasets (e.g. ENA PRJEB14744 or PRJEB29730) for affinity regression and you need to exclude TFs whose enrichment values are inconsistent across SELEX cycles before training or testing.

name: sense-antisense-template-selection-by-longest-alignment
description: Use when analyzing direct-BSP or cloning-BSP chromatogram traces (.ab1) against a reference .fasta and you must decide read orientation and map cytosine positions onto CpG coordinates before computing methylation percentages.

name: sensitivity-curve-analysis-across-cutoffs
description: Use when comparing a method (e.g., TSMiner vs DREM) on recovering a known ground-truth TF set, and you need sensitivity as a function of P-value cut-off plus unique-TF counts across parameter settings.

name: sensitivity-specificity-ratio-analysis
description: Use when you have a set of positive-control SVs with known disease-causative genes plus a larger patient/VUS SV cohort and must compare per-SV pathogenicity scores across multiple classifiers.

name: sequence-book-output-validation
description: Use when a Delila-PY run has finished and the book of sequences emitted by the delila program must be checked against the input sites file before downstream motif cycles (malign/malin, alist/encode, makelogo).

name: sequence-grammar-motif-similarity-computation
description: Use when scoring candidate orthologous target regions after adaptive_liftover: you need motif-based sequence grammar similarity between query (e.g. mm10) and target (e.g. hg38) intervals to feed AdaLiftOver's logistic scoring.

name: sequence-information-content-filtering
description: Use when a Delila-PY cycle-2 per-sequence information content table (in bits, from alist/encode/cmp/rseq) must be filtered to remove poorly matching sequences before regenerating the book for cycle 3.

name: sequence-logo-generation
description: Use when you have a tab-delimited file of genomic binding-site coordinates (chromosome, name, strand, base pair position) plus a GenBank genome and need a reproducible DNA motif logo/PWM.

name: sequence-motif-visualization
description: Use when a single non-coding SNP needs motif-level interpretation: predicting how every base substitution within ~200 bp of the variant alters a specific chromatin profile (e.g. NFE2 binding) and visualizing informative motifs.

name: sequencing-cost-modeling-droplet-platforms
description: Use when planning a multi-sample single cell DE or eQTL study under a fixed budget and you must decide the trade-off between cells per individual, sequencing depth (reads/cell), and number of samples on a droplet (10X) platform.

name: sequencing-depth-downsampling
description: Use when validating that a Hi-C compartment/sub-compartment inference method recovers stable scores at shallow sequencing depths, by simulating trans-interaction summary files at multiple downsampled depths (e.g. 1x, 0.1x, 0.01x).

name: sequencing-depth-downsampling
description: Use when validating that a broad-domain caller (e.g., RECOGNICER on H3K27me3/H3K9me3 ChIP-seq) is robust to sequencing depth by downsampling mapped reads and comparing aggregate domain length and FRIP across depths.

name: sequencing-depth-downsampling-simulation
description: Decision support for whether a ChIP-seq/DNase-seq QC metric like FRiP is a genuine quality readout or merely an artifact of sequencing depth, especially when benchmarking shallow libraries or choosing downsampling conventions.

name: sequencing-depth-matched-model-selection
description: Use when scoring/predicting chromatin loops on a new Hi-C, Micro-C, or DNA SPRITE contact map (.cool/.hic) in a cell type or species different from the training set, and a depth-matched pre-trained model must be chosen.

name: sequencing-depth-normalization
description: Use when computing normalized ChIP-seq signal (buildChIPprofile, recoverChIPlevels, meta-plots, boxplots) from BAM files of samples sequenced at different depths, or when down-sampling to test depth requirements.

name: sequencing-depth-regression-normalization
description: Use when a SnapATAC cell-by-cell Jaccard kernel must be normalized for per-cell sequencing-depth bias before spectral dimensionality reduction of scATAC-seq data.

name: sequencing-depth-robustness-analysis
description: Use when evaluating loop-calling model robustness on downsampled Hi-C contact maps, or when comparing graph-view vs image-view branch performance across sequencing depths (e.g., 1.5% / 39M reads up to 520M reads).

name: sequencing-error-region-sequence-extraction
description: Use when you have genomic coordinates of systematic sequencing errors (e.g. the 3272 monocyte SSE positions on Hg18) and need paired signal/control FASTA inputs for fixed-position IUPAC motif discovery.

name: sequencing-fragment-extraction
description: Use when preparing fragment files for haplotype assembly tools (SpecHap, HapCUT2, FastHare, DCHap, ReFHap) from BAM/CRAM alignments and bgzipped VCF variant calls across diverse sequencing platforms.

name: sequencing-read-alignment
description: Use when simulated (wgsim/LRSIM, PBSIM/DeepSimulator) or real sequencing reads must be mapped to a reference genome and produced as sorted, indexed BAM files as a prerequisite for fragment extraction (extractHAIRS) and haplotype assembly.

name: sequencing-signal-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you have BAM/SAM reads mapped to a genome with a RefSeq refGene annotation and want standardized TSS-centered heatmaps or aggregated meta-plots of ChIP-seq or RNA-seq signal.

name: sex-comparative-epigenomic-aging-analysis
description: Use when you have male and female ATAC-seq peak-level log2 fold-change tables (young vs old) for the same peak identifiers and need a between-sex correlation of aging signatures plus per-sex DA peak counts.

name: sex-dimorphism-aging-group-comparison
description: Use when flow-cytometry or compositional immune-cell data must be split by sex and age groups (e.g., 65-year cutoff) and non-parametric group differences tested against reported statistics.

name: sex-dimorphism-pca-interpretation
description: Use when PCA has been computed on age-stratified PBMC ATAC-seq or RNA-seq samples and you must verify that PC1 scores correlate with donor age, match reported variance-explained, and differ between older men and older women.

name: sex-linked-motif-family-comparison
description: Use when you have two sex-stratified sets of differentially bound calling cards peaks (e.g. female vs male GBM CC Brd4 peaks) and need to identify TF motif families enriched in one sex but not the other.

name: sex-specific-epigenomic-differential-analysis
description: Use when comparing chromatin state sequences of protein-coding genes across male and female Roadmap epigenomic samples to test whether same-sex pairs align better than different-sex pairs and identify sex-linked differentially aligned genes.

name: sex-stratified-aging-signature-interpretation
description: Use when comparing age-related chromatin accessibility or gene-expression changes between male and female donors to determine whether cell-type-specific loci (e.g., B cell loci) close in one sex and open in the other.

name: sgrna-activity-label-binarization
description: Use when a CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa sgRNA screening dataset provides continuous phenotype or activity scores per sgRNA and a classification task (e.g., ROC-AUC evaluation) requires dichotomized activity labels.

name: sgrna-activity-score-regression-prediction
description: Use when you must predict sgRNA gene-silencing or activation activity scores (e.g. CRISPRoff_tiling, 111,682 sgRNAs within ±2.5 kb of TSS of 520 genes) from sequence plus cell-type epigenetic tracks, and benchmark regressors by Spearman correlation.

name: sgrna-genomic-interval-assignment
description: Use when sgRNA loci from CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa screens must be assigned cell-type epigenetic values (accessibility, TSS distance, methylation, expression) by genomic interval overlap before model training or prediction.

name: sgrna-sequence-epigenetic-feature-extraction
description: Use when building or interpreting sgRNA activity prediction models for CRISPR-mediated epigenome editing (CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa) and you need epigenetic feature matrices or SHAP-based feature importance for sgRNA design.

name: shannon-entropy-computation-from-probability-distributions
description: Use when RRBS-derived epiallele proportions phi_s exist per locus per sample (e.g. tumour regions R1-R7 plus normal N) and the goal is to quantify how disordered or heterogeneous each locus/sample is via entropy.

name: shap-feature-importance-interpretation
description: Use when a fitted gradient-boosted tree model needs post-hoc interpretation into ranked feature contributions, e.g. identifying which epigenetic features (nucleosome positioning, chromatin accessibility, RNA expression) favor sgRNA silencing efficiency.

name: shap-sequence-attribution-analysis
description: Use when you have a trained EpiCas-DL model (TensorFlow 2.4.1 backend) plus one-hot encoded 40-bp sgRNA sequences (9 bp upstream, 23 bp target, 8 bp downstream) and want position-specific nucleotide contributions explaining sgRNA efficiency predictions.

name: shiny-app-grouped-analysis-configuration
description: Use when individually analyzed BSP samples (per-sample methylation tables from direct-BSP or cloning-BSP .ab1 trace files) must be gathered into groups, compared statistically, and visualized with publication-ready boxplots, lollipop plots, and methylation profile plots.

name: short-range-chromatin-loop-verification
description: Use when a ChIA-PET dataset (e.g. GM12878 CTCF paired-end FASTQ) must be analyzed for very short-range (<8 kb) chromatin loops that standard pipelines miss due to self-ligation span cutoffs.

name: short-read-directional-extension-to-hdf
description: Use when ChIP-Seq short-read alignments (BED/ELAND) must be converted into a per-bin coverage profile that reflects fragment-length uncertainty, e.g. before HMM-based peak calling.

name: short-read-reference-alignment
description: Use when raw or adapter-trimmed FASTQ reads from ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, DNase-seq, MNase-seq, ATAC-seq, or GRO-seq datasets must be aligned to a reference genome to produce sorted BAMs with alignment statistics.

name: short-read-simulation-from-variant-haplotypes
description: Use when benchmarking haplotype assembly or variant phasing tools requires synthetic reads whose true haplotype origin is known, e.g. from trio-phased 1000 Genomes haplotypes across coverages (10x/30x/50x) and platforms.

name: short-tandem-repeat-signature-modeling
description: Use when benchmarking non-B DNA novelty detection (e.g. GoFAE-DND) on simulated data requires synthetic STR translocation-time windows that resemble experimental STR TT signals from nanopore reads.

name: sigma-factor-regulon-inference
description: Use when you have a candidate regulon list for a transcription factor (from ChIP or literature) plus time-course expression data, and need to predict which candidate genes are genuinely regulated.

name: signal-quantile-gold-standard-definition
description: Use when benchmarking differential-occupancy peak/differential-region callers on ChIP-Seq data without an external truth set: thresholds defined by signal quantiles (0.15 positive set, cutoffs to 0.6) provide a reproducible gold standard.

name: signal-score-continuum-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have centered genomic sequences (e.g. ±200 bp around peak summits) plus a per-sequence continuous score (e.g. MACS2 narrowpeak signal scores) and need motif enrichment as a function of position rather than a single enrichment statistic.

name: signature-gene-extraction-from-consensus-partitions
description: Use when a consensus partition result (e.g. from cola run_all_consensus_partitions over top-value methods SD/CV/MAD/ATC and partitioning methods such as skmeans) already exists and per-subgroup signature genes are needed for interpretation.

name: signature-region-overlap-mapping
description: Use when curated epigenomic/bulk ATAC signature region sets must be intersected with the peaks of a cisTopic object and converted into per-cell AUC enrichment scores (e.g. PBMC marker gene sets on 10X 5k PBMC data).

name: significance-analysis-of-microarrays-sam
description: Use when you have SRIQ cluster assignments (e.g., a diameter 0.63, 6-cluster solution on TCGA LUAD) and a log2-transformed gene expression matrix, and need per-cluster one-vs-rest differentially expressed genes.

name: silhouette-based-cluster-quality-evaluation
description: Use when SRIQ clustering output (e.g. ..._Clusters_Frequencies.pdf) lists multiple candidate solutions across 10 iterations and you must rank them by recurrence, QSS, and silhouette to pick a stable solution.

name: silhouette-score-computation
description: Use when a consensus partitioning run (e.g. cola over multiple k values) needs per-sample or per-k stability assessment, or when ambiguous samples must be excluded before PAC calculation or signature analysis.

name: similarity-matrix-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you have ranked TR (or other entity) tables from multiple methods applied to identical query region sets and need to quantify and visualize cross-method agreement of top-k lists via Jaccard indices and heatmaps.

name: simple-repeat-motif-clustering-across-rbps
description: Use when analyzing Skipper's enriched repeat element results across many eCLIP experiments and you need to characterize RBP sequence preferences for simple repeats, or to validate reproduction of the reported 216/219 enriched-experiment recovery.

name: simulated-annealing-model-regularization
description: Use when fitting dynamical ODE parameters from smoothed time-course expression data and you need unregularized vs regularized (r(β), c ≈ 0.1 × number of smoothed time points) fits compared for model discrimination.

name: simulated-annealing-parameter-optimization
description: Use when fitting non-linear ODE regulation models to smoothed time-course expression data and parameter values (synthesis rate, decay rate, regulator weights) must be estimated by global optimization over a regularized objective.

name: simulated-hi-c-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when evaluating or comparing TAD identification algorithms on simulated Hi-C contact matrices (e.g., Wang et al. IMR-90 noise levels 4-20) where ground-truth TAD boundaries are known and FMS/TAD-quality metrics are required.

name: simulated-mediation-recovery-evaluation
description: Use when you need to verify that a mediation-based cis driver ranking (e.g., WFTM/Sobel-based) actually recovers true underlying cis-trans mediations before trusting it on real SCNA/expression data.

name: simulation-based-method-benchmarking
description: Use when a paper claims a deconvolution or inference method outperforms a competitor and you must reproduce the comparison on simulated mixtures with known ground-truth subpopulation profiles, such as 40x GCB-monocyte bisulfite data.

name: simulation-based-single-cell-power-analysis
description: Use when you need to validate an analytic power-analysis method for multi-sample scRNA-seq DE studies against ground-truth simulations, or when you must quantify the runtime/memory cost of simulation-based power tools.

name: simulation-parameter-grid-sweep
description: Use when validating a statistical test (e.g., Sobel mediation) whose performance depends on sample size and effect strength, by simulating positive/negative controls over a parameter grid and computing per-cell performance metrics.

name: single-cell-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing scRNA-seq cell type annotation methods at the cluster level on benchmark datasets (Chen, Xin, Gierahn), or when reproducing the scCATCH vs CellAssign/Garnett/SingleR/scMap/CHETAH consistent-rate table.

name: single-cell-atac-cell-type-signature-enrichment
description: Use when a selected cisTopic LDA model exists for a scATAC-seq dataset and you must quantify per-cell enrichment of external epigenomic signatures (marker gene sets or bulk ATAC profiles) to assign or visualize cell-type identity.

name: single-cell-atac-copy-number-calling
description: Use when you have a normalized binned single-cell ATAC-seq matrix and need to call CNVs per cell to identify malignant subclones, focal amplifications, or arm-level chromosome gains/losses without a matched control file.

name: single-cell-atac-data-processing
description: Use when raw scATAC-seq fragment files need conversion into filtered, normalized, binned accessibility matrices as input to CNV calling or subclonal deconvolution with Copy-scAT.

name: single-cell-atac-enhancer-classification
description: Use when single-cell ATAC peak sets need to be separated into cell-type-specific CREs and you need an interpretable, motif-based model that names the TF motifs (e.g. MEF2C, NKX2-5, GATA, FLI1) driving the classification.

name: single-cell-atac-gene-score-modeling
description: Use when you have a target scATAC-seq gene score feature matrix plus first-round Cellcano predictions (probabilities and labels) and must retrain a teacher-student KD model on low-entropy anchor cells to label all non-anchor cells.

name: single-cell-atac-seq-imputation
description: Use when the input is a sparse, near-binary scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix (h5ad, txt/tsv/csv, or mtx folder) and the goal is denoising/imputation of missing accessibility values for downstream correlation or clustering evaluation.

name: single-cell-atac-topic-model-interpretation
description: Use when a fitted cisTopic object (e.g. cisTopicObject_pbmc.Rds with a selected 30-topic model) needs biological interpretation: assigning functions, master regulators, or cell-type signatures to each topic.

name: single-cell-barcode-quality-filtering
description: Use when raw cellranger-atac fragment files must be converted into a filtered, binned coverage matrix and low-quality cell barcodes need removal prior to single-cell CNV inference.

name: single-cell-batch-correction-fastmnn
description: Use when single-cell histone-modification datasets (e.g. scCUT&Tag GSE124680 vs GSE124690 replicates) contain distinct technical batches that must be merged before UMAP projection or clustering without losing true K562-vs-H1 biological separation.

name: single-cell-celltyping-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when validating or reproducing reported accuracy comparisons of scATAC-seq celltyping methods (e.g., Cellcano vs scJoint vs ACTINN) from a figure's Source Data file, specifically for tasks whose target is a FACS-sorted gold-standard dataset.

name: single-cell-cluster-marker-gene-identification
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix with predefined cluster labels and need a reliable per-cluster marker gene set before cell type annotation, especially to avoid pseudo marker genes from one-against-all comparisons.

name: single-cell-clustering-analysis
description: Use when scATAC clustering may be driven by CNVs rather than genuine accessibility states, and you need to test cluster stability by removing CNV-bearing chromosome peaks and comparing pre/post-reclustering assignments via AMI.

name: single-cell-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when clustering scATAC-seq data (e.g. the Forebrain.h5ad dataset, 2088 cells, k=8) and you need to compare SCALE against scABC, scVI, cisTopic, or SC3 using ARI/NMI/F1 metrics against reference labels.

name: single-cell-clustering-of-calling-cards-data
description: Use when analyzing single-cell Calling Cards qbed data (e.g., mouse cortex Brd4 scCC from GSE148448) where insertions must be assigned to cell types via Scanpy Leiden/Louvain clustering of matched scRNA-seq before differential peak analysis.

name: single-cell-cnv-calling
description: Use when starting from a scATAC-seq fragment count matrix (e.g., scDataSamp) and the goal is per-cell CNV inference, malignant/non-neoplastic cell classification, or linking genetic subclones to chromatin accessibility.

name: single-cell-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when a normalized single-cell RNA-seq matrix contains two or more condition groups (e.g. TGF-β-treated vs untreated HUVECs undergoing EndoMT) and a per-gene significance list is needed as input for regulatory-element queries.

name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing feature-reduction/embedding methods for scATAC-seq (or similar sparse single-cell) cell-type clustering, where robustness to per-cell coverage must be quantified with ARI/NMI against known labels.

name: single-cell-epigenomic-data-ingestion
description: Use when raw single-cell epigenomic data (paired-end FASTQ or per-cell BED files from GEO accessions like GSE124680, GSE124690, GSE105012) must be converted into count matrices for ChromSCape-based subpopulation analysis.

name: single-cell-expression-probability-model-fitting
description: Use when fitting/validating scPower's expression probability priors on a new atlas count matrix (e.g., Drop-seq, Smart-seq2, 10X) to verify predicted expressed gene numbers match observed counts before power analysis.

name: single-cell-hic-contact-binning
description: Use when starting from per-cell tab-separated single-cell Hi-C contact files (chromosome and mapped-position columns) that must be converted to binned contact matrices at 10-kb resolution prior to imputation or loop calling.

name: single-cell-hic-tld-detection
description: Use when raw (non-imputed) single-cell Hi-C contact matrices (e.g., Tan GM12878, Nagano mouse ES, Flyamer, Lee PFC datasets) need hierarchical TAD-like domain calls, and when benchmarking TLD predictors on sparse per-cell data.

name: single-cell-multiome-pseudobulk-aggregation
description: Use when single-cell multiome ATAC+RNA counts need to be aggregated per cell type into pseudo-bulk profiles before computing gene-peak correlations, as in bootRanges multiomicsCor.R (14 pseudo-bulk cell types).

name: single-cell-qbed-data-processing
description: Use when the input is raw single-cell calling cards qbed/ccf insertion data and the goal is cleaned insertions, called binding peaks, genomic annotation, and a cell-by-peak AnnData/Mudata object ready for differential analysis.

name: single-cell-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices (50kbp/5kbp bins or TSS regions) from scChIP-seq/scCUT&Tag/scChIC-seq must be cleaned of low-coverage and outlier cells before dimensionality reduction.

name: single-cell-rna-atac-integration
description: Use when matched scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data are available (e.g. 10X_PBMC_15K PBMC) and candidate distal regulatory elements must be linked to their putative target genes and validated against cis-eQTLs.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-power-analysis
description: Use when planning an interindividual single cell RNA-seq differential expression or eQTL study and you need to choose sample size, cells per sample, and sequencing depth to maximize detection power under a fixed budget.

name: single-cell-tld-hierarchical-decoding
description: Use when input is sparse single-cell Hi-C contact matrices (e.g., Lee human prefrontal cortex cells) and the goal is to detect hierarchical TAD-like domains per cell and test whether nested TLD features distinguish cell types.

name: single-cell-tsne-embedding
description: Use when you have a chromVARDeviations object (per-cell motif deviation scores) from single-cell ATAC-seq data and need a 2D embedding/visualization of cell-to-cell similarity.

name: single-epiallele-significance-testing-vs-random-control
description: Use when benchmarking bisulfite-seq epiallele analysis: you need per-epiallele frequency/entropy values and chi-square significance against a theoretical random (R) control to show whether frequent individual epialleles are deterministic or stochastic.

name: single-pass-peak-calling-validation
description: Use when a bulk Calling Cards qbed dataset (e.g. Brd4 K562 from GSE148448) needs TF binding site peak calling with a fast, deterministic greedy algorithm whose enrichment logic matches the MACCs method.

name: sliding-window-dna-sequence-scanning
description: Use when you have multi-FASTA ChIP-seq peak sequences (positive) plus a matched negative control set and need to identify over-represented degenerate IUPAC motifs of a chosen length L anywhere within the sequences.

name: sliding-window-saliency-averaging
description: Use when you need to interpret which individual base pairs in a megabase-scale DNA sequence drive a trained deepC chromatin interaction prediction, e.g. fine-mapping sequence determinants of chromatin architecture at base pair resolution.

name: smith-waterman-local-alignment-implementation
description: Use when two genomic regions are represented as single-track chromatin state label sequences (e.g. from ChromHMM) and you need a local alignment score capturing locally similar chromatin patterns.

name: snakemake-conda-workflow-configuration
description: Use when running an end-to-end (cf)MeDIP-seq workflow from raw FASTQ files to QC, alignment, methylation quantification and aggregation, and you need portable Snakemake/Conda environment deployment.

name: snakemake-pipeline-execution-for-clip-seq
description: Use when raw eCLIP FASTQ files with matched IP and input samples must be converted into reproducible enriched binding-site windows transcriptome-wide, replacing per-tool peak calling with an integrated Snakemake workflow.

name: snakemake-workflow-module-implementation
description: Use when implementing or reconstructing a reproducible bioinformatics module (e.g., FASTQ trimming/QC) from a published pipeline, where steps must be encoded as Snakemake rules with Conda-deployed environments and configurable behavior.

name: snap-file-preprocessing
description: Use when starting from raw scATAC-seq FASTQ or aligned BAM files and you need to build a snap file (v4, HDF5) with fragment, barcode, and cell-by-bin matrices as input to the SnapATAC R pipeline.

name: snap-file-read-grouping
description: Use when scATAC-seq fragments are stored in a snap (.snap) file with cluster assignments already computed, and you need to pool fragments from a subset of cells (e.g. a major cluster) into a pseudo-bulk signal for downstream peak calling.

name: snp-activity-difference-computation
description: Use when annotating query non-coding SNPs with per-assay functional impact scores across DNase I accessibility, histone mark, and transcription factor binding profiles, especially for tissue-specific GWAS variant prioritization.

name: snp-coordinate-annotation-handling
description: Use when tabular coordinate data (SNP positions, peak intervals) must be converted into GRanges objects with metadata columns as preprocessing before range-based enrichment or bootstrapped null-set analyses.

name: snp-phased-methylation-track-inspection
description: Use when a WGBS sample may harbor allele-specific methylation at an imprinting locus or known heterozygous SNP, and per-read, genotype-preserving visualization is needed (e.g., A/G SNP at MEST on chr7).

name: sobel-mediation-testing
description: Use when you have paired copy-number/epi-DNA alteration states and gene expression data and need to test whether a cis gene mediates alteration-to-trans expression effects, or to rank candidate cis drivers.

name: somatic-alteration-gene-embedding
description: Use when training or adapting CITRUS on TCGA pan-cancer data where the sparse binary SGA matrix (11998 genes) must be converted into dense gene/tumor embeddings before attention-based modeling.

name: somatic-mutation-burden-testing
description: Use when calling candidate driver elements (coding or non-coding) from tumour somatic mutation callsets (WGS or WES, e.g. PCAWG or TCGA) by testing whether per-element mutational burden exceeds a modelled background mutation rate.

name: source-data-reproduction-check
description: Use when a target finding is tied to a specific figure of a paper with a downloadable Source Data file, and you must verify a directional claim (e.g. male-specific B cell decline) from the published numbers.

name: sox-hmg-motif-family-annotation
description: Use when motif-calling output (e.g. HOMER results via cc.tools.call_motif) on CC differential peaks needs family-level annotation and the HMG/Sox family is a candidate sex- or condition-specific regulator.

name: spark-distributed-data-load-balancing
description: Use when running bisulfite (WGBS/FASTQ) read alignment on a Spark cluster where uneven partitions — e.g. from HDFS chunk boundaries or post-filtering imbalances — cause some executors to lag and dominate wall-clock time.

name: spark-distributed-job-execution
description: Use when aligning large WGBS bisulfite sequencing datasets (tens to hundreds of millions of 95 bp reads, e.g. FASTQ from GSE80911) where single-server aligners like Bismark are too slow and a Spark/HDFS cluster is available.

name: spark-rdd-distributed-processing
description: Use when aligning bisulfite-sequencing (WGBS) reads with the 'three-letter' approach where data volume (up to 4× genome expansion) makes single-node aligners like Bismark or CloudAligner too slow, and a Spark cluster with HDFS is available.

name: spark-rdd-key-value-partitioning
description: Use when building a Spark-based bisulfite alignment pipeline from FASTQ/A reads and you need to convert raw sequencing data into distributed, key-value-structured RDDs for parallel processing.

name: spark-rdd-pipeline-execution
description: Use when aligning bisulfite-sequencing reads (FASTQ/A) at genome scale on a Spark/HDFS cluster, where single-node aligners are too slow and you need scalable 'three-letter' alignment with optional load balancing.

name: sparse-cholesky-factorization
description: Use when standard errors are needed for a fitted GenoGAM tile (e.g. genogam() output with lambda = 4601, theta = 4.51) but the sparse penalized Hessian is too large for a dense inverse.

name: sparse-hessian-linear-system-solving
description: Use when fitting penalized GAMs (e.g., negative-binomial ChIP-Seq count models) whose Hessian is sparse, and you need direct sparse solves of the Newton-Raphson system rather than dense matrix inversion.

name: sparse-matrix-inverse-subset-computation
description: Use when standard errors or variances of fitted smooths are needed from a sparse penalized GAM fit (e.g., GenoGAM tiles with lambda = 4601, theta = 4.51) and explicitly inverting the Hessian would be too slow or memory-intensive.

name: sparse-matrix-iterative-convergence
description: Use when a very sparse Hi-C contact matrix (e.g., single-cell or downsampled to 0.025% sampling rate) needs imputation via RWR diffusion before downstream analysis, with symmetric sqrtVC normalization for convergence.

name: sparse-region-detection-filtering
description: Use when a single-cell epigenomic count matrix (bins, peaks, or TSS regions from scChIP-seq/scATAC-seq) contains sparse regions and you must filter lowly detected regions before dimensionality reduction or differential enrichment.

name: sparse-solver-based-fitting-superlu
description: Use when fitting tiled GAMs to genome-scale ChIP-Seq count data where dense Newton-Raphson matrix operations are prohibitively slow or memory-heavy, and linear runtime/memory scaling in parameters-per-tile is required.

name: sparse-triplet-matrix-generation
