description: Use when you have a duplicate-removed ChIA-PET bedpe file (e.g. prefixname.rmdup.bedpe) plus a tab-delimited chromosome sizes file and need a 2D genome-wide contact map rather than peak-anchored loop calls.

name: spearman-correlation-computation-2d-genomic-predictions
description: Use when evaluating 2D contact map predictions (e.g., Hi-C-derived maps from the DNALONGBENCH contact_map_prediction task) for models such as Akita, CNN, HyenaDNA, or Caduceus, where rank-based correlation is required.

name: spearman-correlation-metric-computation
description: Use when scoring predicted 3D genome contact maps from models such as Caduceus-Ph or HyenaDNA against observed maps on the DNALONGBENCH contact map prediction task, or when quantifying agreement (SCC, alongside PCC) for specific genomic regions like chr6:145,205,248-145,614,848.

name: spearman-correlation-regression-scoring
description: Use when a model outputs continuous sgRNA activity/efficiency predictions and you must quantify rank agreement with measured phenotype or activity scores, e.g. validating EpiCas-DL on independent genome-wide screening datasets.

name: spearman-correlation-statistical-testing
description: Use when comparing regression or classification models for sgRNA activity prediction on datasets like CRISPRoff_tiling (111,682 sgRNAs, 520 genes) and you need rank-based correlation plus significance testing across CV folds.

name: species-specific-marker-mapping-human-mouse
description: Use when a single-cell cluster annotation or marker-lookup task requires a curated, tissue-specific marker reference restricted to human or mouse, or when rebuilding/extending a CellMatch-style cellmatch table.

name: spectral-eigenvector-embedding
description: Use when you have a binarized cell-by-bin accessibility matrix (e.g., 5-kb bins in a snap file) and need a peak-free low-dimensional embedding of single-cell chromatin profiles for clustering rare populations.

name: spectral-graph-haplotype-phasing
description: Use when assembling haplotypes for a single diploid individual from long reads (PacBio SMRT, ONT), Hi-C, or 10X linked-reads, especially very large genomes or high coverage where max-cut/MEC tools exceed memory or time limits.

name: spike-in-chipseq-configuration-handling
description: Use when preparing to run spikChIP on multiple ChIP-seq experiments with exogenous spike-in (e.g. human hg19 + fruit fly dm3) and BAM/peak files must be wired into a configuration file before normalization.

name: spike-in-control-quantification
description: Use when a cfMeDIP-seq pipeline configuration declares spike-in controls and methylation levels must be quantified for those controls from extracted spike-in alignments.

name: spikein-normalization-strategy-comparison
description: Use when you have human+fly spike-in BAM files (e.g. Jurkat H3K79me2 25:75 vs 75:25 mixtures, GEO GSM1465005/GSM1465007) and need to quantify how a spike-in normalization strategy alters background vs peak-region ChIP signal.

name: spikein-read-ratio-scaling-factor-calculation
description: Use when comparing two spike-in ChIP-seq conditions (e.g. H3K79me2 25:75 vs 75:25 with fly chromatin) and you need a ratio-based scaling factor to equalize spike-in read depth before bin-level signal counting.

name: spin-glass-network-scoring
description: Use when gene-level p-values from transcriptomic and epigenomic data must be projected onto an interaction network to find dysregulated modules, or when two module-detection runs (e.g., FEM vs SMITE) need quantitative comparison of overlap and enrichment.

name: splice-aware-rnaseq-alignment
description: Use when RNAseq fastq files in a NEAT project's 'fatsq' folder need alignment and Targets.txt marks samples as RNAseq, requiring splice-aware mapping with Tophat.

name: splice-junction-aware-mapping
description: Use when RNA-Seq FASTQ reads must be aligned to a genome for downstream expression estimation or fragment-bias correction, and known gene annotations are available to constrain splice junctions.

name: spline-glm-fitting-overlap-counts
description: Use when bootRanges overlap counts between differential expression genes (logFC) and differential accessibility peaks must be converted into an optimized, data-driven logFC or SNP -log10(P) significance threshold rather than an arbitrary cutoff.

name: sra-data-retrieval
description: Use when an RNA-Seq reproducibility or bias-correction analysis needs the original public reads from named SRA accessions (single-end or paired-end library preps) before alignment with a splice-aware aligner.

name: sriq-cluster-stability-analysis
description: Use when SRIQ cluster solutions have been obtained (e.g. K3/K5/K6 at BagSize 1200, 10000 permutations) and you must verify that they remain reproducible under parameter or cohort-size perturbation.

name: sriq-cluster-subtype-crosstabulation
description: Use when you have SRIQ core/spiral cluster memberships for TCGA-LUAD samples and need to test whether they partition within, or refine, the Wilkerson TRU/PI/PP consensus subtypes via a cluster-by-subtype contingency table.

name: ssdna-binding-domain-annotation
description: Use when you must determine whether transcription factors (or their direct PPI partners) can bind ssDNA, e.g. to link HOT-region TFs to R-loop or G-quadruplex-associated sequence features.

name: statistical-mediation-testing
description: Use when you have paired copy-number-alteration (or epi-DNA) and gene-expression data with candidate cis genes and need to rank cis genes by how much of the trans expression effect they mediate, or to re-derive Rank-1 cis gene calls under resampling.

name: statistical-significance-testing-of-model-comparison
description: Use when comparing two or more scoring/prediction methods on the same positive/negative region sets and you must show AUC differences are statistically significant, not just numerically larger.

name: stochastic-count-perturbation-simulation
description: Use when a clustering or alignment method needs a ground-truth benchmark of noisy peak-profile signals whose seed-of-origin labels are known, e.g. to score DGW against standard hierarchical clustering via a multi-class MCC.

name: stouffer-pvalue-combination
description: Use when integrating multiple epigenomic/transcriptomic p-value tracks per gene (e.g. expression plus promoter/body/enhancer methylation) into one weighted significance score that accounts for non-independence of the combined values.

name: strand-asymmetry-estimation-of-consecutive-motif-occurrences
description: Use when you have a BED file of strand-annotated occurrences of one non-palindromic genomic feature and want to test whether nearby consecutive pairs show an orientation bias (same vs opposite strand) within a defined distance range.

name: strand-asymmetry-ratio-computation
description: Use when input is strand-annotated BED files of DNA features (e.g. TFBS motifs, ChIP-seq peaks, transposable elements) and the goal is to quantify whether same/opposite or convergent/divergent strand orientations deviate from the random 0.5 expectation.

name: strand-merged-methylation-calling
description: Use when Bismark-aligned MethylC-seq reads (SAM/BAM with XM methylation strings and XG genome designations) must be converted into a sorted table of per-CpG methylation counts, including novel CpG sites absent from the reference genome.

name: strand-orientation-assignment-of-genomic-intervals
description: Use when a BED/interval file lacks strand annotation and downstream strand-asymmetry analysis requires each feature to be oriented relative to an overlapping strand-assigned genomic element.

name: strand-specific-genomic-interval-analysis
description: Use when you have per-window, per-nucleotide translocation-time curves from Tombo re-squiggled ONT reads labeled non-B (e.g. G-Quadruplex_Motif) vs B-DNA, and need strand-resolved divergence testing (e.g. reproducing Fig. 5).

name: structural-entropy-graph-partitioning
description: Use when single-cell or sparse bulk Hi-C contact matrices need hierarchical TAD/TLD boundary detection without imputation, or when TLD hierarchy dynamics (e.g., across cell-cycle stages) must be quantified via modularity or structural-entropy-based partitions.

name: structural-variant-breakpoint-analysis
description: Use when you have unstranded SV breakpoint coordinates (BED) plus strand-annotated repeat elements and need to test whether breakpoints show transcriptional or replicative strand biases.

name: structural-variant-breakpoint-parsing-hg19
description: Use when a user provides raw SV calls (two breakpoints, SV type) from a patient and they must be converted into the 7-column tab-separated hg19 format required by POSTRE before running POSTRE_multiSV().

name: structural-variant-pathogenicity-prediction
description: Use when you need to classify non-coding or coding SVs (inversions, translocations, deletions, duplications in hg19) as pathogenic vs non-pathogenic for congenital-abnormality phenotypes and recover the causative gene and long-range pathomechanism.

name: structured-table-authoring
description: Use when a published figure or table encodes per-system feature assessments (e.g., check/cross/partial notation with footnoted qualifiers) and the goal is to reproduce it as a parseable CSV with one row per system and explicit qualifier text.

name: subcluster-identification-scatac-seq
description: Use when a reads-in-peaks scATAC-seq count matrix (e.g. GEO GSE99172) must be partitioned into sub-populations that can be traced back to cell lines, replicates, or patient-derived samples like SU070/SU353.

name: subpopulation-count-termination-testing
description: Use when deconvolving bisulfite sequencing data from heterogeneous samples where the number of allelic subpopulations per region is unknown and must be inferred from the data itself.

name: subpopulation-prevalence-estimation
description: Use when bisulfite sequencing (Methyl-Seq or eRRBS) data from a heterogeneous sample must yield relative subpopulation proportions comparable to FACS- or flow-sorted cell fractions, and cell-type composition is unknown a priori.

name: subpopulation-reconstruction-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating how accurately a subpopulation methylation deconvolution method (e.g. DXM, methylPurify) reconstructs known minor/major subpopulation methylation states from simulated bisulfite sequencing mixtures.

name: subsampling-performance-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether a computational method's detection performance (precision/recall/F1) degrades gracefully with reduced input depth, e.g. subsampling single-cell Hi-C contact files and comparing calls to a bulk-derived reference loop set.

name: subtype-classification-agreement-comparison
description: Use when a methylation (or expression) matrix with an established external subtype/label set is available and you must decide which top-value method (SD, ATC, etc.) yields partitions that agree with known subgroups.

name: summary-statistics-tabulation
description: Use when you need to tabulate headline counts and distribution summaries (N, provenance split, mean/median sizes, segment counts, copy numbers) from a merged bioinformatic catalog, e.g. reproducing eccDNAdb's 1270-eccDNA summary.

name: super-enhancer-typical-enhancer-sequence-classification
description: Use when the goal is to distinguish super-enhancers from typical enhancers from raw DNA sequences (FASTA) in a given cell line (e.g. mESC), or to reproduce the DeepSE-specific model with epochs=80, learning_rate=0.001.

name: supplementary-figure-reproduction
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce a specific supplementary figure from a published paper (e.g. Supplementary Figure S12) by re-computing the plotted metric for all methods on the same validation data.

name: survival-curve-visualization
description: Use when you have time-to-event clinical data (overall survival time + vital status) matched to gene expression, and need to test whether high vs low expression of an eccDNA gene is associated with prognosis.

name: sv-score-normalization-across-classifiers
description: Use when comparing SV pathogenicity predictions from tools that output scores on different scales, especially when ranking the disease-causative gene for positive-control SVs against a patient-cohort background.

name: svm-based-sequence-quality-discrimination
description: Use when reproducing DNAffinity on HT-SELEX data (per-cycle proteins/{protein}/{cycle}.txt files) and cases show inconsistency between enrichments at different SELEX cycles, biasing training/testing.

name: svm-baseline-reimplementation
description: Use when a study claims a new 6mA-site predictor outperforms iDNA6mA-PseKNC and the comparison must be reproduced under identical 5-fold cross-validation on cross-species, rice, or M. musculus datasets.

name: svm-hyperparameter-grid-search
description: Use when selecting among candidate classifiers (e.g., RandomForest, GradientBoosting, AdaBoost, ExtraTrees, SVM) on an encoded sequence feature matrix and the SVM candidate requires C and gamma tuning via grid search before fair cross-validated comparison.

name: switch-error-rate-evaluation
description: Use when you have phased VCF outputs from haplotype assembly tools on NA12878/NA19240 WGS data (NGS, 10x, Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, ONT) and need to quantify phasing accuracy against trio-phased truth.

name: synthetic-benchmark-dataset-generation
description: Use when you need a ground-truth-labelled benchmark to test whether a clustering or alignment method (e.g. DGW vs hierarchical clustering) can recover known seed patterns from epigenomic peak-profile data.

name: synthetic-community-abundance-estimation
description: Use when comparing sequencing methods (RIMS-seq vs DNA-seq vs bisulfite-seq) for species-level relative abundance estimation in mixed or synthetic bacterial communities with a reference genome per species.

name: synthetic-dna-sequence-motif-implantation
description: Use when benchmarking DNA motif-discovery tools on ground-truth data: you need FASTA pairs with known implanted IUPAC motifs at controlled frequencies and an nCC-based recovery score.

name: synthetic-enhancer-sequence-design
description: Use when BOM's save_shap_multi() SHAP scores identify the most predictive motifs for two conditions and you need concrete synthetic enhancer DNA sequences for reporter/MPRA validation of cell-type-specific activity.

name: synthetic-labeled-dataset-generation
description: Use when benchmarking non-B DNA detectors or classifiers on ONT nanopore translocation times and labelled synthetic windows with controlled non-B-to-B ratios are needed as ground truth.

name: synthetic-reference-genome-concatenation
description: Use when preprocessing spike-in ChIP-seq FASTQ reads that must align to both the experimental genome (hg19) and the exogenous spike-in genome (dm3) before spikChIP bin-level normalization.

name: tab-delimited-output-assembly
description: Use when a completed COnTORT run (GenBank .gbff plus a GEO search term) has produced per-series matched expression files and they must be joined into the final annotated, tab-delimited transcriptomic matrix.

name: tab-delimited-transcriptome-table-generation
description: Use when a task requires anchoring GEO gene expression data to gene annotations from a user-provided GenBank .gbff file and producing a joined, Excel/R-ready tab-delimited table.

name: tabix-indexed-genomic-matrix-generation
description: Use when per-sample cfMeDIP-seq methylation quantification files (e.g. MEDIPS, QSEA, or MEDStrand outputs) must be aggregated into bin-by-sample matrices and made region-queryable across many samples or batches.

name: table-row-subtask-generation
description: Use when an XML Watchdog workflow task definition contains <processblocks> entries and the concrete set of subtasks (one per sequence element, matching path, or table row) must be enumerated before execution.

name: tabular-genomic-data-manipulation
description: Use when you hold a COnTORT mean-centered tab-delimited transcriptomic matrix (locus tag, old locus tag, gene name, gene synonyms, product + GSM-labeled columns) and need ranked co-expressed gene pairs across many GEO experiments.

name: tabular-imputation-quality-control
description: Use when a variant-by-feature score matrix (e.g. EIGEN, CADD, DANN, GWAVA, FATHMM columns from ANNOVAR annotation) contains missing entries that must be filled before feeding the features into the ncDeepBrain/iMEGES deep learning model.

name: tabular-scoring-table-construction
description: Use when building a gene-to-phenotype scoring lookup from HPO (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype.txt) and MPO (mp.obo, HMD_HumanPhenotype.rpt) resources, where each gene needs a tiered score per phenotype group.

name: tabular-sv-input-formatting-hg19
description: Use when SV calls (VCF, BEDPE, or paper tables) must be converted into POSTRE's 7-column tab-separated hg19 format before running POSTRE_multiSV() or the Shiny Multiple SV Submission.

name: tabular-sv-manifest-construction
description: Use when preparing patient structural variant (SV) breakpoints (hg19) for input into POSTRE or POSTRE_multiSV(), and the raw variant list must be converted into the tool's 7-column tab-separated manifest format with phenotypes and unique SV ids.

name: tabular-transcriptomic-data-serialization
description: Use when joining per-experiment GEO expression tables with GenBank annotation into one Excel/R-readable tab-delimited matrix with annotation columns as the key.

name: tad-boundary-calling
description: Use when you need to call TAD boundaries from an NxN intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact matrix (e.g., GM12878 at 50 Kb/25 Kb/5 Kb or simulated IMR-90 matrices) without manual parameter tuning.

name: tad-boundary-delineation-from-cluster-labels
description: Use when you have per-bin cluster labels from HDBSCAN on TOAST graph auto-encoder embeddings plus the source Hi-C matrix resolution (50 Kb, 25 Kb, or 5 Kb), and need to delineate TAD boundaries for visualization or evaluation.

name: tad-boundary-prediction-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing TAD/TLD detection algorithms on very sparse Hi-C contact matrices (e.g., downsampled Rao et al. bulk data at 0.1%/0.05%/0.025%, 40 kb binsize) and ranking them by AMI and WS.

name: tad-boundary-rearrangement-classification
description: Use when a 7-column SV record (breakpoints in hg19, SV type Inversion/Translocation/Deletion/Duplication, phenotype list, SV id) needs its breakpoints classified against cell-type-specific TAD boundaries to build the rearranged enhancer–gene domain.

name: tad-boundary-regulatory-annotation
description: Use when you have TAD boundaries (e.g. TOAST-called boundary files for GM12878) plus ENCODE ChIP-seq narrowPeak files or enhancer/promoter intervals and need to compute per-factor boundary anchoring ratios.

name: tad-calling-pipeline-execution
description: Use when NxN KR-normalized intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact matrices (e.g., GM12878 at 5 Kb, 25 Kb, or 50 Kb resolution dumped from .hic files) must be segmented into topologically associated domains.

name: tad-co-membership-comparison-analysis
description: Use when you have a BHi-Cect cluster hierarchy plus a TAD segmentation and loop anchor coordinates at matched 5 kb binning, and need to compare co-membership of anchor-site pairs across the two partitions.

name: tad-similarity-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when called TAD boundaries (e.g., from TOAST, Armatus, Arrowhead, TopDom, HiCSeg, TADtree, PSYCHIC, or TADbit) must be compared against ground-truth TADs of simulated Hi-C genomes to rank methods or network configurations by FMS and Rand Index.

name: taps-bisulfite-free-alignment-mode-selection
description: Decision support for choosing 3-letter vs 4-letter Msuite alignment when input is TAPS, 5hmC-CATCH, or conventional BS-seq read data and non-CpG methylation levels determine the correct mode.

name: taqman-probe-transcript-mapping
description: Use when validating RNA-Seq expression estimates against independently measured qRT-PCR data, and you must restrict the comparison to transcripts with unique TaqMan probe mappings (e.g., the 907 uniquely probed transcripts on MAQC HBR).

name: targets-file-configuration-for-ngs-workflows
description: Use when building a NEAT project from FASTQ inputs (e.g., truncated H3K4me3 ChIPseq or RNAseq data from mouse embryonic stem cells) and you must declare samples, replicates, and which NEAT modules (unzip, QC, chiprx, map, filter, peakcalling, cleanfiles, granges) to execute.

name: task-dependency-topological-scheduling
description: Reference for driving or reimplementing the Watchdog execution engine: you must parse an XML workflow (e.g. example_dependencies.xml), schedule tasks in dependency order, verify success via custom checkers, and handle failures.

name: tcga-atacseq-bigwig-retrieval
description: Use when a candidate eccDNA region from whole-genome sequencing (e.g. an AmpliconArchitect-called amplicon) needs chromatin accessibility validation using the TCGA pan-cancer ATAC-seq BigWig signal tracks.

name: tcga-clinical-expression-data-integration
description: Use when TCGA gene expression (e.g., EGFR in TCGA-LGG) must be merged with overall-survival clinical metadata and compared between expression-defined patient groups to assess prognosis.

name: tcga-gdc-expression-data-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis needs tumor/normal gene expression values for specific genes (e.g., genes on an eccDNA like hsa_Chr7_3S_1) in a cancer cohort such as TCGA-GBM or CCLE cell lines, to compute expression differences and per-gene p-values.

name: tcga-luad-expression-matrix-handling
description: Use when raw TCGA-LUAD FPKM expression data (samples as columns, genes as rows) must be converted into SRIQ's required log2/median-centered format, or when per-sample TRU/PI/PP subtype labels must be derived from Wilkerson centroid genes.

name: tcga-pancancer-dataset-loading
description: Use when a task requires training or re-tuning CITRUS, reproducing the paper's TCGA experiments, or inspecting the pre-packaged pan-cancer SGA/GEP/TF-target matrices delivered as a pickle file.

name: tcga-pancancer-omics-preprocessing
description: Use when raw Firehose GISTIC2.0 lesion output (arm-level or focal, with q-values) plus paired TCGA RNASeq expression per cancer type must be transformed into iEDGE objects (cn, gep, cisgenes) as RDS for cis driver analysis.

name: technology-specific-extracthairs-parameterization
description: Use when preparing SpecHap input: an aligned BAM plus a variant VCF must be converted into per-read allele observations (a fragment file) for haplotype phasing.

name: temperature-scaled-soft-label-distillation
description: Use when you have first-round MLP predictions on a target scATAC-seq gene score matrix and need to classify non-anchor cells by self-distillation from confident anchors.

name: temporal-cluster-profile-summarization
description: Use when you have compartment scores for the same genomic bins across ≥3 ordered conditions/time points (e.g. dcHiC quantile-normalized PCA scores at 100 kb for days 1/7/28/56/309/347) and want to cluster bins by trajectory shape rather than compare pairs of transitions.

name: ten-fold-cross-validation-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a deep-learning variant-prioritization score (e.g. ncDeepBrain) against labeled disease/non-disease variant sets, where ROC curves and AUC on cross-validated testing data are the required performance metrics.

name: ten-fold-cross-validation-of-sequence-classifiers
description: Use when reproducing or extending promoter-prediction benchmarking that requires ten-fold cross-validation of ensemble sequence classifiers (RF + CNN + weighted average) on labeled promoter/non-promoter FASTA-style training sets.

name: tensorflow-model-shape-verification
description: Use when reimplementing, auditing, or extending the DESSO motif-prediction CNN and you must verify that filter kernels, fully connected weights, and output-layer weights match the published layer dimensions.

name: ternary-and-scatter-method-comparison-visualization
description: Use when you have per-RBP enriched-window/peak counts from two or more CLIP-seq callers (e.g., Skipper, Piranha, CLIPper) on the same ENCODE eCLIP datasets and must visualize and quantify how caller sensitivity compares.

name: tethering-interaction-inference-from-chip-seq
description: Use when ChIP-seq peak files and DESSO-predicted motifs/TFBSs are available for a panel of TFs in one cell type, and you need to identify co-factor-mediated (tethering) binding by finding peaks lacking a TF's own motif that co-occur with another TF's motif-bearing peaks.

name: tf-activation-repression-time-point-detection
description: Use when you have a time-series expression matrix plus TF-gene interaction data and need to determine, per time point, which TFs significantly regulate tree-structure subpaths and whether each TF is activated or repressed.

name: tf-binding-site-precision-recall-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare genome-wide TF binding site predictors (e.g., RoboCOP vs COMPETE vs FIMO baselines) using probabilistic occupancy scores and ChIP-based ground-truth binding annotations.

name: tf-dna-binding-auc-evaluation
description: Use when quantifying how well individual or combined DNA shape features (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) or sequences predict TF-DNA binding specificity across ENCODE ChIP-seq datasets, using test AUC from a trained DESSO CNN.

name: tf-enclave-contingency-table-construction
description: Use when you have BHi-Cect cluster output (named list of loci per cluster) plus TF ChIP-seq peaks for the same cell line and need a count matrix summarizing TF-binding content per bottom enclave.

name: tf-motif-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have two or more sets of differentially bound calling cards peaks (e.g., female vs male GBM CC differential peaks, BED/qbed-derived) and need to find TF motif families enriched in one group but not another.

name: tf-motif-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a gene set of interest (e.g. differentially expressed genes) and need to discover which TF motifs are overrepresented in the regulatory elements EpiRegio associates with those genes in a specific cell type or tissue.

name: tf-motif-scanning-open-chromatin-peaks
description: Use when building a TF-target gene prior from open-chromatin data: e.g., you have an ATAC-seq peak atlas plus a gene expression matrix and need a binary {0,1} TF-by-gene matrix to constrain a model's TF-to-gene layer.

name: tf-overlap-set-comparison
description: Use when a time-specific TF–pathway interaction network has been constructed (e.g., by TSMiner from time-series expression data) and you need to measure how many TFs are shared between consecutive-stage pathways to assemble a regulatory cascade.

name: tf-partner-fraction-analysis
description: Use when you need to annotate a defined TF set with ssDNA-binding domains (OB, KH, RRM, sPC4-like clans) and compute the fraction of TFs having at least one direct interaction partner that carries such a domain.

name: tf-pathway-interaction-network-extraction
description: Use when time-series gene expression data (e.g. mouse LR RNA-seq across post-PH time points) must be converted into time-specific TF–pathway regulatory networks to identify which TFs regulate pathways at each stage.

name: tf-pathway-mutual-interaction-scoring
description: Use when you have time-series expression profiles plus TF–TG interactions and pathway gene sets (KEGG/Reactome) and must decide which pathways significantly interact with a time-specific TF.

name: tf-target-prior-constrained-decoder-tuning
description: Use when training or re-tuning CITRUS on TCGA pan-cancer SGA/GEP data and the decoder's TF layer must remain constrained by the TF-target gene matrix (tf_gene weights) while balancing embedding size, attention, and regularization.

name: tf-tg-correlation-stratified-analysis
description: Use when a time-series expression analysis must distinguish TFs that activate targets (positive TF–TG correlation) from TFs that repress targets (negative TF–TG correlation), producing separate activator and repressor networks per time point.

name: tf-tg-interaction-scoring
description: Use when building time-specific TF-pathway regulatory networks from time-series RNA-seq (e.g. mouse liver regeneration data) plus a TF-gene interaction file and KEGG/Reactome pathway gene sets, and you need significant TF-pathway interaction scores.

name: tf-tumor-type-association-testing
description: Use when you have patient-by-TF activity values from a CITRUS model output (e.g. 'hid_tmr' from output_dataset_CITRUS.pkl) plus tumor barcodes and cancer-type labels, and you need to identify which TFs are significantly activated or repressed in each of the 17 TCGA tumor types.

name: tfbs-coordinate-extraction-from-ucsc-track
description: Use when strand-annotated BED coordinates for named transcription factor motifs (e.g. SP1, YY1) must be pulled from a UCSC conserved TFBS track (tfbsConsSites) to feed strand asymmetry or motif-pairing analyses.

name: tfbs-cross-matching-between-transcription-factors
description: Use when ChIP-seq peaks and DESSO-predicted TFBSs are available for multiple TFs in one cell line (e.g., K562) and the goal is to identify TF pairs where one binds DNA only via tethering to the other's motif-bearing peak.

name: tfbs-motif-importance-ranking
description: Use when you have trained cell-specific enhancer models (e.g. Enhancer-MDLF) plus sequence-derived motif features and need to identify which TFBS motifs drive predictions in each cell line.

name: tfbs-motif-overlap-strand-asymmetry-estimation
description: Use when both a regions BED file and a motifs BED file carry strand annotation ('+'/'-') and the goal is to test whether motif orientation is significantly biased relative to region orientation, e.g. TFBS orientation within CTCF ChIP-seq peaks or relative to transcriptional direction.

name: tfidf-text-document-embedding-of-tld-profiles
description: Use when you have per-cell TLD/TAD partitions from single-cell Hi-C and want a low-dimensional embedding that separates cell types based on nested domain boundaries rather than gene expression.

name: tfrecord-data-loading-for-genomic-tasks
description: Use when you need to feed DNALONGBENCH benchmark data (e.g., contact map prediction .tfr files for a specific cell line like HFF) into a model training or inference loop as batched train/valid/test loaders.

name: three-letter-reference-genome-conversion
description: Use when preparing a reference genome for bisulfite read alignment with a 'three-letter' aligner (BiSpark, Bismark-style): an unconverted reference FASTA must be transformed into CT/GA strand versions and indexed before mapping.

name: threshold-based-gene-classification
description: Use when you have CITRUS 'attn_wt' attention weights plus a gene list and need to binarize genes by attention magnitude to test driver-gene enrichment (e.g., against IntOGen).

name: tiling-chunked-genome-fitting
description: Use when fitting smooth base-resolution models (e.g. GAMs with design ~ s(x) + s(x, by = genotype)) across whole genomes from ChIP-seq counts, where genome-wide computation must be made tractable via tiling and parallelization.

name: time-course-expression-data-analysis
description: Use when you need to infer direct regulons of a sigma factor from time-course expression series (e.g. GEO datasets like GSE6865 or GSE44415) combined with candidate target lists from ChIP-chip, knockout, or database mining.

name: time-course-expression-smoothing
description: Use when time-course expression data (e.g. GSE44415, GSE6865, GDS38) must be converted into smooth continuous curves before fitting an ODE-based gene regulatory model or running regulon recovery comparisons.

name: time-series-deg-modeling
description: Use when an RNA-seq study has three or more conditions, a time-course, or batch effects, so a two-type design matrix (as CIPHER's expInfo schema supports) cannot express the contrasts of interest.

name: time-series-expression-data-input
description: Use when a workflow needs to supply time-series expression data plus TF–target interactions and pathway gene sets (KEGG/Reactome/GO) into TSMiner to build time-specific TF–pathway regulatory networks.

name: time-series-gene-expression-fold-change-classification
description: Use when a time-series expression matrix (e.g. LR RNA-seq time course) must be split into submatrices at candidate branching points of a tree-structure model, prior to Baum-Welch training in TSMiner.

name: time-series-gene-expression-network-inference
description: Use when you have time-series gene expression data plus TF–target interaction lists and pathway gene sets, and need to infer which TFs regulate which pathways at each time point.

name: time-series-regulatory-network-construction
description: Use when a time-series gene expression dataset (e.g., RNA-seq over a biological time course like mouse liver regeneration) must be converted into time-specific regulatory networks identifying when TFs and pathways become active.

name: tissue-specific-chromatin-profile-aggregation
description: Use when prioritizing non-coding GWAS variants in a tissue- or cell type-specific manner: you have per-variant SAD scores from DeepFun pre-trained models and need tissue-level aggregation plus a disease-by-tissue comparison such as a heatmap.

name: tissue-specific-gene-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a differential alignment or ranking of genes across two tissue conditions needs biological validation against a curated set of known tissue-specific genes and GO terms.

name: tissue-specific-gene-set-annotation
description: Use when you have a table of recurrent chromatin state patterns from EpiAlign horizontal alignment and need to determine which patterns carry cell-type-specific characteristics via tissue-specific gene overlap.

name: tld-clique-identification
description: Use when you have single-cell Hi-C contact matrices plus per-cell TLD predictions (e.g. from deDoc2.w/deDoc2.s) and want to detect higher-order multi-TLD structures and test whether inter-TLD contacts within candidate cliques exceed genomic-distance-expectation.

name: tld-partition-ami-evaluation
description: Use when comparing TLD/TAD predictor outputs on single-cell Hi-C contact matrices and you need quantitative, per-predictor quality metrics (2D structural entropy, modularity, AMI) to rank methods on raw, non-imputed data.

name: tld-prediction-robustness-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a TLD predictor (e.g., deDoc2, scHiCluster, deTOKI, Higashi) preserves its domain calls when Hi-C contact matrices are perturbed by controlled noise levels such as 10%, 20%, or 40%.

name: tld-predictor-parameter-configuration
description: Use when benchmarking multiple TLD predictors on scHi-C contact matrices (real or simulated, e.g., D = 750/1000 thresholds) and you need reproducible, fairness-preserving parameter settings per tool, including simulated-data overrides for Higashi.

name: tombo-resquiggle-signal-alignment
description: Use when raw nanopore FAST5 signals must be aligned to a reference at base-event resolution to extract per-position translocation times, because Albacore's fixed block strides are insufficient for timing analysis.

name: top-k-rank-cutoff-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when comparing ranked TR lists from multiple TR-identification methods on the same epigenomic query region sets, to test whether top-ranked hits agree at top-k cutoffs (k = 10, 50, 100).

name: top-value-feature-selection
description: Use when preparing a gene-expression or methylation matrix (thousands of rows) for cola consensus partitioning and a feature-selection step is needed to pick rows that drive subgroup discovery, especially when comparing SD/MAD/CV against ATC.

name: topic-region-binarization
description: Use when a fitted cisTopic object (e.g. the 30-topic 10X 5k PBMC model) must be reduced to per-topic region sets before running rGREAT GREAT() or topicsRcisTarget motif enrichment on hg19.

name: torch7-model-deployment
description: Use when annotating a batch of non-coding SNPs with per-profile functional impact scores using DeepFun pre-trained models locally (e.g. large variant sets beyond the web server), following the Basset SAD tutorial.

name: toxoplasma-gondii-host-cell-epigenomic-analysis
description: Use when SMITE's combined significance scores rise with the number of component p-values per interval in the T. gondii HFF data and you need to remove that p-value-count bias before module scoring.

name: training-log-and-metrics-recording
description: Use when training a DeepSE model (specific or integrative) on dna2vec-encoded SE/TE data and you need reproducible training logs plus saved evaluation metrics tied to the trained Keras model.

name: trans-homolog-interference-removal
description: Use when preparing Hi-C fragment files for SpecHap phasing: read pairs with inferred insertion spanning >40 Mbp signal trans-homolog interactions and higher trans interaction error rates that should be dropped before assembly.

name: transcript-expression-quantification
description: Use when RNA-Seq alignments (BAM/SAM, e.g. from SRA012427 or MAQC HBR libraries) must be converted into per-transcript expression estimates whose non-uniform fragment bias has been corrected before correlation or differential-expression analysis.

name: transcript-level-constraint-aggregation
description: Use when per-window variant-depletion delta scores exist for RBP binding windows and you need transcript-level nomination of constrained RBP-transcript pairs with FDR control.

name: transcript-level-estimate-reconciliation-across-sequencing-technologies
description: Use when two RNA-Seq libraries from different sequencing platforms (e.g. SOLiD MAQC WT-protocol and Illumina SRA012427) need expression estimates compared, and you must quantify how fragment-bias correction improves cross-platform agreement.

name: transcript-sequence-scrambling
description: Use when benchmarking TPX prediction tools on peak regions and you need shuffled-transcript negative controls that preserve nucleotide composition while destroying genuine triplex-forming signal.

name: transcription-factor-activity-inference
description: Use when you have a time-series expression matrix plus TF–TG interaction data and need to identify which TFs significantly regulate each subpath of a tree-structure model and when they are activated or repressed.

name: transcription-factor-affinity-feature-engineering
description: Use when raw DNA binding sequences from uPBM, HT-SELEX or gcPBM must be converted into structural/mechanical feature matrices to train or apply a transcription-factor affinity regressor.

name: transcription-factor-affinity-regression
description: Use when experimental TF-DNA binding data (uPBM training files, gcPBM concentration files, HT-SELEX per-cycle count files) must be converted into per-sequence affinity predictions with an R2-validated random-forest regressor.

name: transcription-factor-binding-motif-scoring
description: Use when you have anchor-centered sequences (FASTA with per-sequence scores in headers) and a motif PWM, and need motif match positions/scores relative to the anchor for positional enrichment profiling.

name: transcription-factor-binding-profile-interpretation
description: Use when a non-coding SNP needs functional interpretation against a transcription factor binding profile, and you want saturated mutagenesis SAD heat maps that reveal which motif and which allele-specific substitutions drive predicted binding activity.

name: transcription-factor-binding-site-detection
description: Use when converting enhancer FASTA sequences (e.g. data/train/NHLF.fasta) into per-motif TFBS count/frequency features for a deep learning enhancer predictor, using HOCOMOCO v11 PWMs with p-value thresholds.

name: transcription-factor-binding-site-mapping
description: Use when you have a promoter nucleotide sequence (FASTA) and a known TF consensus/position-specific motif, and need to enumerate motif matches and test positional overlap with other factors' binding sites.

name: transcription-factor-binding-site-proximity-annotation
description: Use when ChIP-seq peak coordinate files (e.g., MACS2 peak lists from GSE136050 H-NS and GSE136191 LuxR datasets) must be related by interval distance — e.g., counting how many of a structural peak class (H-NS doublets) lie within 1 kb of a TF peak.

name: transcription-factor-co-occupancy-intersection
description: Use when two transcription factors have ChIP-seq peak sets and transcriptomic differential-expression data, and the goal is promoters and downstream genes co-occupied and co-regulated by both factors.

name: transcription-factor-cofactor-motif-annotation
description: Use when you have DESSO motifs/TFBSs and ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks for multiple TFs in one cell line and need to classify indirect binding and infer TF-cofactor tethering from motif co-occurrence.

name: transcription-factor-motif-database-matching
description: Use when a set of de novo TF sequence motifs (e.g., predicted by DESSO from ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks) needs to be labeled as matching documented JASPAR/TRANSFAC motifs or flagged as novel/undocumented.

name: transcription-factor-motif-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have binarized topic-enriched regions from a cisTopic model on single-cell ATAC-seq data and want to recover topic-specific TF cistromes and master regulators such as SPI1 and CEBPB.

name: transcription-factor-motif-occurrence-analysis
description: Use when the input is a genome-wide TF motif occurrence track (e.g. JASPAR PWM-derived BED with strand annotations) and the goal is to quantify orientation bias — same vs opposite strand — between consecutive or paired motif occurrences.

name: transcription-factor-motif-scanning
description: Use when you have FASTA sequences under predicted ChIP-enriched peaks (plus matched control sequences) and need to verify enrichment of an expected TF binding motif family, or compare motif enrichment across peak ranks or platforms.

name: transcription-factor-pathway-interaction-analysis
description: Use when analyzing time-series gene expression profiles (e.g., RNA-seq across a biological process such as liver regeneration) to identify which TFs and pathways are activated or repressed at specific time points.

name: transcription-factor-peak-calling
description: Use when ChIP-seq FASTQ data for a DNA-binding factor (e.g., LuxR or H-NS in V. harveyi) needs trimming, reference alignment, and macs2 peak calling to count and compare binding peaks across conditions.

name: transcription-factor-rank-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing TR-identification tools on query region sets where the true perturbed/active TR is known, and a rank-based metric (MRR) over ranked TR output is needed for fair method comparison.

name: transcription-factor-target-gene-identification
description: Use when you have a TF ChIP-seq peak file (e.g. an ENCODE BED file) and need the set of unique genes whose associated REMs overlap the TF's binding regions.

name: transcription-factor-target-identification
description: Use when the goal is to identify candidate transcription factor targets by correlating gene expression across many diverse GEO experiments, given a mean-centered COnTORT output file with GenBank annotation columns.

name: transcription-initiation-signal-regression
description: Use when benchmarking 100,000-bp DNA sequence models on nucleotide-wise signal-intensity regression for transcription initiation, or when verifying that DNA foundation models underperform a task-specific expert model on TISP.

name: transcriptional-regulator-ranking-from-bit-scores
description: Use when you have a processed peak/DAR region set (BED with chromosome coordinates, e.g., from DiffBind or MACS2) and need to identify and rank candidate transcriptional regulators with uncertainty estimates.

name: transcriptional-strand-asymmetry-estimation
description: Use when strand-annotated motifs (BED files with '+'/'-' strands) must be tested for same-vs-opposite orientation bias relative to template/non-template direction of strand-annotated regions such as GENCODE protein-coding genes.

name: transcriptomic-matrix-tab-delimited-formatting
description: Use when building a cross-experiment gene expression compendium where per-experiment (per-GSM) offsets must be removed before downstream correlation or statistical analysis, following COnTORT's mean-centering-per-experiment output format.

name: transcriptomic-subtype-benchmarking
description: Use when a newly developed unsupervised clustering method for tumor gene expression data must be benchmarked against an established method (e.g., consensus clustering) by quantifying solution concordance per number of clusters K.

name: transfer-learning-fine-tuning
description: Use when a trained multi-input deep learning model must be adapted to a new cell line with limited or divergent enhancer data, and the goal is to quantify which transfer strategy (transfer_1/2/3) counters enhancer specificity.

name: transfer-learning-model-retraining
description: Use when you have Hi-C contact matrices (e.g. HiC-Pro output from GM12878 GSE63525 or downsampled valid-contact subsets) and need a sequence-based chromatin model retrained on that depth, starting from the chromatin-feature-seeded base model.

name: transfer-learning-weight-seeding
description: Use when training a sequence-based deep learning model on scarce, low-depth Hi-C targets and pre-trained chromatin feature weights are available to seed hidden layers before fine-tuning on interaction prediction.

name: transformer-fine-tuning-genomic-sequences
description: Use when benchmarking a sequence-based classifier against pretrained DNA transformers on the same CRE train/test partitions, e.g. comparing BOM or k-mer SVMs to DNABERT/Enformer on mouse mm10 E8.25 distal regulatory elements.

name: translocation-time-computation-from-current-events
description: Use when raw ONT FAST5 files (e.g. SRR15058166, R9.4.1 FLO-PRO002/SQK-LSK109) must be converted into per-position translocation-time signals for downstream non-B DNA structure modelling.

name: translocation-time-quantile-analysis
description: Use when nanopore (ONT) per-base translocation-time data and non-B DNA DB motif annotations (e.g. hg38) are available and the goal is to test whether 100 bp non-B motif windows deviate in TT quantiles from motif-free B-DNA controls, as in Fig. 4.

name: treatment-control-sample-classification
description: Use when processing compiled FRiP QC records (e.g. id_frip JSON from ChiLin's compile_database.sh) and you need treatment-vs-control class proportions passing an enrichment cutoff.

name: tree-ensemble-classifier-training
description: Use when several candidate classifiers must be compared on a fixed feature matrix (e.g., Motif+Kmer+Binary encoded DNA 6mA sequences) via cross-validation to select the algorithm before final model training.

name: triplex-prediction-parameter-sweep
description: Use when calibrating or benchmarking triplex (TPX) prediction parameters: multiple RNA:DNA interaction peak sets and RNA sequences are available and you need to determine which minimal TPX length, masking cut-off or scoring option maximises AUC against shuffled genomic negatives.

name: triplex-scoring-method-evaluation
description: Use when comparing TPX prediction scoring functions (e.g. stability-based vs match-count) on lncRNA peak sets with ROC/AUC, to decide whether biophysical scoring improves prediction over raw match counts.

name: triplex-thermal-stability-scoring
description: Use when predicting ssRNA:dsDNA triple-helix interactions and you need to rank TFO:TTS matches by in vitro thermal stability instead of raw match counts, e.g. within a 3plex/Triplexator-style pipeline.

name: trna-binding-enrichment-testing
description: Use when Skipper reproducible_enriched_windows tables exist for matched WT and mutant eCLIP replicates and the goal is to quantify and statistically test binding shifts toward annotated tRNA (or other repeat/ncRNA) loci.

name: tsa-seq-enrichment-quantification
description: Use when a Hi-C-derived sub-compartment inference (A1/B1/B3) needs quantitative validation against independent nuclear-body or lamina enrichment data such as SON TSA-seq, lamin-B1 cTSA-seq, or H3K27me3 ChIP-seq.

name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when promoter/non-promoter sequences (e.g. the iPro-WAEL 'data' folder human cell-line files) must be encoded with fused sequence descriptors and visually checked for class separation via t-SNE.

name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-visualization
description: Use when single-cell TLD predictions (or other per-cell text-like feature sets) must be visualized or clustered in 2D to test whether domain hierarchy carries cell-identity information.

name: tss-and-cleavage-site-coordinate-anchoring
description: Use when a motif enrichment analysis requires positional interpretation, i.e. you have assay-derived anchor coordinates (TSSs or cleavage sites) and want motif enrichment profiled at offsets around that anchor rather than presence/absence per sequence.

name: ttaa-density-relative-correction
description: Use when calling peaks from Calling Cards (qbed) insertion data with MACCs and computing Poisson p-values comparing experimental vs background insertions, to normalize for local TTAA-site density differences across candidate peaks.

name: tumor-clustering-from-tf-activity-profiles
description: Use when you have a CITRUS output pickle with patient-by-TF activity matrices ('hid_tmr', 'tmr', 'can') and want to check whether inferred TF activities recover known tumor-type distinctions or identify TF–tumor-type associations.

name: tumor-vs-normal-differential-expression-ttest
description: Use when a user asks whether eccDNA genes from eccDNAdb show differential expression between tumor and normal samples in TCGA cohorts (e.g. TCGA-GBM) or matched CCLE cell lines, and wants per-gene t-statistics and p-values.

name: tumour-cohort-burden-stratification
description: Use when GLM and GBM BMR models have been trained on the same train_feature.hdf5/train_y.tsv data and you must decide which algorithm to report or apply per tumour cohort, especially across cohorts spanning high vs low mutational burden.

name: tumour-multi-region-phylogenetics
description: Use when you have decontaminated epiallele profiles t_hat_s for multiple tumour regions (plus matched normal) and need to infer the tumour's phylogenetic tree from epiallele presence/absence.

name: tumour-purity-decontamination
description: Use when RRBS-derived epiallele frequency distributions (phi_s vectors) from multiple tumour regions plus a matched normal are contaminated by normal tissue, and profiles must be purified before identifying loci that differ between normal and cancer tissue.

name: tumour-purity-estimation-from-epialleles
description: Use when RRBS reads from one or more tumour regions plus a matched normal sample have been fit with bed_fit and you need to quantify normal-tissue contamination and produce cleaned (decontaminated) epiallele profiles per locus.

name: two-component-mixture-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating or reproducing DXM deconvolution accuracy on simulated bisulfite mixtures of two sorted cell types (e.g. GCB–monocyte) at known major/minor prevalences over TSS ±5kb promoter regions.

name: two-group-student-t-test-methylation-comparison
description: Use when individually analyzed direct-BSP or cloning-BSP methylation tables exist for ≥2 sample groups and you need comparative statistics (Student's t-test P-values) plus grouped visualization of CpG methylation.

name: two-sample-kolmogorov-smirnov-testing
description: Use when two independent score distributions (e.g. deepC saliency scores for eQTLs vs re-sampled matched background SNPs) must be compared non-parametrically via ECDFs to obtain a KS statistic D and p-value.

name: two-stage-pipeline-dispatch
description: Use when building or reproducing a Nextflow-based NGS pipeline that must share one fixed pre-processing stage (FastQC → trimming → alignment → QC) across dataset types and then dispatch mode-specific downstream analyses.

name: two-tailed-binomial-orientation-testing
description: Use when oriented genomic features (e.g. strand-annotated TFBS BED files) must be tested for significant same/opposite strand preference relative to a null expectation of 0.5 across many feature sets.

name: two-tailed-binomial-pvalue-calculation
description: Use when you have classified strand-oriented genomic events (e.g. same/opposite or convergent/divergent motif orientations) into two classes and need a significance test against a null expectation of 0.5, with multiple-testing correction.

name: ucsc-genome-annotation-retrieval
description: Use when a SeqCode command (e.g. genomeDistribution, produceTSSmaps, matchpeaksgenes) requires genome annotation inputs and the correct chromosome-size and RefSeq transcript files must be fetched for a specific genome assembly.

name: umi-aware-deduplication
description: Decision support for choosing between SAMtools markdup and UMI-tools dedup when aligning cfMeDIP-seq libraries that may or may not incorporate UMI barcodes, as declared in the YAML configuration.

name: umi-barcode-extraction-regex-matching
description: Use when input FASTQ libraries (single-end or paired-end cfMeDIP-seq) carry UMI barcodes for sequence error suppression and barcodes must be extracted and reads lacking the expected barcode filtered before adapter trimming.

name: umi-dependent-gamma-parameter-regression
description: Use when constructing a cell type-specific expression prior for scPower power analysis from pilot scRNA-seq UMI count matrices, requiring gene-mean distributions parameterized by sequencing depth (mean UMI per cell).

name: unet-image-based-loop-classifier-training
description: Use when Hi-C contact matrices (KR-normalized O/E, .cool or Juicer dump format) must be converted to image-view patches and a U-Net classifier trained with binary loop/no-loop labels, e.g. as the image branch or baseline in GILoop experiments.

name: unet-image-branch-training
description: Use when training GILoop on Hi-C contact matrices and you need the image branch to learn from high-depth data — e.g., when combining branches pre-trained at their preferred matrix densities (U-Net at full depth) before mixed-density fine-tuning.

name: unet-image-encoder-coding
description: Use when reconstructing or modifying the GILoop dual-branch architecture and you need to code the U-Net encoder-decoder that produces per-pixel image features from Hi-C contact-map patches for bilinear fusion.

name: uneven-pyramid-resolution-reduction
description: Use when raw Hi-C contact maps (e.g. KR-normalized Rao et al. GSE63525 at 5 kb resolution) must be converted into percentile-tagged skeleton annotations as ground-truth targets for deepC training or prediction.

name: unique-mapping-ratio-qc-statistics
description: Use when screening newly produced ChIP-seq or DNase-seq FASTQ/BAM files for mapping quality, or when comparing a new sample's uniquely mapped read ratio against cumulative historical QC distributions to decide if it passes the >0.5 cutoff.

name: univariate-hmm-fitting-for-chip-seq
description: Use when you have duplicated-read-removed ChIP-seq BAM files for a single sample of a broad histone mark (e.g. H3K27me3) and need genome-wide probabilistic calls of modified versus unmodified regions rather than peak-like summits.

name: unix-text-processing-pipelining
description: Use when a workflow task over plain-text data (e.g. gzipped FASTQ read headers and sequence subsets) can be expressed as chained basic UNIX tools inside a Watchdog XML workflow, and resource-light local execution is sufficient.

name: upbm-sequence-motif-trimming-with-meme
description: Use when preprocessing uPBM training data (long oligos, e.g. 35-mers in proteins/{protein}/{protein}_training.txt) prior to affinity regression, to cut sequences down to the MEME-derived motif region.

name: user-input-burden-comparison-across-pipelines
description: Use when benchmarking CIPHER's speed and ease-of-use against other NGS analysis pipelines (e.g. HiChIP, MAP-RSeq, bcbio-nextgen) on the same public ChIP-seq or RNA-seq FASTQ datasets.

name: vae-gmm-model-training
description: Use when you need to cluster or embed a sparse, near-binary scATAC-seq peak-by-cell matrix and want a VAE+GMM latent representation instead of scRNA-seq tools like scVI or weighted K-medoid methods like scABC.

name: vae-latent-feature-learning
description: Use when the input is a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix (h5ad, txt/tsv/csv, or mtx folder with count/peak/barcode files) suffering from 'missingness', and the goal is clustering, 2D embedding, or imputation of individual peaks.

name: variable-length-sequence-adaptive-pooling
description: Use when converting enhancer/DNA FASTA sequences of differing lengths into fixed-dimensional dense numeric features for a deep learning model, using pre-trained dna2vec k-mer vectors plus adaptive pooling.

name: variance-explained-reconciliation
description: Use when reproducing or auditing a published PCA claim: per-individual PC1 scores, donor age and sex are available, and the variance explained by PC1 and group differences (e.g., older men vs older women) must be verified.

name: variant-allele-depth-quality-filtering
description: Use when preparing 10x linked-read fragment files (e.g. from extractHAIRS --10x 1 output) for phasing and you must remove low-depth/low-quality variants and enforce barcode-level constraints (MAPQ >= 30 ends, <= 60 kb span).

name: variant-annotation-feature-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing ANNOVAR-annotated, genome-wide variant score matrices for iMEGES variant-prioritization training and the DANN, CADD, EIGEN, GWAVA or FATHMM score columns contain missing values.

name: variant-delta-score-scoring
description: Use when you need per-variant sequence-effect scores for SNVs in RBP binding windows — e.g. to test whether disruptive variants (low gnomAD AF) show larger predicted binding changes than common variants.

name: variant-effect-prediction-from-chromatin-interaction-models
description: Use when prioritizing non-coding SNPs (e.g., GWAS loci such as the 17q21 asthma variants rs12936231 and rs4065275) for likely causal status based on their predicted effect on chromatin interaction maps.

name: variant-to-gene-genomic-distance-assignment
description: Use when you have a prioritized list of non-coding variant scores (e.g., ncDeepBrain output on a VCF/Annovar bed input) and need them attached to genes to build gene-level feature vectors for disease-gene prioritization.

name: variational-autoencoder-implementation
description: Use when scATAC-seq peak-by-barcode count data (e.g. Forebrain.h5ad, 2088 cells) are sparse and high-dimensional with severe missingness, and clustering/visualization/imputation requires learning low-dimensional latent features via a VAE with GMM prior.

name: variational-autoencoder-latent-feature-extraction
description: Use when input is a scATAC-seq count matrix (h5ad, txt/tsv/csv, or mtx folder of peak/barcode files) that is sparse and close-to-binary, and the goal is cell clustering, visualization, or imputation via a learned latent feature space.

name: viterbi-decoding-of-binary-methylation-vectors
description: Use when bisulfite sequencing data from a heterogeneous sample has been reduced to per-CpG fractional methylation and coverage over user-defined regions (e.g. CGIs), and the most likely methylation state vector of each underlying subpopulation across the region must be recovered.

name: viterbi-regulator-time-assignment
description: Use when a trained tree-structure model of a time-series expression matrix (e.g., mouse liver-regeneration RNA-seq) exists and each regulator must be assigned to the time point at which it influences its targets.

name: weibull-distribution-fitting
description: Use when significant long-range chromatin contacts must be called from distance-normalized Hi-C/capture Hi-C contact tables, requiring a fitted null distribution for p-value/FDR computation.

name: weighted-average-ensemble-fusion
description: Use when two complementary base classifiers (e.g. RF and CNN) trained on the same promoter/non-promoter sequences must be combined into one ensemble prediction without retraining, following the iPro-WAEL weighted average design.

name: weighted-midpoint-center-computation
description: Use when raw narrow-peak BED files from ENCODE/Roadmap chromatin profiles must be converted into fixed-length (1000 bp), non-overlapping (>200 bp) genomic training intervals for a Basset/DeepFun CNN input.

name: weighted-similarity-domain-matching
description: Use when two sets of TAD/TLD boundary predictions must be compared quantitatively (e.g., noisy vs. reference Hi-C calls, or two predictors on the same matrix) and a contact-weighted domain-overlap score, excluding intermediate windows, is needed.

name: weighted-similarity-scoring
description: Use when comparing TLD/TAD partitions predicted from a raw bulk Hi-C matrix against partitions from downsampled (e.g. 0.1%, 0.05%, 0.025%) or otherwise degraded Hi-C data to quantify predictor robustness to sparsity.

name: weighted-trans-mediation-fraction-computation
description: Use when a copy-number (SCNA) or epi-DNA alteration has both a cis gene candidate set and a trans gene expression signature, and you must rank cis genes by how much of the trans effect they statistically mediate to flag the Rank-1 driver.

name: weighted-unweighted-score-concordance-evaluation
description: Use when a SMITE-style p-value aggregation offers optional per-interval weights (e.g., TSS distance) and you must decide whether weighting materially changes final gene scores, modules, or annotations.

name: wgbs-dna-methylation-quantification
description: Use when each sgRNA locus needs a methylation value from WGBS/GEO tracks assigned by genomic coordinate overlap before min-max normalization and deep-learning model input.

name: wgbs-methylation-profiling
description: Use when comparing DNA methylation levels or methylation variability between pre-defined genomic region sets (e.g., HOT regions, occupancy-binned non-HOT regions, CpG islands) across multiple cell types using WGBS methylation calls.

name: wgbs-read-alignment-bisulfite-mode
description: Use when raw WGBS/BS-seq FASTQ reads must be aligned to a reference genome while preserving cytosine methylation information, and the protocol is bisulfite (not TAPS/5hmC-CATCH).

name: wgs-read-alignment-to-hg19
description: Use when the input is raw WGS FASTQ (or unaligned BAM) from tumor samples and the goal is to reconstruct eccDNA/focal amplifications via the BWA–ReadDepth–AmpliconArchitect pipeline on hg19.

name: wig-format-file-writing
description: Use when a ChIP-Seq workflow needs per-bin read-coverage tracks (e.g. 25 bp bins with end-down-weighted HDF counts) written as WIG files for UCSC genome browser visualization or downstream inspection.

name: wiggle-signal-file-generation
description: Use when a ChIPseq pipeline step must produce a .wig genome-browser signal track (e.g. for IGV), especially when normalized genome-wide signal from standard plus spike-in (exogenous epigenome) alignments is needed.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when comparing a continuous measurement (e.g. cell-type proportions) between two independent groups — such as men vs women, or young vs older donors with a 65-year cutoff — and no normality assumption is warranted.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-sex-comparison
description: Use when comparing a continuous score (e.g., PCA PC1) between two small, non-normally distributed donor groups — specifically older men vs older women from an age-stratified PBMC cohort — without assuming normality.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-significance-testing
description: Use when identifying per-cluster marker genes from scRNA-seq data with pre-defined cluster labels, and you need to exclude genes upregulated in two or more clusters (pseudo marker genes) before cell type annotation.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing
description: Use when you have two independent groups of non-normal, possibly unequal-variance scores — such as pairwise alignment scores per gene — and need a per-item P-value to rank differential behavior.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing-across-cell-types
description: Use when building cell-type-agnostic features for enhancer-target interaction classification and you have enhancer activity and target gene expression measured across many cell types (e.g. 104 ENCODE CTs, 112 DHS tissues).

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing-on-sparse-count-matrices
description: Use when you have a filtered, normalized single-cell chromatin count matrix (scChIP-seq/scATAC-seq, e.g. 50kbp bins or peaks) plus per-cell cluster labels, and you need cluster-specific enriched/depleted regions for downstream gene set interpretation.

name: wilcoxon-spike-in-equilibration-testing
description: Use when you have spikChIP output bin files (FINAL_*_spike and FINAL_*_sample peak/background classes) for ≥2 conditions and need to rank normalization strategies by spike-in equilibration quality and detect background overcorrection.

name: wildtype-versus-mutant-comparative-visualization
description: Use when paired-end MNase-seq data exist for two matched cell populations (e.g. wild type and a temperature-sensitive mutant such as orc1-161 under G2 arrest) and you need to visualize condition-specific DBF/nucleosome occupancy at annotated loci such as replication origins.

name: wilkerson-centroid-subtype-classification
description: Use when you need per-sample TRU/PI/PP molecular subtype calls for a LUAD log2-transformed, median-centered expression matrix (e.g. an SRIQ '_mc_log2_nz' file), or when testing whether a new clustering solution partitions within existing consensus subtypes.

name: window-based-genome-scanning-peak-calling
description: Use when calling TF binding sites from Calling Cards qbed/ccf insertion data, especially when you need genome-wide window-scan peaks with Poisson significance tests and an optional background-free lambda-window variant.

name: window-resolution-parameter-tuning
description: Use when running SeqCode visualization commands on BAM/SAM read data and you must choose or justify a window resolution for TSS/peak meta-plots and heatmaps, or verify results are robust to coarser binning.

name: wms-execution-overhead-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether adopting a workflow management system (e.g., Watchdog or Snakemake) adds measurable runtime cost over raw task execution, by scaling input sample counts and separating scheduling overhead from task compute time.

name: wms-feature-comparison-curation
description: Use when a task requires reproducing or auditing the published feature comparison of workflow management systems (Watchdog vs. Galaxy, KNIME, Snakemake) from Fig. 12 of the Watchdog article, including its footnote qualifiers such as KNIME's paid-extension requirement.

name: workflow-container-initialization-sprproject
description: Use when starting execution of a systemPipeR workflow (e.g., the RNA-Seq template in a freshly generated spr_project directory) and a workflow container with logging must be created before importWF/runWF can be called.

name: workflow-failure-detection-and-intervention-handling
description: Use when a Watchdog XML workflow execution must verify task success with custom success checkers and the run log must record blocked tasks and one intervention action (release, restart, skip, resolve) per failure.

name: workflow-management-system-capability-assessment
description: Use when a task requires comparing WMS capabilities (setup, workflow design, execution, tool integration) from a published comparison figure, or when choosing between Watchdog, Galaxy, KNIME, Snakemake, and Nextflow for distributed large-scale data analysis.

name: workflow-management-system-execution
description: Use when a multi-step bioinformatics analysis (e.g. FASTQ information extraction or RNA-seq replicate analysis) must be orchestrated as reproducible module tasks with error detection, success checkers, or distributed execution across conditions and replicates.

name: workflow-runtime-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking a workflow management system's scheduling overhead: you have a runnable Watchdog workflow XML (or an equivalent Snakemake rule chain) and need to measure how much time the WMS itself adds versus the tasks it executes across increasing sample counts.

name: workflow-runtime-profiling
description: Use when comparing the execution time and parameter/setup burden of NGS pipelines on the same FASTQ inputs, e.g. validating claims that a parallelized workflow (CIPHER) outperforms serial alternatives on ChIP-seq or RNA-seq data.

name: workflow-task-success-verification
description: Use when executing a Watchdog XML workflow and each scheduled task's completion must be checked (e.g. via a custom success checker as in example_checkers.xml) before dependents are released, or when a failed task must be blocked and resolved by manual intervention.

name: x-chromosome-dosage-proxy-classification
description: Use when building or reimplementing per-gene dosage-sensitivity classifications from ClinGen HI/TS scores and you must score X/Y chromosome genes that have no TS entry in the published dosage sensitivity maps.

name: x-inactivated-gene-enrichment-quantification
description: Use when you have differential ChIP-seq region calls for a repressive broad mark (H3K9me3/H3K27me3) and a curated gene list (e.g. the 250 X-inactivated protein coding genes) and must report the percentage of overlapping base pairs and genes per method.

name: x-inactivation-cgi-methylation-analysis
description: Use when bisulfite sequencing data (bismark/bsmap/biscuit .cov or similar) should be tested for allele-specific methylation at X-linked CGIs or imprinted DMRs, e.g. female-vs-male X-inactivation skews or primed-vs-naive imprinting loss.

name: xgboost-gradient-boosting-model-training
description: Use when a labeled enhancer-promoter pair table (ET pairs with CT-specific and/or generic features) needs binary interaction classification, or when reproducing feature-set ablations (CT-specific vs generic vs combined) scored by AUPRC and F1.

name: xml-workflow-configuration
description: Use when a task requires defining or running a multi-step analysis pipeline in Watchdog, editing XML workflow definitions (task dependencies, executors, success checkers, constants), or reusing shipped example workflows such as workflow1_basic_information_extraction.xml.

name: xml-workflow-dependency-parsing
description: Use when an agent must execute or reconstruct a Watchdog workflow from an XML file (e.g. example_dependencies.xml), resolving task dependencies, verifying success with custom checkers, and handling blocked tasks.

name: xml-workflow-placeholder-expansion
description: Use when a Watchdog XML workflow contains process blocks (process sequences, folders, tables, or predecessor return values) and you need to enumerate the resulting subtasks by expanding placeholders into concrete instance variable assignments.

name: z-score-amplification-thresholding
description: Use when you have a normalized binned scATAC-seq matrix per cell and need to call focal amplifications (e.g., double minutes) at single-cell resolution without a matched control sample.

name: z-score-normalization-of-genomic-bins
description: Use when you have dcHiC quantile-normalized compartment scores for multiple ordered time points (e.g., an ESC-NPC-CN developmental course) and want to cluster bins by trajectory shape before time-series clustering.

name: z-score-significance-assessment
description: Use when an observed overlap between query ranges (e.g., caQTL or SNP sets) and target ranges (e.g., ATAC-seq peaks) must be tested against block-bootstrapped null ranges, and a z-score of the overlap rate is needed.

name: z-score-trajectory-normalization
description: Use when a feature-by-donor abundance matrix has an ordered age/time axis and you need to normalize per-feature fitted temporal trends to comparable scale before clustering, e.g. finding shared aging trajectories of peaks/genes across adult lifespan.

name: zero-inflated-count-modeling
description: Use when count-per-bin data (e.g., HDF counts per 25 bp genome bin) shows far more zeros than a Poisson predicts and you need to choose among ZIP, Poisson, and NB emissions for a background state.

name: zero-inflated-gamma-mixture-fitting
description: Use when building scPower expression priors from a pilot UMI count matrix: you have pseudobulk-normalized gene means per cell type and need a zero-inflated gamma model over the means to later compute expression probabilities at chosen read depths.

name: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-mixture-fitting
description: Use when you have preprocessed binned bivariate read-count tables (e.g. histoneHMM BN.txt/SHR.txt) and need to reconstruct or fit the emission densities of a bivariate HMM for differential histone modification analysis.

name: zero-inflated-poisson-background-modeling
description: Use when calling ChIP-enriched regions from HDF per-bin counts (e.g., 25 bp bins) and you need a discrete emission model that explicitly handles excess zeros in background coverage alongside an overdispersed enriched-state signal.
